“You’re incredible to have lasted this long,” he admitted. “I’ve only looped three times and I already feel like I’m at my limit.”

Shuddering at the memory of his last gruesome death, he added, “When I woke up just now, I couldn’t stand staying on that bus another second. Even if I had to die, I didn’t want to die in there again.”

“I’m sorry!”

Li Shiqing flinched at his words, her face going pale.

“Really, I’m sorry! I didn’t know pulling you out would get you stuck too. I thought it would save your life. If I’d known it would drag you into this loop, I’d never have done it!”

What was worse than death?

Endless deaths.

No one knew that despair better than she did.

“Forget it,” the Bespectacled Boy muttered, rubbing his nose as if embarrassed by his own compassion. “With or without you pulling me off, I’d probably still be dead. Didn’t you say the first time you woke up, the bus was already in an accident? That means whenever something happens to the bus, it happens to me too. So what difference does it make if I die inside or outside?”

He gave a wry smile.

“As messed up as this is, at least we’ve been given a chance to figure it out.”

“You… you’re such a good person,” Li Shiqing whispered, staring at him in disbelief.

Her guess had been right. He was a gentle, considerate, sensible man.

“Is that your way of sending me a compliment card?” he joked awkwardly, before cutting himself off, perhaps remembering how she had pulled him off the bus. “I’m not that good. I just think… maybe we can help each other out from now on.”

It was better to be teammates—even in disaster—than to be alone, paranoid, or at each other’s throats.

How many people would have reacted as calmly as he had? How many would have resisted blaming her for dragging them into this hell?

Not only had he refrained from anger, he had even reassured her.

“It’s shameful to say, but if I hadn’t found you—someone else stuck in this loop with me—I probably would’ve just given up and let fate take me,” Li Shiqing admitted, wiping her eyes. “So much hope, only to have it erased… I don’t think I would’ve kept going.”

He stared at her, stunned.

“…I was thinking the same thing.”

They looked at each other and smiled.

“My name’s Xiao Heyun,” he said, extending his hand with a small smile. “I’m a programmer. Just started working.”

“I’m Li Shiqing,” she replied, startled but quickly reaching out. “I’m a junior at U of W.”

That simple exchange of names carried trust and reconciliation.

Li Shiqing was so grateful she nearly cried again.

For a moment, the tiny changing room felt like a safe house after the storm. Cramped, yes, but it drew them closer together.

Strangers only hours ago, they now trusted each other without hesitation. The awkwardness between them melted away.

“It’s 1:55,” Xiao Heyun said after checking his phone. “After an explosion like that, the police must be searching for us everywhere. There’s no surveillance here, but they’ll still find us sooner or later.”

He pushed up his glasses, his expression turning serious.

“Time is short. Let’s exchange everything we know.”

CONTENT END 7

chapters.title: The Ninth Cycle of Time (II)
chapters.content:
After Li Shiqing pulled Xiao Heyun out of the car, he thought he had met a madman, cursed a few times, then admitted his bad luck and continued to the other side of the bridge, trying to find a taxi or hitchhiker to cross.

Before he could get very far, the bus collided with the tanker and even formed a small mushroom cloud when it exploded, scaring him into running away.

He was not far from the scene and lost his hearing from the shock on the spot. In the course of his escape, he fell into the kerosene leaking on the ground, and when he was hit by flying explosives, his clothing ignited and he was badly burned.

Luckily, he escaped the first wave of explosions. Although burned, he at least survived and was later rescued by an ambulance that arrived at the scene.

He was still conscious when he first got into the ambulance. When the paramedics used a note to confirm his identity, he said he was a passenger who had temporarily gotten off the bus, but he passed out from the pain before saying more.

By the time he was brought back from the emergency room, police officers were already waiting at his bedside. But his health was so poor—deafness notwithstanding, with oxygen covering his face and a tube down his throat—that he was unable to say much. He could only give a few key messages: that he had been dragged out of the car and did not know the other person, who had then run away.

The rest, indeed, he knew nothing about.

What he could not have imagined was that Li Shiqing, who had gotten off the bus before him, was not much better. She had hit her head as soon as she got off, giving herself a concussion and completely forgetting what had happened on the bus.

“Are you saying you were near the scene and badly burned?” Li Shiqing asked in shock. “But the officers told me you were deaf!”

She had wondered why they had not gone to the other survivor, when she herself had been questioned until she could hardly breathe. The police had answered that the boy was deaf and could not communicate easily.

Xiao Heyun froze at her words, then after a moment speculated, “It was probably some kind of questioning technique, wasn’t it? If you had been the real culprit in the bus accident, or if you really knew something, you would have slipped up if you knew I was seriously injured and dying.”

After all, there is no proof of death.

“So that time I saw you on the bus, when you jumped up and fumbled with yourself, it was because…”

Li Shiqing’s arms broke out in goosebumps at the thought.

“Mm.” He responded in a low voice. “Imagine it: one moment I was dying in the emergency room, begging God to spare my life, and the next I was alive again on the bus, hands and feet intact, skin unburned, nothing wrong with me except tinnitus…”

The Bespectacled Boy gave a bitter smile. “Anyone would have thought they were dead, right?”

He had been frightened and shaken until he noticed the girl beside him, who seemed both familiar and unfamiliar. He was sure then that she had escaped the crash as he had. Since she had run away from the danger zone without being injured, there was no reason for her to have died like him.

But when she did not recognize him afterward, he became even more certain that this world did not seem real.

“So are we now still lying in a hospital room, or…” Li Shiqing winced, voicing an even creepier thought. “In fact, are we already dead?”

“No, it can’t be.”

The Bespectacled Boy stumbled over his words, turning pale at her speculation. “No one could have survived an explosion of that magnitude, could they?”

Li Shiqing wiped at her tears. “Then why did I wake up with no injuries? If only the soul keeps reincarnating and not the body, doesn’t that mean I’m even more surely dead?”

When she had been alone in the time loop, such speculation had been the last straw. She had not dared think about it, let alone seek out the “truth.” At that time, even if it was just to live another second, she had fought desperately to survive.

Now that she had an ally and a moment to breathe, all the fear and anxiety she had suppressed burst out like Pandora’s box.

“I’ve heard that if someone dies unjustly, they are trapped forever in the same place where they died, cycling through the same day,” she sobbed. “I used to think it was just a legend, but, but…”

But what if it was true?

Hearing her words, the Bespectacled Boy gagged and gasped for air, unable to respond, which made her cry even harder.

“That doesn’t make sense either,” Xiao Heyun said, forcing himself to calm down despite his own shock. “I’ve heard that legend too. Doesn’t it also say that if you find a scapegoat, you can escape?”

He patted her slumped shoulders and tried to reassure her. “If you were a ghost, wouldn’t you have already made me your scapegoat? Why would you still be stuck here?”

“I… I wasn’t thinking about any scapegoat…” Li Shiqing admitted, embarrassed. “I was just scared…”

“I understand, and I don’t blame you. But it’s too soon to conclude that we’re dead.” He nodded.

“There are always things in this world that can’t be explained by science. And in novels and movies, situations like ours usually end with a solution, don’t they?”

Though clumsy at comforting, he still tried.

“Don’t keep thinking of this as God’s punishment. Why can’t you imagine it as a chance from God? Look at me—I should have been blown up on that bus, yet here I am, standing in front of you in one piece.”

He spread his hands. “You saved me, at least.”

Before Li Shiqing could respond, there was a loud knocking on the dressing room door.

“Is someone in there? This is a supermarket changing room! Someone has complained!” an older man shouted.

“You’re occupying public space! If you don’t come out, I’ll call the police!”

They had been inside for almost half an hour. Several people had knocked, and Xiao Heyun had driven them away with his voice, but now someone had gone to security.

When their hiding place was exposed, the two exchanged a look. Xiao Heyun gestured for them to go out and talk. Li Shiqing nodded.

The Bespectacled Boy opened the door and led her out, enduring the security guard’s scornful gaze.

The guard had been ready to scold them, but when he saw Li Shiqing’s tear-streaked face, his anger shifted to concern. He followed a few steps.

“Is something wrong, little girl? Do you need help?” he asked. He cast a wary look at Xiao Heyun, then turned to Li Shiqing. “Don’t be afraid. Tell me anything—I’ll help you.”

Li Shiqing was still upset, but when she heard the man’s words, she realized he had mistaken Xiao Heyun as the threat.

“It’s all right, uncle. I know him,” she said quickly.

She looked up and saw Xiao Heyun’s half-amused expression, then added, “Thank you. He’s my friend.”

The guard, reassured but unconvinced, let them go but lectured them about occupying public facilities and the impact of relationships. Embarrassed, the two fled.

By the time they found an uncrowded fast food restaurant on the top floor, it was nearly three o’clock.

“It’s now been an hour and fifteen minutes since the bus exploded,” Xiao Heyun said. He borrowed a pen and paper from the waiter and began analyzing with Li Shiqing.

“Do you remember where your first accident was?”

“Probably in the middle of the bridge,” Li Shiqing said. “I remember a small pavilion for pedestrians. There aren’t many on the bridge, so it must have been there.”

“And then the second?”

“Still on the bridge.”

“The third time?”

“…It seemed to be just after getting on the bridge,” Li Shiqing said uncertainly. “I only remember already being on it.”

Each time loop blurred her memories, and fear compounded with each cycle. She could no longer recall where she had first awakened, only where the accident struck.

But that was enough for Xiao Heyun.

“The first time I looped, it was near one of the junctions closest to the bridge,” he said, sketching a diagram. “Here’s the crash site, and we were here…”

“The second time, here. The third time, here.” He drew several X’s further back from the bridge. “See the pattern?”

Li Shiqing studied the sketch. “Each time loop puts us a little further from the bridge?”

“Not further from the bridge—earlier in time,” Xiao Heyun corrected. “Time and space correspond. So each loop starts earlier. That means we’re not in the same timeline—we’re in a different world each time.”

Li Shiqing’s eyes filled with tears. She understood why he stressed this point: to prove she wasn’t simply replaying her death.

“If the process changes each time, but only the result stays the same, then breaking the result may be the key,” he said, his voice lighter now.

“We managed to get off once, so just getting off isn’t the way out.”

Li Shiqing added, “I avoided my own death, but I still ended up in the loop with you. So survival alone doesn’t work either.”

“That leaves two possibilities,” she continued. “Either we get the bus safely to the terminal…”

“…Or we save everyone on board,” Xiao Heyun finished.

The words made her face pale. “My god, aren’t those the same thing? We’re just two rookies—should we really be thrown into hell mode right away?”

Saving everyone meant no casualties, not even among the criminals. She was just a college girl, and he was a programmer who could barely run 500 meters. How could they possibly manage?

“It’s actually good news,” Xiao Heyun said, clearly energized. “It means we’ll have more time each loop. Isn’t the ability to start over our biggest advantage?”

Li Shiqing hesitated, then shook her head. “Forget it. Let’s focus on what to do next.”

“We need more information,” he said. “Where the explosives were, how they were detonated, and whether that ringtone was part of the device.”

He looked at the clock. “Even if the police didn’t notice us at first, now, after more than an hour, they must have seen we got off early. They’re probably looking for us.”

They had turned off their phones as soon as they fled and had only now found a place to talk.

“Now we face a choice,” Xiao Heyun said, circling the word police on his notes. “Do we keep hiding from them, or…”

He looked at Li Shiqing.

“…Do we cooperate with the investigation?”

CONTENT END 8

chapters.title: The Ninth Cycle of Time (III)
chapters.content:
Li Shiqing’s last experience with a police investigation had not been a good one, so to this day, whenever she heard the word “investigation,” she looked a little pale.

But she was not one to let her nature get the better of her, and since the Bespectacled Boy would ask for her opinion, she felt she had to consider his view as well.

So she hesitantly asked, “What do you think?”

“My advice is to cooperate with the police investigation,” Xiao Heyun said without knowing about Li Shiqing’s bad experience.

“First of all, we don’t know if we succeeded in ending the time loop this time we got off. We don’t even know how we entered the loop from the hospital last time. What if we got off the bus this time and, by luck, we didn’t loop again?” he continued, pushing up his glasses. “If we don’t go back into the loop, it means we’ve escaped this nightmare, and then we have to think about what comes next in our lives. We can’t leave a ‘suspect’ stain on us.”

In fact, both of them knew this was unlikely. The last time they had been trapped in a ward, one of them had been seriously injured, yet they still somehow appeared back on the bus. But one must always keep some hope.

“And besides, we need to figure out what’s going on,” Xiao Heyun sighed. “We died so many times before we found explosives on the bus. Before that, we thought the crash was an accident or that the explosion had something to do with the tanker collision. Because we were on the bus each time, authorities were confused and the time to respond was short. There were too few clues.”

Li Shiqing nodded.

“But with the police, they can analyse the explosives by surveying the scene. Not only do they need information, we do too. Otherwise we’ll be like headless flies, relying on death to move things forward every time.”

Xiao Heyun looked on the bright side. “If we can get police help, maybe the rest of our situation won’t be so difficult.”

He was clearly methodical and a planner, but Li Shiqing, who had already been through the interrogation, was less optimistic.

“What if the police don’t believe us at all?” she said.

She understood why the two officers’ attitude toward her had changed so quickly. If the police found explosives at the scene, and one of the two remaining survivors returned to the scene in a daze and was half dead, while the other ran away and later claimed memory loss, how could the latter not be highly suspicious? With so many lives at stake, it was humane for the police to treat her condition carefully and ask questions in the ward.

“There is the possibility the police won’t trust us at all; after all, we really don’t know anything,” she added.

Xiao Heyun gave a nonchalant, enigmatic smile. “So we need a plan…”

…

The two of them decided to cooperate with the police. After discussing a basic plan, they both turned their phones back on.

As expected, countless missed messages popped up as soon as their phones were switched on: unfamiliar missed calls, and calls from family members. Li Shiqing panicked at the sight of missed calls from her uncle and her parents. She excused herself from Xiao Heyun and went to an empty corner seat to call her family back.

Even if the world might not be real, she could not ignore the fact that her family worried for her.

Xiao Heyun, by contrast, didn’t call anyone. He opened every social network on his phone and searched for useful information about the crash. As time passed, news of the bus explosion spread across the internet with all kinds of wild speculation.

Local forums and microblogs were mostly reliable, saying a bus had hit a tanker. Elsewhere, people spliced footage and mixed scenes from other disasters: some claimed a chemical plant had exploded, some suggested a gas station fire, and others even said someone on the bus had spontaneously combusted. It wasn’t until about 2:20 p.m. that the police issued an official statement saying there had been a crash on River Road at 13:45 and that casualties had been reported.

“At two twenty, the police released the official notice online…” Xiao Heyun murmured, rubbing his chin.

Unlike trains or airplanes, a bus explosion made victim identification difficult, except for the driver. Passengers boarded and disembarked frequently, and many bodies were burned beyond recognition, so identifying the dead by appearance and belongings was hard.

The police would be informed of this and would likely try to locate passengers who had been on and off the bus. Scanning the police bulletin, Xiao Heyun found links to interviews with passengers, but much of the information available was sparse. After all, bus journeys are short and few people pay attention to others on the bus.

Xiao Heyun absorbed a lot of details from the internet, filtering what might be useful. Meanwhile, Li Shiqing nervously dialled her mother’s number.

The call connected almost instantly. When her mother heard Li Shiqing’s voice, she burst into tears.

“You stupid child, why didn’t you call to tell us about this?” her mother scolded through sobs.

“Mom…” Li Shiqing said softly, tears running down her face. “I’m fine.”

“Are you safe? Are you back at school?” her mother asked, fretful. “Where have you been? When I saw the accident on the news my heart dropped. We only have you—how did you put us through this?”

“Mom, I’m okay. I got off the bus early,” Li Shiqing choked out, trying to steady her voice.

Her mother cried and laughed at the same time. “I’m so glad you’re okay. Your dad couldn’t reach you—he drove off to look for you. I need to call him before he causes an accident! Why did they say the bus exploded?”

“The bus hit a tanker,” Li Shiqing said, not wanting to worry her mother further. “Luckily I got off early because someone was groping me, so I left the bus.”

“How lucky! I can’t believe we have to thank someone for what happened. If anything had happened to you—your father and I couldn’t have handled it.” Her mother’s voice trembled. “Remember, nothing is more important than your life. Be careful.”

“I…” Li Shiqing opened her mouth to answer but the words stuck. She knew nothing was more important than her life, but right now her life was not entirely in her hands. What she was doing required risking it over and over.

“Okay, I got it,” she managed.

Her mother urged her again before she hung up. Li Shiqing ended the call and forced herself to steady her heart.

Before she recovered all her memories, she had been brave enough to call home on her own. After regaining her memories, she had been too afraid to call—afraid no one would answer, afraid the person on the other end would not recognize her, afraid of being helpless. Each loop was short, but each felt like years. Time had blurred for her, and space felt like an unbridgeable gap, yet hearing her family on the phone gradually returned some courage.

“I can’t give up hope. My family is waiting for me,” she told herself. “I have company; we’ll figure this out together. We’ll all go back.”

After speaking with her family, she returned to Xiao Heyun. He ignored the tear stains on her face and shared some of the information he had collected. This time they had been dropped off at a location farther from the crash site—perhaps out of camera range. Xiao Heyun had not been identified at the scene, so the police were slower to identify passengers than before. That explained the timing of the missed calls.

Because the police couldn’t reach them by phone, they were calling family, schools, and workplaces to find passengers, hence the backlog of missed calls.

While Li Shiqing drew strength from her family contact, Xiao Heyun compiled useful online information.

“It doesn’t look like a premeditated terrorist attack—there was no buildup online,” he said. “No one claimed responsibility, no hostages were taken, and in our previous loops there was no police involvement. It seems the news about explosives in the bus didn’t circulate widely. Maybe the police are holding information back to avoid panic, or they have clues not yet released publicly.”

Xiao Heyun looked at Li Shiqing with concern. “Either way, it’s bad for us. No leads means we face suspicion and possible charges.”

“I don’t have connections,” Li Shiqing said, having accepted the situation. She worried for Xiao Heyun to ease her own nerves. “I’ve already been through an investigation and am mentally prepared, but you should be ready for a storm from the police.”

“It’s okay. Don’t we already have a plan?” Xiao Heyun replied with a smile. “We just need—”

Before he could finish, Li Shiqing’s phone rang. Looking at the caller ID she said quietly, “I think it’s the police,” then cleared her throat and answered.

“…Yes, that’s fine. I’m willing to cooperate with the police in their investigation,” she said. “Where are we now? We’re on the top floor of the Café de Coral at the River Road supermarket. Yes, there are others here; the other passenger who got off is with me… Okay, we’ll meet at the supermarket entrance on the ground floor in ten minutes and won’t leave.”

“We’ve got ten minutes to get ready,” she told Xiao Heyun after hanging up. She smiled at the nervous Bespectacled Boy and flagged down the fast-food waiter.

The two drinks on their table remained untouched. Li Shiqing ordered two set meals that could be served immediately and asked the waiter to bring them.

“You never know how long it will take…” she said to Xiao Heyun, making a face.

“Let’s start with a set meal,” she added, trying to lighten the mood.

CONTENT END 9

chapters.title: The Ninth Cycle of Time (IV)
chapters.content:
Ten minutes later, after a quick meal, Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun arrived at the location the police had given and waited uneasily.

Almost as soon as they showed themselves, several stout men in plain clothes surrounded them and took control.

“Li Shiqing? Xiao Heyun?” the man at the head of the group asked, scanning them before nodding to the others.

Li Shiqing had never been treated like this before. When one of the men grabbed her arms and pinned them behind her back, she couldn’t hold back a scream. “Who are you people? What are you doing?” she cried.

Xiao Heyun fared little better. Rough hands pinned him as well; he staggered forward, surrounded by three or four men, looking like a lamb being led to market.

Their minds went blank. They had expected to wait for uniformed officers, be summoned, and then cooperate. No one expected to be seized at the entrance.

The plainclothes men escorted them into a nearby, roomy police car. Only when they saw the police marks on the vehicle did they realise the burly men were police officers in plain clothes, and their panic eased slightly.

“Did the police find explosives that fast?” Li Shiqing wondered, pale. Otherwise, why the heavy-handed approach?

They were pushed into the car from the rear, and two officers—one of whom Li Shiqing recognised—followed and climbed in with them.

The lead officer introduced himself as Du, a criminal investigator. He looked to be in his forties, with a square face, deep-set eyes, tightly pressed lips, and a pronounced furrow between his brows—an unsmiling presence with an air of contained anger. The younger officer was Officer Jiang, the one who had questioned Li Shiqing before.

When Li Shiqing saw Officer Jiang, she immediately averted her gaze and lowered her head.

“You know me?” Officer Jiang asked, still fixing her with a stern look as he sat down.

“Huh?” Li Shiqing panicked and shook her head. “No. I was scared earlier when strangers grabbed me. When I saw it was the police, I wasn’t so scared anymore,” she stammered.

Officer Jiang didn’t let the matter go. “That’s some quick reflexes and natural acting—good for someone who can come up with strange ways to get off a bus.” His tone was casual but his eyes never left her.

Xiao Heyun remained silent, staring at his shoes.

Officer Du read out their details methodically. “Li Shiqing, female, twenty years old, student at U of W, correct?” Li Shiqing nodded.

“Xiao Heyun, male, twenty-four, employee at Hanmer Network Technology, W City branch, transferred here a month ago, correct?” Xiao Heyun nodded.

“The police called you several times this afternoon hoping you would cooperate with the investigation, but your phones were unreachable,” Officer Du continued, reciting the summons procedure. “We sent messages and contacted your relatives and employers, but you did not proactively contact us. Based on that, and with approval from our superior, you are now being compulsorily summoned under the law.” He produced a summons document, showed it to them, made sure they had seen it, and then put it away. “Thank you for your cooperation.”

With the summons formalities complete, the two officers left the car and moved to another police vehicle. Officer Jiang fastened his seat belt.

“Do you see a problem with that?” he asked.

“There’s definitely something wrong, a big problem,” Officer Du said calmly, snorting as he followed the vehicle ahead. He sounded more composed than Jiang’s aggressive manner. “A traffic accident investigation being handled by criminal police—odd, not surprising to them.”

If an ordinary person heard they were being detained over a traffic accident, they might have protested or resisted; yet neither Li Shiqing nor Xiao Heyun offered that. They looked alarmed, but both seemed unnaturally steady for their age.

—

Inside the other car, the two young people—earlier dismissed as “mentally fit” by the officers—sat in stunned silence. The plainclothes officers watching them were stalwart, stoic, and silent, positioned to block any route of escape. Their presence felt different from the uniformed officers the pair had seen before; this calm had been carved by experience.

Xiao Heyun tried to speak with a nervous smile but was cut off by a terse, “Don’t talk. We’ll talk at the station.” The curt dismissal robbed him of confidence; the atmosphere in the car grew heavy, as if the air itself resisted breathing.

Halfway through the ride, Xiao Heyun felt an itch along his face by his glasses frame and reached up to scratch. Several guarded eyes snapped to him at once. Their gaze was like cold steel; he dropped his hand in a rigid motion and dared not move again. The method worked: the silence and focused attention intimidated him into stillness.

Li Shiqing, possibly tougher in her own way, sat quietly and mentally rehearsed the plan they had discussed earlier—an attempt to divert her fear and prepare for what might come.

They arrived at the criminal investigation brigade in the same oppressive silence. Neither of them had ever been to this building before. Officer Jiang and Officer Du led them inside with no trace of the earlier levity they’d shown at the fast-food restaurant.

Because this was a summons rather than an arrest, they were not handcuffed. Each was taken to a separate interview room. A clerk took statements while an officer sat in as witness.

Officer Jiang began straightforwardly with Li Shiqing. “At 13:37 this afternoon, you and another passenger, Xiao Heyun, got off bus route 45 before your stop. Is that true?”

“True,” Li Shiqing answered submissively.

“Why did you get off temporarily?” he pressed.

The question that had nearly driven her mad before now had a fitting answer. “Because a passenger touched my breasts on the bus. I was angry and asked the driver to let me off and to call the police,” she said, biting her lower lip in embarrassment.

There was no reason to hide the emotion; the memory of being groped had been humiliating, and the thought that Xiao Heyun might have done it made her face flush.

In the other interview room, Xiao Heyun’s answer differed. “The girl accused me of touching her, said she’d call the police, and the people on the bus treated me like a hooligan and threw me off,” he said bluntly.

Officer Jiang and Officer Du exchanged surprised looks through their headsets—their statements did not match.

“Did you know your bus crashed into a tanker truck and exploded not long after you got off?” Officer Du asked Xiao Heyun, speaking slowly and deliberately. “The timing of your exit from the bus is suspiciously coincidental.”

“You’d have to ask Li Shiqing—I was shocked too when I heard the bus exploded,” Xiao Heyun shrugged, trying to shift blame. “At first I was pissed I had to get off over something like that. When I saw the bus blow up, I felt relieved, and then scared. It’s better to be vilified as a pervert than to die, right?”

He spoke plainly, his face reflecting genuine panic when he recalled being taken to the hospital.

Hearing the same line of questioning, Li Shiqing burst into tears. “Then why don’t you ask that man? I was enjoying the ride and then this happened. I asked the driver to take us to the police, but he refused! I asked the people on the bus to testify for me, but no one did. They told us to get out and settle the matter ourselves. He forced me off the bus at that exact moment!” she sobbed, accusing the man on the bus.

Her distress was real—the distrust and indifference she had faced from fellow passengers had been humiliating.

Plan A.

—Mutual identification.

Execute.

CONTENT END 10

chapters.title: The Ninth Cycle of Time (V)
chapters.content:
Officer Du did not see too many flaws in Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun’s performance or their responses. Their emotions had seemed too real. The mutual shifting of blame and escape from responsibility also matched the expected attitude of two young people who had not known each other before, when confronted with police questioning.

But his intuition and years of case experience still made him feel something was wrong.

During the time they were summoned, all their schooling and work history from childhood to adulthood, including family details, had already been placed on his desk. Everything had been checked—nothing abnormal. Both were clean: no history of cynicism, no unhappy family background, smooth paths in school and work, and no prior contact with each other.

Yet it was precisely these two “clean” people who, by coincidence, got off the bus early, right before the explosion.

“Did you know at the time that it was the bus you were on that had the accident?” Officer Du and Officer Jiang asked separately.

“At first I didn’t know, then I found out,” both replied, giving the same answer.

“How did you know?” Officer Jiang pressed. “Even if there was a bus accident, it might not have been the one you were on. Many buses come and go.”

This question pushed them past their rehearsed responses.

“I heard later it was the No. 45 bus that hit the tanker. I had just gotten off the 45,” Li Shiqing said, suppressing her turmoil.

“I confirmed it by the photo of the driver exposed online,” Xiao Heyun added quickly. “I remembered his face.”

“Did you notice anything wrong on the bus?” Officer Du asked. “For example, was the driver being held hostage?”

“Absolutely not,” Li Shiqing answered immediately. “The driver was driving the whole time, no one was near him.”

“No,” Xiao Heyun agreed. “I sat behind him before—no one interacted with him.”

“If you didn’t know the bus was going to be in trouble, why did you run together after you got off?” That was not the reaction of two people supposedly in conflict.

“He tried to run as soon as he got off, so I pulled him to stop him from going to the police. He kept running, so I followed,” Li Shiqing said.

“I thought she was crazy and just wanted to get away. Who knew she wouldn’t let go? I figured lunatics these days can do anything, so I tried to run…” Xiao Heyun added in his room. “I didn’t know she could run so fast—I couldn’t even outrun her.”

“Why did you go to the supermarket together?” Officer Du’s frown deepened.

“We hadn’t been running long when the bus exploded. Everyone was terrified and ran forward together. We got swept up in the crowd,” Li Shiqing explained. “If you didn’t run toward the supermarket, you could have been pushed down and trampled.”

“Because that’s where everyone ran,” Xiao Heyun said simply. “I’m not local—I didn’t know where to go, so I followed.”

“Then why stay in the supermarket? Normally, wouldn’t you return immediately after something like that?”

“We didn’t know it was a bus explosion. We just knew there had been an explosion. What if it was a terrorist attack? The supermarket was safer, with more people,” Li Shiqing said. “My phone had died on the bus, and I wanted to charge it there to figure out what happened.”

“Was Xiao Heyun with you then?” Officer Jiang asked.

“No, he disappeared as soon as we entered. I met him later, by chance, in front of a fast-food restaurant.”

Xiao Heyun gave his own version: “The road to Jiangbei was closed and I didn’t know the way. At the supermarket, I looked up how to get across the river. Then I saw the bridge was closed and realised I couldn’t cross. I stayed there reading news and reports on my phone until it ran out of battery.”

“Why did you evade the summons?” Officer Du asked.

“My phone was dead and I didn’t have a charger. When I finally charged it, I called my family first. They told me the police were looking for me, so I called back later,” Li Shiqing said.

“I thought it was a scam call,” Xiao Heyun added. “Aren’t there lots of scam calls? Some even fake caller ID. At the time, I was busy reading online and didn’t want to answer strange calls.”

“Why did you come together to see the police if you said you were separated? Doesn’t look like you’re at odds.”

“She kept following me like a maniac, insisting I turn myself in,” Xiao Heyun said calmly. “And when I saw the police wanted information, as a good citizen I came to cooperate.”

The police pressed on the key points that made them suspicious. But the two young people had explanations for everything. No matter how much they were asked, their answers were consistent. With little time to check the details immediately, the questioning reached a standstill.

Even the police found it difficult. The two had acted panicked, yet their key answers were coherent and matched surveillance footage.

There was a heavy silence in the rooms.

When no more questions came, Xiao Heyun grew restless. “Anything else, Officer Du? When can we leave?”

“There are still questions to clarify. I hope you’ll cooperate a bit more,” Officer Du said, cutting off further talk.

The two emerged from the interrogation exhausted. Questioning required focus not only from those answering but also from the police, who had to analyse every word, gesture, and micro-expression.

“They answered too smoothly. Too reasonable,” Officer Jiang muttered, rubbing his face. “They seem very steady, not terrified. Should we try something more intense?”

“Better not,” Officer Du replied firmly. “They’re only subpoenaed, not suspects. They have no motive and no record. We can’t push without evidence.” He thought a moment. “Next, I’ll throw out that there were explosives on the bus and watch their reactions.”

“So soon?” Jiang asked, surprised.

“Based on experience, they aren’t likely the masterminds. Let’s have Zhang take over the next session.”

Police had different questioning styles—red face and white face. Officer Zhang was known as the kindly one, lowering defenses.

“Together or separate?” Jiang asked reluctantly.

“Start with the man,” Du said.

“Not Li Shiqing? Wouldn’t a girl be easier?” Jiang asked.

“Don’t underestimate her. She’s more resistant than the boy. Remember—she could still answer under pressure, while he couldn’t even look up.” Du patted his shoulder. “Don’t judge on appearances. You need more experience.”

—

When Officer Du left, Xiao Heyun thought Plan A had worked. Their tactic had delayed the investigation while avoiding suspicion of collusion. If each looked guilty of blaming the other, the police would dig into their backgrounds and find no motive, no ability, no explosives. Just a student and a programmer with clean lives. Without evidence, they could not be treated as suspects.

But soon after, an older, kindly-looking officer entered and showed his ID—Officer Zhang, also from criminal police. If Li Shiqing had been present, she would have recognised him from a previous questioning.

A new round began.

Unlike Li Shiqing, Xiao Heyun had no prior interrogation experience. During his hospitalisation he had been too injured to answer. Now he sat nervously, fearing harsher measures. To his surprise, Officer Zhang smiled gently.

“It’s past seven. The others haven’t rested or eaten all day for this case. They’ve gone to eat. They didn’t want you to be nervous alone, so I came to keep you company.”

He didn’t even sit opposite like an interrogator—just chatted casually. “By the way, want some food? Our canteen’s not bad.”

“No, I’ve eaten,” Xiao Heyun said quickly.

“Alright, I’ll get you some water then,” Zhang said kindly, leaving the room.

Xiao Heyun exhaled in relief.

But once outside, Zhang reported through the intercom, “He said he already ate. If he really stayed here this long, that makes no sense. Check the supermarket restaurants—ask staff and security. Find out when and with whom he ate. There may be an accomplice.”

Author’s Note: A little theater. Xiao Heyun: (squinting) Crow’s-eye, real-head-breaking meal? Li Shiqing: …… You’re no better, a seamless “Plan A”? I have a feeling they don’t believe it at all. Xiao Heyun, Li Shiqing: (grimaces) Hmph! The two young men were too young to think they could “get” information from the police or stall for time, but hey. The police dad will teach them to behave.

CONTENT END 11

chapters.title: The Ninth Cycle of Time (VI)
chapters.content:
Mr. Zhang went out for a while to bring Xiao Heyun a glass of water, and when the atmosphere had relaxed a bit, they started talking about family matters.

At first, they just asked Bespectacled Boy about his family, how many people were in his family, how was his relationship, and so on, and then they started asking personal questions.

According to the data, many young men orchestrate vicious incidents with the aim of getting back at the object of their advances.

Some of them think that killing someone would show their “manhood”, such as making their girlfriend regret breaking up with them, or doing something big to show the woman who rejected them.

Essentially, such people were untimely bombs hidden in normal people, and until he shows it, who knows when they would blow up.

“What? Never been in love?”

At the answer, Mr. Zhang looked at Bespectacled Boy closely, noticing that he wasn’t supposed to be talking, and gave a surprised expression, “Don’t young men your age fall in love in college?”

“In engineering college, there were only seven or eight girls in a class, and they were all taken in the first year.” Bespectacled Boy laughed bitterly, “Then there were heavy classes and part-time jobs, so I didn’t have time.”

“You’re still working and studying? Can’t see it.”

Mr. Zhang looked at the cleanly dressed young man, although he could see that he was not wearing any brand name, but also not the goods of the roadside stalls, and the information showed that his parents were both full, the state enterprise double-income family, the conditions should not be bitter.

“Are you often short of money?”

If there was a large shortfall of money due to gambling or other reasons, one may also be desperate to make money.

“It’s simply that I like to save money.”

Bespectacled Boy didn’t expect the policeman to be so gossipy and was a little confused, “It’s not because the family is poor.”

With just a few words, Mr. Zhang had already rejected most of his suspicions in his head.

A young man who was financially well off, had a normal family environment and was not emotionally entangled was mostly free of light-hearted thoughts and one could sense from the conversation that he was not mentally ill.

In other words, no one like that, as long as they were not brain dead, would do something like planting a bomb on a bus or assisting someone to do this.

Not long afterwards, Officer Du’s steady, determined footsteps sounded from the corridor and opened the door to the questioning room and walked in.

As soon as he entered the room, Mr. Zhang leaning on the corner of the table and chatting suddenly straightened out, and the atmosphere in the room, which had just been one of laughter and conversation, suddenly disappeared.

Xiao Heyun unconsciously straightened his back and subconsciously avoided the gaze of the visitor.

Officer Du did not say anything either, and when he entered the room, he played a few recordings on his mobile phone.

“…… Yes, comrade police, I saw them come out of the changing room together with my own eyes.”

Bespectacled Boy’s face changed when the security guard’s voice sounded in the room.

He heard someone on the other end of the recording ask, “What time was it? Do you know what they were doing in there?”

“Around three o’clock I think, they must have been in the changing room for ages because there were several complaints in between that the door inside never opened and they couldn’t even try on their clothes. What for? I don’t know what for, it couldn’t have been anything good anyway!”

“The little girl came out with tears all over her face, and she looked terrified. I knew that man was not nice! I said to the girl, “Don’t be afraid, tell me what’s wrong, I’ll help you. The girl even helped him out, saying he was her friend, so how could I care? I was also negligent, I should have called the police at that time!”

The security guard rambled on the recording, “Something really happened, didn’t it? Is the girl okay?”

Bespectacled Boy’s face was impassive.

Officer Du kept a pair of stern, hawk-like eyes fixed on him, and with a mocking face released a second recording.

“This man? Ah, yes yes, it was about four or five in the afternoon, I think, and he came to our restaurant with a young girl and asked me to borrow a pen and paper, and since there weren’t many people in the restaurant at the time, I remember it very well.”

The bright voice of the fast-food waitress haunted everyone’s ears.

“What’s the paper and pencil for? The boy seemed to be writing something, probably making some sort of plan, and the girl kept listening. They talked for a long time and only ordered two drinks, which they never drank much of. Then the girl went to the corner to make a phone call and the boy sat by himself looking at his phone. Then after that they ordered two orders of chicken and chips, ate them and left.”

“Yes, yes, that’s the girl.”

“How long was it in the restaurant? An hour there I think …… I can’t say exactly how long.”

By the time the second recording was finished, Bespectacled Boy was sweating profusely, but his face was blue.

He knew, of course, that the police would find out sooner or later that they were in contact, but he figured that after the mutual “identification”, the police would have to take at least a detour, if not be led into a ditch, to start a thorough investigation of the two men’s friendships and internet traces and whatnot.

He didn’t even think about being exposed so quickly!

Where did they go wrong?

Officer Du, always looking at him, gave a sneer that shattered his ramblings, “Haven’t seen you since, eh? Li Shiqing followed you around like a madman, insisting that you turn yourself in, didn’t she?”

“Didn’t know it before, never seen it?”

With each word he spoke, Bespectacled Boy became more and more disillusioned.

“What were you doing in the dressing room before three o’clock? What plans were listed in the dining room again? What have you been doing? Matching statements?”

At the end of the day, Officer Du was banging on the table like a roar and roaring out with ferocity.

“Speak up!!!”

Bespectacled Boy slumped back in his chair, breathing heavily, his mental defences having collapsed in full force.

Mr. Zhang, who was on the other side, duly handed over another glass of water and advised bitterly, “Young man, we are old police officers, we can still see whether you have done something bad or not, whether you are a good person or not. Maybe you haven’t done anything bad and are just a person in the know, but to know and not report is the same as condoning crime ……”

He placed the water in front of Bespectacled Boy, knelt down and looked him honestly in the eyes and said, “I know you must have seen and felt something in the bus at the time and got out of the bus because you were scared, right?”

Bespectacled Boy, who was already sweating, nodded subconsciously, as if hypnotised.

The eyes of several officers in the room were tinged with joy at the sight of progress in the case.

“Did you see someone holding the driver hostage? Or did you see something in the bus that shouldn’t have been there? Did the perpetrators see your faces and know who you are? Or was it someone you knew?

Mr. Zhang did not spare Xiao Heyun every subtle expression on his face, but his tone was very gentle, “In fact, you don’t have to worry about anyone retaliating against you, because the police will conceal the identity and privacy of every important witness, and will also send plainclothes to protect your next safety, so that you will not be threatened by criminals in any way ……”

Bespectacled Boy looks up slowly, his eyes beneath the boxy glasses with confusion and hesitation.

“No matter how unbelievable the outcome, we can accept it, and you can be brave enough to tell us the parts you know!”

Mr. Zhang grabbed him by the shoulders and shouted encouragement to him.

“No matter how unbelievable?”

Bespectacled Boy asked weakly.

“Yes! No matter how unbelievable!”

Mr. Zhang nods heavily.

“OK, I said ……”

—

In the other side of the interrogation room, Officer Jiang played all the recordings, as did Officer Du.

The previous questions, both the surveillance footage and the questions asked by the officers, as there was only one footage and no other witnesses, made it difficult to corroborate their words as false.

But now that witnesses from the changing room and the restaurant have been turned up and there are more witnesses, even if Bespectacled Boy Xiao Heyun tore up the piece of paper that made the plan on the way and threw it in several separate bins on different floors, there was no way for them to justify themselves anymore.

More importantly, because they had a history of telling lies, they could no longer be trusted to tell the truth, even if they did.

Officer Jiang has now confirmed that Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun were in the same team, following the experience of the locker room and restaurant discussions.

Unlike Xiao Heyun’s panic and devastation, Li Shiqing accepted the fact that “the police had broken us” calmly, and even with a sense of relief.

“It really doesn’t work ……”

She was not as optimistic as Bespectacled Boy, who had been subjected to urgent police questioning.

“What else do you have to answer for? I advise you to speak honestly this time and not take the police for fools.”

Officer Jiang was furious that they had been fooled, but good professional conduct allowed him to contain that anger well.

“Confession is lenient, resistance is harsh!”

“The truth as I know it will not satisfy you.”

Li Shiqing sighed, “You’ll think I’m crazy.”

“Say it.”

This is all Officer Jiang had to say.

Since his predecessor had advised him that this woman was more resilient than her male counterpart, he had not left Li Shiqing’s table, standing as if he were a statue that would not move or falter.

Li Shiqing gave him a look, and Officer Jiang kept his eyes on her.

“It started when I got on Bus 45 ……”

Avoiding his scrutinizing gaze, Li Shiqing bowed her head, recalling everything that has been happening, and began to tell the story.

If plan A didn’t work, plan B would be implemented.

Plan B was simple: tell the police everything they knew about the bus and let them look for the clues available inside.

So, two questioning rooms, different times, same questions, different answers.

Li Shiqing: “…… My first incident was at 13:45 in the afternoon, when I was sleeping and woke up to a ringing mobile phone ……”

“…… When I had my fifth accident I was so scared and didn’t want to stay in the bus for a minute, so I pulled a random young man I didn’t know next to me and said he was molesting me and asked to get out of the bus and call the police …… “

“Is this the one?”

Officer Jiang interrupted her with some impatience.

“No, not this time.”

Li Shiqing’s face showed a resigned misery as she calmly replied, “This time, it’s my ninth accident.”

She watched Officer Jiang look back at her with that “you make it up, you keep making it up” look on his face, ducked her head and went back to recounting all the details she could remember.

“The fifth time I finally got out of the bus, but I don’t know if it was because I had a concussion from hitting my head or because that past experience was so harrowing I subconsciously tried to forget it, so I lost my memory ……”

Officer Jiang, sitting opposite, rubbed his temples in slight annoyance as he listened to the eight o’clock doggerel and patiently continued to listen to the rest of the story.

On the other hand, Bespectacled Boy, who has had a relatively small number of time loops, has already finished all his time loops in three or five sentences, and could not be more sincere in his plea for the police to believe him.

“…… really, that’s all I know, I don’t know what the explosives are or why they exploded, I was so emotionally tense at the time, I just wanted to get out of the bus quickly to slow down, that’s why I pulled a Li Shiqing act and got out of the bus in a hurry to find a way to deal with it first ……”

Seeing the increasingly disgruntled faces of several officers, Bespectacled Boy’s voice trailed off as he mumbled aggressively, “You’re the ones who said you could take it no matter how unbelievable it was ……”

When he had finished himself, he looked at him again with this look like he was mentally ill.

“It’s unbelievable enough ……”

Mr. Zhang, who had been listening like a book from heaven, looked blankly at his colleague, “You usually read more online novels, what do you think?”

It was a thrilling moment of silence.

“It’s quite a full-on story, the beginning of which probably got a lot of hits online, and it might even be a hit.”

After a long time, Officer Du, who was questioned, said with a smile on his face, “I didn’t know you guys were so good at this, did you? You’ve been working on the plot in the dressing room, haven’t you? I’m sorry, did you even write an outline in the dining room?”

Bespectacled Boy: ……

” Mr. Zhang, ask Little Jiang to find a policewoman to accompany Li Shiqing from next door for a urine test and a blood test, and you, you come with me.”

Officer Du’s eyes were always suspicious and wary, never letting down any of his guard.

“I suspect you’re stoned.”

CONTENT END 12

chapters.title: The Ninth Cycle of Time (VII)
chapters.content:
The results of the tests came back quickly, and both youths were in good health with no problems or the possibility of being high on drugs.

When the results came in, all the police officers were left with a major headache.

The “testimonies” that they gave were not unbelievable; they were simply a “fantasy.” Not many people dared to write novels like this, and it was basically impossible to convince people.

“Take another close look at their experience, focusing on what they said on the internet and their friendships, to see if there’s any possibility of a cult.”

Officer Du struggled to make reasonable speculation, “Some cults are usually buried deep, and if this is the case, it’s best to get rid of them altogether.”

While the police officers in charge of the forensic investigation went to work, Officer Du’s team didn’t stay idle either.

“Anyway, they knew there were explosives in the bus without us telling them, and they were able to tell us when and where the explosion was expected to happen, so if they’re not the main culprits, they’re at least co-conspirators or people with knowledge….”

Officer Du’s face was sullen.

“Next, it’s just a matter of questioning.”

So, instead of the police trusting them more, the two young ones’ confessions pushed them into the abyss of being “suspects.”

When the interrogation room was replaced with tighter security and more equipment, Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun knew that their plan B had also failed.

Round after round of more severe questioning began.

“How did you and Li Shiqing meet? Through some kind of organization?”

Officer Du looked through Xiao Heyun’s file and asked tentatively.

“Are you transferring to W because Li Shiqing is here?”

“No, I didn’t know her before I got on this bus.”

Xiao Heyun was already tired and said with little energy, “I only remember her and the driver’s uncle in the bus when she dragged me off. I don’t know anything you’re asking me.”

“So it was by arrangement with someone else that you got into the same bus? Who was it?”

The glare of the arraignment lights shone directly on Xiao Heyun’s face, so strong that any expression on his face was visible, and Bespectacled Boy was blinded by the glare, which seemed to take on substance, like a million needles stabbing him at the same time, making even his temples ache.

“If someone did arrange it, it was probably God ……”

Xiao Heyun smiled bitterly to himself.

Unfortunately, no one could appreciate his humor.

“What was your and Li Shiqing’s mission? Was it to cover for the real terrorists?”

Officer Du frowned, “Would you guys get off early because you got an early blast time?”

“We didn’t have a mission; we got off early because we had been through this many times. The tanker at that intersection was a ‘bump in the road’ that we hadn’t avoided several times before, and none of us wanted to get blown up; it hurt too much.”

Xiao Heyun mumbled, in a trance, “The burns hurt too much ……”

Officer Du looked to the expert who had arranged it aside, who shook his head at him and said that he could not tell if he was lying from his facial expression.

Bespectacled Boy’s eyes were already glazed over by the light, and he couldn’t help himself; his eyelids drooped, and he tried to hide from the glare by closing his eyes.

“No closing your eyes!”

Officer Du walked up to Bespectacled Boy and suddenly shouted into his ear.

“Ho!”

Bespectacled Boy, who was already in poor spirits, shivered with fright at such a yell and regained his wits.

“Keep asking.”

Officer Du looked up at Mr. Zhang and gestured for him to ask.

“I know you’re sleepy; it’s late, and you’ve been tossing and turning all day. Everyone is tired; we’re tired too, and we can understand that.”

Mr. Zhang said kindly, “Look, even if we believed the statement you gave earlier and made a statement, the public and the families of the victims would not believe it. We need to be responsible to society; we can’t rely on this to fool people. Even if these are your actual experiences, they lack sufficient conditions to convince people; for example, how did the bomb get on board?”

“I don’t know.”

Bespectacled Boy’s response was getting slower and slower: “If I knew how the bomb went up, I would have solved the problem myself with Li Shiqing and wouldn’t have come to the police station…”

“So you still want to help us, right? Then please think about the details more. Is it possible that the bomb in the bus was remotely controlled? You said you heard a mobile phone ringing; could that phone have been the remote control device?”

Mr. Zhang was a good guide.

“I don’t know; I never saw where the bomb was from start to finish, and I don’t know where in the bus it went off.”

Bespectacled Boy shook his head and tried to remember, “I don’t think it was at the front of the bus. I’ve been in the front position with Li Shiqing before, and it seemed the heat flow lifted from the rear.”

Mr. Du, who had already lowered his voice, asked his colleagues from the trace section to help him focus on the rear of the bus.

Previously they were almost misled as to the cause of the explosion because the bus was in a collision with a tanker, and it was the Traffic Accident Division and the Dangerous Goods Transport Department who later examined it together and deduced from the rupture of the tank that there was an external cause of the explosion before the case was transferred to the criminal police side.

Because of this, survey and laboratory time were limited, and because the extent of the damage at the scene was so great, no particularly useful clues have been obtained to date.

Exactly which type of bomb and by what means it was detonated were not known.

“The rear? Which rear exactly? Is it the last row of the bus or the last few rows?”

Mr. Zhang: A little bit of coaxing.

“I don’t remember; I really don’t….”

Bespectacled Boy tried but couldn’t remember if there was anyone sitting behind him.

Who rides a bus and has nothing to do other than to look at who’s sitting in the back?

Not to mention that all they had wanted before was for the driver to stop and let them off, and it was the driver who had the most communication, not the passengers!

When questions about the explosives were unsuccessful, the officers turned to other topics, such as “What was Li Shiqing’s role in this?” and “What was the purpose of the bomb?” questions that Bespectacled Boy simply could not answer.

“I really didn’t know Li Shiqing before. She is a victim like me ……”

The more Bespectacled Boy spoke, the more aggrieved he became, his spirit taut as a string and not knowing when it would break.

“We are obviously all victims—no, we are all survivors—and it is not fair for you to treat us like this!”

He wailed.

“I know it was hard for you to escape; you were all out of your depth, so I was eager to help you.” Mr. Zhang was like a great coachman, pulling on Bespectacled Boy whenever he was on the verge of an emotional meltdown without breaking his spirit.

“But you have to tell the truth so that we can protect you, don’t you think?”

“The truth is that I didn’t know Li Shiqing before, and both Li Shiqing and I have time cycled countless times, returning to the bus each time we die.”

Bespectacled Boy’s eyes were shaking, and his voice was getting softer. “If you don’t believe me, put us here and watch; we might even enter the time loop again…”

“Want us to relax and unwind with you?”

Officer Du was amused. “Are you going to be put to sleep again?”

Bespectacled Boy didn’t answer either, just nodded sleepily.

It was late at night, and with hours of continuous questioning, normal people would be too sleepy to keep their eyes open by now, and Bespectacled Boy was no exception.

“Then you can sleep for a while.”

Suddenly Officer Du laughed. “Think carefully in your dreams about what to answer when you wake up.”

The bright lights went out at once in response, and the questioning room was dimly lit again.

Almost as soon as the lights went out, Bespectacled Boy collapsed on the table and fell asleep with his eyes closed.

When Bespectacled Boy fell asleep, Officer Du walked out of the interrogation room and asked Officer Jiang next door through the headset, “How are you? Any progress there?”

“Li Shiqing’s story reveals quite a few details, and excluding these implausible parts, there is a part of the information trail that can still be extrapolated.”

Officer Jiang lowered his voice and said, “The bus had many ‘accidents’ in the story she told ……”

“Usually in a bombing like this there is a normal demand for either fame or profit, but it doesn’t make sense that no organization or individual has made a request to the police before the bombing.”

Officer Jiang speculated, “Is it possible that, as Li Shiqing revealed, the original location of the bombing was on the bridge, and the real plotters were perhaps trying to blackmail the hostages with something, only to have a sudden accident interfere with the planned bombing? For example, a sudden vehicular accident?”

“It’s possible, but there’s no way to explain how Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun would know the time of the original plan and the location of the original plan unless they were the main culprits and got off the bus early.”

Officer Du leaned against the wall and took a drag on his cigarette; the more he thought about it, the more his head hurt.

“Are you trying to get us to believe that third-rate shit story of theirs?”

Officer Jiang on the other end of the line was silent.

As an evidence-based police officer, he could hardly admit to believing such uncritical conclusions beyond scientific basis.

If they could believe in things like “coming back from the dead,” then what was the point of investigating cases in the future? For every murder case, they could just go to a psychic and seek help from the “ghosts.” Why would one need the police?

“You keep asking questions, repeatedly and carefully, to find out all the details available.”

Officer Du glanced at the clock on the wall and smiled morosely.

“Gave the boy ten minutes sleep too; it’s time to ‘get up.'”

He stepped into the interrogation room and signalled for the bright lights to be turned back on.

The intense light shone once again on Bespectacled Boy’s face, and an assisting policeman stepped forward and gave him a few violent pushes, jerking him out of his fresh slumber.

The sudden awakening of a person who had just fallen asleep was a form of mental torture, not to mention the mental exhaustion caused by the high pressure and repeated interrogations that made Xiao Heyun not know what day it was and think it had been a night when he had only slept for ten minutes.

Bespectacled Boy, who had opened his eyes, suddenly shivered at the sight of the familiar scene before him and then at the room, which was completely indistinguishable from the sky.

Had the time and place of his time loop changed since then to the interrogation room?

Bespectacled Boy closed his eyes in horror and despair, and when he opened them again, he found that nothing had changed.

“Why am I still here?”

His eyes were wide, and he was gasping for air.

“I… I don’t want…”

He’d rather be stuck in the bus forever than be stuck in an interrogation room being repeatedly asked questions he couldn’t answer!

At least he could sleep in the bus and find a way to get off. What could he do when he was stuck in the police station? What could he do to trick these real police officers into letting him go?

Catching perverts?

This was supposed to be a police station!

When the police officer who questioned him repeated the questions he had just been asked, Bespectacled Boy was shaking like a leaf about to fall in the autumn wind, too frightened to breathe.

“I, I…”

He was so scared that his teeth bit his tongue, and he stumbled. “I—I don’t know; I know.”

This “fatigue questioning” was a common interrogation technique, which took advantage of the psychological relaxation of the suspect when he had just woken up to get the desired clues.

“Stop! Stop talking, all of you!”

As Bespectacled Boy’s pupils grew wider and wider, and he looked as if he had just been pulled out of the water, the psychologist sent to assist him immediately interrupted the interrogation process.

“If you want a lunatic, keep asking again!”

She frowned and reached out with a disapproving “stop” gesture.

Everyone threw in the towel and did not continue the questioning.

“Give him a nap.”

The psychologist walked slowly up to him and stroked his hair like a soothing animal cub.

“He’s in a bad state of mind, so when he comes to his senses, I’ll try using hypnosis.”

—

On the other hand, Li Shiqing’s mental health was deteriorating.

She was not on the verge of a breakdown like Bespectacled Boy, but she was clearly too tired to think properly.

When confronted with questions from the police, she also began to babble and make things up, giving as many garbled answers to the same question as the police asked several times.

“How did you and Xiao Heyun meet?”

“Met online at…”

She said in a trance.

“You just said you met them on WeChat.”

Officer Jiang asked impatiently.

“Feel free to shake it, shake it, shake it in the bus.”

“Why were you getting out of the bus?”

“We see eye-to-eye, well, eye-to-eye, to get off and make friends….”

“And you said before that you were catching perverts!”

Officer Jiang yelled in anger.

“Erotic, yes, it’s our erotic, bus pervert and all that.”

Li Shiqing: Nonsense.

“Bloody bus perverts!”

And I’m an old man pushing a cart!

When they heard the question and answer session, the officers next to them couldn’t help but “pooft.”

“What exactly did you discuss in the locker room? Why did you get off early?”

“We, we dry humped… um, locker room passion? Uniqlo, no, or Indy?”

She blurted out the truth with two eyes.

“We can’t wait to get to the station.”

This girl had no more shame!

Officer Jiang narrowly avoided spurting out a mouthful of blood in anger and slammed the table viciously.

“Give me a good answer!”

“Ah!”

Startled by the loud slap on the table, Li Shiqing leaned back, and the chair fell backwards, unsteadily.

After a muffled sound, Officer Jiang jerked back to his senses and rushed to Li Shiqing’s side, crouching down in a frenzy.

“Li Shiqing? Li Shiqing?”

After probing, he looked up in a panic, “Get someone to see if there’s anyone else in the infirmary quickly ……”

“Li Shiqing passed out!”

—

After what seemed like a long time and what seemed like an instant, Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun, who had previously lost consciousness, opened their eyes in a daze.

“Great!”

They looked at each other and suddenly burst into tears as they realized they were back on the bus.

There was never a moment when they felt that the bus was so cozy and peaceful; the warm breeze blowing in their faces and the small but regular swaying of the bus as it moved were so suitable for sleeping.

Then they made the same gesture in unspoken agreement.

–Reclose your eyes.

The swaying bus was like a mother’s cradle, easily lulling the two into a deep sleep.

As for whether it would explode later?

What the hell, let’s blow it up!

Nothing could be more intimidating than a police officer (tears)!

Author’s Note: A little theater. Psychologist: I’ll try “hypnosis” later. Buses: (shaking) Leave me alone! Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun: (hugging and crying) Great to be back on a cozy bus at last!

CONTENT END 13

chapters.title: The Tenth Cycle of Time
chapters.content:
Poor Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun slept through their ninth time loop in the explosion.

The exhaustion was more mental than physical, so when they woke up again, they were both a bit disinterested in getting out of the bus and even a bit reluctant to struggle with the “explosion.”

“I want to lie flat and be a salty fish.”

Li Shiqing lounged on the front seat cushion, looking out of the window.

The warm atmosphere of the bus, the kind driver, and the friendly and welcoming passengers—apart from the fact that the bus was always in trouble—made the environment much nicer than the serious atmosphere of the criminal police.

“I don’t feel hopeful with what someone that powerful can’t find out, just us.”

The road signs outside the window let her know that this time she was further away from the junction where the tanker had crashed but had absolutely no intention of struggling any further.

Xiao Heyun, who was a “priority target” for the police officers, was in a worse state of mind, but he didn’t give up hope.

The first time he opened his eyes, he pulled out his phone and looked at it, as normal as every person who woke up from a nap.

13:27.

If they hadn’t interfered with anything, the bus would have been out at 13:45, which meant they had less than 20 minutes to spare.

“Don’t think about what happened to us; think about the people who were bombed.”

Bespectacled Boy lowered his voice to encourage the unmotivated girl while pulling out a notebook and two pens from his backpack. “Think of your parents; think of all the times we’ve suffered. If you give up now, the real killer will get his way.”

At the mention of her parents, Li Shiqing’s expression sank, and she gradually sat up straighter.

“I never want to go back to the police station in my life.”

Bespectacled Boy drew a crying face in his notebook and went on to write, “We have to think of something else.”

For fear of being overheard by possible “terrorists” in the bus, Bespectacled Boy had to use this method of communication.

Li Shiqing took the notebook handed over by Bespectacled Boy and was delighted when she read the contents.

Not to mention, the penmanship was quite strong and powerful, much better than the dog-eared writing of many of her classmates.

“I don’t want to put my hopes in anyone else either.”

She thought about it and wrote in the notebook, “Catching perverts off the bus has to be our trump card; it’s usually best to use it sparingly. I feel like I’m going to have an absolute mental breakdown after being interrogated a few more times.”

“Wouldn’t adding a Weibo be the end of it?”

When she had finished, Li Shiqing handed over the notebook in wonder.

“It’s a hassle to have to re-add every time.”

Bespectacled Boy blurted back.

When she heard the word “every time,” Li Shiqing, who had been smiling at the familiarity of the “classroom cheat sheet,” curled her smile slightly.

Curious, she reached over and saw Bespectacled Boy drawing diagrams and writing ‘plans’ in his notebook again and grabbed it out of the blue.

Thanks to her last experience, her head now exploded at the sight of blah, blah, blah plans.

“And come to plan?”

Li Shiqing looked at the 13:30 mark on her phone, squeezed her notebook, and glared, “Thinking about plan A and plan B before, it turns out that plans simply don’t catch up with change!”

“But there’s always one more try ……”

Bespectacled Boy subconsciously argued, “You can’t rely on seeing things every time ……”

“Stop it; you’re pressed for time. Do as I say!”

Li Shiqing pulled out her phone, looked up how to contact the police by text message, and lowered her voice to say, “They’ve found ‘that’ in the bus. Is this something ordinary citizens like us can fix? What’s the point of fooling around when you have the best teammates and not using them!”

“But I think…”

Bespectacled Boy wanted to continue explaining.

“You don’t want what you think; I want what I think! Listen to me; I don’t think this is something that needs to be discussed. Listen to me first!”

Li Shiqing’s small hands slapped his, and that was it.

Bespectacled Boy had probably never been in contact with such a “strong” woman before, so he was so cowed by her slap that he just watched her toss and turn.

Li Shiqing turned her mobile phone off to silent, edited a paragraph, and sent a text message to the “12110” SMS alert platform.

I’m on Bus 45 travelling from the River Road section towards Jiangbei station and have not yet reached the Middle River Road intersection. I found a bomb on board. Help!

The text message was sent out without incident.

[12110：Hello, this is the police receiving center, W City police friendly reminder: indiscriminate alarm and reporting false police is a disturbance of public order behavior, and you need to bear the corresponding legal responsibility. Your police report has now been received, please keep your mobile phone open and give us feedback on whether it is convenient to call back to verify the situation.

“So soon?”

This was almost a second reply; there was no way it could be anything other than an automatic system response.

But back and forth, another text message arrived.

[12110: As this is a text alarm, you have provided too little available information. Please describe specifically your current location, the license plate number or exterior characteristics of the vehicle you are travelling in, and the location of the explosives in the vehicle. Thank you for your cooperation.

What divine typing speed for the responding commissioner!

The spirits of both youths lifted.

But when they saw the “license plate number” cloud, both of them were dumbfounded.

“Did you remember that?”

Li Shiqing looked at Bespectacled Boy with bated breath and hoped that he had a good memory.

“Neither did I.”

But it turned out that even Bespectacled Boy’s excellent memory didn’t help.

“Who gets on the bus and remembers that?”

They hadn’t even paid attention to the license plate!

So Li Shiqing scratched her head and continued to compose text messages, while Bespectacled Boy kept an eye on the road outside the bus, which had reached the intersection, ready to warn the driver of motorbikes and tankers.

I can’t be sure if the person who planted the bomb is in the bus, and I can’t talk to him. We are now past the Middle River Road intersection, and I do not know the license plate number of the bus. There is no obvious difference in appearance between this bus and the buses on the same schedule. Estimated time of explosion at 13:45; please resolve immediately! Solve it immediately!

“Driver, watch out for the motorbikes on the right; they’re going to run the red light early!”

Bespectacled Boy stood up and shouted, then sat down again.

Because he used an affirmative sentence rather than a guess or a request, the driver subconsciously slowed down, and the bus passed that junction without a hitch when the text message was sent, brushing past the tanker truck that had just come off the bridge.

It proved easy to get safely through this junction without any disruptive events.

After the first hurdle, the two breathed a long sigh of relief.

[12110: Please continue to keep your mobile phone open and protect yourself; we are already arranging a solution. Do you know the exact time of the explosion because the one in the bus is a time bomb? Was there a countdown clearly displayed on the bomb? Is there a way to get the driver to make a temporary stop and get everyone off? ]

Li Shiqing was worried when she read the police reply.

If it was really a ticking time bomb in sight, it was fine; as the police said, just get off the bus and leave a bus about to explode for the police to sort out.

The problem was that she had no idea if the bomb was timed or where it was planted.

Besides ……

She looked up at the driver, who was concentrating on driving at the front.

Would she have died so many times if she could have gotten the driver to stop and let everyone off?

When Li Shiqing stared at her phone for a few moments, Bespectacled Boy poked her head around to finish reading the police questioning and snapped his fingers.

“It’s easy to find out if it’s a ticking time bomb ……”

He took the phone from Li Shiqing’s hand.

Li Shiqing looked on in confusion as Bespectacled Boy suddenly stood up.

With an almost pompous gesture, the latter switched on the phone’s speakerphone, turned the volume to maximum, and broadcast a call.

[Dudududu, hello, this is W City 110 Command Center. What do you need help with?]

All of a sudden, everyone in the bus who heard him instantly looked over at him, with expressions of either surprise or curiosity.

One couldn’t tell from the expression alone that anything was wrong.

Li Shiqing was dumbfounded; she didn’t expect her companion to use such a “trick.”

“Hi, I’m on Bus 45, which is travelling over the river bridge from River Road to Jiangbei station….”

Immediately afterwards, his roar suddenly resounded through the bus.

“Please call the police immediately; a bomb has been found on our bus!”

Boom!

Almost as soon as the words were spoken, a violent wave of air instantly engulfed everything ……

—

When he woke up again, the corners of Bespectacled Boy’s mouth held a smug upward tilt.

He’d been wanting to do this for a long time, and it was great to be able to shout out, “There’s a bomb in the bus!”

“You’ve just gone mad!”

Li Shiqing, however, was shocked by the sudden explosion and could not recover from it for a long time.

Enduring the tearing sensation and weakness from the blast, she struggled to pull her phone out of her pocket; the time was 13:25.

“It’s a few minutes early again.”

Li Shiqing murmured.

Outside the window, the stop sign for the last stop before going onto the bridge was faintly visible at the back, obviously having just pulled out of the last stop not long ago.

The bus stop sign not far away made her begin to believe the speculations Bespectacled Boy had made in the restaurant.

“Time and space correspond to each other, and we are advancing the time at which each time cycle occurs.”

“It’s not timed.”

Bespectacled Boy braced himself with difficulty.

The explosion just now, as painful as it was, made Xiao Heyun sure of one thing.

“… And, it didn’t ring a bell.”

They had just exploded at a time that was not 13.45.

Unlike Bespectacled Boy’s delight at finding out the truth, Li Shiqing nodded in agreement, but her expression was even more bitter.

If the terrorist attacked with a time bomb remotely controlled by a mobile phone, he might not necessarily be in the bus; he just had to be able to operate it using his mobile phone.

This was especially true as the same mobile phone had rung several times before, which made the two suspect that the bomb in the bus could have been using a timed device.

But just now there was neither a mobile phone ringing nor did it reach 13:45 when the bus suddenly exploded.

The ability to detonate a bomb on the spur of the moment in response to Bespectacled Boy’s alarm could only mean that…

“The man is in the bus.”

“The real killer is in the bus.”

As they came to this conclusion, the two looked around the bus, creeped out.

CONTENT END 14

chapters.title: The Eleventh Cycle of Time (I)
chapters.content:
Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun were both ordinary young people, perhaps a little better than ordinary people in terms of mental capacity and logical reasoning because of their personal qualities, but by no means in the realm of the “extraordinary.”

By the same token, they had received neither systematic combat training nor professional bomb disposal skills.

With the two like that, if they wanted to solve the problem of the bomb and the terrorists in a short period of time, they must do both: tackle and defuse the bomb.

Now, however, the harsh reality was in front of them.
