Among them, Yuandu Plaza was the commercial complex of the Jiangdong District. People living in the Jiangdong District usually go here for shopping and leisure. It was also the stop with the largest number of people getting off the bus.

As for the later Gangwu New Village and Yanjiang East Road stations, most of the people who got on the bus were going to the old town of Jiangbei.

Gangwu New Village Station was the second to last station before going up the bridge. It was also an area with large residential areas on this line. Since the houses in the surrounding communities were old, the rent was very cheap. Many young people who had just started working and migrant workers lived here. The Yanjiang East Road Station behind it was a station with relatively few people.

Li Shiqing had taken this line countless times, but Xiao Heyun had just come to this city to work not long ago. He usually didn’t even go out and had only taken this bus line a few times. He was not very familiar with the route. After listening to Li Shiqing’s introduction, he began to feel scared.

Judging from the situation they were in now, it seemed as if Heaven wanted to give them a chance and kept “giving” them time. From the first time Li Shiqing “exploded upon waking up” to now, when she could “get off the bus normally at the station,” there was a difference of more than twenty minutes in between.

But no one knew what would happen if time continued to “go backwards.”

What if they didn’t stop the explosion even after looping all the way to the first station?

At that time, where could they retreat to?

What if it was not as good as they imagined? If the cycle really only had a certain number of times, who knew if what they “wasted” might be their last chance to survive?

The two young ones were not stupid. After a little thought, they realized the horror of it. Their already tense state became even more serious.

“Next, we must hit the target right away and not waste any more time.”

Li Shiqing thought about Bespectacled Boy’s bruised face after being beaten by the “masked man” and said sadly, “If you can’t take it by force, try to use ‘wisdom’.”

“OK.”

Xiao Heyun agreed while wiping his glasses with a look of relief, “Thankfully, everything is restored every time the cycle is repeated; otherwise, I would have been blind.”

“Isn’t this even more terrifying?”

Li Shiqing’s voice suddenly darkened. “Our bodies, our conditions, seem to recover every time, including your broken glasses and our growling stomachs.”

“But the pain we feel every time and the weakness before each cycle are real. So how exactly are we cycling? If it’s just…”

“Okay, stop talking!”

Xiao Heyun’s hand trembled as he wiped his glasses, and he quickly interrupted her speculation.

He patted his companion’s hand, comforting her and himself at the same time: “Don’t overthink it. The more you think, the more you worry. What we should be thinking about now is how to find the real culprit, eliminate the danger, and get out of this cycle.”

Li Shiqing gave him a hesitant look and nodded despite her heavy heart.

This time they woke up at 1:20 p.m., not far from the penultimate stop, Gangwu New Village Station. The good thing was that this time there were still 25 minutes left before the predicted explosion time of 1:45 p.m., which was more time than any previous time. The bad thing was that they still hadn’t found the suspects and the explosives.

Because the last failure was too “tragic,” this time they decided to regain their confidence from an “easier” target.

“That old man, please.”

After looking at him again and again, Li Shiqing decided on the candidate.

“Although I think this old man looks the least dangerous, he’s carrying a lot of luggage, so it’s best to rule him out. I’ll distract him this time, and you’ll be responsible for dragging the snakeskin bag away. Is that okay?”

“Don’t worry!”

The young man clenched his fist and made a “don’t worry” gesture. “I can’t beat the guy in the mask. I can’t even beat an old man, huh?”

After discussing the challenge, the two of them got down to work. Li Shiqing stood up and wandered around in the bus for a while, then sat down in the empty seat opposite the old man.

The bus was running smoothly, but the old man, like most elders carrying luggage, did not choose to take a nap. Instead, he kept his eyes open and looked at the road outside the window and basically did not make any eye contact with other passengers in the bus.

So when Li Shiqing spoke to him, he was particularly surprised.

“Grandpa, I see the things you’re carrying are quite heavy. Can you carry them by yourself? Do you need help?”

Li Shiqing said it twice before he realized that she was talking to him. He turned his gaze blankly and pointed at himself.

“You talking to me?”

“Yes.”

Li Shiqing forced a smile. “I see your bag is quite big, and there are a lot of things in it. Wouldn’t it be too hard for you to carry it all by yourself?”

“No, no, I’m used to it.”

The old man patted his chest and said proudly, “Don’t look down on my age. I’m very strong. I can carry these two bags of melons back with just a shoulder pole. I don’t need any help at all.”

“Oh, Grandpa, are you selling melons? I love melons the most. Can you sell me one?”

When Li Shiqing heard it was a melon, she was half convinced, but to be on the safe side, she decided to find a way to take a look.

“You’re such a kind-hearted girl. Are you worried that I can’t sell it? Haha, if it were in the past, I would definitely give you one, but not today.”

The old man looked at Li Shiqing’s expression, as if she was the kind of child who “picked up a penny on the side of the road and was eager to hand it over to the police uncle,” both gentle and kind.

“These melons were ordered by a fruit stall owner in Jiangbei. I’m just delivering them now. I have to give them as many as they want, as we’ve already agreed.”

Li Shiqing felt troubled when she saw that he was unwilling to open the snakeskin bag.

Like most young people who were taught to respect the elderly and love the young, she would be fine if she met a rude old man, but when she met such a kind and amiable one, she was too shameless to insist on seeing what was in the other person’s snakeskin bag.

“In this world today, there are still many good people.”

As soon as the old man opened his mouth, he began to ramble, “I’ve been growing melons for so many years, but fewer and fewer people are buying them. Young people don’t like melons anymore. Watermelons are available year-round, and Hami melons are sweeter than melons. Who wants to eat these small local melons? The owner of that fruit stall knows that melons are not selling well, so he often comes to me to buy more because he’s worried that I can’t make a living…”

Li Shiqing looked at Bespectacled Boy awkwardly and urged him to think of a solution.

The old man continued to ramble on: “You are a kind-hearted person, kid. But I still have my hands and feet. As long as I can still work, I will definitely not go hungry. I am used to working. If I don’t work for a day, my whole body will feel weak. So you don’t have to worry about me…”

“I haven’t seen what local melons look like yet. Grandpa, please open my eyes!”

Seeing that the bus was announcing the stop again, Li Shiqing was still hesitating for a long time and “couldn’t make a move.” Xiao Heyun also became anxious and walked forward with a slightly exaggerated movement and expression.

“I’ll take a look and give it back to you!”

After saying that, he squatted down and pulled the snakeskin bag away from under the man’s feet.

“What are you doing!”

The old man was surprised to see that his things had been taken away. He picked up the short shoulder pole leaning against the car window and stood up.

The young man successfully dragged the snakeskin bag away, but problems arose when he was about to take it away.

What the old man said was absolutely right. A person without strength really couldn’t lift the bag. The young man tried his best to lift the bag but couldn’t, so he could only drag it while running.

The old man was so heartbroken by the holdup that he ran after the bag and grabbed it tightly.

“Watch out for my melon! You can’t just snatch it away even if I don’t show it to you!”

Xiao Heyun held the bag with one hand to prevent the old man from getting hold of it and tried to open the bag with the other hand, but the rope was too tight, and he couldn’t open it at all. He was so anxious that he was sweating profusely, but he refused to let go.

“How can you steal other people’s things?”

The old man was not polite to people who behaved like this. “What kind of people are you? You are lawless. If you don’t let go, I will not be polite!”

At this time, the bus had just arrived at Yanjiang Road East Station. The man holding the cat and wearing a mask got on the bus. When he saw the situation in the bus and heard Bespectacled Boy snatching things from an elderly person, he looked at him with contempt as he passed by.

Many people came up to persuade Bespectacled Boy to let go. Li Shiqing also ran up and touched the snakeskin bag a few times under the pretext of “mediating the fight” and found that there was indeed a round object inside, which made a crisp sound when knocked. It was most likely a melon, so she winked at Bespectacled Boy.

Bespectacled Boy comprehended Li Shiqing’s meaning, and his hand subconsciously loosened…

“Ouch, ouch, watch out for my melon!”

The old man, who had lost his weight in the tug, followed a large sack of melons that fell heavily to the ground, and the sack broke with a crash.

The yellow-green juice ran down the seams of the snakeskin bag and soon stained a large moistened area.

At the same time, the sweet aroma of the melon lingered in the carriage with the rupture of the melon body, and the sweet aroma proved once again that the old man was indeed not suspect.

But the situation was completely out of control.

“What a sin! There goes my good melon!”

When he saw his melon being “ruined,” the old man dropped his shoulder pole, rubbed his back, and wailed again.

“Ouch, my back!”

Bespectacled Boy scrambled to his feet and rushed to his pockets.

“Grandpa, don’t cry, don’t cry. How much are these melons? I’ll pay you back; I’ll pay you double!”

“Are you all right, old grandpa?”

Li Shiqing rushed to help him. “What’s wrong with your back?”

“Is this a matter of losing money? I’ve been doing business with people for so many years, and I’ve never missed out on a single deal. You’re hurting me! You’re causing me to lose my reputation! My waist, ouch, my waist!”

The old grandfather’s voice was so loud that it caused the driver to turn around a lot too.

“What’s going on back there? Are you all right, old man?”

“Don’t look back, Uncle Driver; drive your bus properly!”

Bespectacled Boy was scared half to death when he saw the older man looking back again and yelled in a hurry.

“You, boy, are pretty tough! You robbed someone and beat them up, and you dare to threaten the driver and just drive!”

Once again, the oldest man with a set of keys on his belt “did the right thing” and raised his arms.

“Driver, don’t listen to this lad; take the bus to the police station and see if he’s still cross!”

He hit someone?

He just let go…

Xiao Heyun had just been aggrieved when he realized what was wrong and turned back in panic.

“Driver, don’t listen to them; I don’t have…”

“What’s wrong with your back, old man? Don’t move him; don’t hurt your tendons. Should I call 120?”

“Call 120, call 110 first, don’t let anyone get away!”

“Yes, yes, yes, bullying the elderly; he should be taught a lesson. Call the police!”

“Take the bus to the police station!”

“Don’t be angry, old man; I’ll call the police for you. The police will help you teach this ungrateful young man a lesson!”

“No!”

No, no, no, no, no!

Boom!

In the explosion, Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun closed their eyes in despair.

The author has something to say:  what a pair of (wasted) youngsters eating (scraps of) melons.

CONTENT END 21

chapters.title: The Sixteenth Cycle
chapters.content:
Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun woke up again, startled by the announcement that the bus had arrived at Gangwu New Village Station.

Hearing the announcement, Bespectacled Boy struggled to take out his phone and glanced at it.

1:15 p.m.

This time, the point of waking up was very coincidental, just at the time when passengers were getting on and off the bus at the Gangwu New Village stop.

The two were still weak and had not fully recovered. Although they knew the bus had arrived at the station, they could only watch several strangers get off the bus.

At least seven or eight people got off at this stop, and the carriage was much emptier after the passengers got off.

When most of the passengers had gotten off, a strong uncle carrying a duffle bag got on the bus.

The gym bag that had been sitting on the seat was now slung over his shoulder, and it seemed to be stuffed full, even causing his body to tilt slightly.

After the uncle got on the bus, he looked around and finally chose an empty seat to sit down. Then, as Li Shiqing remembered, he put the big bag on the inner seat by the window.

The next person to board the bus was the auntie carrying the large plastic bag.

The plastic bag had been placed at her feet before, and it was impossible to see anything wrong with it. But now that the aunt was carrying the bag onto the bus, anyone could see at a glance that the bag was particularly heavy.

Also, because the things inside the bag were heavy, they had to use two layers of the thick plastic bags from the supermarket to hold them so that the bag would not break halfway, which was a kind of “double insurance.”

They watched the uncle and aunt sit down in their original seats, and even the position of the luggage at their feet and hands was placed in exactly the same position.

“Did they get on at this stop?”

“Did they get on at this station?””

This was the first time the two had seen someone get on and off the bus normally, and they were both surprised.

However, although it was a new discovery, there was no useful information.

This repetitive experience left Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun both physically and mentally exhausted. When they finally recovered from their “weak” state, they looked at the fading bus stop sign, but they were not happy at all.

“You rest for a while; I’ll look around.”

Bespectacled Boy seemed to have suddenly thought of something, stood up from his seat, and went out, wandering around the carriage.

“I’ll check to see if any of the passengers who got off the bus earlier left anything suspicious on the bus, or if anyone secretly hid anything.”

After he had a look around and sat back down, Li Shiqing lowered her voice and asked,

“What are you doing?”

Bespectacled Boy replied, “It’s okay; I didn’t see any suspicious items.”

In an open space like a bus, it was easy to see if there was anything strange left on the bus. With so many people getting on and off the bus, it was impossible to hide anything unless someone on the bus was helping.

“I don’t think it’s likely to be a group crime. If this was a carefully planned act by an organization, then there must be some demand, such as controlling hostages to demand ransom, etc. There is no reason to take such a big risk to blow up a bus with only a few people.”

Li Shiqing had thought about this question long ago.

“And the fact that we were questioned so much by the police shows that no organization has made any demands or claimed responsibility for the incident before or after it, so it is more likely to be an act of revenge against society.”

However, compared with the organized and premeditated bombing, this kind of uncontrollable behavior that could not be understood in the process and motivation is even more terrible. At least Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun have not found any clues except that they know that the criminals must be on the bus.

“Then keep investigating!”

Bespectacled Boy took a deep breath and unobtrusively sized up the robust uncle and the aunt in a floral dress who had just boarded the bus. “Ah?”

“Then we’ll set our next target as…”

Xiao Heyun’s gaze swept over the uncle’s bulging biceps and developed back muscles, and his gaze suddenly shrank.

“Let’s go with Auntie!”

“Ah?””

Li Shiqing was stunned.

“Look at that uncle; you can tell at a glance that he is not good at talking. If you just strike up a conversation, it will definitely backfire and make him more alert. Look at his figure and skin again. He is obviously used to doing physical work, and he must be quite strong. You can’t snatch it from him…”

Bespectacled Boy pushed up his glasses and explained in a serious manner, “I think we’re probably not his match. Moreover, his bag is placed on the inside, so you can’t get the bag without moving your hands. But if you really want to fight with him…”

He gave a dry cough.

“…I think we’re probably no match for him.””

Li Shiqing chuckled, “You don’t need to explain so much; I can understand.”

“I’m giving the most efficient solution!””

Bespectacled Boy’s tone was quite hard, but his expression was obviously one of embarrassment and anger. “There are only four suspicious people in total. If we use the method of elimination, and if the auntie is not suspicious either, then only the uncle with the bag is left. In this situation, ‘desperate’ is valuable…”

“Okay, okay, efficient, efficient. Then we’ll do it the old way and try to outsmart them first.”

Li Shiqing echoed his words in a friendly manner.

The two observed their position. The aunt was sitting in front of them on the right, with an aisle in between. From their location, they could only see the back of her head, and there was no possibility of striking up a conversation.

The huge plastic bag was placed on the open space at her feet. If they were to snatch it, she would not need to bend over to grab the bag. The possibility of snatching it by force was also not great.

“You have so many ideas; think of something,” Bespectacled Boy urged.

Li Shiqing racked her brains for a while and came up with a not-so-brilliant idea.

“There’s a bad reason we can use. I’ll consider it as a last resort. I’ll go and try it, and you can act according to the circumstances!”

“What method?” Bespectacled Boy asked.

“Oh, never mind, I’ll go and try it out. If it doesn’t work, I’ll come back.”

After saying that, Li Shiqing ran to the aunt in front of her in a few steps.

Speaking of which, Li Shiqing was not unfamiliar with this aunt.

The first time she “caught a pervert,” this aunt was the closest to her, so she begged her to get off the bus with her to testify, but the aunt refused on the grounds that she “had to rush home to cook.”

On the few occasions when something happened on the bus, this auntie neither spoke up nor offered to help. She was clearly someone who didn’t like to get involved in other people’s business, just like the man in the mask.

So Li Shiqing had no idea whether she could “trick” such a person.

“That…”

“Is there anything you need?””

Seeing the little girl standing in front of her, looking shy and embarrassed to speak, the thin aunt finally couldn’t help but speak first.

Seeing that the aunt was paying attention to her, Li Shiqing’s eyes lit up. She hunched over and squeezed to her side, her body very close to hers. She lowered her voice and asked softly,

“Auntie, do you have that thing with you? The thing you use when you have your period? My period suddenly came, but I didn’t bring anything to change.”

Although she asked such a nonsensical question, she was secretly staring at the bag at the feet of the aunt.

Through the layers of plastic bags, she could vaguely see a large iron-gray object inside, and a long handle extended out of the bag…

Hmm?There’s a handle?

Li Shiqing wondered what it could be.

“Hey, little girl, don’t stick so close to me!””

The aunt was obviously not used to people getting close to her, and she reached out and pushed her away, shaking her head with a cold face, “I don’t have that thing; you can ask someone else. I haven’t had my menstruation for many years!””

The auntie refused without any euphemism, and not only was she not euphemistic, but her voice was not small, and she did not have the slightest intention of protecting the self-esteem of a “shy” girl.

Luckily, Li Shiqing was acting; otherwise, she would have been embarrassed to death by this shout.

Actually, even though she was acting, Li Shiqing was still a little ashamed.

Many people in the bus still heard the aunt’s words about “menstruation,” especially Bespectacled Boy, who was sitting in his seat and preparing to act according to circumstances. He was dumbfounded on the spot, secretly looking at Li Shiqing, his face full of helplessness.

She had already used this kind of reason to “strike up” a conversation, so what kind of opportunity could she take?

You can’t just run up to her and say you have one, can you?

“Why haven’t you left yet?”

The auntie saw that Li Shiqing had been rejected but hadn’t left and looked at her with a frown and a look of disgust. “Don’t keep standing here!””

“Auntie, you must have toilet paper, right? Facial tissue will do!”

Li Shiqing refused to give up and stood her ground, begging in a low voice, “Anything will do, even a few tissues. I’ll get off at the next stop. I’ll be too embarrassed to face anyone if it gets on my clothes.”

As she spoke, she squatted down at the feet of the woman and covered her stomach with both hands.

“Please help me. You know, I can’t hold it in!”

“How can you be so thick-skinned? I’ve already said no!”

The auntie’s face changed when she saw that she squatted down and refused to leave. She stood up halfway and glanced at the carriage. Seeing that there was no younger woman in the carriage except herself, her face became even darker.

“Get off at the next stop!”

Because she was squatting, Li Shiqing was closer to the object wrapped in the plastic bag, almost to the point where she could reach out and touch it. So she gritted her teeth and chose to take a risk.

“Auntie, I don’t believe you didn’t bring any tissue paper. Just let me take a look. If you don’t have any, I’ll leave it at that!””

She quickly threw out this sentence, and then grabbed the plastic bag and tore it open in her direction!!

“What are you doing?!””

Seeing that Li Shiqing was about to turn over her plastic bag, the aunt panicked, and her voice changed. She raised her leg and kicked Li Shiqing away without mercy.

“Ouch!”！”

Li Shiqing never expected the aunt to kick her, and she fell backward, failing to grab the plastic bag that she had already torn halfway.

She fell heavily into the aisle, her head hitting the ground with a loud thud.

“What’s wrong with you? Why are you kicking people?!”

Xiao Heyun, who had been staring at the front, did not expect such a change. He jumped up in shock and ran over to help.

However, there was another person who was faster than him.

“Little girl, are you hurt?”

The uncle with the bag who got on the bus at the same stop as the aunt in the floral dress helped Li Shiqing up.

The fall was not light, and Li Shiqing covered the back of her head and grinned.

“No, it’s nothing…”

Seeing that the person who helped her up was another “suspect,” Li Shiqing panicked and stammered, “I, I just fell…”

Seeing Bespectacled Boy come over with concern, she signaled to her companion, “I have it hereunder control,” indicating not to worry, but her eyes swept over the great god, who was nervously gathering the mouth of the plastic bag.

Although it was just a fleeting glance, it was enough for her to see clearly.

In the bag was a pot.

A pot with a handle, tall and thick.

As a housewife who was rushing home to cook, it seemed that there was nothing wrong with carrying a pot. Something flashed through Li Shiqing’s mind, but she couldn’t catch it for a moment, so she could only bite the bullet and thank the “suspect” uncle.

“Thank you, uncle.”

“It’s nothing, people nowadays, sigh…”

The uncle, who was dressed in simple clothes, was indeed not good at speaking, as Bespectacled Boy had guessed. Even if he was dissatisfied with the aunt who kicked her, he was not good at saying anything directly.

Seeing that Li Shiqing was about to leave after thanking him, he hesitated for a while and called her to stop.

“Hey, little girl, wait a minute…”

Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy were startled and stopped in their tracks.

He turned back to his seat, pulled the big bag that was on the seat next to him, put it on the seat next to him in front of them, and bent down to rummage through it.

“Little girl, you need tissue paper, right? I have some here.”

He was sitting in the front and vaguely heard a few words of conversation. In addition, the girl had not deliberately lowered her voice when she said “period” or something, so he could roughly guess what the girl was asking the middle-aged woman for.

Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy did not expect things to develop like this. They were completely stunned and stared at the uncle as he rummaged through his bag in front of them.

There was no bomb in the bag as they had guessed, but a pile of inexplicable sundries, including clothes and several pairs of canvas shoes wrapped in plastic bags, and Xiao Heyun even caught a glimpse of a bowl, as if the uncle had stuffed all his belongings into it.

“I took everything with me when I left. I remember there was a pack of unopened tissue paper. Ah, I found it; it’s here!”

He took out a pack of “Xinxiangyin” tissue paper from his bag. “I didn’t open it when I had dinner last time. Anyway, I paid for it, so I took it back. Don’t worry, little girl, it’s unopened and clean!!”

Li Shiqing thanked him in a low voice, took the tissue paper from the uncle’s hand, and followed Bespectacled Boy back to her seat with a cold body.

“Not the masked man, not the watermelon-selling grandpa, not the uncle with the bag, then it’s, it’s that, that…”

Bespectacled Boy was tongue-tied, and his mental state was not much better than Li Shiqing’s.

Previously, because the uncle was too strong, they skipped him and tried to investigate the aunt first. They originally had the idea of the “elimination method” and were prepared to start with the people who looked simple.

But now, by accident, they saw the contents of the kind uncle’s bag without using any “brains” or “brawn.”

If they used the “elimination method” that Bespectacled Boy mentioned, then the answer was only…

“I remember what that thing is.”

Li Shiqing grabbed Bespectacled Boy’s hand, her palm damp with cold sweat.

She looked at her companion in terror and squeezed his hand tighter and tighter.

“She’s got a pressure cooker!”

CONTENT END 22

chapters.title: The Seventeenth Cycle of Time
chapters.content:
During the last normal stop, Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun discussed the fact that in a place like a bus, you couldn’t hide a bomb on the outside, whether you placed it under the seat or in a hidden place, because the mobility of the passengers made it easy to notice a sudden addition.

Considering that the bombs had exploded on cue before, it was most likely that the type of bomb was carried on the person.

Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy also speculated on the possibility that the bomb would be more concealed if it was too small, but both were eventually overruled.

First of all, among so many explosions, even if they excluded the few times when the bus accidentally hit the tanker, the other times were “total annihilation.” At least once Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun had stood on the front of the bus, but they were still blown into pieces. Such an explosion range determined that it could not have been a micro bomb.

Although the perpetrator’s motives were unknown, the fact that no one in the trucks contacted the police or demanded a ransom essentially ruled out the possibility of a group operation. After all, the suspect likely blew himself up, making the claim of revenge more likely than a crime motivated by money.

Besides, bombs weren’t easy to come by. They were not firecrackers, and they came in all shapes and sizes.

To think about it another way, using a micro-bomb and a detonating device, going to such great lengths just to blow up a bus, with no intention of extorting hostages for money—the motive was truly unimaginable.

Now, all the passengers on the bus carrying large carry-on luggage had been “screened.” Aside from the three “suspects” whose bags had already been opened, the only one left was the pressure cooker this woman was carrying. It was the most difficult sealed container to detect and the most likely carrier of the explosive.

However, on this matter, Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun had another disagreement.

Xiao Heyun felt that the pressure cooker wasn’t considered a particularly dangerous item because it was so common.

“A normal housewife carrying a pot—that’s normal, right?”

Seeing how frightened Li Shiqing was, Bespectacled Boy grabbed her arm. “Maybe she was cooking for her family, and there was something stewing in the pressure cooker. She was afraid the smell would escape, so she just took the pot with her.”

“My intuition tells me there’s something wrong with that pot.”

Li Shiqing felt a surge of unease when she thought of the woman’s overreaction when she opened the plastic bag.

“If you were carrying just an ordinary pressure cooker, would you kick someone if they opened your plastic bag, knowing they were in poor health?”

“But it might not be a bomb. This middle-aged woman is just cautious. Maybe she simply doesn’t want others looking through her things. And that act you put on was so exaggerated and fake…” Bespectacled Boy stole a glance at her and muttered in a low voice, “Only an honest man like Uncle-with-a-Bag could fall for that.”

As they spoke, the next stop arrived, and the masked man boarded the bus again, clutching his hidden kitten.

Seeing that Li Shiqing didn’t stop as planned, the woman in flowery clothes gave her a few more glances. The man who offered her the tissue seemed to be hesitant to speak, but ultimately, nothing came of it.

As they drove further ahead, approaching the intersection where the bus often collided with a tanker, Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun discussed it and decided to eliminate the high-risk “pressure cooker” before the intersection.

“What’s the point of discussing a plan now? Just go for it!”

Li Shiqing, less cautious than Bespectacled Boy, frowned and said, “It’s just a confirmation, not a bomb disposal. Why not just open the pressure cooker and take a look? Even if we’re wrong, the most we’ll get is a beating from the woman or someone who thinks we’re crazy. What’s the harm?”

“Still, still have to open it, huh?”

Bespectacled Boy stammered.

“How about this? You hold the woman down while I open it.”

Li Shiqing had a strong feeling the answer she was looking for lay within the pressure cooker.

They’d gone through so many cycles, failed so many times, and died so many times in vain.

They’d suffered so much, endured so much pain, and now the answer was right at their fingertips. If not now, when?

“I’ll go. It’s just to confirm; I’ll give it a try.”

Seeing that Li Shiqing, a girl, had put so much trust in him, Bespectacled Boy couldn’t back down at this point. Though clearly panicking, he gritted his teeth and insisted on going alone. “You’ve borrowed something from her before, and she’s already wary of you. Going with me might backfire. She’s just a frail old woman; it shouldn’t be difficult for me to snatch the pot from under her feet.”

“What if it blows up…”

Li Shiqing nervously grasped his hand.

“It’s bound to blow up sooner or later.”

Having said this, Bespectacled Boy didn’t give Li Shiqing a chance to waver. He stood up and headed straight for the woman’s seat.

He moved swiftly, without hesitation. He squatted down next to the aunt, grabbed the pressure cooker bag, and pulled it free.

The aunt, indeed, panicked at the thought of someone trying to grab the pressure cooker, but she didn’t scream like the masked man or the elderly man before her. Instead, she silently exerted all her strength, working against Bespectacled Boy to pull at the bag.

Seeing that her strength was comparable to the young man’s and the plastic bag was about to be snatched, she wore an almost ferocious expression and directly raised her hand to pull the pressure-reducing valve from the pressure cooker.

Bang!

The moment the pressure-reducing valve was pulled, a tremendous force, accompanied by an earth-shattering explosion, swept through the two people closest to it.

The young man, who was pulling the plastic bag, hadn’t reacted when a piercing pain shot through his body, and he instantly lost consciousness.

—

A new cycle began.

The sudden explosion of the pressure cooker killed everyone in the bus, including, of course, Li Shiqing.

But the person who suffered the most severe physical and mental trauma in this explosion was undoubtedly Xiao Heyun, who had been directly exposed to the explosion’s blast in the face.

Waking up from the cycle again, Bespectacled Boy’s condition was so dire that it seemed he would die at any moment.

He was panting like a fish out of water, his throat making a continuous “ho ho” sound, as if he would faint from suffocation at any moment, and his body was shaking violently.

Li Shiqing was far less weak than he, but she could only struggle to raise a hand and place it on his arm, trembling with him.

Before, they had believed the fear of the unknown was the most terrifying, the agony of desperately pursuing the target that would harm them, yet finding none.

Now, having found the source of their suffering and witnessed the explosion firsthand, they realized:

Compared to the previous terror of the unknown, the unforeseen disasters, and the horror of witnessing the explosion unfold before one’s very eyes, being unable to prevent it was even more devastating.

Li Shiqing felt only the crushing and tearing of the explosion, but Xiao Heyun felt it more deeply.

At the moment of being blown up at close range, the pain penetrated from his pores and skin to his flesh and bone marrow. In an instant, he could feel his head, limbs, and even bones completely detached from his “perception.”

It was hard to say whether he fainted from the overwhelming pain or from the sheer terror of his own imagination.

This fear reached its peak when the aunt carrying the pressure cooker boarded the bus again in front of them.

“How are you? Are you feeling particularly uncomfortable?”

Li Shiqing woke up earlier and was more lucid than Xiao Heyun.

Watching the aunt sit back down in her seat, oblivious to the others, Li Shiqing trembled along with Bespectacled Boy, but the trembling wasn’t due to any physical distress.

“Please don’t get hurt. Don’t leave me alone. I’m scared!”

The aunt, busy with explosives, sat right in the seat in front of them!

At that moment, Bespectacled Boy was still immersed in the excruciating pain and couldn’t hear what Li Shiqing was saying in his ear.

It was an utterly terrifying pain, a feeling of tearing and shattering every inch of your body, yet you couldn’t feel a single inch of your skin, muscle, or bone. His hands and feet couldn’t move, as if everything was fake, but only the pain remained, a constant reminder that it was real.

Xiao Heyun felt himself being constantly shattered and reassembled. He had never experienced such pain before. Every minute and every second in this state seemed infinitely long.

At one moment, he wished he could die quickly rather than endure such pain.

At another, he secretly rejoiced that he had died alone.

If the little girl had endured such pain with him, how heartbreaking it would have been…

After a long while, when the little brother finally recovered from the horrific pain, the first thing he saw was Li Shiqing’s tear-stained face.

“Wu wu wu…”

He raised his hand, trying to reassure her, but only a series of incomprehensible sounds escaped his throat.

“How are you? Are you okay?”

Hearing his hoarse voice, Li Shiqing’s tears fell even more violently.

“Okay, much better.”

Xiao Heyun closed his eyes wearily and leaned against Li Shiqing, his whole body looking as if he had just been pulled out of the water.

“I’ll take it easy; just let me lean on you for a bit.”

This time, his condition was horrific, so bad that he almost thought he couldn’t make it, that he’d “dissipate.”

This also gave him a vague premonition…

The damage inflicted during the cycle might not be harmless to them, nor would it necessarily be “reversed” through the cycle. If their willpower wasn’t strong enough, terrible things could still happen.

At least, considering the pain he’d just experienced, it was worse than death.

Li Shiqing let Bespectacled Boy lean against her, without any intention of urging him or asking what he’d just discovered…

She had just been terrified by his condition.

Whether she wanted to admit it or not, in their shared life and death and their unwavering loyalty, he had gradually transformed from a stranger to a pillar of support she could trust and rely on.

“Next time, no matter what happens, we’ll have to face it together!”

Li Shiqing wiped her tears, beginning to regret letting Bespectacled Boy go alone to determine the situation.

“Even if we die together, it’s better than being left alone in fear.”

They were both ordinary people. They had always relied on each other’s support and help to get to this stage. At this point, if anything happened to either of them, the remaining one would be unable to hold on.

“This was an accident.”

Xiao Heyun knew the young woman was frightened by his own tragic condition. He wiped her tears and soothed her in a calm voice:

“Look, although it hurts a little, I’ll recover with time, won’t I?”

“I’m glad you’ve recovered. I was just worried something might happen to you.”

Knowing that Bespectacled Boy was worried about her, Li Shiqing tried to calm her fear, trying not to seem so pretentious.

“Besides, that sacrifice wasn’t in vain.”

Bespectacled Boy recalled every detail leading up to the explosion. “I know what the detonator is… It’s the pressure-limiting valve.”

He said with a wry smile, “I don’t know the exact mechanism, but as soon as the woman pulled the pressure-limiting valve on top of the pressure cooker, it exploded violently!”

Knowing who the criminal was and what the explosive was, they felt no relief.

Because this meant they would face an even more severe test.

But before facing such a severe test, Li Shiqing gave Bespectacled Boy a conclusion that was even worse.

“You were in such a bad state when you woke up just now that I took out my phone to check the time.”

Li Shiqing’s face paled as she recounted the situation.

“We woke up at 1:15 p.m., just as the auntie boarded the bus…”

“What?”

Bespectacled Boy instantly understood the meaning of Li Shiqing’s words, and his vision went dark.

“I hope I’m mistaken.”

She leaned close to her companion, as if only in this way could she find some warmth from him.

“But it seems like Heaven won’t give us any more time…”

Author’s Note: mini theater. Reader: Did the bomb go off today? Author: (nods) Yes.

CONTENT END 23

chapters.title: The Eighteenth Cycle
chapters.content:
“From this single data point, it’s impossible to tell whether we’ve stopped looping or simply stopped moving back the cycle time. If it’s the former, then we only have one chance to resolve this situation…”

Bespectacled Boy glanced at the clock, his expression heavy. “But it’s already 1:22 p.m. I was in such poor condition earlier, wasting so much time. We might not have enough time.”

Not just enough; it’s practically a case of waiting to die.

“If time simply stopped moving back, we need to consider why this happened.”

He felt uneasy but forced himself to calm down and continue reasoning. “There are two possibilities for time stopping at this station. First, we successfully found the explosives and the criminal. Idealistically, perhaps we ‘met’ certain conditions, and heaven saw no need to give us more time to try again…”

“Second, perhaps the ‘source’ of the incident was at this station.” Bespectacled Boy shuddered. “Then we need to consider what happened at this station. For example, the woman with the pressure cooker boarded the train at this station…”

Because the tragedy was caused by the bomb in the “pressure cooker” getting on the train, there was no point in going back any further. Time froze at this moment. Thinking in this direction made perfect sense.

Li Shiqing understood, but her panic only grew.

“We have to assume the worst.”

She suppressed her panic and anxiety. “If we don’t consider the latter scenario, if this is truly the final cycle, how can we stop this explosion now?”

“It may not be the first scenario. At this point, we can’t let ourselves down. Besides, the current situation isn’t too dire.”

Bespectacled Boy glanced at the Yanjiang East Road station they had already missed and forced himself to explain, “…the explosion just now also gave us a lot of information.”

“First, it’s certain that the explosive was a pressure cooker. I observed that the detonation method was the opening of the pressure-limiting valve. So, during any operation, we must absolutely not let Auntie touch the pressure cooker.”

Bespectacled Boy lowered his voice and whispered in Li Shiqing’s ear. “This woman is aloof and wary and won’t respond to your attempts to attract attention. So, we can’t outsmart her; we’ll have to force her.”

“Luckily, she’s a frail, middle-aged woman. If we both attack her together, there’s a good chance we can successfully seize the pressure cooker.”

“Are you sure you can do it?”

It’s not that Li Shiqing looks down on Bespectacled Boy, but his demonstrated strength has always been particularly worrying.

He couldn’t beat the masked man, and he couldn’t grab anything from the old man either.

The middle-aged woman looked frail, as if she’d collapse at the slightest gust of wind, but could someone so ruthless as to embrace a bomb and perish along with everyone on the bus really be so easily defeated?

“Before, I was just ‘checking the situation,’ which is completely different from actually risking my life this time.”

Bespectacled Boy, knowing what Li Shiqing was worried about, rubbed the top of her head and said with certainty, “I know what’s in that pot. This concerns our safety and our future. We must use all our courage and strength.”

“Since you think it’s possible, I’ll assume we can successfully seize the pressure cooker. But after we do, what should we do?”

Li Shiqing pointedly raised the most practical question: “We can’t just hold onto the pot forever, right? Even if we call the police now, it’s definitely too late.”

“Given the tight timeline, here’s my initial plan.”

Bespectacled Boy took out his notebook and began writing and drawing again, then began his “planning process” again.

“Here, this intersection. I’ve observed it. Many times before, we’ve had accidents around 1:29 p.m. If the driver isn’t distracted, this intersection is usually navigable without incident. Therefore, we shouldn’t attack near this time. If the driver is distracted, it’s easy to crash into the tanker for no apparent reason…”

Bespectacled Boy drew an intersection and marked it with “1:29 p.m.”

“I suggest we attack after 1:30 p.m., and immediately after we successfully pass the intersection.”

“Okay.”

Li Shiqing nodded.

“After passing this intersection, we’ll be on the approach bridge. Speeds won’t be too high there. We’ll attack there.” Bespectacled Boy drew an “X” on the approach bridge.

“The bus will keep to the right after it gets on the bridge. After we grab the pressure cooker, we absolutely mustn’t let the woman touch the pressure relief valve. Once I’ve restrained her, quickly remove the safety hammer and crack the right-hand window. Once the glass shatters, we’ll throw the pressure cooker off the bridge. There’s a river below the bridge, so the damage from the explosion will be reduced.”

“As for the safety hammer, I’ve tried it before when I was trying to grab the safety hammer. It’s easy to remove, and it only takes a little force to completely shatter the window. Don’t hold back. Throw the pressure cooker as soon as the glass shatters…”

As Bespectacled Boy explained his plan, Li Shiqing kept checking the clock. When it reached 27 minutes, she didn’t have time to discuss anything further. She immediately stood up, walked over to the driver, and warned him to be careful of motorcycles and the tanker on the road.

As so many times before, since Li Shiqing was a familiar figure to him, the driver listened to her advice and slowed down, successfully avoiding the difficult intersection.

Seeing they successfully passed the intersection, Li Shiqing didn’t immediately leave the driver’s side. Instead, she patiently waited until the bus slowly pulled onto the approach bridge before turning back to look for her companion.

Seeing Bespectacled Boy stand slightly and nod at her, she took a deep breath and walked resolutely towards the aunt.

At the same time, Bespectacled Boy rushed to the front row, grasped the aunt with his arms, and with all his strength, lifted her up and dragged her out of the bus seat!

The woman, who had been sitting upright, hadn’t anticipated this turn of events. When Bespectacled Boy pulled her off her seat, she screamed, her first instinct being to reach for her plastic bag.

However, Li Shiqing did not give her any chance to touch the plastic bag. She had dragged out the pressure cooker the moment Bespectacled Boy pulled the aunt out and carefully carried it out of the aunt’s reach.

The previous rounds of sparring hadn’t been entirely ineffective. At least the few “naked choke” and “throat lock” techniques Bespectacled Boy had learned at the last minute, while ineffective against the masked man, were effective against the middle-aged woman.

His right arm tightly gripped the woman’s neck from behind, while he used his left arm to hold her down. He simultaneously used the strength of his waist and legs to pin her down, ensuring she couldn’t struggle.

“Don’t touch the pressure cooker! There’s a bomb in it!”

Bespectacled Boy saw someone trying to stop him and shouted, “No one touch it, or we’ll all be doomed!”

Several passengers who were about to approach were frightened, their faces drastically changing as they stopped in their tracks. The area around the pressure cooker instantly became a forbidden zone, with everyone shunning it in fear.

Bespectacled Boy’s shouting startled not only the passengers but also the driver in front.

The driver had no idea what was happening behind him, but then Bespectacled Boy yelled, “There’s a bomb in the pressure cooker!” Perhaps out of fear, the driver’s foot, which was controlling the brakes, involuntarily pressed down, and the bus began to slow down.

But the driver’s slowdown made Li Shiqing, who had been scheduled to knock on the window, panic.

If the bus couldn’t reach the bridge, the bomb couldn’t be dropped into the water. Without the river water to cushion the impact, there would likely be casualties.

“Uncle, you can’t slow down! Keep going onto the bridge!”

Li Shiqing shouted as she quickly unsheathed the safety hammer and pounded hard at several points on the bus window.

Just as Bespectacled Boy had predicted, with each blow of the hammer, the surface of the bus window began to shatter like snowflakes, spreading out like a spiderweb. Soon, the entire window was covered in cracks, ready to shatter with just the slightest tap!

Just as Bespectacled Boy was gradually showing joy and was about to wait for his companions to throw the pot as originally agreed, a sudden change occurred!

The woman, who had been struggling violently under Bespectacled Boy’s control, pulled a fruit knife from one of her pockets and viciously stabbed Bespectacled Boy in the waist!

Bespectacled Boy had never expected the woman to be carrying a “weapon.” The knife struck him squarely on the right side of his waist, causing him to flinch in pain and draining his strength from holding her.

“You… ah!”

Before he could react, the woman had already broken free from her restraints, twisted around, and stabbed again!

Bespectacled Boy was caught off guard, stabbed in his arms, thighs, and other places. The woman, whether out of sheer malice or sheer shock, kept stabbing with the knife, her movements swift and ferocious. In the blink of an eye, several bloody holes had appeared on Bespectacled Boy’s body.

Bleeding gushed from the wounds. Bespectacled Boy’s mind went blank for a moment, staring at the blood on his body, as if even the ability to think had drained away from the wounds along with the blood.

Seeing such a horrific “death” in the bus, those who had originally thought the “bomb” was a joke finally became frightened. The bus erupted in chaos. Forget about trying to stop them. People desperately tried to get as far away from these “madmen” as possible, crowding towards the doors.

Some of them screamed, some shouted “Murder!” Several, despite the traffic jams on the bridge, demanded the driver stop and open the door immediately.

Li Shiqing was stunned by the sudden turn of events.

“Leave me alone, the pot…”

Seeing his companion seemingly paralyzed, he called out weakly, his breath so weak that no one but himself could hear his words.

The woman with a ferocious face had already pushed aside the severely injured young man lying on the ground and rushed towards Li Shiqing, knife in hand.

Seeing the woman, covered in blood, charging towards her like a demon from hell, Li Shiqing instinctively turned and ran, clutching the safety hammer tightly in her hand.

As it turned out, the safety hammer might be useful for knocking against the glass, but it was completely useless against a knife-wielding attacker. She hadn’t even taken two steps before the woman, who had lunged at her like a madman, overtook her.

“Ah!”

A sudden, sharp pain in her back made Li Shiqing’s body stiffen. Then, she felt a powerful tug on her scalp.

Someone grabbed her ponytail, forcing her to gasp and twist her head back. A short, sharp fruit knife was already at her throat.

A face, distorted with emotion, suddenly appeared before her.

“Help, help…”

Having failed to stop the murderer and now in her clutches, Li Shiqing was completely terrified. Tears and snot streamed down her face.

Someone please save her…

The old woman’s eyes remained completely blank. Even as she held a knife to a young girl’s neck, her expression was similar to that of an ordinary housewife preparing to bleed a chicken before cooking.

Wait, bleed a chicken?!

As soon as this thought crossed Li Shiqing’s mind, her fear reached its peak…

A chill ran down her throat, and she completely lost consciousness.

CONTENT END 24

chapters.title: Nineteenth Cycle
chapters.content:
When she regained consciousness, she was back to the moment when the aunt, carrying the pressure cooker, walked towards her seat.

The moment Li Shiqing saw the aunt, she instinctively covered her neck, her throat emitting a sharp wheezing sound like a broken bellows being pulled, unable to breathe properly.

“Don’t be afraid, don’t be afraid; it’s all over.”

Xiao Heyun had also experienced this kind of near-death pain and could tell at a glance that the pain from that previous time was still lingering on her. Heartbroken, he held the little girl in his arms, stroking her back and offering gentle comfort.

“And I’m still here. We’re all here.”

Poor Li Shiqing was just an ordinary female college student. She’d been taught from childhood to “be kind to others and get better together.” The most intense arguments she’d ever encountered were merely a few squabbles between classmates. How could she have ever encountered such a brutal person?

She’d thought constant bombing was the limit of what she could endure, but she hadn’t expected something even more terrifying.

“Too, too brutal…”

She was so frightened that she couldn’t even cry.

Recalling the aunt’s numb eyes, as if she were slaughtering a chicken, Li Shiqing clutched her neck. She could still feel the biting chill in her throat. Even the air, which she breathed with difficulty, tasted of blood.

The cold, bloody chill seemed to penetrate the slit in her throat and penetrate every limb, freezing every inch of her soul.

It was a chill that penetrated deep into her bones.

“Don’t think about what happened before. Think of them as nightmares. Some dreams are over, and what matters is that we’re still alive.”

When Li Shiqing was in trouble, Xiao Heyun had already lost consciousness from excessive blood loss. He didn’t see what happened to her afterwards, nor did he know why she was so frightened.

He tried to hold down Li Shiqing’s hand, which was covering her neck, to cheer her up, but the terrifying chill of her hand gave him a start.

Wouldn’t the little girl have died too often, suffering from post-traumatic stress disorder?

Bespectacled Boy was filled with worry and sadness, but he wasn’t very good at comforting people. He could only clumsily hold Li Shiqing’s hand, holding her in his arms, repeating over and over again:

“Don’t be afraid, don’t be afraid…”

Perhaps it was the warmth of Bespectacled Boy’s body that dispelled the chill that seeped into her bones, or perhaps it was the encouragement from her companions that sustained her near-collapse. With Bespectacled Boy’s repeated soothing words, Li Shiqing’s heart finally began to warm up, and her trembling gradually subsided.

“Are you feeling better?”

Bespectacled Boy looked down at her and asked worriedly, “If you really can’t take it anymore, we’ll get off at the next stop. Forget about it and go and calm down.”

After hearing Bespectacled Boy’s advice, Li Shiqing hesitated for a moment but ultimately shook her head and slowly straightened up in Bespectacled Boy’s arms.

“No, we can’t waste another cycle. No one knows what will happen next,” she said. “I’m fine. I can hold on.”

“Are you sure?”

Bespectacled Boy’s face was filled with worry, and he could only reassure her.

“Seriously, if we really feel uncomfortable, let’s get off the bus and get some fresh air.”

“Really.” Li Shiqing nodded again.

Seeing Li Shiqing, clearly terrified yet still forcing herself to continue, Bespectacled Boy felt even more sad.

This kind of growth was truly cruel.

“Okay then.”

But at his companion’s insistence, he could only sigh and respect her insistence.

“My last encounter with that auntie convinced me of one thing.”

As Li Shiqing spoke, she unconsciously stroked her neck. “That auntie is probably mentally ill.”

“Huh?”

Bespectacled Boy was stunned.

“Isn’t it obvious? What sane person could do such a thing?”

“Not the kind with mental problems.”

She shuddered as she spoke.

“I can’t sense any human emotion in her eyes or expression.”

She felt the fear of being hurt, the hesitation of hurting others, and the struggle of wanting to kill—all of these should be normal “human” emotions, but she couldn’t feel any of them.

When the aunt tried to kill her, she felt like she was a piece of stone.

Or the kind of stone that has stood in a waterfall, even after decades or centuries of being buffeted by the rushing water, still so hard it refuses to wear away.

It was as if even the wear and tear was there; it was because it willingly let the water wash it away.

“There’s no way to communicate with someone like that, let alone try to influence her.”

Li Shiqing shook Bespectacled Boy’s hand and said, “Even if she appears calm now, it’s to hide her true face, a face that could easily be used to smother someone.”

How could one possibly shake someone who was completely devoid of emotion? Does the torrent rushing across the riverbed care what the rocks already there think?

“We’ve always overlooked one thing, and that is…”

Her face was pale, and she could barely speak.

Sensing her fear, Bespectacled Boy gripped her hand even tighter.

“We’re facing a madman who’s planning to blow up a carload of people with a bomb.”

She finally faced this truth, and the experience was incredibly painful.

If their previous experiences resembled a disaster movie, then the close encounter with this woman was a true thriller.

With each previous “explosion,” they faced a seemingly routine dilemma—finding the killer, finding the explosives, finding a solution. While the process was arduous, the difficulties were often unknown, only to reveal themselves unexpectedly.

Especially the previous “investigations,” which had almost always gone unnoticed, like a series of farces, numbing the little vigilance they’d painstakingly cultivated and fostering a sense of complacency.

It wasn’t until reality slapped them in the face that they finally woke up.

As for Bespectacled Boy’s excuses about “women looking easier to subdue,” it brought tears to their eyes.

“What have you been through… Oh, never mind.”

Bespectacled Boy looked at Li Shiqing, who seemed to have suddenly matured, and hesitated several times to speak.

But he chose not to ask. After all, his lower back still ached, and there was no need to provoke others.

“So what do you want to do? Do you think my plan is not perfect?”

He had no objection to his companions questioning his plan.

“There’s nothing wrong with our plan; we just overlooked a few points.”

After experiencing death once, Li Shiqing finally cleared up her dependence and began to seriously learn to fill in the gaps in Bespectacled Boy’s plan.

“First, in our plan, we underestimated the aunt’s ‘force’ and overestimated our own strength.”

The fundamental reason they chose the aunt and avoided the uncle was because they felt “the aunt was easier to target than the uncle.” Both Bespectacled Boy and she were intimidated by the muscular figure of the burly uncle. With this contrasting figure, they subconsciously assumed the frail housewife would be easier to deal with, subconsciously lowering their guard.

“Second, we misjudged the psychological state of the passengers on the bus.”

Thinking back to the crowd that hurriedly dispersed after hearing the cries of “Bomb!” and the despair of the aunt waving a bloody knife while no one dared to approach, and her desperate cries for help met with no response, Li Shiqing felt a pang of resentment.

After all, they weren’t just risking their lives for themselves but for everyone else on the bus.

But she also understood clearly that in this kind of situation, you can’t blame others for being afraid.

She was just an ordinary person. Could the other passengers be specially trained Terminators, ready to face bombs and criminals with equanimity?

Bespectacled Boy had clearly thought of this, sighed, and patted her shoulder in understanding.

“Emotions are contagious. When one person displays intense fear, everyone else becomes afraid. In a dangerous situation like that, no one wants to step forward and potentially be the first person to get stabbed.”

“If we were uniformed police officers, it would be fine, but the two of us…”

She looked from Bespectacled Boy to herself.

One was a young man with glasses and a scholarly air, and the other was a petite, delicate girl with a youthful face…

How many people would come to help someone like them if they shouted “Bomb”? They themselves seemed unreliable, so how could they give others the reassurance that “helping me will be okay”?

“If you help us without knowing anything, the risk is too great.”

Taking down a criminal with a knife or even a thug with a bomb was not the same as taking down Bespectacled Boy.

Bespectacled Boy exuded a harmless, gentlemanly air, while the woman with the knife was clearly not a normal person. In a confined environment like a train or bus, most people’s first reaction was to leave the unsafe “danger zone.”

It wasn’t just doing bad things that was a problem; doing good things was, too.

Li Shiqing recalled the scene of Bespectacled Boy being stabbed and the passengers panicking and trying to interfere with the driver’s driving. She continued, “Third, and this is what we should do most…”

She looked up and forward.

“…We should get the driver’s help.”

“Ask the driver for help?”

Bespectacled Boy was stunned, his mind subconsciously worried. “But in many previous cases, accidents have always been caused by the driver’s emotional instability. Isn’t the driver’s ability to react and control his emotions that strong?”

“Besides, if the driver knew there was danger in the bus, would he still be able to drive safely? What if the driver heard there was a bomb and stopped the bus and left us behind?”

He expressed his biggest concern.

“But you can’t deny that without the driver’s help, we might not reach our destination due to various mishaps, let alone drop the bomb.”

Li Shiqing wasn’t prepared to leave her life in the hands of the passengers. “Last time, we seized the pressure cooker and nearly succeeded, but that doesn’t mean we’ll be so successful every time. What if the elderly people in the bus panic and try to grab the driver’s steering wheel? What if they try to assault the driver and demand he stop, only to have something happen to them?”

“What if we’ve already seized the pressure cooker and secured the driver, but the driver, distracted by the panicked passengers, gets into an accident? Wouldn’t that be even worse? Who knows how this bomb detonates? Would a collision trigger an explosion? What if the previous accidents caused by crashing into the tanker were all accidental explosions?”

She kept raising questions, making her case.

“You have to admit it’s a possibility, right?”

Bespectacled Boy was a bit bewildered by Li Shiqing’s barrage of questions, but he wasn’t one to argue or get angry. Instead, he paused for a moment to reflect.

“You’re right.”

After some reflection, he had to admit that her scenario was indeed very likely to happen.

His suspicion of the driver stemmed from a subconscious distrust of strangers, leading him to simply chalk him up to a “risk factor” and minimize his involvement in his “plan.”

But as the situation gradually evolved, this “risk factor” became their best option for mitigating risk.

“We have to restrain the woman and keep her separated from the pressure cooker. Meanwhile, if we get the driver’s help and ensure he can get to a safe spot on the bridge, stop the bus, and open the door once the pressure cooker is snatched, the chaotic crowd can immediately get off, and we can quickly and safely throw the pressure cooker over the bridge.”

Unlike Bespectacled Boy, Li Shiqing often took this route, occasionally chatting with him in the front seat, and got to know the driver better.

“Besides, I don’t think he’d be the type to abandon a whole busload of passengers and run away.”

Bespectacled Boy looked at his companion, who analyzed the situation with such clarity that she seemed to have “stepped up a level,” and was speechless with shock.

“Alright, then, let’s do as you say!”

Bespectacled Boy checked the time, a familiar sense of urgency washing over him.

“What should we do first? Go to the driver?”

“No…”

Hearing the chime signaling the arrival of the next stop, Li Shiqing shook her head and looked at Bespectacled Boy.

“We should first find reliable help.”

The author has something to say:  Seeing so many readers questioning why no one on the bus tried to grab the knife or throw the bomb, I can only express my relief that you, as readers of mine, each possess such high moral standards. I greatly appreciate your questioning. But you’ve forgotten the premise of my writing about this bus, which underscores the entire book: there are almost no young people on board at that particular time. They’re either elderly men and women or idle middle-aged and elderly people. Should we use a cane to stop them? If something happens to a middle-aged person, what will happen to the whole family, with elderly parents and young children? Perhaps it’s because I’m old and can’t think passionately anymore… Every book in the “Kai” series tells the story of how “ordinary people” like us break free from the shackles of fate.

CONTENT END 25

chapters.title: The Nineteenth Cycle (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Old Jiao sat on the bus with vacant eyes, wondering where he could spend the night.

The construction site he had previously worked at had suffered a major accident, and work could no longer resume. Three months earlier, the foreman had paid them their last wages, leaving them to fend for themselves.

It was hard to find work in the city. He was already in his forties, and despite his strength, people preferred younger men. Not to mention that he was a bit slow in his words, and whenever the recruiters asked too many questions, he would stutter.

His fellow workers on the construction site felt that life in the city was too difficult. Some had already returned to their hometowns, while others urged him to go back and not waste his time in the city.

But if he returned home, he would have to farm. His wife had died early, and the family’s land was now entirely taken care of by the elderly. He also had a daughter who was still in school, and farming alone certainly wouldn’t be enough to support her college education.

They said children from poor families grew up early. His only daughter had been sensible and diligent since childhood. She now had good grades and attended a middle school in the county town. The only downside was that the child’s living expenses and accommodation were a significant expense for him. The family relied on him working outside the home to earn money, and this worry was always on his mind, fearing that the child would be delayed.

To prevent his daughter from dropping out of school, Lao Jiao gritted his teeth and persevered in the city. When his work housing closed, he rented a cheap garage for temporary shelter.

Local old houses sometimes rented out their garages as regular homes. While these garages lacked windows, they were large enough to fit a bed and a cabinet, and with the roller shutters closed, they became a self-contained, small room.

Garages were cold in the winter and hot in the summer, lacked ventilation, and lacked a private bathroom. Ordinary people wouldn’t rent them, but they were cheap, and there were always those who didn’t mind these difficulties to save money.

The “severance pay” offered by the foreman wasn’t much, and Lao Jiao figured every penny counted until he found a new job.

After over a month of job hunting, he’d worn out a pair of shoes and still hadn’t found a reliable job. Luckily, a former coworker at a construction site was delivering food, earning decently, and wanted to get Lao Jiao involved.

But delivering food would require buying an electric scooter and a decent phone that could install apps. Although his coworker offered to give him a discarded phone to use first, the electric scooter issue remained.

If he didn’t buy an electric scooter, he could rent one, but the monthly rental alone would be 500 yuan. If he didn’t make much money in the first few months, after deducting rent, food, and the scooter, he’d be lucky to break even. Even having money to send back home was a problem.

Lao Jiao’s previous jobs had provided food and lodging for free, requiring only physical effort. This was his first time taking on such a “big thing,” so he was inevitably hesitant.

As if to top it off, a garage recently caught fire, and the tenants inside were in trouble. Now, old neighborhoods across the city were filled with banners declaring, “Garages Cannot Be Rented” and “Living in Garages is Illegal.” His landlord, no longer willing to rent out the garage, refunded him this month’s rent and let him go.

Perhaps feeling bad, when telling Lao Jiao to leave, the landlord gave him his son’s old gym bag, asking him to pack up his belongings.

The burden of carrying large and small plastic bags made the scene even more desolate.

In reality, what possessions did someone like Lao Jiao have?

A few pieces of clothing, a few pairs of shoes, and whatever else he could fit into the bag—all packed to the brim—became his entire possessions.

Without arguing with the landlord, Lao Jiao accepted the several hundred yuan and walked out of the garage, carrying the old gym bag. A mixture of joy and worry filled his face.

Happy that the landlord had refunded him a few hundred yuan, which covered his first month’s delivery rental.

Worried that he was out of places to live again. If he rented another place, not only would he find it difficult to find such a good deal, but the few hundred yuan he had just received would have to be used as a deposit, and he wouldn’t be able to find work.

The labor company recruiting delivery drivers was in Jiangbei District. Lao Jiao hesitated for a moment, then grabbed all his belongings and boarded the bus to Jiangbei. He began to wonder whether he should sleep in a park or at the train station for the next few days.

“Or, if it’s sunny, I’ll sleep in the park; if it rains, at the train station…”

Old Jiao thought indifferently, “Both places have toilets and free water for washing. I’ll make do for a while. Once the delivery business picks up, I’ll find a proper place to stay.”

He was so lost in thought that he didn’t notice two young ones standing up from the bus, let alone one of them standing right in front of him.

When a large shadow appeared before him, he belatedly looked up and saw a young man wearing glasses.

Before he could say anything, Bespectacled Boy squatted down beside him and handed him a half-page slip of paper.

“I don’t…”

He had seen this kind of thing before; some were handing out flyers, others were selling things. Although this was his first encounter on the bus, he subconsciously assumed this guy was a “promoter” selling something.

But Bespectacled Boy in front of him made a “hush” gesture and held the slip of paper horizontally in front of him, beckoning him to read it. The scrap of paper was covered in neat, powerful handwriting, perfectly written and easy to read.

But the content was completely ridiculous.

[ Hello, I’m a plainclothes police officer. I’m on a bus to perform an official duty and need your assistance. The middle-aged woman in a patterned shirt in the back seat of the bus is carrying a bomb and a dangerous knife. She could detonate the bomb at any moment, endangering the safety of the passengers. I need your assistance. Please help me subdue her. ]

Old Jiao’s eyelids twitched uncontrollably when he saw this, and he looked at Bespectacled Boy in front of him with a strange expression.

“You…”

He pointed at the words “Plainclothes Police” on the scrap of paper, his face filled with suspicion. “Young man, are you kidding me?”

Think he was easy to fool just because he was from the countryside? Police officers now had to undergo a physical examination. This young man wore glasses and was so thin. How could he look like a plainclothes police officer?

This must be some new scam that was specifically targeting honest people!

Bespectacled Boy seemed to anticipate his suspicions, so he leaned over and whispered, “In your bag, there are two pairs of canvas shoes, an old blue towel, army green pants, several pairs of insoles, a stainless steel bowl and chopsticks wrapped in a red plastic bag, and, oh, and an unopened pack of tissue paper. It’s a knockoff of ‘Xin Xiang Yin’ (heart-to-heart seal), with the word ‘Xiang’ in the middle.”

With every word Bespectacled Boy spoke, the look of surprise on Old Jiao’s face grew more intense. Especially when he mentioned the word “Xin Xiang Yin,” he opened his bag in disbelief and began to rummage through it.

When he pulled the tissue paper out of his bag, he was stunned to see the words “Xin Xiang Yin” written in the middle.

He had hurriedly packed all these things that morning. He was so consumed by the devastating news of his impending lack of a place to live that his mind was completely blank. He had shoved many of the items in his bag without even looking at them.

For example, he had no idea whether the plastic bag wrapped around the rice bowl was red or white.

And then there was this “Xin Xiang Yin” tissue paper—he’d taken it home at the foreman’s farewell dinner, feeling it was a shame to leave it unopened. He’d never opened it.

It had been months; who would even remember the brand?

But this young man not only knew every item in his bag, but he could also accurately describe its contents. This was definitely not just luck.

Although the uncle looked strong and fierce, he was essentially a simple and honest person. Seeing this, his mind was filled with wild thoughts.

“I’ve heard there’s a type of police officer who specializes in technical matters, who can investigate anything, and who are all top students. Could this young man be one of those technical officers, scanning our luggage with something that can reveal what’s inside someone’s bag?”

The thought startled him again.

“It’s over! If they can find everyone’s belongings, is there really a bomb in this bus?”

The thought of a bomb in the bus nearly made Old Jiao jump out of his seat, his face paling.

“But, but do the police need the help of ordinary people to investigate a case?”

He mimicked Bespectacled Boy’s mysterious demeanor and lowered his voice, whispering in his ear, “Don’t you know to send more people up there?”

“We’re afraid of alerting the enemy…”

Bespectacled Boy smiled wryly and said, “So we’re shorthanded right now, so we can only ask the passengers for help.”

“So, what kind of help do they need?”

After Bespectacled Boy’s demonstration of his skills, Old Jiao subconsciously felt a sense of awe for Bespectacled Boy before him. “I don’t know anything!”

Bespectacled Boy smiled without saying anything and turned the piece of paper over.

There was writing on the back of the page, too.

[ The middle-aged woman in the back seat, wearing a flowery dress, is carrying a pressure cooker filled with explosives. If the valve is pulled, it will explode. We need you to help us restrain this woman. Grab her hands or arms and make sure she can’t touch anything. She’s also carrying a fruit knife, so it’s dangerous to subdue her. We must be extremely careful and not give her the opportunity to use a weapon. After we seize the pressure cooker, we’ll throw it out of the bus. ]

Old Jiao read this long passage with trepidation, staring at Bespectacled Boy’s glasses. He felt a chill run down his spine.

Joining the police in subduing a middle-aged woman wasn’t a big deal, but the problem was that this woman wasn’t just armed with a knife; she was also carrying a bomb!

There were so many people on the bus, and this young man came to him first. What right did he have to do that?!

“Uncle, please help me…”

Bespectacled Boy’s eyes were filled with pleading. “After all, this matter concerns the safety of everyone on the bus. There are so many people on this bus, young and old, and there aren’t many people like you who are both strong and reliable. After all, ahem… if something goes wrong, no one on the bus will be able to escape…”

“I—I don’t think I’m suitable. Can’t you find someone else?”

Old Jiao nervously rubbed his hands, awkwardly avoiding the “plainclothes officer’s” pleading gaze.

“It’s not that I don’t want to help. My parents are old, my wife died young, and we have a daughter who’s still in school. I’m the one who takes care of everything. What if something happens to me…”

With every word he spoke, the hopeful glint in Bespectacled Boy’s eyes dimmed a little, and even the way he squatted there took on a hint of pity.

“I understand…”

He slumped his shoulders like a dog being refused access, trying to persuade him. “You, you should reconsider. This is saving lives, a good thing…”

But as he spoke, he couldn’t continue.

It sounded easy to ask a man with elderly parents and young children, the pillar of his family, to risk his life to subdue a criminal, but the actual act felt like moral coercion.

Xiao Heyun was no saint, but looking at the old man’s washed-out coat and pants and his hesitant expression as he clutched his bag, he couldn’t bring himself to continue persuading him.

“Okay, I’ll look…”

He was about to stand up when someone held his shoulder.

“Young man, I heard there’s a bonus for ‘heroic acts,’ right?”

Old Jiao seemed to have suddenly remembered something, his eyes gleaming with eagerness. He tugged at Bespectacled Boy’s sleeve, a mixture of shame and embarrassment.

“Ah, there is…”

Bespectacled Boy seemed unprepared for Old Jiao’s question and was momentarily bewildered.

“How much? A thousand?”

Thinking of his impending homelessness, of the prospect of being forced to return to his hometown to farm if he couldn’t afford to rent an electric scooter and find a new job, Old Jiao felt a wave of desolation.

What was more terrifying than death was poverty.

Bespectacled Boy was visibly surprised to hear that Old Jiao wanted money, but he quickly came to his senses and pulled his wallet from his trouser pocket.

“Yes, yes. I’ll give you a thousand yuan right now.”

He quickly counted out ten red bills from his wallet and stuffed them into Lao Jiao’s hand.

Seeing the actual money in his hand, Lao Jiao gritted his teeth.

“Okay, I’ll help you!”

CONTENT END 26

chapters.title: The Nineteenth Cycle (Part 3)
chapters.content:
Bespectacled Boy and Li Shiqing needed help, and the most important choice before them was who to ask for help.

In this era of popular taxi apps, those who still rode the bus were either elderly men and women or young people with little money. A decent-earning office worker like Bespectacled Boy would take the bus simply because he was new to the place and wanted to get to know the city this way. Otherwise, he would have relied on taxis most of the time.

They couldn’t be too old. Once this criterion was set, half the passengers on the bus were unsuitable. Of the remaining passengers, those who could help must have: (1) the strength to subdue the others; (2) the courage to step forward; and most importantly, (3) they must be reliable and not suddenly fail at the last minute.

If they used these three criteria, there would be very few people who could be selected. After all, in every cycle, there were always people who panicked, people who looked on coldly, and people who shouted the loudest but moved the least.

For example, the uncle with the bunch of keys hanging from his waist always shouted the loudest and hid the furthest. Last time, he even led the way in clamoring to get off the bus.

If they asked him for help, he might shout loudly enough for everyone on the bus the moment they mentioned the bomb in the bus.

After considering various factors, Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy finally chose the muscular man and the masked man. The muscular man was the first choice, and the masked man was the backup. If both agreed, that would be best. If not, even if only one of them could help.

Bespectacled Boy then wrote a note, and Li Shiqing headed to the back to ask for help.

The man that Bespectacled Boy wanted to persuade was sitting close to the front, so to avoid others hearing too much, a combination of text and speech was the most convenient way to communicate.

But the masked man was different. He had chosen the most secluded seat in the back row. The bus was already noisy, and speaking in a low voice made it even harder for anyone to hear.
