Compared to Xiao Heyun’s polite demeanor, Li Shiqing was much more direct.

“Handsome man, I need a favor…”

Both young people, Li Shiqing chose to be direct with the masked man.

A guy who could save stray kittens must be a kind and compassionate person, right?

“What?”

The masked man, clutching his bag, looked warily at the girl who had inexplicably run up to him and called him “handsome.”

He was wrapped up so tightly, and he was still being called handsome?

If someone was being too attentive without any reason, they were either a traitor or a thief!

“Do you see that woman in the flowery dress up front? She has dangerous antisocial tendencies. Not only is she carrying a bomb in a pressure cooker, but she’s also carrying a knife…”

Li Shiqing, facing the masked man’s disdainful gaze, continued, “We’re going to subdue her later, but we’re shorthanded. I’m hoping you can help hold her down together.”

“Have you had too much to drink?”

The masked man subconsciously eyed the girl.

If she wasn’t drunk, why would she be spouting such nonsense?

“I know you won’t believe this, but it’s true. After we learned there was a bomb in this bus, we checked almost every suspect, including you…”

Li Shiqing didn’t directly say she was a “plainclothes police officer.” She explained vaguely, but her tone was forceful.

“The bag you’re holding contains a kitten, orange and white, wrapped in an army green jacket. It’s about a month old, its fur is very dirty, its eyes are large, and it looks listless from malnutrition.”

She spoke of the “secret” in the masked man’s bag, her face expressionless. “You know the bus doesn’t allow pets, and you were worried people would notice you have a cat and ask you to get off, so you hid it in your backpack. As soon as you got on, you found a seat in the last row to avoid being seen.”

Li Shiqing’s words were firm and decisive, with no hint of bluffing. The masked man’s eyes, visible from outside the mask, grew wider and wider.

“Are you investigating me?”

The masked man was a young man, his first concern being the “offense” he’d been subjected to. With an unpleasant look in his eyes, he accuses, “You’re violating citizens’ privacy!”

“We’re also working for public safety.”

Li Shiqing didn’t directly address the issue but continued to persuade him, “What we’re saying is true. The woman with the plastic bag has a pressure cooker that can explode, and she’s carrying a knife. If we can’t subdue her, everyone in the bus will be doomed! We need your help!”

If Li Shiqing hadn’t accurately described the contents of his bag, the masked man might have dismissed her as a liar or a lunatic. But she spoke with such certainty about the cat in his bag, so certain that she seemed to know exactly what he was feeling at the time. This made the situation seem a bit “weird.”

He cautiously leaned over to glance at the “target mission.” Seeing the woman was rather frail and seemingly harmless, he breathed a sigh of relief.

If the bus had been filled with thugs, he’d probably have been even more terrified.

“Is that okay?”

Li Shiqing pulled out her phone, checked the time, and saw two more minutes had passed. Her tone was a bit anxious.

“How did you know what we were carrying? Is it a superpower?”

Young people were more receptive to new things than older people. After this “sudden incident,” the masked man’s initial fear and surprise faded, and he even felt a subtle thrill. He pressed Li Shiqing:

“Is everything they say online true? Do we have any ‘superpower’ troops in our country?”

“…Handsome man, a bomb is about to be dropped on your face. Could you please be serious?”

Li Shiqing nearly lost her breath.

“Okay, okay…”

Having his “secret” known, the masked man’s grip on the cat bag unconsciously relaxed. He raised his head and asked, “What do you want me to do? Let me make it clear, I’m a weakling. I can’t do anything too difficult!”

Weakling?

Li Shiqing recalled how he had beaten Bespectacled Boy black and blue and couldn’t help but complain.

You’re so polite!

“You’re too modest! Our plan is this…”

She hurriedly told the masked man the plan she and Bespectacled Boy had laid out, then added, “…your mission is simple. Once things get chaotic, you’ll act accordingly. If my companions and I can’t control the woman, please help hold her down and prevent her from touching the pressure cooker. If my companions do subdue her, please keep an eye on the pressure cooker and don’t let anyone touch it until we throw it off the bridge.”

The masked man’s eyelids twitched at the thought of having to fight the knife-wielding woman and even watch over the explosive pressure cooker.

“My mom always told me to stay out of other people’s business and be careful not to get into trouble.”

The masked man touched his mask, his tone hesitant. “I’m wrapped up so tightly; the criminals shouldn’t recognize me, right? I won’t run into accomplices later, will I? I heard that these kinds of crimes aren’t usually committed alone. If there are accomplices, you have to ensure my safety…”

“They won’t recognize you.”

Li Shiqing was completely convinced. Why had she thought this masked man was kind of cool before?

“Just help control the situation.”

While she was communicating with the masked man, her attention remained focused on her companion out front, who was communicating with the man.

Bespectacled Boy pulled his wallet from his pocket, counted out a wad of bills, and gave it to the man. Then he stood up and gave himself an “OK” sign in the back row.

Convinced so quickly?

Did he pay someone for help?

At least, it was good to have a reliable helper.

Three people should be enough.

“Do you agree?”

She asked again.

This time, not only was her tone unusually serious, but her entire being exuded a stern, “I’m about to fight!” aura, which made the masked man pause in his attempt to ask more.

He discarded his chaotic thoughts, thought carefully for a moment, and shook his head.

“It’s too dangerous. I can’t agree.”

The masked man glanced at the woman again. “You said ‘we,’ which means there’s more than just you, right? She looks quite thin, so a few people should be enough to subdue her.”

What if the criminal was subdued, only to have a few more holes in his body? What a loss!

Perhaps feeling that this sounded too cowardly, he thought for a moment and added, “How about I help you keep an eye on the pressure cooker? I won’t let anyone else touch it.”

Li Shiqing had already given up hope, so the other party’s willingness to look after the pressure cooker was a pleasant surprise. She thanked him and told him that her “cough” was the signal to proceed.

After giving her instructions, she glanced out the window and saw that they were almost at the intersection with the tanker. She hurried back to the front of the bus.

As she passed her companion, she quietly gave an “OK” sign.

The driver’s face became bright.

“Uncle driver, watch out for the motorcycle on the right! They’re about to run a red light!”

After reminding the driver of the “dangerous factors,” Li Shiqing didn’t leave.

“That was a close call!”

Thanks to Li Shiqing’s prompting, the driver avoided another accident. He breathed a sigh of relief and turned to look at Li Shiqing. “You’re quite quick, little girl! I didn’t even notice.”

“I know a lot.”

Seeing the bus steadily driving along the road to the approach bridge, Li Shiqing smiled and feigned interest in driving. She stood beside the driver, bent down, and said softly,

“For example, I also know there’s a bomb in the bus.”

After hearing the girl’s words, the driver’s hands, which had been tightly gripping the steering wheel, trembled. He turned to look at her in disbelief.

“Uncle driver, don’t look at me; look at the road.”

Li Shiqing understood the uncle’s current panic. When they first learned there was a bomb in the bus, they had been much more panicked than the driver was now.

“Oh, oh…”

The uncle seemed still dazed. He gripped the steering wheel in a daze, trying to look back.

“Uncle, don’t look back. You might get spotted.”

Li Shiqing’s phone vibrated. It was Bespectacled Boy reminding her that it was time to act.

Time was pressing, so Li Shiqing could only give the driver a rough outline.

“Uncle, I know this sounds a bit unexpected, but there really is a bomb in the bus. It’s in the pressure cooker carried by the woman in the flowery dress in the back seat. We’ll subdue her later, but it’s not safe to leave the bomb there. I need you to drive onto the bridge and find a deserted spot so we can drop the bomb into the river.”

“When I yell, ‘Uncle, stop the bus, open the door, and let everyone out,’ okay?”

“Drive onto the bridge and stop?”

The driver, his face pale, repeated Li Shiqing’s request.

“Are you sure?”

“Yes, it might get a bit chaotic later. Driver, please be careful with the passengers. Don’t stop the bus until you’re on the bridge, or the woman in the flowery dress will see you, and the bomb might detonate prematurely…”

Li Shiqing said hurriedly. “Okay? Please, I ride in your bus often; I’m not some weirdo. Just trust me for once?”

The driver gripped the steering wheel tightly and glanced at her.

Perhaps because Li Shiqing’s expression was too serious, he hesitated but nodded.

Great!

Li Shiqing was shocked and coughed heavily.

Everything was ready; the operation officially began!

Hey, hey, hey, I just arrived in this city not long ago, so I keep some cash on me just in case. Author: (holding up the microphone) What do you think about the masked man’s belief that you have superpowers? Hey, he’s probably talking about the power of money… right?

CONTENT END 27

chapters.title: The Nineteenth Cycle (Part 4)
chapters.content:
From the very beginning, the greatest enemy facing Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun wasn’t the criminals or the bombs, but time.

Each cycle, from just a few minutes at the beginning to the thirty minutes before it finally stopped regressing, while the time Heaven gave the two young people to act gradually increased, the time they had to react was far too little.

Not to mention the many opportunities in the previous cycles, which were even wasted.

From the moment they realized they had to do something to resolve this, the two of them almost immediately reflected on their previous “mistakes,” constantly correcting and adjusting their strategies based on those errors and formulating new plans.

All their experience and plans were built on each mistake, often leaving them with little time to even think, let alone execute.

Sometimes, they regretted their actions later, but in retrospect, they realized that in the urgent circumstances at the time, they had no other choice but to take the action they did.

If they had waited until they’d considered the pros and cons and weighed the best course of action before making a move, the bus would have exploded long ago.

Before this, they’d already gone through the cycle eighteen times and died a dozen times. Each time, the process was brief, but these cycles and deaths weren’t entirely meaningless.

It was precisely with these countless failures as a foundation that the two young people had come up with their most detailed and well-thought-out plan.

Under the dread of not knowing if each cycle would be the last, Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun’s mental state reached its most perilous point. Now, only a positive outcome could bring them comfort.

While Li Shiqing was conversing with the driver, Xiao Heyun, having already convinced the older man, was like an athlete poised for the starting gun. A cough rang out, and he immediately stood up.

As he stood up, he could even feel the muscles in his arms aching slightly—from the sheer tension of clenching his fists, his arm muscles were stiff.

The uncle, who had been paying close attention to Bespectacled Boy, subconsciously touched the banknotes in the inner pocket of his clothes after he stood up. After making sure that the money would not fall out, he also stood up.

One of them was in the front of the bus, the other in the back. Aside from the masked man in the back row, no one noticed they both rose simultaneously until they both lunged at the same target…

The woman in the flowery dress!

This was the person who had caused these two so many deaths, so many beatings, and so much suffering. Even the mildest-tempered young man would be filled with negativity when facing her, let alone show mercy. He would pull her out with the utmost force.

The woman’s reaction was undeniably quick. The moment Bespectacled Boy touched her, she tried to reach for her plastic bag. Unfortunately, everyone knew what was inside and was well-prepared for her. They wouldn’t let her touch anything, not even move.

So, when she was pulled out unexpectedly, before she could even scream in pain, another pair of large hands grabbed her wrists tightly.

The muscular uncle took action!

The uncle was a sturdy man who’d earned his living by hard labor. He could carry hundreds of pounds up the stairs without even taking a breath. At this moment, restraining the middle-aged woman was a piece of cake for him. His only concern was the knife she carried.

The thought of the knife in her possession made the uncle’s grip on her wrist even tighter.

“Ah!”

Feeling her arm as if it were clamped in a vise, unable to move, and a piercing pain piercing her wrist, the woman’s eyes flashed with ferocity, and she kicked the muscular man in front of her like crazy.

Faced with such ferocious resistance, the uncle couldn’t control her effectively. He simply dragged her to the front of the bus and, like he had with Bespectacled Boy, delivered a powerful kick to her calf, pinning her to the ground.

The commotion was so loud that everyone in the bus was stunned. Coupled with the man’s formidable appearance and muscular build, some instinctively pulled out their phones, ready to call the police.

Li Shiqing was a girl, and she had previously suffered a painful lesson from the aunt, leaving a psychological scar. Therefore, for both her physical and psychological safety, Xiao Heyun did not intend for her to directly participate in subduing the aunt during this operation.

Her assigned task was to calm the passengers and maintain constant communication with the driver to facilitate coordination.

In their plan, if the driver cooperated, they could even skip the safety hammer and break the window. As soon as the bus came to a complete stop, they could simply rush out with the pot and throw it into the river. This eliminated a step and countless variables.

“Police investigation, don’t be afraid!”

As soon as Li Shiqing noticed the passenger’s mood change, she shouted, “This person is mentally ill, carrying a knife, and is dangerous. Stay away from her.”

As she spoke, she had already crouched beside the aunt and searched her body thoroughly. Sure enough, she found a sharpened knife in her coat pocket.

When the knife was found in front of everyone, even the most nosy passengers fell silent, not daring to say another word. They all remained seated, completely silent. There was no trace of the panicked, frantic rushing around like last time.

The woman pinned to the ground, a look of despair at the words “police investigation,” became even more frantic after the knife was found.

Not only did she struggle desperately, despite the pressure the man exerted on her, but she also let out hysterical screams.

“Wang Xingde, you bastard! You will die a horrible death, and even as a ghost I won’t let you go!”

She cursed, trying to grab and attack anything she could reach, her voice emitting terrifying screams. She looked less like a human being and more like a zombie-like infected person in a movie, as if anything she touched would be horrible.

Seeing the woman being held down by the “police” going berserk, the previously silent passengers all began to believe Li Shiqing’s reasons. Some, seeing the “madwoman” subdued, relaxed their previously tense moods and even took to watching the scene, not only pointing and talking about the woman on the ground, but some even pulled their phones out of their pockets and started snapping away.

At this point, Li Shiqing and the others couldn’t care less about what the other passengers were doing; they just stared nervously out the bus.

“Driver, faster!”

When they realized the bus had smoothly driven onto the bridge and was heading towards the widest section of the river, Li Shiqing shouted anxiously, “The woman has been apprehended. Wait, see where there are fewer people and stop!”

Hearing Li Shiqing’s words, the woman struggling frantically on the ground raised her head and glared at her. Her gaze was piercing, and the hatred within was so thick that even the blind could sense it.

Under such hostile gazes, Li Shiqing, who had been calmly controlling the passengers’ emotions, felt a chill run down her spine. Instinctively, she rubbed her neck and took a half step back.

“Help me! I can’t hold her back!”

Under the woman’s almost self-harming resistance, the man quickly felt the pressure and began to call for help. “She’s struggling so hard!”

Seeing the woman’s violent struggles, Bespectacled Boy, who had been carefully guarding the pressure cooker, quickly called out to the masked man.

The masked man, relieved to see the situation under control, thought he could just watch the show. Suddenly, he heard the man with glasses yell, “Mask-wearing man, help me!” Fearfully, he put down his bag and tremblingly took the pressure cooker.

He didn’t dare hold the pressure cooker either, so he placed it on the ground, staring intently at it, as if it could take off.

On the entire bus, apart from the four of them, no one knew what was inside the pressure cooker, so naturally, there was no panic.

At Li Shiqing’s urging, the bus accelerated and drove steadily towards the center of the bridge. Everything went in an orderly manner as planned, so smoothly that it seemed like a dream.

“Uncle, stop the bus! There’s a traffic jam ahead. Let’s get off here!”

Li Shiqing saw the traffic ahead starting to pick up and quickly warned him.

The driver, hearing her urging, slammed on the brakes, slowly slowing down.

“Xiao Heyun, I’ll get off to drop off that thing!”

Li Shiqing ran to the masked man and snatched up the pressure cooker from the ground.

“Please keep an eye on it. Thank you.”

Fearing the woman might cause trouble again or drag another innocent person into a cycle, she decided to get off alone.

Xiao Heyun, upon hearing Li Shiqing’s words, understood her concerns and subconsciously felt a sense of unease.

Because things were going so smoothly, he worried things wouldn’t end so easily. He specifically warned his companion, “Be careful when you get out of the bus! Be careful not to get hit by passing cars!”

Just as he finished speaking, Li Shiqing still had a “hmm” in her mouth when the woman pinned to the ground suddenly let out a shrill howl, as if provoked by something.

The howl was so terrifying it didn’t even sound human.

Li Shiqing, already carrying the pressure cooker to the rear door, was so startled by the sound that she almost dropped the handle.

She bit her lower lip hard, using the pain to distract herself from the woman.

The bus had come to a complete stop.

“Driver, open the door!”

Composing herself, Li Shiqing took a deep breath and called out to the driver.

The woman pinned to the ground stopped howling and began to sob loudly.

The cry was filled with sorrow and pain, as if it contained the greatest sorrow and suffering in the world. It filled everyone with panic and unbearable pain.

Many passengers who had been snapping away were overwhelmed by this desolation. With complicated expressions, they put down their phones and stopped pointing at the person on the ground.

Only Li Shiqing remained unmoved, staring intently at the pressure cooker in her hand.

“Uncle, open the door!”

She urged again.

The bus stopped, but the door didn’t open.

Now, the people pinning the woman down began to sense something was amiss.

“Uncle driver, open the door!”

Bespectacled Boy yelled passionately.

“What’s going on? Didn’t you discuss this? Damn it!”

The masked man, realizing what was inside the pressure cooker, panicked and rushed to the door, yanking it open.

“Uncle?!”

Li Shiqing’s arms were beginning to ache from carrying the heavy pressure cooker.

An incredible thought suddenly flashed through her mind, and she abruptly turned to look at the driver.

The driver, having parked the bus, lifted his hands from the steering wheel. Amidst the woman’s grief-stricken sobs, he slumped back in his seat and let out a long sigh.

“Xiao Heyun, think of a solution!”

Li Shiqing’s anxiety over this incident brought tears to her eyes. She had only her companion to lean on.

“Hold her down!”

She didn’t need to ask for help; Bespectacled Boy had already let go of the woman’s hand, stood up, and rushed to the nearest safety hammer.

The other passengers in the bus, confused as to what was happening, looked at each other, afraid to speak.

Just then, the familiar Canon alarm rang out once more.

They hadn’t heard that terrifying ringing for so many times and had even subconsciously ignored it. But the ringing sound was like a curse. The second it rang, it rekindled Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun’s deepest fears.

Li Shiqing’s scalp tingled, and she felt as if she had fallen into an icy cave in the coldest days of winter, her whole body shivering with cold.

“No!”

The familiar pain, in a way she least wanted to accept…

came upon her again.

CONTENT END 28

chapters.title: The Twentieth Cycle (Part 1)
chapters.content:
“F—k, just one step away!”

Even Bespectacled Boy, who had always behaved so gentlemanly, couldn’t help but curse when he woke up again.

“So that ringing sound was a timer? Or a detonator?”

The feeling of failing so hard at the last minute was too awful. Bespectacled Boy couldn’t accept it.

Li Shiqing’s situation wasn’t much better.

Just like Bespectacled Boy’s previous experience, the pressure cooker exploded while she was holding it. The explosion destroyed her instantly, and when she regained consciousness, she could no longer feel her hands.

But even more unbearable than the physical pain she endured was the driver’s sudden change of heart at the end of the previous cycle.

Li Shiqing never doubted the driver, not even once.

She wasn’t from this city, having come here alone to attend school. To save some pocket money, like most college students, she usually took the bus.

Her family had a car, and before college, her parents usually drove her to distant destinations, while she walked or rode her bike for shorter trips.

Learning to ride the bus and understand bus routes wasn’t something she learned until she arrived in the city.

Because her school was on this route, she took the Bus 45 the most, and the driver she met the most on it was this driver.

When she first learned to ride the bus, she encountered numerous problems. Sometimes she missed her stop, sometimes she rode the wrong way, sometimes she kindly offered her seat to an elderly person only to have it snatched by a younger person…

Many times, it was only with the patient help of this kind driver that she successfully reached her destination.

It was this driver who made her fall in love with this city’s human touch and with riding its buses.

Unlike the lifeless subway or the monotonous taxi ride, riding the bus offered so much more.

She loved the low fares and the bright and clean windows from which she could gaze out at the city’s scenery, and she loved exploring every inch of the city in this manner.

She liked listening to the locals chatting loudly in their local dialect about everyday happenings on the bus, enjoyed the fleeting encounters with strangers as people boarded and alighted, and appreciated spending those simple, yet vibrant, few dozen minutes on the bus with so many different people.

Every time she boarded the bus, if it wasn’t too crowded, she liked to sit behind the driver, occasionally chatting with him. Sometimes, she didn’t even need to speak; just sitting behind him made her feel at ease.

As long as she politely asked the driver for help when boarding, she never had to worry about missing her stop.

Although Li Shiqing never told the driver, she was deeply grateful to him in her heart and always wanted to say “thank you.”

She was grateful for his kind guidance and selfless help when she first arrived in the city and felt lost and helpless.

And she was grateful for his reminders before each stop and for his protection when there were any conflicts with other passengers.

When the “bus loop” incident started, she tried to get the driver to stop the bus and to turn around and even created various scenarios to persuade him, but every time, the driver insisted on taking the passengers to their stops and drove away.

At that time, she even worried about his excessive “professionalism.”

Her companion had questioned the driver.

As soon as the incident happened, he subtly asked if the driver’s mental state wasn’t good, which caused the accident.

—That time, she explained to him and dispelled his doubts;

He questioned whether the driver might abandon all the passengers and escape or simply not believe their words.

—She firmly refuted his speculation, even saying, “He’s not that kind of person.” It was because of her blind trust in the older man and her overconfidence in her own judgment that she insisted on choosing this “easiest” way to “get through this situation”…

But in the end, all her efforts were in vain.

The driver wasn’t the kind of person who would abandon everyone and run away; what he wanted… was for no one to be able to get off the bus.

“Why would this happen…” Li Shiqing was filled with disbelief and doubt, muttering to herself, “…Why would the driver do this?”

No matter how she thought about it, she couldn’t connect the vicious “criminal” with the kind and friendly driver.

“Regardless of why, we can now be certain that the driver and the hysterical woman are accomplices. The name ‘Wang Xingde’ that the woman kept shouting hysterically might be the driver’s name…”

The sudden twist of events at the last minute left Bespectacled Boy feeling terrible, but fortunately, he didn’t know the driver, so he wasn’t too affected.

“They probably knew each other beforehand; he was probably also aware of the explosion.”

“They must have had their reasons…”

Li Shiqing murmured to herself.

She remembered the last look the man gave her.

That look was too complex; it seemed like he had so many things to say, but in the end, he could only remain silent.

She was too young and inexperienced to understand the meaning of that look, but she could see the deep guilt and pain in his eyes.

That wasn’t the kind of look a “criminal” who wanted to take everyone down with him would have.

“Whatever the reasons, with this unexpected turn of events, the plan has to change…”

Bespectacled Boy took off his glasses, rubbing his throbbing forehead irritably, and said somewhat impatiently. He had made so many plans, but he had never included the “driver” or “other people” in them.

In his view, everyone except himself and Li Shiqing was an uncontrollable factor; in his plans, everything and everyone besides the two of them was considered a “risk.”

Where there was risk, there was uncertainty. He never trusted his life to others, so his plans were never about “asking for help” but about “self-reliance.”

But Li Shiqing was different.Having never left school and having received so much kindness from others during her upbringing, she always trusted people with the utmost good faith. When faced with problems, her instinctive reaction was to seek help.

Her decision to call the police, even in such a time-sensitive situation, demonstrated this character trait.

This character trait wasn’t necessarily bad; at least she never failed him at critical moments, and she always maintained a positive and optimistic attitude and unwavering resilience.

This attitude had also influenced him, preventing him from collapsing under the weight of such a terrible situation, and instead, he worked with her to find a solution.

But now, because of this very character trait, the driver’s “betrayal” had dealt her a devastating blow.

“It’s all my fault; it was my suggestion that went wrong…”

Li Shiqing lowered her eyes and apologized softly.

“It’s not your fault. At least with the help of the uncle and the masked man, we could easily subdue the woman. It’s just that no one expected the driver wouldn’t open the door. And if the driver was an accomplice, we really had no chance. Even if we controlled the woman, as long as he didn’t get out of the bus, he could easily cause an accident.”

Thinking that the driver and the woman were probably working together, Bespectacled Boy felt a heavy burden on his heart. “Ugh, the driver is an accomplice too! This makes solving this problem so much harder…”

None of them knew how to drive, and if the driver deliberately wanted to cause an accident, there were countless ways he could kill everyone on board.

Not to mention, the bomb could be detonated in ways other than just by pulling the pressure valve.

“And that bomb—we already know of two ways to detonate it.”

In the previous cycle, they had the woman and the pressure cooker under control, but the pressure cooker still exploded.

Although he didn’t have time to check his phone, Bespectacled Boy was 80% certain the bomb’s timer was set for 1:45 p.m.

“So that ringtone was indeed a timer…”

Manual detonation and timed detonation—those were two possible scenarios.

If the timer was a cellphone, and the driver could also detonate it by making a phone call, then there were three possible scenarios…

This was a hopeless situation no matter how one considered it.

“Uncle has been driving this route for years. Why would he do this?”

Li Shiqing was still obsessed with the previous cycle, mumbling to herself, unable to get out of it.

“What’s the relationship between uncle and aunt? Why did they set this bombing? Why always at 1:45 p.m.? Why set it to go off at 1:45 p.m.?”

“Let’s calm down first and then come up with a proper plan.”

Bespectacled Boy, concerned about Li Shiqing’s mental state, reached out to touch her forehead, but Li Shiqing pushed his arm away.

“Don’t dwell on it. Since the driver was the auntie’s accomplice, they were just on the same side.”

“You don’t understand!”

Li Shiqing suddenly became agitated, her voice rising an octave.

Seeing the other passengers’ attention drawn to her sudden cry, Li Shiqing regained control, but her expression remained stubborn.

“You’ve never met the driver, so you don’t understand. He and the auntie are completely different!”

Though she lowered her voice, she couldn’t conceal the emotion in her tone. “When the auntie killed me, I felt no emotion from her at all. She was like a heartless killing machine. But the uncle is different…”

Li Shiqing recalled the look from the driver uncle.

“I can sense the uncle is in pain. He must desperately want help!”

She grabbed her companion’s hand and pleaded, “He might have some reason for doing this! What if his family was coerced? What if someone else has evidence that forces him to comply? If we can find the reason and dispel his doubts, maybe he’ll abandon this terrible plan and help us?”

“But he didn’t even open the door…”

“But he told me to get out! He told us to get out!”

Li Shiqing growled uncontrollably, tears finally streaming.

“If the driver wanted to take everyone with him to their deaths, then why were we able to get out?!”

Even if there were perverts on the bus, he would have chosen to perish with everyone else. Why would he let them off mid-trip?

Xiao Heyun was stunned.

Before this, he had never considered this question.

“You’re right…”

Bespectacled Boy sighed softly and wiped the tears from Li Shiqing’s face with his thumb.

“In that case, let’s get off the bus.”

“Huh?”

Li Shiqing looked at him blankly, hearing the familiar station announcement.

“Don’t you want to find out the truth?”

Bespectacled Boy took Li Shiqing’s hand and led her to the back door.

The bus stopped at the Yanjiang East Road stop and slowly opened the door.

“Then let’s get off the bus!”

chapters.content:
“F—k, just that little bit!”

Even Bespectacled Boy, who had always acted so gentlemanly, couldn’t help but curse when he woke up again.

“So that ringing sound was a timer? Or some kind of detonation method?”

The feeling of failing so close to the finish line was awful; even the usually calm Bespectacled Boy couldn’t accept it.

Li Shiqing’s situation wasn’t much better.

Just like him before, this time the pressure cooker exploded while she was holding it. The explosion destroyed her instantly. When she regained consciousness, she couldn’t even feel her hands.

But even more unbearable than the physical pain she endured was the driver’s sudden mutiny.

Li Shiqing never doubted the driver, not even once.

She wasn’t from this city, having come here alone to attend school. To save more pocket money, like most college students, she usually took the bus.

Her family had a car, and before college, her parents usually drove her to distant destinations, while for shorter distances, she walked or rode her bike.

Learning to ride the bus and understand bus routes wasn’t something she learned until she arrived in the city.

Because her school was on this route, she took Bus 45 the most, and the driver she encountered most often on that bus was this driver.

When she first started learning to ride the bus, she encountered all sorts of problems: sometimes she missed her stop, sometimes she took the wrong direction, sometimes she kindly offered her seat to an elderly person only to have it taken by a younger person…

Many times, it was only with the patient help of this kind driver that she was able to successfully reach her destination.

Unlike the lifeless subway and the monotonous, boring taxi rides, the bus offered so much joy.

She loved the low fares, the bright, clean windows, the view of the city outside, and this way of capturing every inch of the city.

She loved listening to the locals chat loudly in their dialect, the fleeting encounters between people as they boarded and alighted, and the simple yet vibrant minutes spent with so many different people.

Every time she boarded the bus, as long as it wasn’t crowded, she liked to sit behind the driver, chatting with him from time to time. Sometimes, even without saying a word, she felt at ease just sitting behind him.

As long as she smiled and pleaded with the driver when boarding, she never had to worry about missing her stop.

Although Li Shiqing had never spoken of her feelings to the driver, she was deeply grateful for his kindness and always wanted to say “thank you.” She was grateful for his kind guidance and generous help when she first arrived in this city and felt helpless.

She was also grateful for his constant reminders before arriving at the bus stop and his support during conflicts.

When the “bus loop” incident began, she tried to get the driver to stop and turn around and even staged various incidents to persuade him, but he always insisted on taking the passengers to the stop and drove away.

At that time, she was still troubled by his excessive “professionalism.”

Her companion had questioned the driver.

As soon as the incident happened, he indirectly asked if the driver was mentally ill and if that was why the accident happened.

—That time, it was she who explained things to him and dispelled his doubts.

He had questioned whether the driver might abandon a busload of passengers or simply didn’t believe their words.

—It was she who firmly rejected his suspicions, even saying, “He’s not that kind of person.”

It was because of her blind trust in the man and her overconfidence in her own judgment that she had stubbornly chosen what she considered the “least challenging” “way to clear the gate”…

But her efforts ultimately failed.

The driver certainly wasn’t the type to abandon a whole busload of people and flee. He wanted… no one to get out.

“Why would this happen…” Li Shiqing muttered to herself, lost in deep disbelief and suspicion. “…Why would the driver do this?!”

No matter how hard she tried, she couldn’t connect the vicious “criminal” with the kind and friendly driver.

“Whatever the reason, it’s now certain that the driver and the frantic woman are in cahoots. The ‘Wang Xingde’ the woman had been screaming hysterically earlier might have been the driver’s name…”

A sudden twist occurred at the last moment, leaving Bespectacled Boy feeling gloomy. But thankfully, he didn’t know the driver to begin with, so he wasn’t too upset.

“What should we do? There are only two of us, and we have to subdue two?”

“Then try again!”

After the initial shock and disbelief wore off, this near-miss only fueled Li Shiqing’s fighting spirit.

Compared to being stabbed by a vicious woman, the feeling of being betrayed by someone you trusted so deeply was even more infuriating.

“The driver is at fault too. Let’s subdue him too! If he won’t open the door for us, we’ll find a way to open it ourselves! If one or two can’t help, then three, four, or five!”

Li Shiqing’s eyes seemed to be blazing with fire.

“I just can’t believe it! I know who the real culprit is, where the bomb is, and how it went off, and we still can’t find a solution!”

Li Shiqing was truly terrifying like this. Her whole body exuded an aura of “Don’t mess with me!” She was so gloomy that even Bespectacled Boy felt a sinking feeling in his heart for no apparent reason.

But now the arrow was on the string, and it had to be released. For a moment, Bespectacled Boy couldn’t think of a better way to control both the driver and the woman, so he followed Li Shiqing’s idea and tried again.

Just like last time, they each took a note and persuaded others to help. This time, they also had to subdue the “driver,” so relying solely on the masked man and the uncle with the bag wasn’t enough. Since the bus was mostly filled with the elderly, the weak, and the disabled, they had no choice but to turn to another younger, middle-aged man, “Uncle Key,” hoping for his help.

Uncle Key, after reading the note, not only did he not agree to help, but he also ran off the bus in a panic at the next stop, Yanjiang East Road.

“…What should we do?”

Bespectacled Boy, who had already successfully persuaded the uncle with the bag and the masked man, was dumbfounded. “Next time, won’t we have another ‘companion’?”

“Can a coward like that be called a companion?”

After repeated failures, Li Shiqing was completely consumed by anger and resentment. Hearing Bespectacled Boy’s words, she burst into laughter. “People like Uncle Key are just a ‘burden,’ right?”

At this point, she and Bespectacled Boy were lucky enough not to go crazy. They were still concerned about saving people; they could be considered saints.

Li Shiqing watched indifferently as Uncle Key scurried out of the bus, her eyes cold.

He had chosen to get out of the bus on his own initiative. Even if he had entered the cycle, they couldn’t be blamed.

—They hadn’t dragged him into this hellish situation; it was entirely his own choice.

Unable to find any other reliable help, and with time running out, the two could only grit their teeth and, using their previous method, successfully subdued the woman.

However, at the moment when Bespectacled Boy broke the window with the safety hammer, the aunt who was pinned to the ground screamed. Li Shiqing had already prepared to pounce on the uncle driver, but she was not faster than the driver.

The driver immediately stepped on the accelerator, crashing straight off the river bridge.

The pressure cooker exploded violently the moment the bus hit the water.

Upon waking up again, Li Shiqing took a deep breath, her first act being to go check on Uncle Key, who had gotten off the bus.

In the new cycle, the man sat quietly in the bus, with none of the panic he’d shown in the previous cycle, nor was he aware of the bomb aboard.

“Uncle Key got off the bus last time, too. Why didn’t he enter the cycle?”

After the severe headache subsided, Bespectacled Boy began to examine the man, wondering, “Couldn’t getting off the bus be the reason for entering the cycle?”

“Don’t think about it. There’s no time. Now’s not the time to dwell on this!”

Li Shiqing silently averted her gaze, unable to tell whether she felt relieved or a little disappointed.

“Since there’s no need to worry about anyone getting caught in the loop, let’s try getting a few more people to help!”

This time, they showed the note to every passenger on the bus. It didn’t matter how many people could help, as long as one more person could help; one more person meant more strength.

However, this time, even more passengers got off at Yanjiang East Road Station.

Old men and women, who had staggered unsteadily upon boarding, sprinted away without a glance back. The key-carrying uncle even pushed down a gray-haired old man as he got off, completely lacking the righteous demeanor he had displayed when he’d previously “taken down” Bespectacled Boy.

In a blink of an eye, only a handful of passengers remained.

Li Shiqing’s face darkened horribly.

But one passenger, for some unknown reason, simply left without a second thought. As he was about to get off, he even shouted into the bus:

“Run! There’s a psycho with a knife on the bus!”

So this loop was the shortest they’d ever experienced. Almost as soon as he finished shouting, the bomb in the bus exploded.

.

Waking up from the loop again, the two of them couldn’t even muster the energy to “work.”

“What do you think we’re working so hard for?”

Thinking of the inexplicable “sudden death” in the previous loop, Bespectacled Boy said wearily, “Not only are we toiling away, but we’ve also died over and over again. Aside from a paid helper and a hesitant masked man, not a single passenger dared risk helping. Not only did they refuse to help, but they also held us back…”

“Then we don’t want their help.”

Li Shiqing gritted her teeth, her face cold. “We don’t want those old men and women to help us. We’ll call the police.”

This time, they called the police right from the start.

But time was so tight that even if the police had arrived as soon as they received the alarm, they wouldn’t have been able to disguise themselves as ordinary people and board the bus at the last stop. They could only set up a checkpoint and close the bridge midway to evacuate passing vehicles and prevent further casualties.

Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy had no idea that their call to the police would ultimately result in the bus being found alone on the deserted road…

Seeing the road leading to the bridge blocked by a roadblock, the woman in the bus let out a strange laugh and opened the pressure relief valve.

“It’s no use dying all the time…”

After dying several times, Bespectacled Boy regained consciousness and stopped Li Shiqing from “robotically saving and reloading.”

“We can’t stop both the uncle driver and the aunt at the same time. Why don’t we try to ‘take them down one by one’?”

“Take them down one by one?”

After so many attempts with no results, everything seemed back to square one. Li Shiqing was exhausted, and even when Bespectacled Boy proposed a new plan, she couldn’t muster any energy.

“Didn’t you say you know the driver well? Why don’t you go and test him to see if there’s any way to ‘turn him over’?”

Bespectacled Boy had resorted to this “stopgap measure” out of desperation.

He pushed his glasses.

“This uncle driver has been running this route for so long. There must be a reason he’s helping the aunt to do this, right? Maybe he’s being coerced, maybe she’s got something on her hands, or maybe it’s an emotional entanglement. If we figure out the source and resolve the issue, maybe we can win the driver over.”

To be honest, Li Shiqing felt resentful of the uncle’s “betrayal.”

But deep down, she also harbored a faint hope, hoping the uncle had his reasons for doing this, rather than simply being a bad person.

Li Shiqing still remembered the uncle’s glance.

A man with that look of guilt and pain couldn’t be a cold-blooded killing machine.

After hesitating for a moment, Li Shiqing looked at the uncle driving ahead and gritted her teeth.

“Okay!”

She pretended to stretch in the bus, then quietly walked over to the driver’s side and began her own probing.

“Uncle, didn’t you sleep well last night?”

Li Shiqing said, feigning a joke. “You seem rather listless today.”

“Huh?”

The driver glanced at her, uncharacteristically silent.

The conversation stalled at the outset, but Li Shiqing remained undeterred, probing further. “Uncle, you must be tired from driving all day. How do you get lunch? Do you go home for lunch?”

“Just something to eat on my own,” the driver said casually.

“Huh? No one’s bringing you lunch? I thought you all had someone bringing you lunch. Don’t your wife and children help with that?”

Li Shiqing wanted to start by discussing his family situation.

After all, the most common scenario for coercion was a family member being kidnapped.

However, the conversation stalled again. The driver fell silent upon hearing Li Shiqing’s words, clearly distracted.

“Uncle driver…”

Li Shiqing was about to ask more when, out of the corner of her eye, she saw a tanker approaching. Her expression suddenly changed.

“Uncle driver, uncle, watch out for the truck ahead!”

Bang!

The moment the bus collided with the truck, a scorching wave of air swept over everyone.

.

“He didn’t respond to my words.”

Waking up again, Li Shiqing looked out the window and felt the urge to simply crash into it.

“Every time I brought up a crucial issue, he remained silent.”

She really didn’t want to continue.

Let it be. Whatever happened, it was a broken jar. After all, there wasn’t anything worth saving on this bus.

From her initial naiveté to her subsequent guilt and sense of responsibility towards Bespectacled Boy, to the excitement of gradually perfecting her plan, and finally to her relentless determination to persevere, Li Shiqing felt as if she had burned out all the passion, perseverance, and enthusiasm she could ever possess.

But even at this point, there was still no way out.

How could one control a driver who was driving?

His feet were on the accelerator and brake, and his hands were on the steering wheel. The bus door was hydraulic and pneumatic; if he didn’t open it, they couldn’t open it, no matter how hard they tried.

The masked man had tried it using the emergency door opening device at the time the bus exploded after being “betrayed” by the driver; it was completely broken.

The lives of everyone in the bus were already in the driver’s hands, not to mention the terrifying woman with a bomb in her arms threatening him.

Bespectacled Boy was exhausted, his head pounding. All his plans were a mess, and he couldn’t even think clearly.

The two exhausted young people slumped in their seats, like two salted fish thrown into a bus.

After a moment of slumping, the familiar announcement of “Yanjiang East Road Station” reached their ears.

“Never mind, let’s get off the bus!”

Bespectacled Boy wiped his face and jumped to his feet.

Under Li Shiqing’s sullen gaze, Bespectacled Boy pulled his companion to his side.

“Since we can’t break the situation on the bus, let’s get off and find a way!”

He led Li Shiqing to the back door, tightly gripping her wrist.

“Forget about it for now; let’s get off the bus and relax!”

CONTENT END 30

chapters.title: The Twentieth Cycle (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Taking Li Shiqing off the bus was a desperate move.

Neither of them could drive, and subduing an elderly woman armed with a weapon and explosives required help. Add to that the fact that the bus driver was already moving and there was nothing they could do to stop the situation. Any rash action could easily trigger an overreaction from the driver.

Not to mention that after their initial failure, both Li Shiqing and he were beginning to feel a bit fed up. As the saying goes, “One push is enough, the second weakens, the third exhausts.” If they kept pushing on, they might both go crazy on the bus.

No matter how they thought about it, they had already done everything they could on the bus, and now they had encountered a new obstacle that they couldn’t overcome. It seemed like a dead end. They might as well get off and search for some useful information.

After getting off, the two of them stared at the bus as it gradually receded. Not only did they not feel relieved at all, but on the contrary, their hearts were so heavy that they were speechless.

“Call the police?”

Watching the bus go away, Li Shiqing chose to talk to his companion first.

“You’re already exhausted. Let’s take a breath.”

Bespectacled Boy patted Li Shiqing’s shoulder. “If something happens on the bus, the police might call us. We’ll cooperate with the investigation then.”

He had always been worried about Li Shiqing’s mental state, especially after the uncle’s “betrayal.” “Let’s go.”

After discussing it, the two decided to go back to the park they’d been to last time.

After finding a pavilion to sit down, Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy, without prior agreement, both pulled out their phones.

Realizing they shared the same idea, they exchanged a smile.

“You check what happened on the bridge at 1:45 p.m., and I’ll check if there were any accidents on Bus 45.”

Bespectacled Boy asked his companion, “A middle-aged housewife seeking revenge, if it’s not something to do with her children, then it’s probably a romantic relationship. Let’s investigate that direction. If the uncle was coerced, he and the aunt probably have some connection in real life.”

“Okay.”

Li Shiqing opened the search engine on her phone.

For the next few minutes, the two of them didn’t talk much, just quietly searching for news and information, occasionally discussing it.

“Look at this. Bus 45 is considered by locals to be the most prone to problems. There’s been a lot of trouble, all because of the bridge across the river…”

Bespectacled Boy showed Li Shiqing a post on a local forum complaining, “If you miss your stop, the round trip is delayed forty minutes. People often miss their stop and then clamor to get off.”

Li Shiqing, having ridden this route for years, was well aware of the situation and nodded. “That’s true. Then it would be difficult to investigate Bus 45.”

If there were a lot of people online complaining about this route, there would be an explosion of useless information.

“Could it be this? A theft on Bus 45?”

Bespectacled Boy muttered to himself, looking at his phone.

But he quickly dismissed his suspicions.

“Oh, so it’s phone theft? That’s pretty common. It shouldn’t be…”

Elsewhere, Li Shiqing’s search for “1:45 p.m.” wasn’t yielding many results. The cross-river bridge that Bus 45 crosses connected two important areas of the city, with a massive amount of traffic. Consequently, there were numerous accidents every year, both major and minor. The total volume was a terrifying amount, and even fewer mention specific dates.

On a larger scale, there were pileups and trucks colliding with cars and catching fire. On a smaller scale, there were simple scrapes that led to fights and cars that broke down and blocked traffic…

Even searching for buses and times revealed stories of people rear-ending others, being hit by others, and having to turn around due to illness on buses. The entire page was filled with countless details.

The two searched until their eyes were dazed, but the results were like searching for a needle in a haystack; they could find no useful information at all.

While modern, highly developed society had made searching for information much easier, finding the information they needed within this vast sea of ​​data had become their biggest challenge.

“Look at this! Someone got into a bus accident while getting off a bus around 1:00 p.m. Could it be…”

Li Shiqing suddenly found something that looked useful and was about to show it to Bespectacled Boy when she heard a muffled sound.

Bespectacled Boy, who had just leaned over, shuddered, and both of them involuntarily looked towards the cross-river bridge.

From the northeast, a thick plume of smoke billowed into the sky, rising into the air. The thick black smoke, like a ferocious demon, tearing through the clear sky with its fangs and claws.

“Is that… the direction of the bridge?”

Bespectacled Boy shuddered and asked Li Shiqing uncertainly.

He glanced down at the time on his phone; it was exactly 1:45 p.m.

“It’s the bridge.”

Li Shiqing estimated the distance, a heavy weight sinking in her heart.

“It looks like the explosion happened on the bridge this time.”

The billowing smoke reminded them of the countless lives lost.

“Don’t overthink it.”

Bespectacled Boy pulled Li Shiqing’s shoulder, preventing her from looking at the smoke. Gazing into her eyes, he said earnestly, “Just remember, we’re resting now to ‘go further.'”

Li Shiqing nodded dimly, her grip on the phone tightening.

“Why did the driver insist on driving onto the bridge before detonating it? Was the 1:45 p.m. explosion time a prediction by the perpetrators, or was it simply a ritual? Or was it a moment of profound significance to them?”

This time, the accident wasn’t a collision with the tanker, but the outcome was even more uncertain, and Li Shiqing’s doubts grew deeper.

“The bridge, the bus, the explosion—all these details put together don’t seem like a simple act of revenge against society. They seem more like…”

“…like a sacrifice.”

Bespectacled Boy was stunned, his face grim as he continued.

This bus, sending everyone to hell, truly conjured up the most sinister plots in fantasy. The passengers on board looked all too like “sacrifices” to evil spirits or demons.

This connection only made the two feel worse.

The billowing smoke in the distance added to the lingering tension.

“Don’t overthink it. Actually, think about it from another perspective. A bus exploding on a bridge might actually be more advantageous to us!”

Bespectacled Boy rubbed his chin and suddenly said, “The last few times the police couldn’t find any leads, it was because the bus collided with a tanker. The explosion site was so severely damaged that they couldn’t find any useful clues, so they had to rely on questioning us to make progress…”

“But this time is different.”

He frowned. “This time the bus exploded on a bridge, so it should be easier for the police to find some clues. Maybe if we just wait a while, we’ll get some crucial information…”

“No, that’s too slow…”

A glimmer of hope slowly returned to Li Shiqing’s eyes. “Perhaps we should try to proactively provide the police with clues?”

“What?”

Bespectacled Boy felt a little confused.

“Why can’t we find any useful information online? Because our search methods are so inefficient! What if we could leverage the police’s power?”

Following Bespectacled Boy’s earlier suggestions, Li Shiqing struggled to clarify the flash of inspiration in her mind.

“We already know the auntie is the perpetrator, carrying a pressure cooker packed with explosives. The driver is an accomplice, or at least an accessory to the crime. He never considered opening the door to let anyone escape…”

Bepectacled Boy also realized what was happening, sobering up as if struck by a stern warning.

“You’re saying, if we can’t find out, the police can?!”

“A veteran driver like the uncle should have a complete personnel file at the bus company, right? It should be easy for the police to investigate the driver. If they know the auntie is suspicious, perhaps they can find her real information through the surveillance footage from the bus?”

Although Li Shiqing wasn’t entirely sure, she continued to think along these lines.

“Just like the police investigated us before, if they can investigate their social connections, interpersonal relationships, and past events, they might be able to uncover the aunt’s motives and why the uncle helped her!”

“We got off the bus normally this time, so there’s nothing suspicious. There’s no need to worry about the police questioning us like they did the other time.”

Her voice trembled with excitement. “Instead of searching like we’re looking for a needle in a haystack, why not just cooperate with the police and be a good citizen, providing them with useful clues and guidance!”

“That’s a good idea!”

Even Bespectacled Boy had to admit that it was indeed a useful suggestion given the current impasse.

“Then all we have to do is wait for the police to summon us!”

They had gotten off the bus several times before, and they knew that the first thing the police did after a case occurred was to gather useful information from passengers who had gotten off the bus before through phone calls and visits.

As the two passengers who got off at the nearest stop, the police would find them sooner or later to find out what happened. At that time, all they had to do was provide as many clues as possible based on the police’s questions.

“Come, let’s organize our thoughts and summarize which pieces of information are crucial…”

With a clear direction, Bespectacled Boy’s brain began to work again, and he pulled out the pen and paper he had brought with him.

“This time, we absolutely cannot return empty-handed!”

—

The explosion occurred at 1:45 p.m. Since this one was directly on the bridge, unlike the previous attempts to get out of the bus and crash into a tanker, the impact was even more devastating and unacceptable.

After Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy discussed their strategy for dealing with the police, they waited for the incoming call while poring over various online news with a sullen expression.

Although they knew that simply browsing the news was futile, as two young people, they found it difficult to resist the urge to search online for relevant information.

Almost an hour passed, and Bespectacled Boy’s phone rang with an unfamiliar number.

“Is it the police?”

Li Shiqing looked at Bespectacled Boy with a mixture of nervousness and anticipation.

“That should be… right?”

Bespectacled Boy took a deep breath, gathered his thoughts, and answered the phone.

But the next moment, his breath was gone.

“Huh? What delivery? I’m not in the dorm. Just leave it in the security office.”

Bespectacled Boy glanced at his companion guiltily, wanting to end the call quickly. “What? Cash on delivery? Then can you deliver it tomorrow? Or I’ll pay you through Alipay…”

“Courier, I’m really busy right now. How about you take care of the other deliveries first? If it doesn’t work out, I’ll contact you later, and I can pick it up myself at the courier, okay?”

The other end was obviously about to say something, but Bespectacled Boy was worried the police wouldn’t be able to get through if the line was busy, so he ended the call hastily.

After hanging up, the atmosphere was a bit awkward but also a bit amusing.

“I bought this digital product secondhand on Xianyu. The seller was so stingy, he actually requested it be paid on delivery…”

Bespectacled Boy explained dryly.

The previous times he’d either turned off his phone or blocked the calls, but this was the first time he’d received this call.

“I hope you actually receive this package tomorrow.”

Li Shiqing offered her best wishes, a pun intended.

“I hope so.”

Bespectacled Boy smiled wryly, not holding out much hope for a break from this cycle tomorrow.

With this unexpected incident, their tense nerves relaxed a little, each hoping to wait for the police to contact them with a more positive attitude.

A dozen minutes later, the police called and summoned them.

“Are you together? Great! Please come to the W City Criminal Police Detachment immediately. We’ll send someone to meet you at the door. The address is on XX Road. Please assist us with the investigation as soon as possible!”

Upon learning that the two passengers who had gotten off the bus were together, the other party was overjoyed, their voices rising in rapture.

Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun chose to proactively respond to the summons this time. They took a taxi and headed to the Criminal Police Detachment together.

The address was familiar; they had been there before, albeit escorted in a police car. This time, they went on their own, and their emotions grew even more complicated. On the way to the Criminal Police Detachment, the taxi driver listened to the traffic announcement regarding the explosion. The detailed description of the explosion scene on the radio made both of them physically and mentally uncomfortable.

The cramped space of the taxi, coupled with the frequent mention of words like “explosion” and “bus” on the radio, made them feel suffocated. Li Shiqing even felt like vomiting, and they could only hold each other’s hands tightly to cheer each other up.

The approaching distance to the Criminal Police Detachment brought back negative memories of the previous times they had been here. The calmness and courage they had just used when discussing “countermeasures” vanished. As they neared their destination, their palms began to sweat.

“You don’t know yet; a bus exploded over there on the cross-river bridge!”

The taxi driver, however, couldn’t stop talking, constantly finding new things to say.

“I heard the scene was horrific. The bodies were so badly blown up that they couldn’t even be identified. The bus doors were so deformed that everyone had to climb in through the windows to rescue people! Hey, there were bombs, so how could anyone be saved?”

“So, it’s safer to take a taxi. On an open bus, you never know when a lunatic might get on. There were news reports of bus arson attacks before, and now there’s an explosion. There are always one or two crazy people in the world. What if you run into one?”

The taxi driver continued to ramble, “What do you think?”

“Driver, we’re getting off here!”

Li Shiqing’s face suddenly changed, and she asked to get off a little way from the Criminal Police Detachment.

Bespectacled Boy paid the fare and hurriedly followed his companions out of the taxi; then he saw Li Shiqing vomiting into a roadside trash can.

As the one who always made the “proposal,” she felt immense pressure.

“Are you okay?”

Bespectacled Boy hurried forward, patting her back with a hint of concern.

“Don’t come over here; it’s dirty…”

Li Shiqing waved her hand behind him, signaling him not to come.

“Sorry, I’ve delayed you again…”

She bent down to suppress the nausea in her throat. “Let me get some fresh air; it’ll be fine in a moment.”

Bespectacled Boy sighed, went to the roadside to buy a bottle of water and a pack of tissues, and handed them to her from behind.

When Li Shiqing stood up again, her eyes were slightly swollen, and even her nose was red. She couldn’t tell if the vomiting had triggered natural tears or if she’d cried out of sadness.

Perhaps it was both.

Bespectacled Boy considerately pretended he hadn’t noticed anything. He checked the navigation to see the location of the Criminal Police Detachment and patiently led Li Shiqing by the hand towards their destination.

Arriving at the Criminal Police Detachment’s entrance, there was indeed a uniformed officer anxiously peering out from the doorway.

Seeing the young couple approach, his eyes lit up, and he quickly approached them.

Once they had a clear view of the officer’s face, Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun’s pace gradually slowed.

Then, even Bespectacled Boy’s nose felt strangely sore.

“You are Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun, right?”

The officer’s tone was unprecedentedly enthusiastic. After receiving a positive response, he introduced himself and extended his hand.

“We called you earlier. Let me introduce myself. I’m one of the officers in charge of this case. You can call me Officer Zhang, or just call me like everyone else…”

He squeezed Xiao Heyun’s hand tightly.

“Old Zhang.”

CONTENT END 31

chapters.title: The Twentieth Cycle (Part 3)
chapters.content:
In this timeline, being able to see Old Zhang, to feel that he was still alive, was in itself enough to comfort the two young people. Or rather, after all the cycles of being screwed, this was one of the few times they felt their efforts were worthwhile.

Li Shiqing had just cried, and now, seeing Old Zhang, she felt a mixture of joy and sorrow, her eyes welling up.

“Hey, what’s wrong with you? Are you afraid of seeing the police?”

Seeing the girl halfway through tears, Old Zhang smiled and soothed her like a child, “Don’t be afraid. The police don’t catch good people; they only catch bad people.”

“I know…”

Li Shiqing forced a smile and nodded.

“What’s wrong with her?”

As Old Zhang led them inside, he noticed that Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy acted very familiar, their gestures very intimate, so he mistook him for Li Shiqing’s boyfriend and asked him quietly.

“Why is she feeling off?”

“She’s soft-hearted. Ever since she found out about the bus accident and the deaths of so many people, she’s been upset. Just now, on the way to the police station, the taxi’s radio was broadcasting this story again. She couldn’t hold it in, and as soon as she got out of the taxi, she ran to the side and vomited.”

After his previous experience, Bespectacled Boy knew better than to lie to these well-trained detectives, so he told the truth.

“We just saw someone, and then suddenly he was gone. It’s just too much to handle psychologically.”

“How can you think that? You should think, ‘It’s a blessing that nothing happened after such a big thing.'”

After hearing Bespectacled Boy’s explanation, Old Zhang’s eyes softened as he looked at Li Shiqing, and his voice softened. “Little girl, don’t blame yourself, and don’t be afraid…”

Having studied psychology, he understood that some “survivors” suffer from a kind of “moral trauma,” feeling they didn’t do enough during the disaster or blaming themselves for not doing anything. This leads to deep guilt and psychological problems. This kind of “moral trauma” is known in psychology as “survivor guilt,” also known as “survivor syndrome.”

Unlike PTSD (post-traumatic stress disorder), people often prioritize PTSD over those who experience it, often overlooking those who suffer from it. By the time tragedy strikes, it’s often too late.

Li Shiqing was still so young, and Bespectacled Boy before him seemed so refined. Old Zhang couldn’t sit idly by and watch their mental health deteriorate to such a level. As they walked, he tried to soothe the two young ones’ negative emotions.

“No one wants something like this to happen. Don’t feel like you’ve done anything wrong, and don’t dwell on the tragic events. Don’t think you’re wrong for what you did or didn’t do. This has nothing to do with ordinary passengers like you…”

People who experienced this kind of “trauma” were often those with strong moral compasses. A selfish and indifferent person, on the other hand, didn’t have this problem.

“…The people who planted the bomb should be blamed and punished, not you lucky ones who escaped.”

Sometimes, sensible people bore the brunt of the burden, which made Old Zhang feel even more sorry for the two young people.

He repeated so much, just to convey one message:

[It’s not your fault.]

It’s not your fault.

These simple words completely overwhelmed Li Shiqing.

They had strived for so long, failed for so long, seen the dawn of hope, and endured the depths of darkness.

Sometimes, they felt as if the entire world was telling them to give up, but they refused to admit defeat or resign themselves to their fate. No matter how great the setbacks or how deep the pain, once they sobered up, they would grit their teeth and tell each other, “Try again.”

But even with all their efforts, nothing could be rescued.

After experiencing this cycle last time, Li Shiqing had grown faintly weary of it all, feeling that such “strange” things were unworthy of happening to “ordinary people” like her. She was so foolish, so weak, that the “opportunity” Heaven had bestowed upon her was a complete waste. She couldn’t do anything well, and she could do nothing at all. She could only watch helplessly as everyone on the bus perished again and again.

But now, someone was saying to them:

—”It’s not your fault.”

Understanding the meaning behind Old Zhang’s words, Li Shiqing burst into tears.

Perhaps feeling both hypocritical and ashamed, she frantically wiped away her tears, shielding her eyes tightly with her arms.

Not to mention Li Shiqing, even Xiao Heyun, a man who rarely cried, felt a wave of uncontrollable pain and quietly raised his head.

They had suffered so much, truly so much.

So miserable they couldn’t even handle a word of comfort.

Old Zhang hadn’t anticipated how his few words of comfort would stir the two young ones so severely. However, his intuition, as a seasoned criminal detective, immediately influenced him.

If they had simply gotten off the bus, the two children wouldn’t have been so emotional. They must have learned something on board but didn’t actually act on it, leading to a deep sense of guilt.

Speculating this, Old Zhang felt a surge of ecstasy, and his attitude toward the two young ones became even more cautious.

They had made numerous calls to passengers who had gotten off the bus to assist in the investigation. These two were the most forthright, the most willing to respond without hesitation, and the fastest to arrive. Now, Old Zhang sensed that they seemed to know something, suggesting a high probability of cooperation!

Old Zhang led them to the task force’s office. Officer Du, who was already on the phone, saw them enter and, too busy to speak, simply gestured to them from a distance, “Sit,” and continued speaking into the phone.

Unlike last time, when they arrived and went straight into the interrogation room, this time they were called in as “assisting investigators.” Besides Old Zhang, who had gone out to meet them, and Officer Du, whom they had met before, there were many other officers coming and going in the office, but everyone was quite friendly.

“Has the trace department’s stuff turned up yet?”

“No!”

“Where’s the file? Has the victim’s file been sorted out yet?”

“The forensic doctor is still working on it!”

Officers constantly rushed in with case files, then snatched up their belongings without even touching a step, occasionally barking out requests for something, their work utterly frantic.

Perhaps because they were so busy, when they saw Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy, they only glanced at them curiously, not feeling any discomfort.

“Hey, are these the two young ones who got off at the last stop? We’ve been waiting for them! Come on, Fangzi, get them two glasses of water!”

A passing officer’s expression relaxed as he shouted.

A passing police officer brought two paper cups over and placed them on the coffee table in front of them. He glanced at Li Shiqing and winked at Old Zhang. “What’s wrong?”

Why are her eyes red?

“The little girl heard that the bus exploded and was terrified.”

Old Zhang said nothing more, shoving the officer’s back. “Go about your business!”

By the time Officer Du finished his call and came over, Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun had calmed down and sat down, leaning against each other, on a bench, quietly waiting for the police to ask questions.

“Thank you both for complying with the police summons and coming to assist with the investigation of this explosion. On behalf of our task force, I’d like to thank you both for your support and trust in us. I’m the team leader. My last name is Du, and you can call me Officer Du.”

Officer Du was a calm and serious man, speaking concisely and to the point, concluding his opening remarks in just a few words.

“I’m sure you both know that the bus you were on crashed. We’ve asked you to come here because it was severely damaged in the explosion, and many traces at the scene are illegible. We need your assistance. Please recall as much as possible about the bus and provide us with useful information.”

“There are also some questions we’d like to know, so please answer them truthfully.”

Here it comes!

“Okay, Officer Du!”

Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy were startled, sitting up straight and nodding like two good children answering a teacher’s question.

“Why did you take this Bus 45? What’s your relationship?”

Officer Du began by asking them questions related to him.

“I’m going to the Youth Bookstore in Jiangbei District to buy some professional books for my thesis. Several bookstores near our school don’t have them, and it’s too late to buy them online.”

Li Shiqing stated her purpose.

“I’m going to the Apple flagship store in Jiangbei District to check out the latest phones.”

Bespectacled Boy replied, “She and I are friends. We bumped into each other on the bus and found she was also taking this one today, so we just sat together and went together.”

“You were both going to Jiangbei District to buy things. Why did you get off at Yanjiang East Road?”

Officer Du frowned, his tone unconsciously becoming stern.

“Boss, let me ask.”

Old Zhang, watching Bespectacled Boy turn pale, quickly intervened.

“Just asking about something. No need to be so serious!”

“Sorry, I’m not upset with you. It’s just my professional habit.”

Officer Du realized his tone was too harsh and nodded apologetically. “Then, Old Zhang, you go ahead and ask.”

Old Zhang’s attitude was much more gentle.

“Did you notice anything unusual on the bus?” He carefully observed the girl’s facial expression and asked soothingly, “You got off the bus because you sensed something was wrong, right?”

Because of the possibility of a new breakthrough, Officer Du and the other officers who overheard the questioning grew nervous, holding their breath as they awaited their response.

Li Shiqing raised her head, returning Old Zhang’s encouraging gaze, and nodded.

“What is it?!”

Instantly, every officer’s eyes lit up with excitement.

“The woman in the flowered shirt sitting in front of us is mentally ill. She keeps rambling on about 1:45 p.m. and Wang Xingde. I just felt like there was something off about her, and subconsciously, I was a little scared, so I dragged Xiao Heyun off the bus at the next stop.”

Li Shiqing wasn’t sure if the excuse she and Xiao Heyun had come up with would convince the police. She could only hold Xiao Heyun’s hand tightly, drawing courage from her companion.

“But not long after we got off the bus, we saw smoke coming out of the cross-river bridge…”

When they heard the words “1:45 p.m.” and “Wang Xingde,” Officer Du and Old Zhang exchanged a look of grave concern.

The explosion occurred at 1:45 p.m.

And Wang Xingde was the driver of this bus.

Neither of these pieces of information would be something an average passenger would know; the clues they provided could be true!

“The lady in the flowered shirt? Do you remember what she looked like? What was she carrying? If I show you the surveillance footage from the bus at the station, can you tell which one is her?”

Old Zhang’s premonition had come true, and he was overcome with excitement.

“She brought a pressure cooker.”

Li Shiqing didn’t even need to recall; she could already identify the pressure cooker. “It was wrapped in a large, double-decker supermarket plastic bag. It was huge, and it was right at her feet.”

She nodded and added, “I remember her. If you show me the surveillance footage, I can tell.”

“Fangzi, check the surveillance footage and find the information of the middle-aged woman who brought the pressure cooker into the bus!”

Officer Du acted decisively and gave the order.

“Especially her social connections!”

“Yes!”

“Old Wang, urge the Trace Investigations Department to hurry up! Determine if the explosives are in the pressure cooker, and focus on analyzing any debris that might be pressure cooker debris!”

“Yes, Boss!”

“Fangzi, once you find out the identity of the woman with the pressure cooker, immediately notify Xiao Jiang to lead a team to search her residence!”

“Roger!”

The other officers from the task force gathered around after hearing about the significant discovery.

The officer who had just called for information from the Trace Investigations Department pulled out two bus interior floor plans from nowhere and handed them to Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun.

“There are no further stops after Yanjiang East Road. You were the last to get off, and we haven’t seen any suspicious individuals boarding the bus from surveillance footage along the way. We suspect the perpetrator of the bombing was likely on the bus at the time.”

He said, “We want to know who was on the bus and where they were seated, especially that suspicious woman in flowery clothes you mentioned. I hope you can recall as much as possible and mark their locations on the floor plan.”

“Let me do it.”

Xiao Heyun took the pen from Old Zhang, thought for a moment, and began marking the floor plan.

“Over here is an old lady. Over here is an old man carrying a snakeskin bag with something round inside, probably fruits… Over here is an old man carrying a black gym bag, and over here is an old woman carrying a vegetable basket.”

He drew Xs on the floor plan, noting who sat in each seat, even noting what they were carrying.

“…Here, here is the lady in the flowered shirt.”

Xiao Heyun paused, then drew another X. “She’s carrying a pressure cooker, sitting right in front of us.”

Based on his memory, he mapped out everyone’s position, except for the masked man who got on later.

Because they had gotten off at the same stop the masked man boarded at, they probably had no idea where he was sitting.

As he drew and gestured, several police officers gasped.

“A broken black gym bag was found on the bus earlier!”

“There were definitely traces of melon at the scene!”

Summoning passengers who had gotten off the bus for information was just one way the police gathered information. The amount of information they could gather depended entirely on how much the assisting investigators could remember.

In the past, it was common for frightened individuals to panic and even speak incoherently. Even clues provided by seemingly normal insiders often lacked logic or were inconsistent, requiring repeated verification before they could be used.

But this time was different. The cooperating witness was perfectly lucid, and his words and the information he had noted were supported by sufficient traces or evidence at the scene.

“You’re incredible, young man! You remember it so clearly!”

Old Zhang patted Xiao Heyun’s shoulder excitedly, his trust in their clues growing stronger.

“I have a good memory. I was bored on the bus and enjoyed observing the passengers.”

Bespectacled Boy accepted the compliment and pushed his glasses up. “I’m glad I can help.”

With this new lead, the direction suddenly became clear. They no longer had to search for information from all directions as before.

For a moment, the entire task force was like a machine running at full speed, humming along quickly and efficiently, methodically carrying out their tasks according to Officer Du’s every instruction.

Meanwhile, Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun anxiously awaited the results of the police investigation.

Just as the police expected from them, they also hoped that the police would use their leads to provide them with more information that would be difficult for ordinary people to uncover.
