After waiting for almost an hour, Old Zhang, having gathered sufficient evidence and information from his colleagues, pulled up a surveillance photo on his phone and rushed over to the two young ones.

“Look, is that the woman with the pressure cooker?”

The photo was a bit blurry, and it was hard to make out her features. All that could be vaguely seen was a woman holding the large plastic bag that Li Shiqing had mentioned. There was no way to tell from the surveillance footage whether it contained a pressure cooker.

But the clothing was incredibly familiar to Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun. “It’s her.”

Li Shiqing nodded. “I remember her clothes.”

“It was definitely her. She was using a bag from FamilyMart.”

Bespectacled Boy said confidently.

“Investigate! Check this woman’s identity immediately to see if she’s related to Wang Xingde! Tell Xiao Jiang to request a search warrant and be ready to go!”

Over an hour later, news arrived from the Trace Investigations Department.

“The Trace Investigations Department has confirmed that the explosive was in the pressure cooker!”

A few minutes later, Old Zhang, who was investigating the middle-aged woman, hurried over and whispered in Officer Du’s ear, “Old Du, the young woman is right. This woman is a major suspect…”

“She and the driver, Wang Xingde, are married!”

CONTENT END 32

chapters.title: The Twentieth Cycle (Part 4)
chapters.content:
The explosion in W City was a horrific tragedy. The sheer number of casualties and the magnitude of its social impact were the highest in years. Consequently, both public opinion and repeated concerns from all sides placed immense pressure on the task force investigating the case.

Even without the pressure from various parties, any police officer who visited the explosion site and witnessed the devastating scene would have a deep desire to uncover the true culprit and motive.

Why did they do this?

Was there a larger criminal organization behind them, preying on public security?

Solving major cases required more than just speculation; a complete chain of evidence, both human and physical, was needed to corroborate the facts uncovered. This process of finding evidence often took time.

Furthermore, the damage inside the bus was so severe, and no one on board survived. Even the remains found after the explosion were in a state of disarray, further complicating the investigation.

But now, the clues provided by the two young ones have provided the task force with a clear direction and a major breakthrough, bringing the situation into sharper focus.

With a clear direction, the evidence-gathering process would be greatly streamlined.

“Heaven has eyes, and the net of Heaven is vast, leaving nothing untouched.”

This was Old Zhang’s only thought regarding the quick discovery of the clue.

“Thankfully, two youths, one alert and the other clever, provided us with such significant assistance.”

“But don’t you think they are a bit too alert and a bit too clever?”

Officer Du felt a sense of unease as he recalled Bespectacled Boy taking the map and effortlessly “memorizing” each person’s location.

“A normal person’s mind wouldn’t be completely confused if they encountered something like this, but he managed to remember it perfectly. And that girl…”

If she knew there was a problem, why didn’t she call the police?

He didn’t express his dissatisfaction, but Old Zhang understood.

“I know what you’re worried about; I share your concerns. But in my experience, these two youths are likely innocent. A suspect in a bombing wouldn’t proactively help the police or respond to a summons, much less bear such a heavy psychological burden over the heavy casualties suffered by the passengers on the bus.”

Old Zhang felt a pang of pain as he recalled the little girl’s tears after being comforted. “Ordinary people would be too busy looking after themselves in such a situation, but they still thought of helping others. They’re good people. Besides, haven’t we already investigated? They have clean backgrounds, simple social lives, and no criminal record. They have no motive to be accomplices.”

“There are always some unconventional geniuses in this world, some with incredibly fast reflexes, some with exceptional memory for images. Perhaps this young man possesses such talents? Since he said he usually likes to observe the passengers on the bus, it’s not surprising that he could recall something at a crucial moment. And since the girl had already noticed something was wrong with the person in the front seat, it’s reasonable for a friend to pay more attention.”

Old Zhang understood Old Du’s anger and regret over the case, but emotionally, he was more inclined to trust the two youths.

“As for why the girl didn’t call the police, I don’t think there’s anything to dwell on. She had no evidence. She just thought the middle-aged woman’s soliloquy was strange. People’s intuition shouldn’t be used as evidence. Many people, faced with such situations, think calling the police is overkill.”

“You’re right.”

Officer Du sighed. “I was just too nervous.”

“Relax, don’t push yourself so hard.”

Old Zhang understood his urgency perfectly.

“I know you’re very responsible, but protecting people’s safety and maintaining public order is our responsibility. You can’t hold two ordinary young people to the same professional standards and moral constraints.”

“They will actively cooperate with the police to solve the case. They’ve already done the best they can.”

Even then, assisting the police, Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun quickly received the answers they needed.

“Are the driver and the woman married?”

Upon learning of their relationship, Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy nearly collapsed in expression.

If the police hadn’t said anything, who would have guessed the driver had such a connection with that lunatic woman?

“Are you saying this bus driver could be an accomplice?”

Bespectacled Boy asked nervously.

“It’s very possible, but the final outcome depends on the evidence we find,” said Old Zhang.

“You look surprised. Why?”

Although Officer Du accepted Old Zhang’s explanation, out of professionalism, he immediately noticed something was amiss with Li Shiqing. This was an occupational hazard they couldn’t control.

“Because I’m quite familiar with this driver.”

Li Shiqing didn’t try to hide it, speaking from the heart. “I’ve been riding this bus for over two years, mostly on school holidays. I’ve always met the driver of today’s bus. He’s very considerate of students and doesn’t seem like the type to do such a thing.”

Hearing that the girl was familiar with the driver, Officer Du’s interest piqued.

“Oh? He was supposed to be taking care of the students? What exactly? Tell us.”

Li Shiqing recounted all her memories and perceptions of the driver to the officers.

When she first arrived, she was unfamiliar with the area and too shy to bother others. But even in such an unfamiliar place, most of the people she met were kind, which made her unwilling to assume malice.

Compared to the ruthless woman, she trusted what she saw and felt more deeply, and she was more inclined to believe the driver had some hardship.

“After we got on the bus, the driver didn’t speak to any of the other passengers, including the woman with the pressure cooker.”

Li Shiqing said hesitantly, “We didn’t expect the driver to have such a relationship with that woman.”

“He does sound like a nice person, not like someone with a sociopathic personality…”

Officer Du rubbed his chin and asked his assistant, “Fangzi, are the driver and the suspect, Tao Yinghong, a married couple? Do they have any children?”

“Yes, they were married 25 years ago. They were originally from Q City, S Province, and moved here three years ago.” Fangzi frowned as he looked at the documents in his hand. “They had a daughter, but she’s deceased.”

Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy exchanged glances, their eyes growing even more surprised.

Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy had previously discussed the possibility that the uncle might have been forced to succumb to a criminal organization because his family had been kidnapped or held hostage. They had also hypothesized that if the police could uncover this information, rescuing the hostages from the outset might have garnered the driver’s help…

But now, the police investigation revealed that the driver’s so-called “family” was actually the lunatic aunt, and his daughter was no longer alive…

That path suddenly closed.

“Check on their daughter.”

Old Zhang interjected, “Anything that could make a middle-aged woman do such a thing is likely related to her children.”

“What else can you recall? Please tell us everything you can, including any other suspicious individuals in the bus, and whether there’s any possibility of a gang operating…”

Old Zhang said anxiously.

Given the findings from the investigation into the driver uncle and aunt, Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy carefully considered whether they might have overlooked anything but ultimately shook their heads.

“The bus was full of elderly people who weren’t working. We didn’t see anything wrong, at least not that we could spot,” Bespectacled Boy replied cautiously.

Just then, Officer Du’s phone rang.

“Xiao Jiang.”

Officer Du glanced at the incoming call alert and quickly picked up.

“Great! Well done! Keep searching and see if you find anything else!”

As if they’d shared some good news, a faint smile crossed his usually serious face. “I’ll cooperate with you in the search.”

“What’s up? Did Xiao Jiang find anything?”

Old Zhang asked impatiently.

Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun couldn’t help but look up at him, their eyes filled with anticipation.

Officer Du’s gaze swept over the two youths. He hesitated for a moment but didn’t shy away. He spoke to them directly.

“Xiao Jiang found bomb-making tools and remaining raw materials in a detached garage on a property owned by the suspect couple. It’s now virtually certain that the bomb was made by this couple.”

“In a residential area?”

Old Zhang’s face lit up with anger when he heard where the raw materials were found.

“They bought a second-hand house in Gangwu New Village only three years ago. According to the neighbors across the street, the husband usually lives away from home, returning home two or three times a week. The wife also comes home about as often as the husband does. She rarely socializes with the neighbors and seems rather unsociable.”

With this important discovery, Officer Du calmed down.

Soon after, the officer investigating driver Wang Xingde and his wife, Tao Yinghong, arrived at the task force office with their information.

“Driver Wang Xingde used to be a truck driver, running haulage in his hometown of S Province. His wife, Tao Yinghong, has been a high school chemistry teacher at Q City No. 1 Middle School…”

He spoke as he handed his documents to Officer Du. “Three years ago, Wang Xingde applied for a job with this city’s bus company through a labor dispatch agency. After a period of pre-job training, he officially became a bus driver. Two years ago, he was officially transferred to this route.”

“That same year, Tao Yinghong resigned and followed Wang Xingde to this city. Because of her chemistry background, she worked as a quality inspector at a chemical factory until she resigned six months ago.”

Now, not only was the suspect confirmed, but the conditions for bomb-making were also in place.

“Why would they give up their stable jobs in their hometown and settle down in W City?” Old Zhang wondered. “Bus drivers can’t be paid more than truck drivers, right?”

No matter how one looked at it, this suspect couple was fraught with suspicion.

“Old Zhang, continue talking to them and see if there’s anything else we’ve missed. You stay with the team and coordinate. We’ll meet up with Xiao Jiang. Call if there’s anything.”

With a lead, Officer Du wasted no time, eager to gather more evidence.

After Officer Du left, Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy sat on a bench. Seeing a room full of busy officers, while they sat there alone, feeling a little awkward.

Old Zhang noticed the two youths’s discomfort, thought for a moment, and said to them with a smile, “It’s a bit chaotic here. How about you come with me to my office, where it’s a little quieter?”

Because Bespectacled Boy and Li Shiqing were the only ones who could accurately describe the appearance of the last passengers on the bus, neither Old Zhang nor Old Du had any intention of letting them go back so soon.

But leaving these two young people like this while they were investigating a case wasn’t really appropriate.

“I have a camp bed in my office. You can lie down if you get tired. There’s also a charging cable and hot water. You can rest for a while, play with your phone, or something…”

Old Zhang led them into his office, found two chairs for them to sit on, and rummaged through his drawers, looking for something to treat them with. He only found a few bags of compressed biscuits to keep them occupied.

“Sorry, I don’t snack, so I don’t have much to eat. If you’re hungry, just have these for now. I’ll treat you to dinner tonight!”

Old Zhang looked at the biscuits awkwardly.

“It’s okay. These are delicious. I haven’t had them in ages.”

Bespectacled Boy took the biscuits without a hint of disdain.

Xiao Heyun’s thoughtfulness made Old Zhang even more fond of the two young people. While they waited for Wang Xingde’s daughter’s information, Old Zhang chatted with them, mostly asking about the situation on the bus, hoping to learn anything he might have missed.

As they chatted, something flashed through Li Shiqing’s mind, and she looked a little dazed.

“What’s up? Did you remember something?”

Old Zhang asked with a smile.

“Officer Zhang, I have a question I want to ask. Please don’t laugh at me…”

She scratched her head, as if embarrassed.

“Well, ask it.”

“Hypothetically, I mean hypothetically…”

Though she said “hypothetically,” Li Shiqing’s expression was serious.

Thinking she had something important to ask, Old Zhang also took on a serious tone.

“Suppose I open my eyes tomorrow and find myself back on this bus that exploded…”

Facing Bespectacled Boy’s surprised expression, Li Shiqing asked earnestly.

“There were only thirty minutes left before the explosion. Xiao Heyun and I knew there was a bomb in the bus, and we knew the culprits were the aunt and the driver. Given the limited conditions, what could we do to prevent the explosion?”

CONTENT END 33

chapters.title: The Twentieth Cycle (V)
chapters.content:
Many people have experienced this:

Long after an event, they still dwelled on their poor performance, even regretting it for the rest of their lives.

It could be a momentary misstep during an interview, a wrong choice before a major decision, or even a simple lack of sharpness during an argument; for years to come, it would become a lingering knot in their hearts.

So, this question, which might seem a little “odd” to others, was once again interpreted by Old Zhang as a reflection of the girl’s resentment for not raising the alarm earlier.

How strong must one’s sense of justice be to feel the pain of being a “survivor”?

Having never experienced this, Old Zhang couldn’t empathize with this, but that didn’t stop him from respecting the girl. “Ah, that’s an interesting question…”

Old Zhang paused for a moment before pondering.

“But I haven’t thought about it. I need to think carefully before I can answer.”

A young girl, after a brush with death, her first thought wasn’t to escape but to help the police find the real culprit. In the process, she even pondered the question, “If I were to encounter this same situation, what would I do to avoid regrets?” Even if it seemed like a fairy tale, her question deserved serious consideration.

“Your conditions are too demanding…”

Old Zhang pondered for a moment, then said with a slight headache, “First, we only have thirty minutes. You have to understand that if you call the police directly, it takes time from receiving the call to dispatch, plus the dispatch… And your bus is a moving bus, and its position could change at any time…”

Old Zhang raised the very question that bothered Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun the most.

They had called the police before, but that call directly resulted in Old Zhang’s “sacrifice” in that cycle. “So, what you’re saying is, if we encounter something like this, we shouldn’t call the police but instead try to resolve it ourselves?”

Li Shiqing asked, quietly recording on her phone.

“No, you two don’t have the ability to resolve this situation. Regardless of whether you’re in time or not, you should still notify the police first.”

Old Zhang, unconcerned with the two youths’s pride, said bluntly, “There’s a bomb on the bus, and the driver is an accomplice. You two alone can’t deter the perpetrators, nor can you gain the passengers’ trust and help through your identities. Resolving the situation on your own will only make matters worse. If you don’t succeed, you might even provoke the killer.”

“A few years ago, we handled a bus arson case. The arsonist had been unemployed for years and was disillusioned with society.” Holding a grudge, he wanted to do something “big” to exact revenge. He boarded a bus carrying two gasoline-filled water bottles. Passengers noticed the strong smell of gasoline and confronted him.

He sighed, “The criminal was already guilty. As soon as someone asked about the gasoline smell, he smashed the two water bottles and set them on fire with a lighter. That bus arson incident was also devastating. Although the driver opened the door in time, it still caused numerous casualties.”

Old Zhang worried that the two youths might be overly impulsive, so he used a real-life case as a warning.

“When facing a vicious criminal, it’s best not to engage in direct confrontation, let alone provoke them. Often, the criminal’s inner struggles are intense, and you never know what they might do next.”

Ah, he hit the nail on the head.

Bespectacled Boy sighed inwardly, almost nodding frantically.

“Thirty minutes, as you say, is indeed too short.”

As Old Zhang spoke, his interest piqued. He picked up a scrap of paper and began to draw a diagram.

“Let me think about it… Well, buses usually move at a constant speed. You can use your phone’s map to find the distance between stops, and you can roughly estimate the time…”

Today, their task force had been researching the explosion case. They knew the starting and ending points of this bus line by heart, and they quickly drew a map.

“You said you only have half an hour. That’s roughly around here, near the penultimate stop, ‘Gangwu New Village’… Hmm?”

Old Zhang scratched his chin with his pen. “Isn’t this the platform where Tao Yinghong boarded the bus?”

“Yes.”

Bespectacled Boy nodded. “Let’s assume she’s already boarded the bus and it’s already left the station…”

“Indeed, if she hasn’t boarded yet, you could just detain her at the platform and call the police. There’s no point asking how to stop the explosion.”

Old Zhang had just said that casually. He muttered to himself for a moment before returning to his drawing.

The veteran police officer’s intuition was incredibly sharp, terrifying.

Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun breathed a sigh of relief.

“According to the surveillance footage, this bus’s average speed is 32 kilometers per hour. Based on the distance, we estimate it’ll arrive at the next stop around 1:23 p.m….”

Old Zhang roughly calculated the bus’s arrival time at each location by estimating the time.

“But there are only eight to ten minutes from receiving the call to dispatching; even the fastest possible time wouldn’t be enough. Even if you could contact our criminal investigation team directly and dispatch them as quickly as possible, it would still take about fifteen minutes to get from here to the Bus 45 bus route.”

“At 1:30 p.m., the bus will probably arrive here…”

Old Zhang circled the intersection on the map.

He glanced at the location and frowned.

“Even if it arrives, there’s still the problem of how we can get on the bus.”

Old Zhang had completely immersed himself in Li Shiqing’s scenario.

Looking at the map, Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy exchanged a look, both startled.

It wasn’t just coincidence or fate, but the intersection Old Zhang circled happened to be the taxi pick-up and drop-off point where they’d gotten off the first time they’d “caught a pervert.” “What if we were on the bus at the time and could have created a disturbance to force it to stop at this location?”

Li Shiqing pointed to that spot and quickly pressed on.

“If we could have made a temporary stop, we could have taken advantage of the opportunity to board when the bus stopped and the doors opened. However, it would have been extremely difficult to simultaneously subdue the driver and the suspect carrying the bomb. It would have been an unusual stop, and the sudden arrival of several people could have easily alerted the suspect, leading to serious consequences.”

Old Zhang rejected Li Shiqing’s “plan” and offered a solution.

“So, if it were me, and I had learned you had a way to cause a disturbance, the correct course of action would have been to teach you to stall between the first and second stops, delaying the bus’s arrival.”

Old Zhang pointed to “Yanjiang East Road Station.”

“If we can successfully delay the bus until they arrive at this station, we can disguise ourselves as ordinary passengers and board the bus from there.”

“Once a police officer disguised as an ordinary passenger boards the bus, we can position ourselves based on the suspect’s location, subdue them at the perfect opportunity, and seize the pressure cooker carrying the explosive.”

Cool!

Ask the police officer! It was definitely a good idea!

The two youths’s eyes lit up.

“But, but!”

Old Zhang, seeing the two youths seemed excited about this outcome, couldn’t help but throw a bucket of cold water on them.

“In my years of experience handling cases, I’ve learned one thing: no matter how perfect a plan is, all sorts of complications will arise during execution…”

“The greatest difficulty and potential complications with your proposed scenario lie in how to control a moving bus. In my opinion, even if we police can successfully board the bus and seize the pressure cooker, it doesn’t guarantee we can simultaneously control the driver.”

Old Zhang shook his head. “The driver controls the steering wheel, the brakes, and the accelerator, effectively controlling the lives of everyone on the bus. Furthermore, he’s a dangerous individual intent on ‘mutual destruction.’ Even the slightest misstep in the arrest process could result in the destruction of both the bus and the people involved.”

As Old Zhang’s “explanation” unfolded, the emotions of Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy, which had just heated up at the discovery of the answer, gradually cooled with the cold water Old Zhang poured on them.

“So even if time could be turned back, there’s still no surefire way to resolve this incident?”

Li Shiqing asked dejectedly.

“Little girl, life isn’t a game. Not everything can be redone. Sometimes, a single thought can lead to a result no one wants.”

Old Zhang knew they were trying to find an “answer” to comfort themselves. But the truth was, even if their assumptions were to happen to him, a veteran of the criminal investigation, he couldn’t guarantee a 100% solution.

“I don’t know how many comrades have died in the line of duty because of that slight change. Many of them are smarter than me, and many are stronger. But intelligence and strength are useless in certain situations. Sometimes, it really is just a little bit of ‘luck’ that counts.”

“What if it’s like playing a game, and you can try again and again?”

Bespectacled Boy suddenly asked, his mind stirring. “What if we could keep ‘correcting’ and ‘trying’…”

“Haha, you two really have a vivid imagination!”

Old Zhang was amused by Bespectacled Boy’s “what if.” Now he was certain the two youths were joking, and the atmosphere, which had just been dull, suddenly lightened.

“If we can try again and again, then of course we can ‘correct’! As long as the plan is meticulous, the execution is perfect, and we can successfully subdue the driver, we’ll eventually succeed in stopping this bombing.”

“The key lies with the driver. As long as we can control him and prevent him from having any self-destructive thoughts, there’s a good chance of success.”

Old Zhang pointed out the key point.

“Therefore, it’s crucial to understand the driver’s and his wife’s motivations.”

Just as they were discussing this, the police officer named “Fangzi” knocked on the door.

“Old Zhang, check this out!”

The phone he held was playing a news clip from several years ago.

“Four years ago today, at exactly 1:45 p.m., driver Wang Xingde and his wife, Tao Yinghong’s, only daughter was involved in a bus accident on the cross-river bridge and died instantly!”

CONTENT END 34

chapters.title: The Twentieth Cycle (Six)
chapters.content:
Once they had found the victim’s name and family situation, it was easy for the police to investigate her life story. It didn’t take long before they had the story of Wang Xingde’s family on their desks.

Their story wasn’t complicated, actually.

Wang Xingde had an only daughter named Wang Mengmeng, who had come to W City from her hometown in S Province to attend college. She had previously studied at W University.

One day a few years ago, Wang Mengmeng accidentally missed her stop on Bus 45 to Jiangbei District. To avoid wasting time, she demanded to get off the bus abruptly. To avoid disrupting normal operation, the driver illegally let her off at a spot where there was no platform. As a result, she was run over by a dump truck while crossing to the sidewalk on a bridge.

This traffic accident wasn’t a serious one, and the responsibility lay largely on Wang Mengmeng herself. Even though Wang Xingde’s wife, Tao Yinghong, traveled to W City several times to “seek justice” for her daughter, the court ultimately ruled that the dump truck and the bus company were only secondarily responsible. However, because this incident was so regrettable, the other two responsible parties, out of compassion, compensated Tao Yinghong’s family financially.

Wang Xingde was a truck driver who worked interprovincially, often away from home. Because his wife was a teacher, their daughter’s life and education naturally fell entirely in the hands of her mother. It was easy to imagine the time and energy Tao Yinghong devoted to her only child. After her daughter’s accident, she was devastated.

When the accident first happened, she insisted the bus company be held responsible, leading to several heated clashes. Fortunately, the company’s manager exercised reasonable restraint and prevented the situation from escalating to a more serious outcome. He also prevented Tao Yinghong from meeting the driver and even instructed the company to conceal the driver’s information. As an outsider, Tao Yinghong ultimately never met the driver in person.

Later, Wang Xingde, who was out on business, received the news and rushed to W City. After mediation by various parties, he was able to bring back his wife, accept compensation, and handle the child’s funeral.

“That’s not right. If Wang Xingde had already accepted the outcome, then why did he and his wife go to W City to seek revenge?”

Old Zhang flipped through the copy of the judgment for Wang Mengmeng’s traffic accident, looking at Wang Xingde’s signature below. He asked in confusion, “Forget about Tao Yinghong. Wang Xingde was a truck driver and should have known the danger of his daughter getting off the bus. The primary responsibility for the accident lies with Wang Mengmeng.”

“The matter was resolved at the time, and they returned home. But after this incident at home, Wang Xingde felt deeply guilty and even quit his job at the transportation company, saying he wanted to be home with his wife. Tao Yinghong also returned to work at Q City No. 1 Middle School three months after their daughter’s death. While this incident is regrettable, they will eventually return to normal life…”

Fangzi, who had been running around outside, took a swig of water and continued, “But by some strange coincidence, a TV station broadcast her daughter’s story.”

“Huh? Why broadcast this?”

The people in the office were stunned.

“Aren’t there those bus accident compilations that try to convince people to obey traffic rules, the kind that show all sorts of traffic accidents? The dump truck that hit the person recorded the entire incident with its dashcam. The owner later uploaded the video online, and because it was so clear and horrific, someone edited it into a video clip.”

Fangzi sighed.

“You can imagine a mother at home, nearly maddened by hearing her daughter was killed in an accident. Just as she was calming down, she suddenly saw on TV how her daughter was run over and killed…”

“That’s not all. Many bloggers reposted the compilation online, not even blurring the girl’s face. The moment she was hit is crystal clear. Especially since Wang Mengmeng’s accident was the most intense and bloody, it immediately became a hot topic, with headlines like ‘Don’t Seek Death, Don’t Die Series.'”

Upon hearing Fangzi’s findings, Old Zhang pursed his lips. His expression shifted from his earlier gentleness to a serious, almost terrifying one.

“This video kept getting circulated and ended up in their local media. A reporter discovered that the girl in the video was from their city. Somehow, they managed to find out from Q City No. 1 Middle School what Tao Yinghong thought about the incident and asked her if she would provide traffic safety education to her students in the future to prevent such disasters from happening again…”

“That’s too much.”

Bespectacled Boy frowned and said disapprovingly, “What kind of reporter is this?”

“According to information relayed by the local police, although this interview wasn’t released, it still impacted Tao Yinghong’s life.”

Fangzi shook his head and sighed, “Tao Yinghong’s daughter got into trouble. Originally, everyone just knew she was in a bus accident, and they were quite sympathetic. They tried to comfort and counsel her and tried their best to distract her during their work. Her psychological trauma was almost healed, but now this reporter is doing it in front of the whole office.” With the teacher in the office and a reporter chasing her for an interview, everyone knew her daughter’s bus accident was her fault. It was inevitable that gossip would spread behind her back, much like the video’s title, ‘Don’t be stupid, you won’t die.’

“Plus, some students and teachers were curious and searched for the video. They were all high school students, and many had cellphones, so they downloaded the video and circulated it around the class and school as gossip. You can imagine the situation…”

The task force office suddenly fell into an eerie silence.

“Not long after the interview, a violent conflict erupted between Tao Yinghong and a student. According to the school, Tao Yinghong was the first to hit the student on the head with a chair. However, considering the incident at her home and the fact that the student responsible for circulating the video also bore significant responsibility, neither the school nor the student’s parents held Tao Yinghong responsible for the injury.”

In the office, only Fangzi’s voice could be heard. “But since then, Tao Yinghong’s mental state has deteriorated day by day. She often loses consciousness or becomes inexplicably violent and hurtful. This situation has lasted for nearly a year.”

“Later, she resigned from the school, claiming she had to leave the area with her husband.” After her resignation, the school quickly approved it, considering her condition unsuitable for continued teaching. To protect the school’s reputation, the school never disclosed her pre-resignation situation to students or the public.

“But that doesn’t warrant revenge on society, does it?”

Officer Du asked suspiciously from the other end of the group call. “If it were simply public pressure, there’s no reason why they would sell their property and belongings to work in W City for so many years, only to choose this path.”

“That’s part of the story.”

Fangzi finished his glass of water and poured another. “It’s said that… when the incident first caused a stir at school, Tao Yinghong repeatedly stated emotionally that her daughter wouldn’t demand to get off the bus simply because she’d missed her stop. She must have been feeling unwell or had experienced something unpleasant on the bus, and she wouldn’t have demanded to get off without a reason.”

“We also sent someone to interview the person responsible for the incident at the bus company. They stated that Tao Yinghong had repeatedly raised this point during the dispute with the bus company regarding her daughter’s accident, arguing that her daughter wouldn’t demand to get off the bus without a reason and wanting to confront the driver. However, given her intense emotions at the time, out of concern for the driver’s personal safety, the person in charge disagreed.”

“I was concerned that Tao Yinghong’s suspicions were correct, so I went to the traffic police station to retrieve the accident report. Although Tao Yinghong believed her daughter must have gotten out of the bus for some reason, this was merely her subjective assumption, lacking any supporting evidence. The in-bus interviews also revealed nothing unusual. Just because her mother believed this, Wang Mengmeng, who voluntarily requested to get out of the bus, shouldn’t be excused from primary responsibility. Furthermore, after reading the accident report, Wang Xingde accepted the findings.”

The whole thing sounded complicated, but the reality was actually quite simple.

“The bus company driver who illegally let a passenger off the bus was also punished and disqualified from driving. He later resigned and left the area. His current job and location are still under investigation.”

“Perhaps Tao Yinghong isn’t trying to determine who was responsible but rather to understand her daughter’s motive for getting off the bus!”

After hearing Fangzi’s findings, Officer Du lamented, “The bus company manager is clueless. They simply believe less is more! A life is at stake. If they don’t explain the situation clearly to the mother, will she accept it?!”

“I’m afraid even if he explained everything, Tao Yinghong won’t believe it. Mothers protect their children.”

Old Zhang murmured with a heavy heart, “It’s been so long since the incident, and the child has been buried for so many years. Why bother? Sigh…”

“So what was Wang Xingde’s situation with this whole incident? Was he at odds with his wife?”

Officer Jiang, who was collecting evidence on the other end of the line, asked.

“Why did he become a bus driver?”

“Local police also interviewed Wang Xingde’s relatives and friends in Q City. Most people thought he was a nice guy, gentle and patient, never getting into conflicts. He was just a bit cowardly and often got the short end of the stick in the bus fleet.”

Everyone knew what “nice guy” meant; it was often a substitute for “overly nice guy.”

“Because of this, he didn’t firmly stand by his wife’s side. After being persuaded by the bus company and family relatives and worried that his wife, Tao Yinghong, might get into trouble as a result of this, he chose to sign the agreement and take Tao Yinghong home first.”

“Because of this, Tao Yinghong never forgave Wang Xingde. Later, after the school incident, word spread that Wang Xingde was selling his house and wanted to take his wife away from this sad place. Although his relatives felt sorry, they expressed understanding. “

The pain of families who have lost their only child was unimaginable to ordinary people.

“At this point in the investigation, the situation was relatively clear. Furthermore, Officers Jiang and Du have uncovered a large amount of direct evidence in Tao Yinghong’s workplace and residence, sufficient to form a complete chain of evidence. At this stage, the case was essentially solved.”

“Our investigation revealed that Tao Yinghong, leveraging her position, purchased numerous banned chemicals online. She previously co-led a high school chemistry club and later worked as a quality inspector at a chemical factory, giving her ample access to chemicals. During holidays, she would bring the contraband hidden at the factory home and assemble it in her basement garage. Large quantities of leftover raw materials were left at both sites.”

Officer Jiang said, “Wang Xingde had been living in the company’s single dormitory. No one knew he had a wife, and his colleagues assumed his wife and children were back home.”

“Based on the written drafts Tao Yinghong left in the garage, we can roughly infer that they had a premeditated plan to detonate the bomb at 1:45 p.m. today, the same day and location where her daughter died.”

“Why wait so long?” Old Zhang was particularly sensitive to this number. “Does it have any special meaning?”

“If the local police hadn’t visited, we’d never have guessed it!”

Fangzi couldn’t help but quip when he brought this up. “There’s a custom in Wang Xingde’s hometown: birthdays are celebrated according to the solar calendar, while memorials for the deceased are held according to the lunar calendar.”

“Her daughter died on the 30th day of a leap month, a date that only happens once every few years. It just happened to fall this year. When the local police visited Wang Mengmeng’s uncle’s home, her relatives were preparing incense, candles, and offerings for her death. They said her deceased niece only lives on this ‘big day’ once every three or four years, and she must be starving, so they were burning extra food and supplies. The local police thought this was a crucial clue, so they sent us this information.”

Now, all the pieces of the puzzle fell into place.

Because their daughter’s death anniversary doesn’t fall every year, Wang Xingde and his wife chose this year’s anniversary as the time for their operation.

To successfully achieve their goal of “driving the bus to a specific location at a specific time,” Wang Xingde and his wife traveled to W City, trained at a labor dispatch company, and diligently worked to become a bus driver for this route, preparing for this day ahead.

His wife, meanwhile, spent the past few years secretly preparing the most important prop for the entire operation—a bomb.

On the appointed day, they risked everything, choosing this very way to depart the world with their daughter.

Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun understood why they couldn’t find any specific information online.

The “beginning” of this incident wasn’t a major incident, or even significant compared to other major incidents like arson and rear-end collisions that had occurred at this location.

If it hadn’t been included in a bus accident compilation, the story of a girl’s death on this bridge might have faded from people’s memory, like the gossip most people read after dinner.

Regardless of why the girl got off the bus, she was now dead, and her parents had also passed away in this devastating accident. The truth, and their thoughts, was now lost.

As the police pieced together the facts bit by bit, those who learned the truth could only sigh at this regrettable beginning and lament this heartbreaking ending.

》》》

Based on the clues provided by Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun, the police quickly investigated the entire case and provided relevant evidence. The Trace Analysis Department extracted the explosive components from the wreckage at the explosion site and found a match with the items left in Tao Yinghong’s garage, confirming the physical evidence.

Later, the police obtained a list of chemicals Tao Yinghong had purchased through her online transaction records. Following this lead, they apprehended and arrested several suppliers of banned chemicals.

Wang Xingde’s company also confirmed that Wang Xingde had chosen to work during his shift and had been doing so for over two years.

This route was busiest and most demanding during weekends and holidays, and many bus drivers were reluctant to take on these shifts. However, Wang Xingde, known for his hard work and lack of family responsibilities, volunteered to drive during these hours. The bus company annually awarded him the title of “Model Worker,” and he gradually became a veteran employee on the route.

After the incident, few colleagues believed that Wang Xingde, a gentle, considerate, and honest man, could have done such a thing. The supervisor in charge of his daughter’s case couldn’t even remember what the girl’s father looked like, as Wang Xingde was a man with little presence and no personality.

After deducing the motive for the crime and uncovering the perpetrator’s complete crime process, the case was finally solved.

After understanding the full details of the case, the police held a press conference with several reputable mainstream media outlets, providing information and explanations on the case and officially declaring it closed.

The task force took just five hours from accepting the case to solving it. This was not only logical but also based on sufficient evidence and clear facts. This efficiency and speed earned praise from all sides and sparked heated online discussion about the efficiency of the local criminal police team.

Meanwhile, countless online media outlets and netizens began digging deeper into the “accident” that year, perhaps brewing even more heated discussions…

But this was no longer the issue that concerned Xiao Heyun and Li Shiqing.

After receiving their desired results and understanding the driver’s motives for assisting the woman, the two youths, as key witnesses in the case, completed a full statement and went through the necessary procedures before finally being allowed to leave.

“Thank you again for your help.”

It was Old Zhang who greeted them and escorted them from the Criminal Police Detachment.

“I’m so sorry. I originally wanted to treat you to a meal, but I had so much to do later. So busy late at night, I can only treat you to a boxed lunch…”

“It’s okay, it’s okay. The lunchbox was delicious, too.”

Bespectacled Boy and Li Shiqing quickly expressed their indifference.

“Do you need me to take you home?”

Old Zhang checked the time. It was already nine o’clock.

“No, we’ll take a walk back.”

Li Shiqing shook her head, making a bitter face. “I don’t want to take any vehicle for now.”

The memories of these rides were too horrific.

Whether it was the terrifying bus, the intimidating police car, or even the taxi that kept broadcasting the accident scene, they all left a psychological scar on her.

She would rather ride a shared bike than ride in any bus again.

Bespectacled Boy who had been accompanying her chose to go back with his friends.

“Okay, be careful on your way back.”

Old Zhang smiled understandingly.

“Officer Zhang…”

Just as the two were about to part, Li Shiqing hesitated for a moment, then suddenly called out to Officer Zhang. “What if? I mean, what if…”

She paused, and seeing Bespectacled Boy’s expression of “What are you thinking now?”, she began to raise another series of “what ifs” with this officer they trusted.

“What if, today, you were sitting in your office and suddenly received a text message from a stranger informing you that there was a bomb on a bus, and that it would explode at 1:45 p.m., and that they urgently needed your help? Would you help immediately?”

Old Zhang was stunned for a moment, thought for a moment, and nodded.

“I would,” he answered firmly.

Bespectacled Boy’s expression of concern for Li Shiqing suddenly turned into a look of surprise.

“If someone intentionally made a false police report, wasting scarce police resources, we will find them no matter how they try to cover it up. The law will hold them accountable and make them pay a substantial price.”

Old Zhang said, “But if this is true, it could save countless lives. Compared to this, the risk of wasting police resources is nothing.”

“What’s more, even if it’s just an ordinary person, a stranger, as long as someone asks the police for help, we will provide assistance without hesitation. That’s why we choose to wear this uniform.”

Old Zhang smiled.

“You may think I’m just talking some high-sounding official rhetoric, but we really will do it. There’s no doubt about it.”

“I have no doubt. I believe you are such good police officers.”

Li Shiqing smiled brightly and took out her phone. “Officer Zhang, could you please leave us your contact information? If we think of anything we’ve missed, we can contact you.”

CONTENT END 35

chapters.title: The Twentieth Cycle (Part 7)
chapters.content:
After leaving the Criminal Police Detachment, the two stood at the intersection where they had gotten off the bus, somewhat unsure of where to go.

“Now that we’ve found the truth, will we still be trapped in this cycle?”

Bespectacled Boy, startled awake by the cold night wind, sighed and asked.

“I think ‘finding the truth’ isn’t the solution to breaking the cycle, but if that’s enough, that would be great.”

Li Shiqing thought optimistically, “Maybe when we wake up, we can go to school or work?”

“I hope so.”

Bespectacled Boy smiled, saying this, but in his heart, he felt that he was being a little too optimistic.

The night breeze ruffled Li Shiqing’s hair, and the streetlights cast a warm, dim glow over the two young people.

The darkness in the distance seemed shrouded in a hazy fog, with the occasional flash of bus lights piercing the silence.

They stood in the soft, dusky glow and began to discuss where to go.

“How do we get back? Do we really have to walk?”

Li Shiqing had just used this excuse to decline Old Zhang’s offer to drive them.

So the two youths took out their phones to calculate how long it would take to walk back, then silently put the phones back.

“I think…”

Bespectacled Boy coughed dryly. “Look, our last two loops were both due to accidents. You fell off a chair and hit your head, and I rolled down a slope and hit the back of my head. This means that in a loop, once we lose consciousness, we’re very likely to be trapped in it again…”

“Then let’s find a safe place and stay up all night.”

Compared to being trapped in a loop in the bus, Li Shiqing said she could handle staying up all night.

While discussing whether to stay up late, the two of them had a disagreement.

“Should we go to an internet cafe? There are those little private rooms with sofas where you can sleep.”

As a programmer, the first thing that came to mind when it came to staying up late was an internet cafe.

“The sofas in internet cafes are so filthy!”

But as a girl who didn’t play games, Li Shiqing couldn’t accept that.

“Besides, internet cafes often have all sorts of disputes. If someone gets into a fight or an argument, and it gets to us, wouldn’t that be disastrous? If this keeps happening, shouldn’t we find a quieter place where we won’t be disturbed and discuss our next steps?”

“Oh, okay, you’re right.”

Bespectacled Boy agreed with his companion’s suggestion, somewhat disappointed.

“Then where should we go?”

Li Shiqing glanced into the distance. In the darkness, the illuminated sign on a tall building stood out.

“Do you have your ID?”

She suddenly asked.

“Huh? I brought it…”

Bespectacled Boy nodded blankly.

“Let’s go!”

Five minutes later, Li Shiqing led Bespectacled Boy to the entrance of a hotel near the Criminal Police Detachment.

Bespectacled Boy had been skeptical to begin with, and when he finally reached the hotel entrance, his face flushed.

“Go, go to the hotel?”

He stammered, “The two of us?”

“Of course we’re staying in the hotel. What better option is there? Do you really want to walk home?”

Li Shiqing gave him a strange look. “Besides, this hotel is quite upscale. There’s gated access, and it’s right next to the Criminal Police Detachment. Safe, absolutely.”

If she could just spend a peaceful night, maybe she could escape this cycle!

“Then, let’s go in?”

Bespectacled Boy couldn’t tell whether he was feeling more nervous or shy. Seeing that the only people entering the hotel were couples, his blush deepened.

Li Shiqing, on the other hand, walked into the hotel lobby without a trace of shyness and confidently went to the front desk to check in.

Bespectacled Boy, carrying a bag, followed Li Shiqing, watching his companion go through the paperwork with a bit of unease.

“One or two?”

The front desk clerk asked.

“Two!”

“One!”

“Why two? Is it expensive?”

Li Shiqing lowered her voice. “This hotel isn’t cheap! We’re just looking for a place to stay up late and discuss things, not to rest!”

The front desk clerk glanced at them with a strange expression. A group of young people waiting in line behind them began to snicker, and a girl whispered something in the boy’s ear.

Bespectacled Boy, embarrassed by the look, muttered in a defensive tone, “This, this isn’t for your reputation…”

“It’s already this late, and you’re still worried about that!”

Li Shiqing glared at him, turned her head, and said to the front desk, “One room, a quiet one, away from the elevator, okay.”

The receptionist at the front desk calmly checked them in and took their ID cards. When it came time to pay, Bespectacled Boy insisted on paying.

“You don’t even have a job yet; how can I ask you to pay…even for AA!”

Seeing Li Shiqing was about to transfer money to him, Bespectacled Boy got anxious and pulled her hand.

“That’s enough; don’t be so serious!”

Li Shiqing was stunned. Seeing the young couple in line behind them looking at them with strange expressions, she gave up and put her phone away.

After completing the check-in process, the staff member, who had been expressionless until then, handed the room card to Bespectacled Boy and suddenly smiled at him.

“It’s done. I wish you a pleasant stay tonight.”

“Huh? …Thank you?”

Bespectacled Boy strangely understood something from that smile. His already hot face burned all the way to his neck. He followed Li Shiqing into the elevator as if fleeing in panic.

The room was on the top floor.

Li Shiqing came from a well-off family. When booking the room for two people, she sought both quiet and spaciousness, so she booked a rooftop room with a view, which cost quite a bit.

When Bespectacled Boy said he’d cover for the room, she felt a little guilty. She should have known better than to ask for so much.

When they arrived at the room, Li Shiqing changed her shoes and checked the room for any potential hazards. Finding the plumbing and electricity were working properly, and nothing seemed amiss, she breathed a sigh of relief.

“It’s okay. I was just worried about any complications. Just in case, let’s just skip showering tonight and stay in the room. Let’s not have it be like a horror movie, with someone tripping in the middle of a shower or getting a power outage…”

It was his first time in a hotel with a girl, and Bespectacled Boy had initially felt a little uneasy. But as he listened to Li Shiqing’s serious discussion about how to handle the situation, his hesitation and fantasies gradually faded, and he nodded.

“Okay, I’ll make two cups of instant coffee to keep you from getting sleepy.”

“No, boiling water is dangerous!”

Li Shiqing hurriedly stopped him. “Just drink some mineral water and chat!”

Since getting off the bus, the two of them looked as if they could finally relax, but in reality, they were already on edge, their past experiences still leaving an indelible scar on them.

After a long day of tossing and turning, both were a little tired. To avoid falling asleep on the softer sofas, neither dared to lie down, so they leaned on the floor-to-ceiling windows. Each of them held a bottle of mineral water and began to chat.

“This hotel in W City is much bigger than the one I stayed in before traveling with my parents. The luxury room is just different… but it’s too expensive for you… You really don’t want me to transfer the money? I was the one who suggested it!”

Li Shiqing’s upbringing made her a little uneasy about taking advantage of others.

“My parents give me enough pocket money, so don’t be polite.”

Bespectacled Boy had just moved to this city and was working as a programmer. Didn’t he just spend half a month’s living expenses on someone else?

“My income isn’t that low.”

Understanding Li Shiqing’s meaning, Bespectacled Boy was at a loss whether to laugh or cry.

“Besides, if I can really break free from this cycle, even if I have to live on coarse food for a month, I’ll be happy!”

“That’s right.”

Seeing that Bespectacled Boy didn’t seem to care, Li Shiqing stopped dwelling on the issue and got down to business.

“Did you write down the phone number Officer Zhang gave you?”

“I did.”

He fluently recited a long string of numbers.

“Me too.”

Li Shiqing took out her phone and asked Bespectacled Boy for a charging cable. While it was charging, she turned on the speaker and played the recording she had secretly recorded at the police station.

“Then let’s discuss our next strategy.”

As they discussed the case at the police station, they chatted sporadically. Li Shiqing had a lot of thoughts running through her mind, but they all flashed through her mind. Under the circumstances, she couldn’t ask or remember anything, so she secretly recorded the entire conversation, hoping to find a quiet place to discuss it with her companions later.

“First of all, even Officer Zhang said half an hour is too short…”

Bespectacled Boy continued to analyze the details, drawing the topographic map that Officer Zhang had drawn earlier from memory.

“According to his instructions, we need to create a commotion between Gangwu New Village Station and Yanjiang East Road Station, forcing the driver to slow down or even stop for a while.”

“Then let’s use the ‘catch the pervert’ method.”

Li Shiqing thought for a moment and suggested, “We’ve tried many methods before, but none have ever succeeded in getting the driver to stop. Only this method has gotten the driver to stop, which means it has a high success rate.”

“Okay, then, when we get to this location, we’ll start causing a commotion…”

Bespectacled Boy marked the topographic map while comparing it to the map on his phone. “Our goal is to get the driver to slow down or even pull over temporarily, but we can’t get out of the bus. The situation could be a bit chaotic, so we have to hold on!”

“Wait for the police. Once the casually dressed officers get on board, we won’t sit in the back; we’ll go to the front…”

Bespectacled Boy drew a cross in the front row. “We’ll be responsible for ‘stabilizing’ the driver. If necessary, we’ll try to pull the handbrake and force him to stop.”

“I think now that we understand the driver’s motive, maybe we can try to ‘persuade’ him.”

Li Shiqing, however, held a different view. “Officer Zhang said that even the police would have difficulty stopping both the aunt and uncle simultaneously, because the driver holds the lives of everyone on the bus in his hands. If…”

“Li Shiqing, I know you feel the driver and his wife deserve sympathy for what they’ve experienced, but I think you shouldn’t hold out too much hope of persuading the driver.”

Li Shiqing understood the logic, so she simply sighed.

“They’re adults; they know what they’re doing. After all, they’ve been planning this for years, so it’s unlikely they’ll give up just because of a few words.”

Bespectacled Boy, worried she’d soften her stance again, said sternly, “Besides, if the police’s intervention could sway him, the driver wouldn’t have refused to open the door when we pretended to be plainclothes officers. After all, they’re a couple; he might be soft-hearted with his wife, but he might not be with you.”

As soon as he mentioned this, Li Shiqing could almost hear the woman’s heartbreaking sobs.

At the time, they didn’t know what she’d been through; they just assumed she wasn’t mentally sound and her cries were excessive.

Thinking back now, she was sobbing and cursing at her husband, probably because she mistakenly thought he’d called the police when he got on the bus, which was why the plainclothes officers who knew about the situation were on the bus and captured her.

If the driver had hesitated, the moment his wife was apprehended and the bomb was taken, he should have given up and surrendered to the police.

But he didn’t. He chose to stop and close the door.

What was the driver thinking as he stopped?

They didn’t know.

So they couldn’t gamble.

“Okay, you’re right.”

Li Shiqing agreed but felt a pang of discomfort. “Our priority is to assist the police in subduing the driver.”

Over the next few hours, they meticulously refined every detail of their “operation,” including what to say and what to do. They even rehearsed it in their room, like two actors reviewing a script late at night.

During this time, Officer Zhang and Li Shiqing’s roommates called to inquire about their situation and to check on them to know they were safe.

When Officer Zhang learned that Li Shiqing was staying at a nearby hotel, he said nothing, simply asking her to get some rest.

Li Shiqing’s roommates, however, were concerned about her mental state and chatted for a long time. When they heard she wouldn’t return to her dorm room, they became even more anxious.

Li Shiqing had gone through this cycle so many times, but this was the first time she felt so relaxed.

Listening to her roommates’ worried greetings, familiar voices echoing in her ears, and long phone calls, she felt as if she had returned to the time before she boarded the bus.

Every day used to be comfortable and relaxing for her…

Perhaps it was because she’d been so tense all day, and once she relaxed, she felt incredibly sleepy. So, when Bespectacled Boy came out of the bathroom after washing his face with cold water for the umpteenth time, he found Li Shiqing asleep by the window, phone in hand.

“…”

Bespectacled Boy looked at the bottle of mineral water he had taken out of the refrigerator, intending to let Li Shiqing wash her face, and chuckled self-deprecatingly.

He walked to the floor-to-ceiling window, ready to nudge Li Shiqing awake.

“Forget it…”

Seeing Li Shiqing’s exhausted face, he shook his head gently, carefully removed the hung-up phone from her hand, muted it, and placed it next to her.

Since he hadn’t entered the loop yet, Li Shiqing’s sleep shouldn’t matter, right?

“Should I let her sleep more comfortably?”

He thought, reaching out to carry Li Shiqing to bed.

But after a moment’s hesitation, he pulled his hand back.

Finally, Bespectacled Boy chose to sit beside her, carefully tilting her head against his shoulder so her face wouldn’t rest against the cold window.

Outside the floor-to-ceiling window, the cityscape gradually faded into darkness, no longer the vibrant lights and bustling traffic of earlier. It seemed as if all this was just a spectacle, a spectacle that would eventually end with the passage of time…

“If only there were still tomorrow…”

Xiao Heyun muttered to himself, gazing out at the night view outside, his eyes scanning the reflections of the two people leaning against each other in the glass.

Afraid he’d fall asleep too, he pulled out his phone and began browsing the online news following today’s case, hoping to gain more information.

Flipping through pages…

》》》

Waking up on the bus at the familiar station announcement, Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun exchanged glances and exclaimed in unison…

“Damn it!”

“Did I fall asleep last night?”

Li Shiqing wiped the corner of her mouth, feeling as if something was there.

“I saw you were sleeping so soundly I didn’t have the heart to wake you…”

Bespectacled Boy explained weakly.

“So what happened to you?”

“I don’t know. I was just looking at my phone, and… uh…”

His mind was hazy about that memory.

“Forget it, it’s fate!”

Li Shiqing looked at the familiar carriage and resigned herself to her fate.

“It’s good to get some sleep…”

She took a deep breath.

“I’ll have the energy to work!”

Author’s Note: Mini-Theatre: But after a moment’s hesitation, he pulled his hand back. Bespectacled Boy: (Inner thoughts) Forget it, mention the “bed,” hold it up, and then it’ll go through the review process. This chapter is easy to lock.

CONTENT END 36

chapters.title: The Twenty-First Cycle
chapters.content:
“Alright.”

Completely editing the message as quickly as possible, Li Shiqing sent it to Officer Zhang’s phone.

[ There’s a bomb on Bus 45 that just left Gangwu New Village. License plate number XXX. The woman in the flowered shirt sitting in the sixth row, near the door, is carrying a pressure cooker containing a bomb. The driver is an accomplice. The pressure cooker will explode if the valve is pulled. The timer is set at 1:45 p.m. Please immediately dispatch plainclothes police officers to the Yanjiang East Road station for support. Please subdue both the driver and the woman. I’ll try to slow the driver down. Please don’t alarm them before taking action. ]

After sending the message, she called Officer Zhang again.

After answering the phone, she heard Officer Zhang on the other end ask,

“Who are you? Did you send that text just now…”

“I’m in the bus right now, so it’s inconvenient for me to make a phone call.”

Li Shiqing tried to answer the phone more naturally. “Time is running out. Please follow the instructions in the text message. I’m not a scammer. If I am, I’m willing to bear any consequences.”

She was afraid to waste precious time by continuing, so she hung up.

Li Shiqing nervously gazed out the window at the scenery. When they reached the location they had agreed on last night, she quickly nudged Bespectacled Boy’s arm to warn him.

“We’re here!”

This was the flattest part of the road between the two stops. There were few cars and pedestrians, so if cars slowed down, accidents wouldn’t be likely.

Bespectacled Boy extended his hand knowingly.

“Pervert!”

Li Shiqing screamed, slapped the back of his hand, and yelled.

“Driver Uncle, there’s a pervert in the bus!”

This time, Li Shiqing specifically called out the driver for help.

“What’s going on?”

He slowed down while driving and turned to take a look.

“Driver Uncle, the guy next to me groped me!”

Li Shiqing, familiar with the situation, quickly got into the act.

“Can you please turn around and go to the police station?”

He couldn’t do that; he’d have to turn around.

“You can’t turn around here!”

As expected, the driver had no intention of doing so.

Then, as before, they argued: one insisted he had touched her, the other insisted he hadn’t. They argued all the way to the driver’s side, insisting he judge.

The driver wasn’t particularly concerned about whether Bespectacled Boy had touched anyone. He simply shouted irritably, “If you want to argue, go to the back and do it. Don’t bother me driving!”

“Who’s arguing? I’m just trying to reason with her, aren’t I?”

Bespectacled Boy continued to huddle near the driver, refusing to leave.

“Besides, who said I touched her? Did anyone see it?”

Bespectacled Boy raised his voice. “There’s no witness. Just because she said it, you want to kick me out?”

He put on a scoundrelly face and shouted into the bus:

“Did you see it? Who saw me touching her?”

As with the previous times, most people were either sleeping or resting. Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun were sitting in the back, so almost no one saw anything. Bespectacled Boy asked, and everyone shook their heads.

When Li Shiqing asked for help, the passengers in the bus all said they didn’t know and didn’t want to get involved.

Although it was just an act, Li Shiqing couldn’t help but sigh inwardly when she saw this helpless situation again.

As her mood sank, the girl, standing next to the driver with her head bowed, looked particularly pitiful.

“Hey, who would blackmail someone with something like this for no reason? You don’t look like a rich guy, so they wouldn’t blackmail you if they wanted to.”

The old man selling melons shook his head.

“If you really did it, apologize to the girl and explain it nicely!”

Bespectacled Boy, of course, denied it.

Seeing the driver still driving, with no sign of slowing down, Li Shiqing gritted her teeth and once again pleaded with him to stop, using the “get out and call the police” tactic.

“The next stop is almost here, little girl; please wait a moment.”

The driver glanced at the two young people and spoke quietly.

“Get off at the next stop.”

Not only was Li Shiqing stunned, but even Bespectacled Boy standing next to her was a little confused.

“I want to get off now.”

Li Shiqing glanced outside the bus, noticing that the speed hadn’t slowed much, and she became anxious.

“I can’t stand being with someone like that for even a minute!”

The passengers in the bus were getting annoyed as the two youths were making more and more noise next to the driver.

“What’s wrong with you? You’re interfering with the driver’s driving. He’s going to have an accident!”

The cowardly uncle with the keys shouted louder than anyone else.

“Can’t you solve any problems yourself? Don’t you have a cellphone? Can’t you call the police?”

As soon as the cowardly uncle said, “You can call the police yourself,” the driver suddenly slowed down.

“Then I’ll call…”

Seeing something was going to happen, Li Shiqing pretended to pull out her phone and checked the time.

It was 1:25 p.m., a few minutes before Officer Zhang’s expected fastest response time.

“Forget it, I’ll pull over and let you get out.”

Seeing Li Shiqing about to call the police, the driver suddenly agreed and slowly pulled the bus to the side of the road.

Bespectacled Boy and Li Shiqing saw that the driver had indeed slowed down and stopped, and they were both delighted.

Li Shiqing walked slowly to the rear door but didn’t get out immediately.

The driver waited for a moment, then saw the girl didn’t get off. He frowned and asked, “What’s going on? Didn’t you say you were getting off?”

“Driver Uncle, I’m not getting off.”

Li Shiqing shamelessly checked the time on her phone while shouting to the front.

“I’ve thought about it. It might be too late to get a taxi if I get off. Could you please take me to Jiangbei? I’m in a hurry.”

“What the hell!”

The driver was clearly annoyed, but he said nothing. He quickly closed the back door and drove off again.

After this scene, although the two didn’t get off, it was difficult for them to sit together. Li Shiqing chose an empty seat near the back door, while Bespectacled Boy, facing the disdainful gazes of many, sat in front of her.

After this delay, they successfully extended the time between the two stops by five or six minutes. It was now 1:29 p.m.

According to Old Zhang, if they responded as quickly as possible, they should have arrived at Yanjiang East Road Station by 1:30 p.m.

Perhaps because of the delay, the driver drove very fast for the rest of the journey. Within minutes, Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun saw the bus stop ahead and could vaguely make out several figures standing beneath it.

Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy, who had turned his head, exchanged a glance, their eyes gleaming with excitement.

The police had indeed arrived!

On every previous trip, only the masked man had boarded the bus at this station!

They stared out the window, their mouths dry with anxiety as the bus inched closer to Yanjiang East Road Station.

Closer, closer, closer…

“Something’s wrong! Why isn’t the bus slowing down?”

Li Shiqing was the first to notice something was wrong.

She immediately stood up, ran to the back door, and shouted to the driver:

“Driver Uncle, I want to get off! Stop now!”

The bus had already approached the bus stop, and she could even see a familiar figure standing there through the back door window.

Officer Zhang and Officer Jiang, along with two other officers, dressed in casual jackets and disguised as passengers waiting to board the bus, were waiting at the bus stop.

The masked man who had boarded the bus at this stop was nowhere to be seen, presumably persuaded to leave by the police.

“What’s wrong with you today? You’re constantly getting on and off!”

The driver yelled angrily.

“Didn’t you just say you were in a hurry?”

“But there are people getting on!”

Li Shiqing shouted, pointing out the window.

“There’s someone at the bus stop!”

“It’s too late! We’ve wasted too much time on the way. We can’t stop now!”

However, the driver ignored Li Shiqing’s “reminder” and, without even looking back, sped past the stop and headed straight for the intersection before the bridge.

Seeing the driver didn’t even stop, Officer Zhang’s plan proved completely useless, and Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy panicked.

Bespectacled Boy sat in his seat, peeking out the window.

The bus was already some distance from the station. He could vaguely see several police officers who had been at the bus stop hurriedly running forward, shouting something as they chased the bus for a distance.

When they realized the bus showed no sign of stopping, they stopped chasing and turned back toward the road.

“It’s over!”

Li Shiqing’s heart raced. Standing in front of the back door, despair welled up in his heart.

“Why can’t they get on the bus!”

Woo-woo-woo

Just then, a police car bell suddenly rang from behind the bus.

“Pull over! Bus ahead, pull over immediately! Everyone, get off immediately!”

Inside the police car, officers shouted through a loudspeaker at the bus.

Two ordinary-looking cars, their roofs adorned with police lights, sped towards them, attempting to force the bus Li Shiqing and her companions were on to stop.

The two youths were completely stunned.

The piercing wail of a police siren would have been enough to cause panic and disorientation even at ordinary times, let alone at this tense moment.

The passengers panicked as they saw a police car approaching their bus.

“Driver, what’s going on? Pull over!”

“Is there a fugitive on board? Driver, stop the bus!”

Let’s fight!

Bespectacled Boy reacted faster than Li Shiqing, his eyes fixed on the woman in the flowered shirt.

We hadn’t even reached the bridge yet. A bus accident was better than being killed. As long as we could get the bomb out, there was still some time before it exploded!

He raised his head and met Li Shiqing’s gaze, a look of determination in his eyes.

Li Shiqing understood his meaning and nodded. Amid the passengers’ panicked cries, they all rushed towards the woman sitting in the back seat.

Outside the window, two police cars, regardless of the danger, sandwiched the bus from the front and the back, forcing it to slow down and pull over and prohibiting it from driving to the cross-river bridge with heavier traffic.

Just as Li Shiqing grabbed the aunt’s hand, Bespectacled Boy threw himself on her…

But it was too late.

As the driver slammed into the police car in front of him, the woman in the flowery shirt kicked the pressure cooker under the seat with her foot.

Li Shiqing watched helplessly as the pressure-limiting valve of the pressure cooker was knocked off. The red valve rolled onto the floorboards of the bus, and with the vibrations of the collision, it rolled away…

“No!”

Boom!

CONTENT END 37

chapters.title: The Twenty-Second Cycle
chapters.content:
When they woke up again, Li Shiqing’s and Bespectacled Boy’s minds were filled with “???”.

Nothing was more infuriating than having a meticulously planned plan go awry.

“Is he in a hurry to reincarnate?”

Bespectacled Boy looked up at the aunt and driver uncle in front of him, his eyes filled with rare fury.

According to the police investigation, in the years following her daughter’s accident, Aunt Tao Yinghong had clearly become mentally unstable, often falling into fits of rage and losing control. She was also usually aloof and indifferent to others, clearly suffering from an emotional disorder.

But the driver wasn’t like that.

Every time, just when he and Li Shiqing thought the driver could “move on” a little, the driver would give them a harsh rebuke, leaving them dizzy and dazed.

“Isn’t he in a hurry to reincarnate…”

Li Shiqing smacked his head hard, trying to clear his head.

“So what do we do now? We’re stuck in another vicious cycle.”

Bespectacled Boy said coldly, “If we don’t delay at Gangwu New Village Station or Donggang New Village Station, the police won’t be able to get on the bus to help. If we delay, the driver, worried about delaying the scheduled explosion, won’t stop at any station, and the police still won’t be able to get on the bus…”

After so many times, Li Shiqing hadn’t given up hope, but Bespectacled Boy’s suppressed negativity was on the verge of exploding.

Giving hope again and again, and then shattering it again and again—not to mention humans, even gods can’t stand it.

He scoffed.

“So what’s Heaven trying to say? Telling us to stop relying on others and rely on ourselves?”

Aside from the time they got off the bus and she called the police, Bespectacled Boy had never acted like this before. He is simply full of thorns.

“Whatever happens, call the police first.”

Li Shiqing pulled out her phone, preparing to type another text message.

“Don’t try; it’s too late.”

A hand reached out from the side, covering Li Shiqing’s phone.

Li Shiqing looked up, and what struck her mind was her companion’s bloodshot eyes.

Her hand stopped instantly.

Something was wrong with Bespectacled Boy, very wrong.

“Okay.”

She meekly took the phone away.

“I’ll do as you say.”

Nothing was more important than him right now, not even the bus that was about to explode.

Her companion had never shown much of a “personality.” Although he was adept at making suggestions, he didn’t insist on making his own decisions. Instead, he was accustomed to constantly revising his plans according to the team’s needs, like one of those “strategists” often seen in ancient times.

Of the two, she seemed to have the stronger personality and made more decisions, but Li Shiqing knew in her heart that it wasn’t her who had kept them going until now, but Bespectacled Boy’s ever-present, magical, gentle grace.

And she wasn’t the backbone.

If she hadn’t been lucky enough to find a “strategist” teammate, she would have been cannon fodder long ago.

Bespectacled Boy was her spiritual pillar, and he must not fall.

Li Shiqing couldn’t imagine what would become of her if Bespectacled Boy truly had a mental breakdown after repeated cycles, leaving her to cycle through reincarnation alone.

Perhaps it would be a living hell where even suicide was impossible.

Thinking of this, Li Shiqing gently grasped his hand, tightly gripping his cold palm.

“What are you going to do? Let’s figure it out together.”

What he needed now was an outlet to vent.

“Stop thinking about the police. It’s too late.”

Bespectacled Boy no longer expected the police to help him.

The last time, the police hadn’t boarded the bus, decisively choosing to “sacrifice.” Knowing there was a high probability of a bomb on board, they still tried to stop the bus with their police car, simply to prevent it from driving onto the more heavily trafficked cross-river bridge.

Didn’t those officers know they would die if there was a bomb in the bus?

They knew, but they still did it.

It was because a bomb’s blast radius was limited; the narrower the space, the greater the damage.

Under the approach bridge was an open, suburban road. To prevent the bus from exploding on the crowded bridge and causing further casualties, they had no choice but to use this method to force the bus to the side, disrupting its normal movement.

With the bus refusing to stop, even the police had to resort to self-sacrifice to prevent further casualties. How could they guarantee the safety of those on board?

Bespectacled Boy, who had always insisted on “self-rescue,” decided to face the truth and no longer rely on others.

“Aren’t the driver and the aunt married?”

Although Bespectacled Boy was on the verge of a meltdown, his mind remained clear. “Since you think the driver asked you to get off because he hasn’t completely lost his humanity, then let’s start there!”

Li Shiqing couldn’t help but look at the aunt.

The aunt looked out the window with empty eyes, but one of her hands remained in a position ready to grab the plastic bag at any time, as if it had become her instinct.

She stared at the woman, her voice almost gnashing through her teeth.

“I remember the knife was in the right outer pocket of her shirt. Let’s stick with our old method: first, seek the help of the strong man, and then we can all hold her down together.”

The man’s tone remained calm throughout, but his eyes held a fierce glare.

“Once we’ve subdued her, I’ll retrieve her knife, hold it to her neck, and force the driver to stop.”

Li Shiqing was completely shocked.

She had never imagined he would come up with such a lousy idea.

“But they were planning to commit suicide anyway…”

Li Shiqing said, stunned. “You, are you sure this will work?”

“We’re just betting on what the driver will do.”

Bespectacled Boy said coldly, “We can’t control the driver, so we can only take that one in ten thousand chance. As long as he hesitates, we can find a way to get through to him later.”

“Who wants to die when they can live? What if there’s a chance he can avoid death? What if his wife was threatened and had to stop the bus and abandon the plan? Then he wouldn’t have to die, right? We’ve even found a reason for him. Maybe the driver can get over his own hurdle? Didn’t the police say he was a good guy?”

“His daughter is pitiful, but her death was her own fault. Even if it wasn’t, every wrong has its perpetrator. Why should so many people be buried with her? Do they deserve it? Did his daughter deserve it?”

Bespectacled Boy’s words weren’t an analysis but more of an outburst of his own anger.

“If he doesn’t understand, I’ll make him!”

Li Shiqing felt a faint unease as she watched the “willful” Bespectacled Boy. Her intuition told her that his “attempt” might be a waste of time.

But ultimately, her concern for his mental state prevailed, and she could only reluctantly say, “Hmm.”

“Okay, then. You tell me what to do, and I’ll do it.”

After a simple plan, they successfully used the note and the “bonus” to convince the strong man to agree to “help” again, and the masked man also agreed to help watch the pressure cooker.

This time, Bespectacled Boy didn’t want to waste even a moment. Almost the moment the strong man agreed, he pounced on the woman.

Even though Xiao Heyun was just a weakling, he had experience dealing with the same person so many times. And with the strong man’s help, despite the woman’s violent struggles, she was subdued.

As the muscular uncle twisted the aunt’s arms, Bespectacled Boy pulled a knife from her pocket and put it against her neck.

“Don’t move! Tell your husband to stop the bus! Stop it!”

The moment the knife was placed across the aunt’s neck, the passengers in the bus began to panic.

The aunt pursed her lips tightly, not saying a word, but instead sneered.

Bespectacled Boy then turned and yelled at the driver to stop the bus.

The driver didn’t stop either.

After glancing back at them, he silently accelerated.

Li Shiqing felt a wave of desolation in her heart.
