Hope was already slim, and now they were directly telling them that threatening their lives was a dead end and would only incite them, prompting the driver to “execute” their plan even more quickly.

“Boy, what are you doing?”

“Young man, put the knife down!”

“Comrade, that’s not what you just said. You said you just wanted me to help catch someone…”

Even the muscular uncle turned pale with fear. He didn’t agree to helping him kill someone!

“Li Shiqing, break the window!”

Bespectacled Boy watched the bus accelerate toward the bridge and signaled to his companion, who had just handed the pressure cooker to the masked man, to “save yourself.”

They didn’t say a word the entire time. The passengers, unaware of what was happening, quietly called the police or took photos.

“Are you the police?”

Even with a knife pressed to her neck, the woman showed no fear, only a hoarse voice.

“Yes.”

Bespectacled Boy lied calmly, his face calm and his heart steady. “We already know about your situation. I also know what was in that pressure cooker. Although I regret what happened to Wang Mengmeng, that’s no reason for you to take everyone in the bus with you to their deaths. It’s not too late for you to stop your evil deeds and surrender yourself to seek leniency.”

Hearing the words “Wang Mengmeng,” the woman froze.

The next moment, her entire body tensed.

“You know my daughter? You investigated her!”

Her voice was hoarse, a hoarse sound emanating from the knife’s hold. “Why didn’t you investigate sooner? Why didn’t you investigate when she was in trouble? She’s dead; she’s been dead for four years, and you’re telling me you’re sorry now! It’s no use; nothing you say will matter.”

Under the guidance of Bespectacled Boy, Li Shiqing successfully broke the window with a safety hammer, but the bus was speeding and had already rushed onto the bridge. The driver kept forcing lanes, forcing himself onto the busier road.

The bridge was full of vehicles, and the bus was driving unsteadily. She had no way of finding a safe place to drop the bomb.

“Wang Xingde, if you and your wife were to commit suicide by taking a bomb to the bridge now, others wouldn’t feel pity for your family of three. They would only think your daughter deserved death!”

Bespectacled Boy began to shout.

“What, a bomb?”

The passengers in the bus were shocked when they heard there was a bomb!

Some frantically rushed to the rear door, desperately banging on the emergency door release mechanism, demanding to be let out. Others simply shouted out the window, “Police, help!”

But no one paid any attention to these disoriented passengers. The driver and his wife both wore indifferent expressions.

Bespectacled Boy’s eyes were fixed on the driver’s seat ahead.

“What do you think others will think of you doing this? A girl got out of her bus on her own and got into an accident, and her parents are using this as revenge, carrying a bomb and intending to die with the people on the bridge? Do you know how many people will die? You’re adding to your daughter’s sins, and she will never be able to redeem herself!”

Xiao Heyun’s attitude seemed to be solely focused on venting his anger, his words like cold swords, with no regard for whether they would irritate the two “murderers.”

“This matter will be resurrected by netizens, and the video of your daughter’s death will be replayed over and over again. Now it’s even worse. They’ll also bring the video of you and your wife dragging a whole bus of people to their deaths, and everyone will curse you, saying you deserve to die!”

“You think this is ‘revenge’? You think this will draw public attention to your daughter’s case? No, you’re trying to have your daughter’s corpse ‘whipped’!”

“What do you know!”

The driver reached the designated spot, braked immediately, and finally roared in anger.

He stood up, his face livid, and turned around, facing Bespectacled Boy holding his wife hostage, his eyes blazing with fire.

“My daughter has been well-behaved and obedient since she was young, yet you’ve labeled her a foolish, unreasonable woman who deserved it! I simply wanted her to rest in peace and to ease my wife’s grief, so I chose not to investigate further. Yet, you’re taunting us, saying we deserved it and are playing the victim! If we had known the outcome would be like that, even if my wife and I had died right then and there, we wouldn’t have let it go!”

“One moment you were asking us to ‘accept your condolences and take care of ourselves,’ and the next you were laughing at our daughter for ‘bringing it upon herself’ and blaming us for not raising her well! How my daughter died, how we live, and how we die—what does it have to do with you? We worked so hard to raise a child for twenty years, and she’s gone just like that. Isn’t that tragic enough? Why do you have to remind us again and again?”

“Besides mocking and taunting us online, have you ever done anything humane?”

“My daughter…”

Tao Yinghong trembled as she heard her husband’s accusations, tears streaming down her face.

“You’re still arguing about life or death? It’s too late!”

The driver looked out the window at the chaotic scene, then at the pressure cooker held by the masked man. With a sneer, he removed his white driving gloves and threw them to the floor.

“Go ahead and kill my wife! It’s time! My wife and I will be reunited with our daughter soon!”

“Let’s go! Give me the pressure cooker later!”

While Bespectacled Boy and the driver were confronting each other, Li Shiqing had already led the masked man toward the bus window. As soon as the bus stopped, she closed her eyes and jumped out the window.

The moment she jumped out the window, a familiar Canon ringtone rang from the direction of the woman in the flowery dress.

“Forget it! Throw it away!”

Li Shiqing’s face paled. Ignoring the excruciating pain in her ankle, she frantically reached out to the masked man at the bus window.

The masked man hurriedly leaned forward, attempting to pass the pressure cooker through the window.

But it was too late. The bus incident had already been noticed by many people. Passengers, desperate to escape, leaped from the bus one after another, throwing traffic on the bridge across the river into chaos. Furthermore, some of the passengers who had gotten off earlier were already shouting, “There’s a bomb on the bus!” Many private cars, ignoring the traffic, either turned around or accelerated against the bus. Now, not only was the bus stuck, but the vehicles in front and behind were also stuck.

Li Shiqing glanced around and knew there was no way she could get through the traffic jam. She threw the pressure cooker under the bridge, resignedly closed her eyes, and welcomed her impending fate…

Boom!

》》》

Restoring from the horrific explosion, Li Shiqing felt as if her brain had been blown to pulp.

A constant buzzing sounded in her ears, her eyes were filled with white light, and even her skin felt a burning pain. She briefly forgot where she was and what she was doing. The excruciating pain forced her to slump over the seat in front of her, groaning silently.

She didn’t even have the energy to scream.

After finally coming to terms with her discomfort, Li Shiqing’s first move was to check on Xiao Heyun beside her.

He wasn’t in good shape either, his head covered in cold sweat, his face pale as a ghost, but a smile lingered on his face, even a laugh.

To Li Shiqing, that smile held an indescribable sense of satisfaction, like the smile of someone who’s scored a pre-set question on a difficult exam or whose first date plans were all entirely to their girlfriend’s liking.

But the problem is, he just failed in his plan and nearly came to nothing?!

“It’s over, it’s over.”

Li Shiqing’s mind went blank.

This guy’s still crazy!

Bespectacled Boy, his forehead smeared with sweat and a strange smile on his face, nudged Li Shiqing and whispered in her ear, “Call the police, Old Zhang, and request assistance.”

“What?”

Li Shiqing asked, still preoccupied with the news that Bespectacled Boy might have been driven insane.

“Write a text message… Never mind, I’ll do it.”

Seeing Li Shiqing’s dull expression, Bespectacled Boy assumed his companion hadn’t yet recovered from the recent death and chose to contact the police himself.

When he was almost done composing the message, Li Shiqing came to her senses and leaned over to take a look.

[ Officer Zhang, we’ve discovered a bomb on Bus 45 that just left Gangwu New Village Station. The explosion is expected to occur at 1:45 p.m. on the cross-river bridge. The bus is expected to enter the bridge between 1:30 p.m. and 1:40 p.m. Please immediately block traffic on the bridge and evacuate vehicles, but do not prohibit the vehicle from entering. The driver is an accomplice, so he won’t detonate the bomb upon discovering the bridge is blocked. My companion and I are in the bus. We will try to control the individual carrying the bomb and throw the pressure cooker loaded with the bomb under the bridge. Please meet us after the vehicle stops. Time is running out, and we can no longer contact you. Please trust us! ]

“Do you have a new plan?”

Li Shiqing was surprised to see Bespectacled Boy texting Officer Zhang.

“That cycle just now confirmed one thing…”

Before putting his phone away, Bespectacled Boy checked the time and said to Li Shiqing, “You’re right. The driver can be moved.”

“He became angry at my questioning and sarcasm.”

Bespectacled Boy said, “A person who desires nothing more than death won’t become angry when faced with certain death. At most, they’ll be like the aunt, mocking us before dying.”

“Anger means he has regrets, and those regrets don’t come from others but from himself.”

Bespectacled Boy slowly wiped his glasses, preparing for his next move.

“…and with regrets come weaknesses.”

Li Shiqing wasn’t stupid. On the contrary, she possessed excellent empathy.

So, after just a moment’s reflection, she successfully understood the tension between the two.

“The aunt keeps blaming others for only now investigating her daughter’s case, which suggests her regret is ‘time.'”

Four years ago, when her daughter was in the accident, traffic police thoroughly investigated the accident and found nothing unusual. While the driver was at fault for dropping her off mid-trip, that wasn’t the primary factor in her death. Because her daughter wasn’t coerced into leaving the bus, the accident verdict ultimately held her primarily responsible.

But the aunt had always doubted this verdict and hoped the police could give her the answers she needed, proving her daughter wasn’t forced to leave the bus without reason.

The girl was already dead, and whether she was responsible or not was irrelevant, though it could offer comfort to her mother.

But the investigation concluded everything was normal, and without corroboration or physical evidence, the aunt’s suspicions warranted no police intervention. Later, facing such a public outcry, the aunt likely hoped for justice and support, and the police were the most trusted voice.

But the bus accident case was long over, the victim buried, and time could no longer be reversed.

“The uncle kept emphasizing ‘others did this’ and ‘others did that,’ accusing others of mocking him for his compromise. In reality, he was simply trying to escape his own initial cowardice. When his daughter’s accident first happened, Tao Yinghong hoped to investigate further, but he, concerned about the opinions of others and the pressure from his extended family, chose to sign the agreement and return home, effectively acknowledging that his daughter was primarily responsible.”

If they had later moved on from their grief and everything had returned to peace, the uncle might have felt that his compromise was the right thing to do. But with the outcome, the driver must have felt guilty.

This might be why the driver agreed to conspire with his wife to commit this act on their daughter’s death anniversary.

The police investigation revealed that the driver was usually a “nice guy,” widely considered a non-confrontational and compromising individual. Perhaps, deep down, he also wanted to do something so “significant” to prove he was more than just a “nice guy.”

“Yes.”

Bespectacled Boy nodded, summing up.

“And when you get to the bottom of it, they have all sorts of emotional ties…”

“It’s because they don’t believe their daughter is the kind of person who would make a fuss and get off the bus.”

CONTENT END 38

chapters.title: The Twenty-Third Cycle (Part 1)
chapters.content:
“So you were acting that last time when you were so aggressive, threatening the aunt’s life to stop the bus?”

After listening to Bespectacled Boy’s explanation, Li Shiqing suddenly understood.

“Were you trying to find out what their weak spot is that will move them?!”

“It wasn’t all acting.”

Bespectacled Boy smiled sheepishly. “At first, I was really furious, and I thought it was a good way to let off steam. But then I came to my senses and realized it was stupid to threaten two people who were about to commit suicide with ‘life’…”

“It’s probably the same as you did before. Suddenly, an idea popped into my head.”

He mentioned the previous cycle, not wanting to exaggerate. “Anyway, I think there’s still hope. Let’s try again.”

“Okay!”

Li Shiqing gave him a thumbs-up.

After the text message was sent, all that remained was the actual execution.

After so many cycles, the two of them had developed such a tacit understanding that they could communicate with just eye contact. Some details didn’t need to be planned in advance. The only thing Bespectacled Boy needed to do was give a few more instructions on “persuading” the driver.

“It’s the same as always. Leave this aunt to me, and you take the driver.”

He lowered his voice and whispered in Li Shiqing’s ear, “Perhaps you haven’t noticed yet, but the driver treats you differently than other passengers.”

“…differently?”

Li Shiqing was stunned.

“Remember that time I tried to talk the driver into watching for the motorcycle on the right? He ignored me when I spoke to him, but you persuaded him, and he listened.”

Bespectacled Boy recalled some details from the past. “When there was a commotion on the bus, and others were calling for help or yelling, he would at most ask what was going on. Only when you yelled did he keep turning his head. Only when you asked did he patiently answer your questions.”

“And, most importantly, he hesitated to let you get off the bus.”

Bespectacled Boy looked at his companion and said gently.

“Like you said, he asked you to get off… Not only did he do it because you insisted, but he also suggested getting off at the next stop.”

“…Li Shiqing, maybe he didn’t want you to die.”

Hearing her own words, her eyes were filled with confusion, disbelief, and mostly sadness.

After so many cycles of brutal torture, Li Shiqing’s eyes still held a glint of innocent wonder.

Xiao Heyun didn’t want to sadden her.

Both then and now, he found Li Shiqing’s “softness” incredibly precious.

“Didn’t the police tell you? The uncle’s daughter went to W University, the same school as you, and often took the same route. His slight sympathy for you might be due to some similarities between you and his daughter, or perhaps simply because you knew him well. People are more likely to be soft-hearted when they’re around acquaintances…”

Bespectacled Boy sighed, “Regardless, your entry into the cycle might not be a coincidence.”

“Perhaps there’s something in the universe that’s uniquely unattainable for you, and that’s why Heaven has granted you this ‘luck.'”

After so many trials and tribulations, even Xiao Heyun felt his heart had hardened. In the past, he would never have put a knife to someone’s neck, even if that person was a criminal.

But now, he felt he could kill the woman without hesitation if necessary.

But Li Shiqing was different. Perhaps it was because of the difference in gender or the difference in perspective, but even at this point, she still maintained her bottom line and refused to “take risks.”

Even if she encountered such a thing, she still hoped that the police would send these two for “trial.”

This “gamble” wasn’t so much a bet on their ability to hit the driver’s soft spot as it was a way for him to protect his companion.

Perhaps every woman hoped for a story with a perfect ending, without regrets, where everyone was happy, so she wanted to give it a chance.

“So, go ahead and try…”

Bespectacled Boy patted her hand.

Since you started it…

“Come and try to put an end to this tragedy.”

Please end it yourself.

》》》

Wang Xingde had been driving this route for thirty months. He knew it so well that he could clearly picture the section ahead even with his eyes closed.

He used to be a truck driver, and driving was an instinct ingrained in his muscle memory.

He spent most of his life on the road, sometimes feeling like he couldn’t do anything else besides driving, even suffering from midlife anxiety.

Ironically, it was precisely this single ounce of “confidence” that allowed him to easily eliminate those whose driving skills weren’t as good as his and successfully gain admission to the bus company.

When he was first accepted, he was furious.

He didn’t hide his identity out of “revenge.”

The name “Wang Xingde” must have been immediately associated with the accident that happened to his daughter six months prior. When seeing this name, at least some people would have some doubts about it.

On those sleepless nights filled with regret, he repeatedly imagined how he would respond to the “doubts.” He even prepared every accusation for his daughter’s death, waiting for the moment his “revenge” would be revealed.

Wang Xingde couldn’t wait to see these people’s faces, from their condescending attitude to their panicked expressions.

However, even after he completed all pre-job training and obtained his bus driver’s license, no one realized he was the father of “Wang Mengmeng.”

The name “Wang Mengmeng” vanished from everyone’s memory the next morning, like the mermaid princess disappearing into the sea’s foam.

No one even remembered “Wang Mengmeng,” let alone the name “Wang Xingde,” who appeared only on the accident report.

Yes, at first, he didn’t believe his wife’s “revenge” could succeed and even thought the “plan” was ridiculous.

In his imagination, he didn’t even need to reveal any flaws; as soon as the executive responsible for recruiting him saw his name, his wife’s various plans would be “aborted.”

He agreed to come to W City with his wife to accompany her on this and that activity simply because her mental state was so bad at the time. He even noticed her attempting suicide several times by walking into the street. For this reason, he simply quit his job and stayed with his wife every day.

He had no special abilities; he simply wanted to make her happy, even if it didn’t seem “normal” to others.

He had already lost his daughter and didn’t want to lose his wife too.

When he first took over this route, the old driver familiarized him with the route, explaining the difficult sections and the travel time between each stop. Because this route was the “Yellow Spring Road” that led to his daughter’s death, he often lost his focus, but the old driver didn’t take it seriously.

Finally, one day, as the bus drove near the spot where his daughter had died, he couldn’t help but raise his inner questions.

“Has there ever been an accident on this road? A girl died because she got off the bus prematurely? Should I pay more attention to traffic conditions on this bridge next time?”

“Ah, maybe.”

The driver who was leading him replied nonchalantly, “Which road hasn’t had accidents? Which road hasn’t had people die? Who cares? Just don’t get yourself into trouble. The passengers on the bus don’t care about what happens on the way; they just care about getting there on time. That’s what matters most.”

[ Who cares? ]

This was the final conclusion of her daughter’s short life.

He traveled constantly, but that was to survive; it didn’t mean he didn’t love his daughter.

For over a decade, on every long-distance trip, no matter how far the journey or how tight the deadline, he would, like the father in his daughter’s fairy tale, ask her what gift she wanted before leaving and bring it back.

Although his home was humble, with his family by his side, it was the most wonderful place in the world.

Driving was tedious, but with his family waiting, every return trip was filled with joy.

His daughter was sweet and well-behaved; she could play the piano and dance, and when she smiled, her eyes curved like the moon on the treetops. Whenever he thought of her smile, it soothed all his fatigue.

He had driven for over a decade without a single serious accident, because he always remembered that there were people at home who longed for his safe return and that others, too, had families who wished for theirs.

But the words of his “master” made him realize that not everyone cared so much.

“Everyone is a sinner.”

It was only then that he began to believe his wife’s thoughts were right.

His anger was like a sudden wildfire, burning everything in its path. His rationality, his luck, his hesitation, and even his love and family were all understated layer by layer…

Burned away.

Over these thirty months, amidst the tedious day-in, day-out work, he had become a master of this route. He had complete control over both the route and this vehicle, allowing it to bend to his will.

He frequently broke the vehicle’s surveillance system and locked the emergency door switches, never proactively reporting any repairs. His colleagues had grown accustomed to the vehicle’s inconsistent performance; no one could have predicted that this outstanding employee, consistently recognized as a “model,” would engage in such behavior.

As if even Heaven supported their “revenge,” the process went smoothly for his wife. With her credentials as a quality inspector at a chemical plant, the “unqualified” raw materials arrived in her hands, bit by bit, like ants moving house.

They were like two spiders lurking in the shadows, weaving a web of revenge.

Today was the day to close the web.

Everything went perfectly smoothly. The only thing that left him feeling a bit disappointed was that a girl he knew got on the vehicle.

He hadn’t expected her to get on. At this time of year, most students had already gone home for the holidays. She shouldn’t have stayed in W City, shouldn’t have stayed in school, and certainly shouldn’t have traveled outside on weekend.

She was a girl, just like his daughter, with eyes that shone like crescents when she smiled. She was just as innocent and lovely as his daughter. They even attended the same school and studied the same subjects, which reminded him of his own daughter.

Every time she got on the bus and there was an empty seat behind him, she would sit there, chatting with him about family matters and asking about his recent situation.

Because of her, he had often wondered if, when his daughter came to W City to attend school, he had quit his job to accompany her to this city, becoming a bus driver on her way to school, would her daughter have survived?

Would her daughter have been like this girl, sitting behind him, chattering about her day’s experiences and begging him to go shopping together after getting off school?

He wasn’t a timid person, but he drove carefully, and he would never let anyone get into trouble.

Every time he lost himself in his imagination, regret and longing tore at his heart. He hated the world, and even more so, his cowardly and pathetic self.

Sadly, once the arrow was shot, there was no turning back. While the girl was lovely, she wasn’t his daughter after all.

“I’m sorry…”

Looking at the bridge gradually appearing ahead, Wang Xingde’s eyes slowly filled with tears.

Their family would finally be reunited.

The author has something to say: This chapter was difficult to write because of my empathy, but after much deliberation, I decided to write from the driver’s perspective. I don’t think the driver’s actions were right, nor do I intend to explain the couple’s repeated choices, whether reliable or not. I simply wanted to tell a story, one with cause and effect, a beginning and an end. The readers are free to independently decipher the truths and wrongs of this story. This story is coming to an end. I originally only wanted to write this one, but while writing this book, another inspiration suddenly struck me, so there’s a special story based on this worldview later. These two stories together make up this book, and the tone of that one is more cheerful (facepalm). I hope I don’t feel so bad writing it, haha.

CONTENT END 39

chapters.title: The Twenty-Third Cycle (Part 2)
chapters.content:
This time, everyone was extremely careful, including Li Shiqing.

When she sat behind the driver, he didn’t even notice there was an extra person in the empty seat behind him.

As the bus passed the intersection with the tanker, Bespectacled Boy took the initiative.

This time, he was more experienced. He had borrowed the coat with the kitten inside from the masked man beforehand, and as he walked past the aunt, he threw the coat over her head.

“What are you doing?”

The aunt, who had been staring out the window, was blinded by the coat that suddenly fell from the sky. She instinctively reached for her plastic bag, but the burly man grabbed both of her hands and lifted her from the seat.

Bespectacled Boy took the opportunity to pull the knife from her pocket and, along with the uncle, pinned her to the floor of the bus.

“And then? What do we do next?”

The masked man, knowing there was a bomb in the pressure cooker, trembled as he dragged the plastic bag from the seat. He didn’t dare hold it, crouching there in a state of panic.

The passengers were completely bewildered, confused as to what was happening inside the bus, and no one took the initiative to ask.

“Hey, young man, even if this person had a knife, you can’t hold her down like that…”

The uncle with the key observed Bespectacled Boy carefully and, perhaps deciding he didn’t look like a bad guy, couldn’t help but launch into another verbal attack. “If they’ve really committed something, you can handle it yourselves and let us get off the bus first, okay?”

After a few rounds, Bespectacled Boy’s biggest annoyance was the uncle with the keys. He offered no help at all, yet was the talkative one. When something happened, he’d yell for others to help, then run away faster than anyone else, wishing he had two more legs.

Seeing he was still nagging, Bespectacled Boy frowned and snapped, “It’s none of your business; stop rambling!”

The uncle’s face immediately turned sour at being confronted. Just as he was about to say something else, Bespectacled Boy, who had just scolded him, glanced at him menacingly.

That look was filled with impatience and a fierce determination to get his way, not to mention the knife he’d found on the woman.

The uncle with keys was so frightened that he choked back the words he was about to say.

He talked so much, yet nothing happened in all these years because he knew who to mess with and who to avoid. Now, he didn’t dare to speak again and retreated obediently into his seat.

It happened so quickly that the driver only had time to glance back. A quick glance revealed only a young man and a burly man pinning his wife to the ground. He couldn’t deduce what was happening.

He already had a nagging feeling, so he glanced away, feigning ignorance and continuing to drive.

But Bespectacled Boy’s next words shattered his last shred of hope.

“Wang Xingde, we’ve got your wife under our control, and we have the pressure cooker too. Pull over now, and you still have a chance to mend your ways.”

Bespectacled Boy didn’t remove the coat covering the woman’s face but simply shouted at the driver in front of him.

“The police won’t allow your plan to succeed. Turn yourself in before it gets out of hand!”

Hearing the passengers restraining his wife not only call out his name but also reveal their deepest secrets, Wang Xingde’s mind raced, his heart pounded, and he nearly lost control of the steering wheel.

“How did you find out?”

The woman pinned to the ground, her coat covering her face, couldn’t see what had happened, but she knew her secret had been exposed. A sinister voice echoed from beneath her coat.

“We haven’t told anyone about this.”

Bespectacled Boy made no effort to answer her, staring nervously at Li Shiqing in the front seat.

He had done what he could; the rest depended on Li Shiqing’s performance.

The same question lingered in the driver, Wang Xingde’s, mind.

“How did they know?”

“Have we been targeted for a long time?”

“Who is this guy? Are all the people in the bus plainclothes?”

Although he was still driving instinctively, his mind was a tangle. The sudden and bizarre changes in the bus made him feel something was amiss, and the more he thought about it, the more suspicious he became.

“Even if there are police on the bus, they can’t do anything to us…”

The sudden turn of events made it impossible for him to think clearly, and he wasn’t a meticulous person to begin with. “They’re in my bus now, so I have the final say.”

“As long as I’m on the bridge before 1:45 p.m., everything will be over,” he thought. “Yes, I just need to drive to the bridge and lock the doors. They won’t be able to escape even if they try.”

“The bomb will explode in a few minutes. The bridge is full of cars, so they can’t stop us…”

Bespectacled Boy’s straightforward approach in explaining his purpose still irritated Wang Xingde’s already tense nerves.

To avoid further complications, Wang Xingde stepped on the accelerator, driving the bus at full speed and heading straight for the bridge.

“Ouch!”

The bus’s sudden acceleration caused many passengers to jerk around and scream in panic.

“Drive slower!”

The masked man in charge of “guarding” the pressure cooker was terrified. When the bus suddenly accelerated, he panicked and grabbed the plastic bag, securing it to the ground, fearing the pressure cooker would explode with the jolting.

The reckless bus quickly passed the approach bridge and waded into the stream of traffic crossing the river. Seeing the bus’s rapid speed, the vehicles waiting in order at the bridge entrance moved aside, allowing the speeding bus to cross first.

Once the bus reached the bridge, Wang Xingde finally felt certain. He turned back to look in the direction where his wife had been subdued. This time, he didn’t see her but instead caught sight of someone else.

“What’s going on?”

Wang Xingde was startled.

“Why is she sitting here?”

Noticing his gaze, Li Shiqing glanced at him and, as usual, gave him a warm smile.

Wang Xingde suddenly felt as if struck by something and abruptly averted his gaze.

“Wang Xingde, where are we?”

Unable to see what was happening, and with his captors remaining silent except for a few shouts, the aunt lost her composure and screamed.

“We’re already on the bridge!”

Wang Xingde replied frantically, “Don’t worry!”

But as he drove, he began to sense something was amiss.

After passing the section where he had just entered the bridge, the traffic on the bridge gradually thinned out, a stark contrast to its usual bustling situation. A little further on, the entire bridge was completely deserted.

As a major thoroughfare connecting the city’s two busiest areas, Wang Xingde had made countless trips back and forth that day, adapting to the complex road conditions. Yet, never once had he seen such a deserted bridge.

With no other vehicles blocking its path, and having previously accelerated, the speeding bus arrived at the scene of Wang Xingde’s daughter’s accident much earlier than expected.

Squeak—

With the sound of tires scraping against the ground, the driver mechanically raised his hand and stopped the bus on the empty bridge.

The deserted river bridge seemed like a carefully staged scene, completely unaware of reality.

“What’s going on?”

The passengers, mostly locals and incredibly familiar with the bridge, stared out the windows in bewilderment, their faces as if sleepwalking, whispering to themselves.

“Why isn’t there a single vehicle?”

Even without explanation, they sensed something serious was about to happen.

Anxiety spread throughout the bus like a contagion. Some passengers suddenly stood up, then sat back down again, bewildered, like frightened animals with nowhere to hide.

Some of the more irritable ones shouted directly at Xiao Heyun.

“What are you doing? Driver, open the bus door!”

“Hold her down! Don’t let her move!”

Amid the chaos, Bespectacled Boy let go of the woman and ran to the nearest safety hammer. He pulled it out and began banging on the window.

“Wang Xingde, what happened?”

The sound of a safety hammer hitting the glass suddenly rang out, and the woman being pinned down thrashed as if struck by lightning, shouting hoarsely, “Why did the bus stop?”

Wang Xingde didn’t answer his wife.

He instinctively realized that something was slipping in a direction he couldn’t imagine and subconsciously reached for the gearshift.

“Uncle Wang, give up.”

A petite figure suddenly appeared beside the driver, tightly grasping his wrist, trying to stop him from starting the bus again.

“Don’t stop me!”

Wang Xingde’s expression was complicated, but he reached out without hesitation, ready to push the girl away.

“Uncle Wang, Wang Mengmeng wouldn’t want you to do this!”

Li Shiqing gritted her teeth, gripping the steering wheel with her free hand and shouting, “If you all die, no one will care about what happened to her!”

At the sound of his daughter’s name, Wang Xingde’s grip on Li Shiqing’s shoulder trembled, and he stared at the girl in amazement.

Just as Li Shiqing and Wang Xingde were locked in a stalemate, the police cars waiting at the other end of the bridge raced over at top speed, surrounding the bus in a double formation.

Two officers exited the lead car and, as soon as they got out, sprinted straight to the shattered window, reaching upward.

“Where’s the stuff? Where’s the pressure cooker with the bomb? Hand it over to us!”

Officer Zhang yelled, “Be careful!”

“Wang Xingde! Wang Xingde!”

“Get a few more people to help! I can’t hold her down anymore!”

The muscular uncle looked like he’d been pulled out of the water. The auntie kept struggling, and he kept pushing, his muscles twitching as he struggled. He was about to give up.

“She and the driver planted a bomb in the bus!”

With this shout, Wang Xingde knew the whole situation was exposed. The police had even set up security on the bridge and in the bus. He didn’t care what Li Shiqing said. He pushed Li Shiqing out with all his strength!

“Ah!”

Li Shiqing fell headfirst onto the windshield.

The bus started again. Wang Xingde gripped the steering wheel, waiting for the bus to move, ready to accelerate out.

At that moment, the passengers in the bus suddenly seemed to realize what was happening. They rushed forward in a panic, all helping the muscular man to hold the woman down.

Bespectacled Boy holding the pressure cooker heard his companion’s screams and held his breath in fear. He forced himself to resist the urge to look back. With all his strength, he leaned out and handed the plastic bag containing the pressure cooker to Officer Wang, who was waiting under the bus window.

The bus suddenly moved forward.

“Be careful!”

Seeing Bespectacled Boy almost fall out of the bus with the bomb, the masked man helping him was almost terrified. He quickly pulled him back.

Bespectacled Boy’s plastic bag teetered, barely touching Officer Zhang, who was waiting below.

Li Shiqing, who had been pushed to the ground, quickly scrambled to her feet, gritted her teeth, and rushed over to hug the driver.

“Uncle Wang, I know you’ve been wronged. I know! We’ll help you; we all will. Please don’t do this!”

Li Shiqing couldn’t tell if she was scared or just overly nervous. All the words she’d prepared rushed out of her mouth without a second thought, tears streaming down her face.

“If your daughter truly had been wronged, wouldn’t your death now make the people who murdered her proud? Those who laugh at you won’t feel guilty about your death; they’ll only be happier!”

She trembled, her voice stuttering with nervousness. “Not all people online are bad. I know what happened to Wang Mengmeng. I’ll post a thread for you when I get home. I’ll tell everyone about your grievances and mobilize netizens to find those who knew about what happened back then! With so many people on this trail, someone will definitely know what happened!”

“Please, don’t give up! The police will help you too. Don’t commit suicide!”

“How did you know?”

Hearing what she said, Wang Xingde looked down at the girl in his arms, so shocked he momentarily stopped moving.

“I know, I know everything! I know you’re here to see your daughter today! Your daughter is right here, watching you!”

Li Shiqing felt utterly terrible, sobbing and babbling.

“She told me to stop you! She didn’t want you to see her like this! She didn’t want more people to die in obscurity like her!”

“She’s here, Uncle! She’s right here!”

Why was she the one to enter the loop?

Why did it have to happen on this particular day?

Could it really not be because Wang Mengmeng was still around?

Gradually, the woman with a coat covering her face struggled more and more slowly until her violent struggles ceased.

“Young man, let go!”

Seeing the bus wouldn’t start, Officer Zhang decisively gave the order.

Bespectacled Boy let go, and Officer Zhang and Officer Jiang, who were standing by, caught the pressure cooker securely.

With the pressure cooker in hand, Officer Zhang, clutching it, ran desperately across the deserted bridge. Officer Jiang followed closely behind, his eyes fixed on the pressure cooker in his arms.

“Forty-four minutes!”

Scanning his phone screen, Xiao Heyun leaned out the window, his eyes reddening as he roared at their backs.

“Throw it away!!!”

“Ah!”

Officer Zhang suddenly grabbed the plastic bag by the handle, his right hand swung in a huge arc, and with a frantic cry, he hurled the pressure cooker off the bridge.

Boom!

The pressure cooker, shaken violently, exploded just as it hit the bridge!

With a deafening roar, a scorching wave of air swept the two officers closest to it. Fragments of the explosive even pelted the bridge pillars like hail, creating a muffled clanking sound.

The people in the other police cars had been warned to stay away. As soon as the pressure cooker was released from their hands, they immediately fell to the ground, instinctively covering their ears. Even so, some of them cried out in pain from the flying debris.

Officer Zhang, lying on the ground, looked up at the sky, two streaks of blood slowly flowing from his ears, but a satisfied smile appeared on his face.

“The bet was right…”

He thought happily, his heart suddenly relaxed.

He let his consciousness sink into darkness.

“Old Zhang!”

“Open the bus door!”

“Hurry, hurry, call the nearest ambulance, get a doctor over!”

After the explosion died down, the passengers in the bus looked at each other in shock.

“She—why isn’t she moving…”

The first to regain consciousness was the sturdy uncle who had been helping.

When he realized the woman he had pinned down was motionless, he panicked and pulled away the coat covering her face.

“No, she’s suffocated!”

The woman, who had been struggling violently, collapsed unconscious on the floor, her face a purple hue.

In that situation just now, a group of people surrounded her, trying to prevent her from escaping. Some pressed down on her clothes; others pressed down on her shoulders. Perhaps it was because of the chaos, but someone pressed down on the jacket, blocking her mouth and nose, suffocating her.

“We didn’t do it; you asked us to help!”

“I was pressing on her legs!”

Hearing that someone might have died, the crowd of passengers dispersed.

“Stop the bus, open the door, you’re surrounded!”

The police shouted from outside the bus door.

Seeing the situation was hopeless, the driver, Wang Xingde, slowly released his grip on the steering wheel, his eyes blurred with tears.

In his increasingly hazy vision, the sobbing girl before him had a face that strangely overlapped with her daughter’s.

He raised his finger, vaguely tracing the outline of his daughter’s face, and called out to Li Shiqing.

“Mengmeng…”

Li Shiqing’s ears were filled with the humming sound of the explosion. She wiped her tears streaming down her face, dazed, and didn’t hear the driver’s words at all.

“Mengmeng, if you want to blame someone, blame Dad…”

The driver let out a bitter smile, mumbling, “It’s Dad who’s cowardly and incompetent. Your mom said that if we do this, the police will investigate what happened and give you justice…”

“But since you don’t want us to do this, we won’t. Mom and Dad will turn themselves in.”

He pressed the door release mechanism.

With the sound of air being released, the front and rear doors swung open simultaneously.

The police officers leaped in.

He was only focused on his “daughter.”

“…Don’t cry. You won’t be pretty if you cry…”

The author has something to say:  There will be no reincarnation. When the driver “let go,” the cycle ends. Shhh, there are no supernatural events. After the founding of the People’s Republic of China, demons were not allowed to become spirits, and no supernatural ghosts could appear in a socialist society… This story has a few more chapters to go, which will explain some foreshadowing and the lives of Bespectacled Boy and the young woman after the incident. But this book isn’t over yet; there’s still one more unit! I wish you all a happy Mid-Autumn Festival. I won’t make you all anxious during the holiday. I’ll write more about happy things tomorrow!

CONTENT END 40

chapters.title: Ending the Cycle (End)
chapters.content:
As soon as the police boarded the bus, they apprehended the driver, Wang Xingde, and carried Tao Yinghong, who lay unconscious on the ground.

Then, they began evacuating the passengers, thoroughly searching the vehicle for more explosives, taking photos, and preserving the crime scene.

Just as Bespectacled Boy and Li Shiqing were being pushed off the bus by the hurriedly disembarking passengers, the music of Canon in D Major suddenly began.

“Heavens!”

More?

Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy felt their scalps tingle, their faces turning pale with fear.

“Hurry up!”

The passengers on the bus panicked even more at the strange ringing. It turned out that the bus had run away.

Even after getting off the bus, everyone was still dazed and cautiously moved as far away from it as possible.

Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy wanted to flee, but the stress reaction had left their limbs cold and weak, rendering them completely defenseless.

Standing under the bus, they watched as a police officer pulled a cellphone from Tao Yinghong’s pocket as she was being escorted off. A chill ran down their spines, their expressions filled with terror, as if something was about to explode in their faces at any moment.

“Don’t be afraid; it’s just an alarm!”

A gloved officer carefully returned the phone to the evidence bag. Looking up at the two youths’ startled expressions, he smiled.

“Here, it was set for 1:45 p.m., and it just happened.”

“It’s… it’s just an alarm?”

Li Shiqing stammered, “Isn’t it a bomb timer?”

Then, couldn’t the ringing they’d heard so many times before be a timer for the pressure cooker?

“It’s just an alarm.”

The officer smiled. “Even if it was a timer, the bomb in the pressure cooker has already gone off. It can’t go off again, can it?”

As soon as the driver was arrested, the detectives thoroughly searched the bus, including the undercarriage, but found nothing suspicious, including explosives.

The passengers who had gotten off the bus, witnesses to the crime scene, weren’t allowed to leave yet. They sat or stood in groups on the empty bridge. Some called their families to report their safety, while others excitedly discussed the thrilling, movie-like scene.

The masked man hurriedly opened his bag upon exiting the bus. The poor kitten inside, frightened by the deafening roar, defecated and urinated in the bag, unprotected by his coat.

“Don’t be afraid, don’t be afraid. It was just thunder. We’ll find something to eat when we get home.”

He wasn’t angry at all. He took off his mask and casually wiped the dirt off the kitten’s skin with it. Then, lovingly, he held the frightened kitten in his arms to comfort her.

“The bad guys have been caught. There won’t be any more thunder…”

The sturdy man planted his feet on solid ground, breathed a long sigh of relief, and collapsed onto the devastated street.

Of all the people on the bus, he was the one who had to work the hardest.

Controlling someone from moving was easier said than done.

Not to mention that he knew the middle-aged woman was carrying a bomb and other weapons. One could imagine the tension and pressure he felt.

Even with Bespectacled Boy’s help, given his size and age, if something really happened, would he expect a bunch of kids to risk their lives?

He definitely had to take on more responsibility.

Now that the police had arrived, the bad guys had been apprehended, and the bomb had exploded beneath the bridge, the uncle finally relaxed the tension he had been holding. Suddenly, his muscles stiffened and ached, and he slumped to the ground.

He touched the thousand yuan tucked into his inner chest pocket, feeling the weight of the bills.

With that thousand yuan, he could buy a used electric scooter or rent a small house. After all, the future was still there, the hope was still there, and as long as everyone was safe, the risk of his life had been worth it. The money was secure, and his life was saved—it should have been a joyous occasion. However, once the initial tension and urgency had passed, he finally began to feel a sense of bitterness and lingering fear, silently wiping away tears.

For some people, even their sorrow was silent.

Once the police had fully secured the scene, and the ambulance had taken the injured Officer Zhang and the unconscious Tao Yinghong away, Officer Du finally had time to search for the kind citizen who had “called the police.”

“Excuse me, who on the bus called the police?”

Officer Du asked loudly from the bridge.

“It was me.”

Bespectacled Boy glanced at Li Shiqing and raised his hand.

Officer Du, along with several other officers, approached them, shook his hand, and expressed his gratitude.

“Thank you so much for providing the clue and for working with the passengers on the bus to apprehend the criminal!”

“It wasn’t just my credit. After all, the culprit was stopped with the help of several passengers on the bus…”

Bespectacled Boy was stunned for a moment, then quickly explained.

He pointed at Li Shiqing in front of him, then at the young man, who had taken off his mask and was holding a cat.

“And that uncle. They helped me subdue the aunt.”

The other police officers, upon hearing his words, looked at Bespectacled Boy in surprise.

Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun, one looking no more than his early twenties, the other a youthful student still fresh out of school, were the primary contributors to stopping this bombing?

When they first received the text message, because it was concise and well-organized, highlighting all the key points, they assumed the person in the bus who had encountered this situation was an experienced veteran or a police officer on leave. They didn’t even have time to verify the phone number’s origin. They simply notified the traffic police, blocked traffic, and rushed to the bridge.

“Young people, that’s impressive! Your courage is commendable!”

A police officer praised them, “Thank goodness you were here; otherwise, this would have been a disaster!”

“As long as we haven’t caused any trouble for the police.”

Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun exchanged glances, still unsure if the matter was truly resolved.

They were so exhausted from this day and had tried every possible method. If they still couldn’t end the cycle, they would definitely go crazy.

“Everyone, please come with us back to the police station to give your statements. Thank you for your hard work! A bus will be taking you back later. Please cooperate with the police.”

Officer Jiang shouted from the other end, “A large bus will be here soon. Please get on board!”

Soon, a police bus slowly drove onto the blocked bridge, carrying away all the stranded passengers.

Watching the bridge recede in the distance, feeling the gentle breeze blowing through the window, Li Shiqing smiled. She leaned against Bespectacled Boy’s shoulder and fell asleep sweetly…

》》》

Two weeks later, in a private room at a teahouse.

“How have you been lately?”

Li Shiqing entered the room, removed her cap and mask, and greeted Bespectacled Boy, who had arrived earlier. “I heard you’ve been going through interviews for half a month?”

“How could you be as happy as you? Just go abroad and travel for half a month?”

Xiao Heyun was at a loss for words. “You posted a long Weibo and then disappeared. What if no one else came to interview me?”

“I didn’t mean to abandon my comrades!”

Li Shiqing shrugged, laughing without a trace of guilt.

“My parents were worried I might have some psychological trauma, so they took me to a psychologist for a week. It was the psychologist who persuaded them to take me out for some fun, to get away from it all, so I was taken on a trip. I didn’t really want to leave; I just wanted to see if there were any new developments back home!”

“It’s truly Heaven’s blessing that this matter was resolved so smoothly.”

Xiao Heyun sighed, grateful that they had so easily cleared their suspicions.

After the incident, the first question the police asked was how they knew Officer Zhang’s phone number. Fortunately, they had discussed it for a long time in the hotel that night, including how to handle the subsequent police investigation if they were to succeed.

That night at the hotel, they searched online for Officer Zhang’s phone number and discovered that it had been released on the local police platform during a previous bus arson case.

The arsonist in that case first burned himself beyond recognition when the fire started, and later his body was totally charred. The police’s night contact number at the time was the mobile phone number of the person in charge, Officer Zhang, in order to make it easier for people who knew the arsonist’s situation to provide clues to the police.

Xiao Heyun said that when he realized something was amiss, he immediately searched for “bus case police,” found the phone number, and sent a text message.

After receiving the text message, Officer Zhang texted back to inquire about the situation. However, due to the urgency of the situation, they didn’t have time to respond. However, confirming that the number was still in use by the police gave them great confidence.

The police later tested the method and confirmed that they could indeed find Zhang’s phone number.

Afterwards, the police praised Bespectacled Boy’s intelligence. Besides being thankful that the information was still traceable after so many years, they also commended his decision to contact the criminal police directly.

Otherwise, relying on 110 to call the police and then dispatching police would be a complicated and slow process, potentially allowing the suspect to detect the incident beforehand.

As for how they discovered the bomb on the bus, they used the same excuse: “We were sitting behind a woman and heard her mumbling to herself.”

They told the police they called them because Li Shiqing heard the woman muttering things like “The bomb is in the pressure cooker,” “I’m going to see my daughter at 1:45 p.m.,” “Wang Xingde, drive faster,” and “Hurry to the bridge,” and felt something was amiss.

Li Shiqing said that after noticing something was amiss with the woman, she consulted with Bespectacled Boy sitting next to her and decided to call the police. Since time was short, she tried to find help on the bus to apprehend the suspect. She frequently took this route and was familiar with the driver, knowing his surname was Wang. This led her to infer that the “Wang Xingde” the woman was referring to was likely the driver and thus a suspected accomplice.

In reality, this explanation would likely crumble if confronted with Tao Yinghong. However, during their search for the truth, Officer Zhang had clearly revealed that Tao Yinghong’s mental health had been poor and she might have a mental illness. They were betting that Tao Yinghong might have a problem in this area and that even a confrontation wouldn’t be enough to justify their suspicions, so they continued to use this narrative.

In the end, perhaps Heaven had opened their eyes to feel sorry for them or something else, but after regaining consciousness, Tao Yinghong’s mental health did indeed deteriorate.

At the time, she was pinned down by the panicked passengers. Whether it was brain damage from her coma or the inability to face reality after her plan was shattered, she suffered a mental breakdown. Although she was later revived in the hospital, she now showed no reaction to any external stimuli, like a living corpse.

Even if she didn’t spend the rest of her life in prison, she would likely be confined to a hospital.

Uncle Wang Xingde, likewise, never revealed to the police that Li Shiqing knew about his daughter. He simply said that Li Shiqing resembled his daughter and that when the attack occurred, she had begged him to stop, which reminded him of his daughter, and he softened his heart. Furthermore, the bomb had already been unloaded from the vehicle, and the situation was already hopeless, so he chose to give up.

Because Tao Yinghong was mentally ill and Wang Xingde concealed the truth for unknown reasons, this already suspicious incident was left without evidence. Thus, the two youths, with their good behavior, clean pasts, and reasonable explanations, were quickly released after a brief questioning. Not only did they avoid punishment, but they were even rewarded by society.

After leaving the police station, the two did not return home but instead stayed in a nearby hotel.

This time, they learned their lesson and stayed up all night, drinking coffee and watching movies, until dawn. Seeing the dawn light outside the window and the sun slowly rising, they double-checked that it was truly the next day before relaxing and drifting off to sleep.

When they woke up, the internet was abuzz.

The “explosion” in W City, once exposed by the media, quickly became the most talked-about news story online.

According to the two suspects’ planned scheme, the bombing would have caused far greater casualties. However, thanks to the alertness of these two youths, they were able to detect the incident early. Not only did they call the police, but they also worked with the passengers in the bus to subdue the suspect and successfully assisted the police in detonating the bomb in advance…

The bombing itself was sensational enough, but coupled with the bizarre twists and “legendary” resolution, the case quickly became a trending topic on all major media platforms.

Li Shiqing, one of the witnesses, wrote a long post on her Weibo account, detailing everything that happened to her and her companions in the bus.

With the police’s permission, she included some information she had learned from their cooperation in the investigation in her Weibo post. At the end of the post, she solicited information from anyone who knew about Wang Mengmeng’s bus trip.

Li Shiqing’s long post, providing firsthand information, garnered over a million shares and comments within two weeks. Even renowned directors and screenwriters approached them, hoping to turn the story into a film.

Because of this, Li Shiqing, Xiao Heyun, the muscular uncle Wang Yong, and the masked man Fang Xiao all entered the public eye, becoming hailed as “heroes.”

Officer Zhang, injured in the explosion, was awarded a first-class merit for bravely throwing the bomb at a critical moment, thereby preventing the disaster. He not only received commendations from the police force but also received praise and gratitude from various groups and local residents while in his hospital bed. Flowers and fruits were poured daily, and visitors streamed in constantly.

Unfortunately, the violent explosion caused him to suffer sudden deafness. Diagnoses indicated it would take two weeks to a month for hearing to fully recover, forcing him to communicate in writing. Consequently, despite the many visitors, he could only manage a smile, unable to engage in the cheerful banter he once enjoyed.

He also jokingly admitted that if it weren’t for the constant stream of visitors in his ward, he’d surely find the noise overwhelming. Now, he could simply close his eyes and rest in peace.

After the life story of the strong uncle and the “one thousand yuan” tale were dug up by the media, he immediately received olive branches from many local companies, hiring him to take up positions offered by their companies, most of which were security-related.

In the end, Uncle Jianzhuang chose to become a food delivery driver. The company that hired him awarded him a five-figure “bravery” bonus and a brand-new electric scooter as a new job gift.

The uncle used the money to rent a slightly larger house near his company. His next step was to urge his daughter to get into a university in the city so he could be close by to take care of her.

The masked man and his kitten also became famous. Now, the kitten, named “An An,” has become an internet celebrity. Every day, many people flock to the masked man’s Weibo, just to admire the cat and see this little angel who survived the ordeal.

Half a month passed, and the passengers on the bus seemed to have gradually moved on from the tragedy. Only Li Shiqing wanted to know, “What happened to Wang Mengmeng?” She hadn’t received much information.

“No clues at all?”

Xiao Heyun asked, frowning after listening to Li Shiqing’s account of the past two weeks.

“After all, so much time has passed, and there haven’t been any witnesses who could provide conclusive information. But there are still clues…”

Li Shiqing took out her phone and gestured to Bespectacled Boy to read a few private messages. These private messages were all from strangers. They all began by saying they weren’t on Wang Mengmeng’s bus and therefore couldn’t provide details about the situation. However, like Wang Mengmeng, they often traveled that route back then.

They all had one thing in common: they had experienced sexual harassment on this route.

The women who took this route were mostly college students who boarded the bus at the last stop. They were young, beautiful, and full of energy. Furthermore, having not yet entered society, they lacked some experience and were somewhat immature, making them easy targets for these perverts.

At the time, they were young and timid. When they encountered such behavior in a crowded area, they didn’t know who was responsible. They either quickly got off the bus or found a male companion for the next trip. All these years later, the disgusting feeling still lingered in their memories. Especially as they graduated and started working, gaining more courage and experience, they increasingly regretted not speaking out when they encountered such behavior.

“But a private message like this isn’t enough evidence.”

Bespectacled Boy poured cold water on her. “Since it’s groping, the person who did it must be very secretive. As long as they can’t be caught, this can only be considered speculation, not the reason why Wang Mengmeng got off the bus.”

“I know.”

Li Shiqing nodded, not looking discouraged.

“But at least, this can serve as a warning to many girls.”

Bespectacled Boy was stunned.

“I’ve got the girls’ consent. I’m going to make this public…”

Li Shiqing said seriously, “As an ordinary girl, encountering something like this on a bus, their first reaction is fear. Shyness and fear often prevent them from seeking help. They either endure it silently or flee in panic, only to embolden these scumbags, who will continue to extend their claws to the next victim.”

“Perhaps this wasn’t the reason Wang Mengmeng got off the bus back then, but as long as people like this exist, tragedies will always happen. Who knows if the next girl will be another Wang Mengmeng?”

Li Shiqing still couldn’t hide her pity when she mentioned that girl.

After the incident, the media dug up the story behind Wang Xingde and his wife. Wang Mengmeng was a very pretty, seemingly petite, and delicate girl. She had always been both good at studying and helpful at school. She had never been unreasonable or even argued with anyone.

But because of this, when scumbags were looking for targets, such delicate and gentle girls were often their first choice.

Many parents raised their daughters to be obedient and gentle, to be quiet and well-mannered, but they forgot to teach them how to protect themselves.

“Some may believe it, some may not, but that’s not the point.”

Li Shiqing had further thoughts on this. “I hope that the girls who saw this incident will bravely stand up to such perverts and scumbags the next time they encounter them on the bus. They will never compromise and fight to the end against such disgusting behavior.”

“They will also have the courage and confidence to break through difficult situations.”

Upon hearing Li Shiqing’s boast, Xiao Heyun didn’t laugh at her childishness. Instead, he offered encouragement: “You have a good idea.”

“Speaking of ‘perverts,’ I’ve always wanted to tell you something, but I was embarrassed before.”

Li Shiqing flipped through her private messages and casually said, “Every time we did “catch the pervert,” you didn’t actually have to reach out your hands. All you had to do was make me scream. Seriously!”

“Cough!”

Bespectacled Boy, sipping tea, coughed awkwardly upon hearing this, a crimson flush spreading from his face to his ears.

Li Shiqing was about to put her phone away when she accidentally clicked on something, and a video popped up.

“What’s this?”

Bespectacled Boy quickly shifted his focus.

“It’s a newly released interview with the driver who’s about to be taken to prison.”

Li Shiqing glanced at the video with a complicated expression, hesitated, and then clicked on it.

After the incident, the aunt suffered mental damage and became a living corpse. The uncle took the initiative to reveal the entire story and offered to take full responsibility.

Although there were no casualties beyond the police officer, he was ultimately convicted of “endangering public safety by dangerous means” and faced a long prison sentence.

Li Shiqing had mixed feelings about the uncle. After the cycle ended, she had been avoiding news and information about the driver. This was the first time she had paid attention to the follow-up to his situation.

The reporter conducted the interview directly with the uncle.

“When you knew the bomb could harm the passengers in the bus and the innocent people on the bridge, didn’t you have any hesitation or regret?” the reporter asked.

“My wife and I, at that time, felt nothing but hatred.”

The driver, Wang Xingde, was indifferent. “If I had any hesitation, it was probably because there was a girl on the bus who often rides my bus. I’ve always thought she looked a lot like my daughter. When I saw her get on, I hesitated.”

Li Shiqing and Bespectacled Boy were stunned.

“So you’d just watch her die, right?”

The reporter, knowing that the girl was one of the young ones who later stopped the driver and his wife, asked, “If you had known she would call the police and stop you, would you still have regrets and hesitations?”

“This reporter… is trying to stir up trouble!”

Bespectacled Boy said angrily.

The uncle was only imprisoned, not sentenced to death. He’d be released someday. If he was provoked now, what else could it be but stirring up trouble and creating chaos?

“She’s a good kid.”

The driver seemed deeply disgusted with the reporter, his words laced with sarcasm. “She’s much better than some people who only care about gossiping behind her back!”

Although there was no footage of the reporter, the reporter was clearly embarrassed and quickly changed the subject.

“If it happened over again, would you do it again?”

“I don’t know.”

The driver’s tone was downcast. “When I first became a bus driver, I hated these people. They just drove mechanically, not caring about the passengers or what might happen if they suddenly got off. After driving for a few years, I realized that some things are beyond the driver’s control, and some people are simply unreasonable. It’s not easy for anyone…”

“But even though you knew how difficult it was to be a bus driver, you still did it. Why?”

The reporter asked angrily.

“Because my daughter died.”

Wang Xingde said numbly.

“This route is over an hour long. Didn’t you and your wife ever consider the possibility of being discovered along the way? How did you manage to drive so calmly?”

“…I did. And I wasn’t calm.”

The driver spoke wearily. “During this journey, my mind wandered a lot, and I had wild thoughts, especially about that girl. I kept hoping she’d get off the bus early…”

“When we passed the intersection, I saw a motorcycle running a red light, and I wondered if I should just scrape past it, create a little friction, pull over, and let the people off…”

“I also thought, if something happened to someone on the bus, like someone suddenly fell ill or started an argument, I could pull over and let them off. But most of the passengers were asleep, so there wasn’t much chance of an argument…”

As the driver recounted his thoughts, Li Shiqing’s and Bespectacled Boy’s expressions grew increasingly serious, and they even shuddered.

“Tell me, could what we experienced just be the driver’s imagination?”

Li Shiqing had barely begun to speak when Bespectacled Boy quickly clicked away.

“Stop watching, stop imagining things. We’ve already escaped the loop!”

Bespectacled Boy snarled.

“It’s all in the past. No matter what happened, it can no longer affect us!”

[But his imagination matches the loop we’ve been through…]

Li Shiqing felt a chill run down her spine as she considered a certain possibility.

“Don’t think about that. Think about something better. Think about your reunion with your parents, and mine. Think about the uncle with the bag finally having enough money to buy an electric scooter, and the guy in the mask having a cat. We’ve already gotten out!”

Xiao Heyun, noticing Li Shiqing’s faltering mental state, grabbed her hand.

Although they seemed to have escaped the shadow of the loop, they both knew deep down that the loop had already taken a toll on them, a toll that wouldn’t heal overnight.

Now, what they should learn was to return to normal life.

“No matter what the reality is, as long as we’re still alive, still living, and everything around us remains unchanged, that’s enough!”

Li Shiqing was stunned by Bespectacled Boy’s scolding, but she gradually came to her senses.

“Yes, you’re right…”

She pulled herself together and took a deep breath.

“Life must go on.”

(The Bus That Never Arrives at the Stop, End.)

The author has something to say: The next chapter is a short story based on this worldview, a kind of self-entertainment experiment. The protagonists are not Bespectacled Boy and Li Shiqing. At the end of each chapter, readers will be able to choose the possible developments themselves, similar to how we interact in an RPG, saving you the pain of following the update every time. This time, the protagonist’s fate is in your hands; I’m just the writer. I hope I had fun writing this, hahaha.

CONTENT END 41

chapters.title: The Undeliverable Package
chapters.content:
You are a newly employed courier, delivering goods along Kejiao Road in the High-tech Zone.

Today is your first day away from your “master” and attempting to deliver packages on your own.

You’re not a local, having returned to this city after serving in the military. Unaccustomed to the 9-to-5 office life, you yearn for a more relaxed work environment, so you choose to become a courier.

As you follow your “master” through the routes and familiarize yourself with the area, you’re confident you’ve become incredibly familiar with your area of ​​responsibility, knowing every building within it like the back of your hand.

The area near Kejiao Road you’re responsible for is one of the first developed areas in the High-Tech Zone. Most of the buildings are very old, and the complex lacks elevators, property management, or security—a nightmare for every courier.

But you’re not afraid. You’re a veteran, and you believe you’re adept at enduring hardships. You believe you can make it to the end.

Early in the morning, you set out with your waiting packages, delivering them one by one from north to south.

On the way, you passed a breakfast stand and bought some Jianbing Guozi for breakfast. But after the food truck left, you spotted a homeless elderly man on the side of the road. You got out and gave the Jianbing Guozi to him.

This led to you feeling dizzy climbing the stairs later, as many families wouldn’t let you leave packages at their doorsteps or security rooms and insisted you deliver them.

Most of those unwilling to come downstairs lived on the upper floors.

Thinking it was your first day on the job alone and you couldn’t afford to receive any complaints, you gritted your teeth and delivered to several more houses.

One family on the top floor was having breakfast when you arrived. Seeing the table full of steamed buns and the aroma of meat, your stomach growled.

The family’s chubby child laughed out loud when he heard your stomach growl. Just as you were about to start feeling embarrassed, you saw the child quickly climb onto the table, grab a large steamed bun, and walk towards you.

But the next moment, the hostess, having already signed for the package, closed the door in front of you.

So you decided to wait and buy some meat buns.

You bought them at the nearby farmers’ market, and the moment you ate them, you felt so good you wanted to cry.

Wow, so delicious.

It was already past eleven by the time you finished your meal, and you weren’t sure if it was “lunch before breakfast” or “lunch after breakfast.” In short, you probably didn’t need to eat lunch so you could focus more on your delivery business.

You began pedaling your delivery bike toward the Seventh Street Apartments, known as “Programmer Street.”

This area is home to programmers working for nearby tech companies, and it’s also where the couriers primarily deliver and receive packages. It’s one of the better-equipped apartment complexes, with built-in storage, elevators, and the ability to temporarily store packages.

The bad thing is, the security and property management at these apartments always treat you as suspicious. Couriers can’t just enter without permission. They have to squat in a small storage room, registering each package with the management team, including which household it’s for, who it’s destined for, and the name and phone number of the courier company.

Each delivery takes five minutes, and the registration process takes half an hour.

The property management staff, seeing you’re a stranger, interrogate you for a long time, like they’re catching a thief. They even take a photo of your work ID before letting you in to record the items.

You grumbled for dozens of minutes, your hands sore, until you finally finished recording and counting all the packages, sorted them, and called the owners who were supposed to receive them.

Some said they understood and told you to leave them in the security room.

Some said the items were too valuable to leave in the security room and asked you to come back in the afternoon.

Some simply couldn’t get through.

You kept the items you could deliver and stacked them to one side of the property management room. You took the ones you couldn’t deliver and started delivering to the next apartment complex.

By 2 p.m., you’d finally finished delivering packages to most of the neighborhoods. Your “driver” called you and told you to return immediately to the delivery point. He’d picked out a new batch of packages for you to deliver that afternoon.

Your delivery company requires a two-hour delivery schedule, so you drove your truck back to the delivery point.

While helping to load the truck, you overheard a few colleagues chatting quietly.

They said the neighborhoods here were starting to install lockers for temporary storage of packages, allowing users to send and receive packages using a text message code. Once these lockers became commonplace, the company would undoubtedly face massive layoffs, and the commission income from delivery services would decrease.

Fearing you’d lose your job, you worried about the consequences, not even having time to drink a sip of water. You loaded the new packages and started out again.

The afternoon brought even more deliveries, and your phone battery died from calls. Someone even complained about you waking up their nap and complained endlessly.

You swallowed your anger, accepted the criticism, and asked them to come downstairs to pick up the packages. Finally, it’s your turn to deliver a package addressed to “Xiao Heyun.”

You’ve placed it with special care, as the packaging says, “Valuable item, handle with care. Open the box in person and collect if everything is correct.”

The information indicates it contains valuable digital products, and it’s a cash-on-delivery item.

You called Mr. Xiao Heyun, but no one answered.

This is a courier’s biggest dread: not only is there no one to pick up a cash-on-delivery package, but it’s also a valuable item that requires constant care to avoid bumping or damaging.

You finished delivering the other packages in the neighborhood and called Xiao Heyun again, but still no one answered.

At this point, you’re certain this package won’t be delivered immediately, so you anxiously leave a message for Mr. Xiao Heyun, hoping he’ll contact you after reading it, then take the package and leave.

It’s time to leave, and you’ve finished your day’s deliveries, exhausted as a dog.

You start to think that having a storage locker like that would be nice. At least you wouldn’t wear out a pair of shoes every two weeks.

Of course, that’s assuming you’re not among those laid off.

On the way back, you see a news report about a bus accident playing on the big screen outside the mall.

This afternoon, near the city’s cross-river bridge, a bus collided with a tanker truck and then exploded, resulting in a devastating traffic accident. It was a tragedy.

You lamented the dire traffic conditions, thankful you weren’t assigned to that particular area, and drove your delivery truck back to your point of sale.

It was already eight o’clock in the evening after handing over your work for the day. Your driver was furious that you hadn’t called Mr. “Xiao Heyun” and delivered the package. He was worried that if the valuables inside had been damaged, the delivery company wouldn’t be able to explain.

You’d been delivering packages all day and were exhausted. After promising to cover any damage to Mr. Xiao’s package, your driver let you go home.

You grabbed a bowl of beef noodles outside, returned to your rented basement, quickly washed up, and fell into a deep sleep.

》》》

The next morning at six o’clock, you were refreshed and ready to go to work.

This time, you finished breakfast early before arriving at the company, ready to accept the package that was being sorted for you today.

As you entered, you heard Old Wang, who was squatting outside smoking, on the phone, worrying about whether his daughter should apply to Tsinghua University or Peking University.

You figured Old Wang must be driven crazy by his daughter’s Gaokao exam, because yesterday, when you arrived at work, he was squatting outside, worrying about the same thing.

You entered the company, and your boss was delighted to see you so early.

“Excellent! That’s the kind of energy you should have on your first day of independent work after your internship!”

You froze, explaining that you’d already worked a full day on your own yesterday.

Then you saw your boss retract his admiring expression.

“Ah, young man, are you still asleep?”

He said, “Do you want to go wash your face?”

Drowsily, you were directed to the restroom, where you washed your face. On the wall opposite, you saw a notice listing the assigned and completed tasks for the month.

Next to your name, “Song Budao,” it says the number of deliveries completed this month is 0.

You’re furious and run out to argue with your team leader. You’ve already completed the 150 daily deliveries required of new employees yesterday, so your total shouldn’t be 0.

Your team leader, with a cold face, pulls out the dispatch book that records your work from yesterday and throws it in front of you.

“The work you did during your internship with your master doesn’t count. Today is only your first day on the job. Where did you get 150 deliveries?”

You take the dispatch book. The last record of your work is from the day before yesterday. All the records for yesterday, including the two pickups, are gone.

At first, you’re furious, thinking they’re bullying the newbie.

But then you notice that your master and your colleagues also don’t have records from yesterday.

You start to feel something is amiss.

Seeing you’re silent and flipping through the book, your team leader reminds you that it’s time to start work. If you still want this job, hurry up and load the truck and get ready to go.

You suppressed your inner uneasiness as you joined the driver in loading today’s packages.

Seeing the names on the packages, you began to grow increasingly terrified.

You remembered the owner of this “Baihuayuan” complex. You remembered the chubby baby he had at home and the delicious smell of his steamed buns.

You remembered the owner of this “Dahu New Village” complex. He lived on the 7th floor. You climbed up the stairs, exhausted, but he was dawdling and refused to open the door, forcing you to wait outside for five or six minutes.

You frantically searched through today’s assigned packages, only to discover that most of them had already been delivered yesterday. The package from Mr. “Xiao Heyun,” the one you were most worried about, wasn’t among them, as it hadn’t been sorted until noon.

You took a dejected step back and took out your phone to check the date.

It wasn’t today’s date, but yesterday’s.

Unconvinced, you rushed to the delivery driver’s computer and checked the system date in the lower right corner, only to find it was still yesterday’s.

“Xiao Song, what are you doing?”

Your colleagues at the delivery station all think you’re weird, and your driver grabs you.

“If you’re not working, why are you running around?!”

You look at your driver, your mind a tangle of knots.

Now, you have two choices.

Take a leave of absence and go out to relax, or continue delivering packages.

The author has something to say: Originally, I envisioned “The Bus That Never Arrives at the Stop” using the first person, and “The Package That Can’t Be Delivered” using the second person.
