You offered to leave, but the young lady grabbed your arm, refusing to let you go.

As her soft body pressed against yours, your mind went blank, and you felt a wave of nervousness.

“I’ve never seen anything like this before!”

Her eyes lit up terrifyingly.

“I haven’t introduced myself yet. My name is Qin Rourou, and I’m a screenwriter, a bit of an unknown one…”

She clasped her hands together in a pleading gesture.

“Please, could you please not leave and tell me more about your cycle? We’ve been through thick and thin together, so why not just consider us friends?”

You looked at her, scratched your head, and began to feel torn.

Should you stay and be friends with her?

Or should you not tell her too much and just get on with your business?

CONTENT END 48

chapters.title: The Undeliverable Package (Part 8)
chapters.content:
The other person had just shielded you from being taken away by the police, and you felt like walking away would seem a bit selfish and heartless.

But you still had a lot of packages to deliver.

“Well, then I’ll stay for another half an hour…?”

You checked the time and said hesitantly, “I have a package delivery this afternoon, so I can only give you half an hour.”

“Okay, okay!”

To save time, the young lady didn’t even bother changing into her pajamas. She went to her bedroom, pulled out a notebook, and began chatting with you about your recurring problems.

She was a little disappointed that you were still delivering packages even after getting “free” time.

“Can’t you use this half day to do something else?”

She advised, “Have you seen movies like this? You could use this half day to learn something, or try something you’ve never dared to try before…”

She briefly told you about a few movies with similar plots.

“I did.”

You told her about your clothes shopping and your fancy dinner.

Her expression only grew more regretful.

“Don’t you know how to try things you wouldn’t buy before? The same goes for food. You have to at least try a little bit of everything, even the most exotic of dishes. That’s the real life experience!”

“And then, if you wake up the next day and suddenly realize time doesn’t repeat, can you just spit out all that delicious food and keep going?”

You’re a pragmatic person, never willing to believe that good things happen to you for no reason.

“This is only my first day on the job, and I still have a month to get paid!”

The young lady sighed, probably feeling exhausted.

“After such a bizarre experience, why are you still considering a job? Isn’t delivering packages every day boring? Even if I wrote a script about your choices, it would be so boring that no one would read it.”

“What does it matter if I keep delivering packages every day? So many people who don’t repeat themselves still do the same thing every day?”

You said.

The young lady was stunned.

“Students study every day, office workers repeat their nine-to-five routines, factory workers work on the assembly line every day, and soldiers in the army complete the same training day after day…”

You cite numerous examples. “So I deliver packages every day, what’s wrong with that?”

“But you don’t have to deliver packages every day. You’re different from them; you have a choice…”

The young woman tries to “comfort” you.

“If everything is destined to return to square one the next day, what’s the point of putting effort into it? Eating a lot of food and seeing a lot of sights will make you happier as you cycle through them? No, gaining and losing only makes you more miserable.”

You’ve experienced the loss of clothes you’ve carefully selected disappearing, or the feeling of being sticky after washing yourself. These are just two of the “losses” you can handle, and they’re still unbearable. What if there are more?

“No one knows if I’ll be able to stop the cycle tomorrow. Rather than hoping for it later, I might as well just treat this day as an ordinary one and do what I need to do.”

“But what if you’re stuck in this cycle forever…”

The young woman bit her lower lip and told you this terrifying possibility. “If everyone and everything around you remained the same, and you were the only one stuck, doing the same thing over and over again, wouldn’t that be painful?”

“…I think so.”

You imagined it and had to admit it was terrifying.

“But I haven’t been through this cycle many times yet, and I don’t know what will happen next. Maybe the next day will be the next day when I open my eyes? If it’s really like you said, and I’m stuck in this day forever, maybe to avoid going crazy, I’ll choose to do something different, as you said, but that’s for the future.”

“But I hope God won’t punish me like this. It would be best if I could discover this mistake sooner rather than later.”

You sincerely hoped.

The young lady, knowing your thoughts and choices, stopped trying to persuade you to use these cycles to “try” new things. Instead, she became interested in you and asked about your personal life.

You felt this was a bit superficial, so you gave a brief explanation and, checking the time, decided to leave.

Before leaving, the young lady saw you off at the entrance and handed you a business card.

“Here’s my contact information, you can save it…”

Seeing your puzzled look, the young lady uncomfortably tugged at her hair, blushing slightly as she explained, “You’ve only just started the cycle, so you might not find it too troubling. But being stuck in the same routine day after day can be exhausting. Want to talk to someone?”

“I’m a screenwriter. I’ve seen many films and TV series with experiences similar to yours. Many of the protagonists in these films ultimately suffer immense psychological pressure, some even on the verge of collapse.”

She looked at you worriedly. “I’m thinking, if one day you really find this monotonous repetition of life boring, I’d be willing to try something different with you. Sharing the burden with someone else might make it less painful. Don’t think I’m bothering me. After all, it’s just a day spent with a stranger, right?”

But just because you’re willing to listen now doesn’t mean you’ll be willing to listen every time.

Thinking about the blunder you almost made just now, you expressed your concerns.

“Then let’s come up with a secret code, one only I know.”

The young lady’s eyes lit up when she saw that you weren’t opposed to this kind of “relationship.”

“Hmm, let me think about it…”

She leaned against the door, thinking for a moment. “Next time you come to see me, you can just tell me that I had a crush on our class monitor in third grade and secretly placed roadside wildflowers under his window for a month…”

Hearing her “secret,” you couldn’t help but laugh.

“I’ve never told anyone about this. No one in this world knows about it except me. As long as you tell me from the other timeline, I’ll believe you.”

She began to feel embarrassed. “If you want a change of heart, you can come to me. Trust my professionalism and imagination to accept such a bizarre thing, and I’d love to be your friend.”

After all, not everyone would risk their lives every day to save someone they have nothing to do with.

Risking falling from the fifth-floor balcony.

This time, you accepted the business card Qin Rourou handed you and promised her you’d remember her phone number.

From today on, you had to remember not only the winning lottery numbers but also a new set of numbers—the phone number of your new friend.

Descending the stairs of the young lady’s apartment building, you quietly touched the lottery ticket hidden in your pocket and nervously wiped the sweat off your face.

“Thank goodness I was smart enough to insist on delivering the package every day…”

You mentally congratulated yourself.

“What if she asks for her lottery number? Should I give it to her or not?”

Feeling a slight sense of guilt for not bringing your new friend along on their “struggle to get rich,” you chose to continue delivering the remaining packages. You’d spent too long at the young lady’s house, and before you knew it, it was almost three o’clock, and you still had more than half of the packages to deliver.

You sorted the remaining packages into different categories, quickly completing the remaining work based on your experience from the previous few days. On the way back to the office, you bought some braised dishes and returned to the sales point.

As soon as the cold-faced team leader saw you return, he surrounded you and asked about what happened that afternoon, why the police called to check your information, and whether you’d caused any trouble outside.

You didn’t dare try to fool the team leader with your “girlfriend” trick. You simply shared your concerns and the blunder, explaining that the police had already reprimanded you. But the team leader still wouldn’t let you go.

He told you that their company never tolerates criminal offenses, from minor offenses like stealing packages from their owners to major crimes. Anyone caught will be fired. It’s true that you illegally broke into someone’s home today. Although the police didn’t pursue the matter and the victim has forgiven you, you can’t just break into someone’s house based on your own assumptions.

Your actions have constituted “illegal operations” and damaged the company’s reputation. Therefore, according to company rules and regulations, you don’t have to come to work tomorrow. You’ll be responsible for the handover over the next two days.

He also told you that your employment contract stipulates that if your actions create any negative public opinion about the company, you’ll be responsible for compensating the company for any resulting losses.

You clearly intended to “do what’s right,” but this misunderstanding left you feeling deeply frustrated.

You tried to explain your urgent situation to your team leader and sought help from other “colleagues.”

However, when faced with your pleading gaze, your colleagues averted their gazes. Your “master” gritted his teeth and pleaded with the team leader, only to be reprimanded.

You handed over your work ID with a grim expression and walked out of the office.

After you’d walked quite a distance, your “master” caught up with you, shouting your name from afar.

Thinking things had taken a turn for the better, you paused expectantly, waiting for the “master” to share some exciting news.

But he simply caught up with you and silently handed you the bag of braised vegetables you’d bought on the roadside.

“You haven’t eaten yet, and this… well, remember to eat anyway, don’t go hungry.”

He stammered, thrusting the bag of braised vegetables into your hands. “Nothing is more important than food. If you lose a job, you can always find another. You have strength and perseverance. This city is big, there’s no shortage of jobs.”

You stiffened as you took the bag, bowing your head and thanking the “master” who had taught you for two months.

The master sighed and left, and you sat down on the side of the road.

Although you know that the company’s decision to “fire” you today might not affect your future;

You also know that the 100 lottery numbers in your pocket guarantee that even if tomorrow doesn’t repeat, you can still live a good life without working…

But you still feel ashamed and embarrassed.

You feel that you have failed your “master” who has nurtured you for so many months and has high expectations of you.

The last time you felt this way was when you had to leave the army for your mother’s sake.

You were a posthumous child. After your father, who served in the army, passed away early, your mother raised you alone. Your parents married and had children at an advanced age, so your grandparents had long since passed away.

Although you have a city hukou, your family is not well off. So, instead of continuing your studies, you chose to join the army, just like your father.

You loved life in the military and hoped to stay here through your own hard work, thereby changing your family’s lives.

However, your mother’s cancer ultimately dashed this hope.

To save her life, you sold your home, sacrificed your dignity, and borrowed from every possible friend and relative.

In the end, to raise enough money for a lifeline and to pay off your debts to your relatives, you chose to shed your uniform:

—just for that one severance pay.

As you left, your leader slid a thick envelope into your hand.

“Even after you’ve retired, don’t forget that you’re a soldier from the military. Keep working hard.”

His expression of regret echoed that of the commander who had just seen you off.

The envelope was filled with donations from your fellow soldiers.

You ultimately didn’t save your mother, but the money made her passing less painful. Even for that alone, you have no regrets, only regrets.

After your mother’s death, you became an orphan.

So you left your sad hometown and chose to work hard in the city where your father was born. This was your first job after demobilization, and you wanted nothing more than to do it well.

You never wanted to be a deserter, nor did you want to let anyone down.

But fate always played tricks on you, making you experience the meaning of “things going against your wishes.”

Expelled, abandoned, misunderstood, your articulate nature left you at a loss for words, unsure how to defend yourself or gain their trust.

It was then that you realized—not everyone is like the girl named Qin Rourou.

You pulled Qin Rourou’s business card from your pocket and tried hard to memorize her number.

After memorizing it, you dusted yourself off and stood up.

Thankfully, perhaps you still had a “tomorrow” to choose from.

Tomorrow, you would strive to do better and not let anyone down.

Carrying the braised dishes that were supposed to be enough for a lunch with colleagues at a business location, you had no desire to eat them.

You suddenly remembered the homeless man you missed that morning, and you decided to share this bittersweet “delicious meal” with him. So, carrying your braised dishes, you returned to the street corner where you’d encountered him every day.

But the homeless man wasn’t there. Instead, a large crowd gathered around him, pointing and talking.

Full of questions, you squeezed past, only to hear people chattering.

“Oh, that’s tragic! That car just ran him over!”

“He must have been hungry. I saw he couldn’t even walk when he stood up!”

“Hey, if I’d known, I’d have passed by this afternoon and given him something to eat. Homeless people like these, who don’t have enough to eat, often have low blood sugar levels, and hunger makes them dizzy and lightheaded!”

Listening to their chatter, a sinister suspicion welled up in your mind. This suspicion made you frantically push through the crowd to ask what was going on.

From their answers, you learned that the homeless elderly man had suddenly collapsed while crossing the road. Because it was late, a passing vehicle failed to notice him lying in a blind spot and accidentally ran over him.

You arrived at an unfortunate time, just as the ambulance had taken the injured elderly man away.

Just as you were mentally vowing to do better and not let anyone down, you realized that your forgotten “good deed” might have indirectly led to the elderly man’s even more tragic fate.

Upon learning the truth, the braised dish fell to the ground, and you collapsed to the side of the road, devastated.

The previous indignation and the current burden of conscience overwhelmed you. You clasped your head in your hands, hiding your face between your knees.

At this point, should you inquire which hospital the homeless man had been taken to, and see if he was safe…

Or should you try to resolve your guilt and place your hope on “I’ll do better tomorrow”?

CONTENT END 49

chapters.title: The Undeliverable Package (Part 9-1)
chapters.content:
You’ve never had a savior complex. Even when you’re trapped in this cycle, you never think of saving the world. You simply treat it as a few extra days in your long life, striving to make the most of each one.

You’ll casually help the elderly, simply because you can’t bear to see them suffer, and it reminds you of your own elders.

But you never imagined that a single, impulsive action could actually change a life.

You’re lost and helpless, not understanding the purpose of God’s cycle.

Is it to save the cat litter box lady who was injured by the air conditioner operator?

Or is it to save the homeless elderly man who collapsed on the street due to hypoglycemia caused by hunger?

You’re already treading on thin ice carrying the burden of your own life, so how can you shoulder the heavy burdens of so many people’s lives?

“What’s wrong with you? Do you know that old man?”

Someone saw you sitting on the side of the road, distraught after hearing the news, and nudged you. “If you know him, why are you still sitting there? Find out which hospital he was taken to. Go check it out!”

This push woke you up, and you scrambled to your feet as if awakened from a dream.

Luckily, the incident had just happened, and the driver of the car involved was negotiating with the traffic police who had arrived. You went to find out which hospital the old man was taken to, and found it wasn’t far away, so you jogged over.

When you arrived at the hospital, breathless, to inquire about the old man’s condition, the nurse at the emergency department reception desk asked what your relationship was with him. He was receiving emergency treatment and wouldn’t accept strangers.

You were at a loss again.

In this cycle, did you know the old man?

No, you didn’t.

Not only do we not know him, but we haven’t even been friends for breakfast.

Even if we met him, what could you say?

He’s already in such a state; is he still going to have to endure the stares of strangers while he’s sick?

“I was just a passerby at the scene, wondering how he’d fared.”

You paused, then gave a helpless smile and found a spot outside the emergency room to sit and wait.

Even though you couldn’t see him, at least you wanted to know if he’d be alright.

The hospital was a place you knew all too well. After shedding your military uniform, you spent the last few months of your mother’s life there, witnessing countless joys and sorrows.

But nowhere else did you feel like you were constantly racing against death like in the emergency department.

You watched the tall ambulance driver and the accompanying doctor push the cart into the emergency room and saw the patient’s family members wailing and wailing as they emerged.

You saw the patient crying for help, and the one being rescued screaming, “I don’t want to live anymore.”

There was no news from the old man.

You learned from the family members waiting next door that the bus-tanker accident that occurred this afternoon affected many people. Because this hospital’s burn unit is relatively well-equipped, many patients were transferred there. The emergency department is currently so busy, all because of that afternoon’s accident.

You were shocked to hear that the accident had caused heavy casualties, with the death toll now exceeding twenty.

The nurse in the emergency department initially thought you were a relative of the elderly man, but it turned out you were just a kind passerby. She curiously eyed you and asked about his condition.

The homeless man was severely malnourished and elderly. This time, exhausted from hunger, he collapsed on the road and was run over by an oncoming car.

Luckily, the incident occurred in the city, the car was traveling slowly, and the driver reacted quickly, preventing any secondary injuries.

However, due to his poor health, numerous health issues, and osteoporosis, the originally simple first aid became difficult, and his internal organs suffered varying degrees of damage.

Meanwhile, the driver finally arrived.

Most people, when faced with any situation, might first think they’ve been scammed, but this driver was incredibly kind from beginning to end.

He not only paid the necessary fees but also explained that his car was insured and would cover the elderly man’s subsequent medical expenses. He asked the hospital to do its best to treat the elderly man. Knowing he was homeless, he would also cover his hospital care and living expenses.

You listened to the driver’s words and breathed a sigh of relief.

You wanted to do something for the elderly man, perhaps help with his expenses, but you were incredibly broke. All your money combined was less than three thousand yuan.

Three thousand yuan might not even cover the cost of a single operation.

Just then, a doctor hurried out of the emergency room, talking on the phone.

“I don’t care about you guys. The man who just arrived after the accident has type AB blood. Our department is running low on AB blood. If you don’t find a way to get some blood, it could be fatal!”

Perhaps the communication wasn’t going smoothly; she almost sounded like she was about to curse.

“I know blood is in short supply after today’s explosion, but if your blood bank is completely empty, how can we perform surgery? How can we save lives? We’re doing emergency surgery, and this blood is waiting to be used! Without a transfusion, this patient will die!”

“I don’t care how you raise it; even if it’s yours, you have to send it to me!”

After finishing the call, she asked the nurse for something and hurried back to the operating room.

“Just mine!”

Hearing the doctor’s muttered words, you instinctively stood up and rushed to the doctor.

“Doctor, I’m type AB. Where can I donate blood so that I can give to the elderly man just now?!”

You’ve never been so grateful to God that you could still help and save this elderly man’s life.

After testing at the hospital, your blood was confirmed to be suitable, so you donated 400cc of blood at the hospital’s designated blood collection center and hurried back to the hospital, awaiting the elderly man’s emergency response.

You waited outside the emergency room for over an hour until the old man finally finished surgery, his life being well, and was transferred to a general ward.

Learning the result, you breathed a sigh of relief in the emergency room.

You hadn’t eaten dinner, and you were incredibly nervous. Add to that the fact that you’d had 400 cc of blood drawn, and now, feeling relieved, you felt completely exhausted. You slumped down on the bench, sweating profusely, unable to stand for a long time.

The nurse who had been in charge of receiving and directing your blood draw saw you like this and hurried over with a glass of sugar water. She helped you drink it and fed you some bread and snacks.

You thanked her for her help and were about to leave when the nurse glanced around, quietly snuggled up to you, and whispered in your ear:

“The old man’s already in the general ward. I see you’re worried about him. Shall I take you to see him?”

You worried it might be inappropriate, but the nurse assured you it was okay.

You followed the nurse to the back ward, where you found the homeless elderly man who had just been brought to a four-person room.

Unable to locate his family and lacking valid identification, the driver who hit him and the traffic police officer who had been assigned to help him complete the admission procedures.

Seeing you being led there by the nurse and realizing you were the kindhearted individual who had donated blood for him, they all expressed their admiration and gratitude for your selfless help.

You accepted the compliments with a wry smile and walked over to the bedside to check on the elderly man.

Just as you bent down to pull the blanket over him, he suddenly woke.

Seeing you, he seemed to mistake you for someone else and weakly grasped your hand.

“Don’t be like me!”

His fingers were limp, but his gaze was fixed on you as he spoke word by word, “You must do everything well. Every task is important! Don’t become like me.”

You shivered at the touch of the elderly man’s cold fingers, who was still receiving an IV drip, and stared at him in surprise.

“He’s awake!”

The driver and police officers, who had been waiting for the patient to regain consciousness, gathered around.

Doctors and nurses rushed over, some taking his temperature, some questioning him.

Unfortunately, after you released your hand, the old man was still unconscious and unable to speak clearly, mumbling incoherently.

As others gathered to inquire about the old man’s condition, you withdrew your hand and quietly left the ward.

The two of you had only met by chance, a connection formed through chance, but how could you truly say that your feelings were truly deep?

Knowing he was alive and cared for was reassuring.

You finally felt relieved.

Before leaving the hospital, the pretty nurse, with her wide eyes, asked you to leave her your contact information so she could text or call you if there was anything else going on with the old man.

You declined her offer.

As you said, you were just an ordinary passerby. You offered your kindness, but you didn’t consider the lives of others your responsibility.

The consequences of your negligence were compensated by your blood donation, and you felt no regrets towards the homeless elderly man.

And tomorrow might not be the same day. What follow-up would the elderly man have, and whether he left a phone number or not was meaningless.

You brushed off like a knight who does good deeds without leaving a name, not noticing the young nurse stamping her feet in frustration in the night breeze.

After you checked on the elderly man’s condition and left the hospital, it was already 10 p.m., well past the lottery winning window.

But it didn’t matter; you could check today’s lottery results online on your phone.

After a day of tossing and turning, you finally felt hungry. You found a convenience store, made a bowl of instant noodles by the window, and pulled out your phone to search for today’s lottery results.

You placed the lottery ticket you had just pulled out of your pocket on the noodles, slurping them as you waited for the results to come in.

A few minutes later, you tossed the lottery ticket into the trash.

The lottery was drawn, and someone had once again won 500 million yuan, but the numbers weren’t the ones you bought, and the winner had become a lucky winner from another province.

And the lottery numbers you painstakingly memorized yesterday were now just a piece of waste paper.

This was the only hope for someone in your class to change their life, and now it’s shattered.

You held a bowl of hot instant noodles in your hands, but your body felt as cold as if you’d fallen into an icy cave.

[It turns out that everything is subject to change, except you, trapped in this day.]

The author has something to say: Because Bespectacled Boy and Li Shiqing are desperately trying to change the timeline, every day is actually different, not just a struggle within the same timeline. Any altered time will be fanned by the wings of a butterfly, producing different results, including the daily lottery numbers. Therefore, the young man’s whimsical plan to use the lottery to make a fortune the next day is not very reliable.

CONTENT END 50

chapters.title: The Undeliverable Package (Part 9-2)
chapters.content:
You returned to the basement, sleepy and exhausted, and fell asleep as soon as your head hit the bed.

When you opened your eyes again, you were still in that dim, cramped basement, still as energetic as ever.

Your young body seemed to have endless energy. No matter how many flights you climbed or how far you ran the day before, you could wake up and feel as good as new.

But your heart was so exhausted that you didn’t want to get up.

Your body and mind felt strangely disconnected.

Lying in bed, you lazily thought that even such a bizarre event wouldn’t be a grand event for an ordinary person like you.

But soon, you thought of the homeless old man on the street, the cat litter shop owner who was once assaulted by an air conditioner operator, the regretful look your boss gave you yesterday, and the earnest advice your boss gave you before he left…

You wiped your face and sat up resignedly.

After folding your quilt neatly and making your bed, you changed into the uniform you’d almost taken off yesterday, washed your face and brushed your teeth, cleaned yourself up, and headed out.

You bought three breakfasts on the street. You ate one at the store, brought one to your boss, and gave one to the homeless man on the corner, reminding him to be careful when crossing the street.

Just in time, neither too early nor too late, you entered the office, handed the pancakes to your boss, and quietly went about carrying the packages you were supposed to deliver today.

As you left, you heard Lao Wang mumbling again about whether his daughter should go to Tsinghua or Peking University, and you casually said to him,

“Tsinghua. Even if you choose Peking University now, you’ll have to change your daughter’s choice this afternoon.”

Under Lao Wang’s puzzled expression, you drove the delivery truck out of the distribution point.

This time, you didn’t offer him a cigarette. Instead, you joined the other delivery company colleagues, listening to them complain about the “annoying” regulations. Like them, you labored through filling out forms and moving packages.

Before leaving, you took the trash piled in the mailroom and tossed it into the trash can outside.

You delivered a package to the family with the overweight child, and when the child cried, you folded a paper airplane for him, successfully distracting him.

You didn’t think about the big buns anymore. After all, you’d already had your Michelin-rated morning tea, and your stomach was full.

You delivered most of the packages at a moderate pace, neither too fast nor too slow. You didn’t rush the ones you missed, like a seasoned delivery driver, returning to the point of delivery just in time for lunch.

After chatting with your team leader and the other drivers about your morning deliveries, you finished your lunch and watched as the driver loaded another cart for you.

So you began your afternoon deliveries.

You first found the digital product “Xiao Heyun” had, made a few calls, and when no one answered, you set an alarm for yourself to go off every hour.

Then you waited until almost two o’clock and called Miss Cat Litter, Qin Rourou.

After confirming she was home, you sat downstairs for half an hour waiting for her to wake up. Then you carried the bag of cat litter and brought it to Miss Cat Litter’s door.

You delivered the cat litter outside without going in. After reminding her not to open the door to strangers in her pajamas, you returned downstairs and continued to wait in the flowerbed.

You saw the air conditioner worker enter the unit.

You followed him, watching him stand in front of 402’s door for a moment before suddenly going up to the fifth floor and knocking on 502’s door.

Having been to Miss Cat Litter’s balcony before, you knew why.

Outside her balcony, many women’s skimpy clothes were drying, each one delicate and lovely in color and style…but nothing for men.

Miss Cat Litter didn’t open the door. You saw the air conditioner worker suddenly trying to open the door and then reaching for his tools. A sudden surge of anger welled up in you, and you leaped forward, grabbed the worker’s neck, and pulled him down.

He struggled violently, his prison-trained rebellious instincts driving him to attack you.

But you were younger, stronger, and more trained, so in the hallway, you gave him a good beating.

“Rat Third, you’re still not behaving yourself right out of jail?”

You stamped on his hand as it tried to pull the hammer from his bag, looking down at him.

“If you dare approach the fifth floor again, I’ll beat you up every time I see you! I know where you live, and I know where Old Liu, who got you the job, is. If you dare do anything, I won’t let you off…”

Last time at the police station, you had a rough idea of ​​the air conditioner worker’s identity and background.

You looked at his expression of fear and surprise, sneering and threatening him.

“After all, no one cares where someone like you dies, right?”

The man ran away in terror, tears streaming down his face, vowing never to return to this neighborhood.

You know the person was only temporarily frightened, and over time, they’ll still harbor criminal thoughts.

People like this are fundamentally mentally ill and shouldn’t be released until they’re cured.

So you called the police, telling them you saw someone trying to pick someone’s door, that you stopped them, and that you learned the name of the air conditioner repairman from the argument.

The police replied they’d visit the repair shop and investigate the identity of the person registered with the contact information.

After leaving Miss Cat Litter’s house, you picked up your phone again and added the woman who had been cheated on on WeChat, stating that you’d seen her husband being intimate with a younger man. Then, you left it alone.

Passing by the lottery station again, you paused at the door for a moment before turning around and leaving.

You kept calling Xiao Heyun’s number every hour but couldn’t reach him.

You shook your head and sighed, placing it with the other undeliverable packages, no longer trying to contact their owners.

After delivering the package, you returned to the business point, reported your work for the day, asked your team leader to stick around, and signed in. After completing all the paperwork, you were off duty.

Today, you didn’t want to go back to sleep in the damp, dark basement.

Checking your account balance, you opted for a five-star hotel near your workplace, spending over a thousand yuan to book a room for the night.

Perhaps because you were wearing the uniform of the company you frequently deliver packages to, or perhaps because it wasn’t a holiday and there were no vacancies, the receptionist upgraded you for free.

For the price of a standard room, you got an Executive Deluxe room with a stunning view.

You’d never stayed in a room this nice before; even the bathroom was bigger than the one you were staying in in the basement.

You didn’t even need to bring any toiletries; the hotel had everything you needed…

“And maybe even things you wouldn’t need.”

You thought silently, pinching the lotion and cotton pads placed by the bathtub.

Lying in the bathtub, you gaze out the floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the entire city. The bustling traffic and vibrant lights outside seem incredibly unreal.

Your thoughts drift away.

“After all, no one cares where someone like you dies, right?”

You think of what you said today when you punched the air conditioner operator.

Actually, aren’t those words also about you?

You’re working hard, trying to establish roots in this city. You care about everyone around you, striving to change others’ fates…

But no one cares; no one notices you.

To shake off your sudden depression, you rise from the bathtub and refresh yourself with the cool air from the air conditioner. Then, donning a bathrobe and stepping barefoot onto the soft carpet of the guest room, you begin to “explore” your suite.

At first, you’re intrigued, checking out the hotel’s free TV programs and then opening the refrigerator to examine the shockingly expensive food items.

You flipped through the hotel’s room service menu, stunned by the prices. Then a thought occurred to you:

You figured if you didn’t deliver packages anymore, you could opt for takeout delivery in an area with more five-star hotels.

You began to wonder what the difference was between the plain noodles at a five-star hotel and your mom’s.

So you called and ordered room service.

It turned out the plain noodles at the five-star hotel were just like your mom’s, except the portion was bigger than the hotel’s…

The initial excitement wore off, and you looked at the empty room, feeling a bit bored.

No matter how big or luxurious the room, without your family, it’s just an empty shell, a place to sleep comfortably.

Having lost your family and sold your old house, you no longer have a home.

You suddenly felt like it was a waste to stay alone in a hotel like this.

You felt a strong desire to chat with someone, to share your unexplained “impulse spending.”

At this point, you have two options.

Should you try to contact the cat litter box lady whose number you’ve memorized…

Or should you go look for the homeless old man on the street?

CONTENT END 51

chapters.title: The Undeliverable Package (Part 10)
chapters.content:
As a man, naturally, you long for a beautiful woman to accompany you under the moonlight, but looking at the time, you give up the idea.

Calling a woman to a five-star hotel for a “long chat” after 8 p.m.—what kind of person is that?

You think of the old man wandering the streets.

You know the bridge he lives under has been renovated, leaving him with nowhere else to go. So where will he rest tonight?

And what he said in the hospital yesterday…

You feel like you can’t sleep tonight with all this nonsense, so you put on your coat, grab your room card, and walk out the hotel door.

You quickly walk towards the place where the old man stayed during the day, but you’re not sure if he’ll still be there.

That’s not a place to rest.

You hurriedly crossed several streets, and just as you were about to cross the last one to look for the elderly man across the street, you saw the homeless man stand up and walk towards you.

“Old man, the light’s red!”

The light flashed red, and you anxiously watched the unconscious man walking towards you, calling out in frustration.

The man was walking perfectly fine, but startled by your shout, he suddenly staggered and fell in the middle of the street.

Watching him sprawled on the ground, motionless, you remembered what had happened to him earlier. No longer concerned with the rule against running red lights, you darted over, stooped, picked up the homeless man, and ran.

Just as you were running away with the man in your arms, you heard the sharp screeching of brakes.

The frightened driver got out and asked worriedly if you were hit by his car. After finding you all fine, he wiped the sweat from his brow and drove away with a look of relief.

Passersby who had witnessed the incident gathered around you, praising your brave act of saving the life. Only the old man stood there, terrified, his face blank, lost in thought behind you.

After the crowd dispersed, you turned around and pulled up the old man’s hands and feet to check if there was anything wrong.

“Young man, you shouldn’t have saved me.”

The skinny old man sighed, “I just didn’t want to get up.”

“What did you say?”

You were stunned, unable to recover for a long time.

You and the old man had always met in the early morning, the only time at night, and that was in the hospital.

Aside from that one time, you had never paid any attention to where the old man was at night or whether he was still living a strong life.

Could it be that the old man’s fall and inability to get up in the middle of the road yesterday weren’t due to low blood sugar or hunger, but rather, just like today, he was already determined to die?

“What’s the point of living for someone like me? It’s a complete waste of time.”

The old man’s expression darkened as he sat on the side of the road, a numb expression on his face. “Let me run free on my own. Maybe it’ll be a relief.”

You could see the old man was seriously upset, and leaving him there without knowing what would happen, you forcefully took him back to the five-star hotel.

The old man, with no will to live, was like a puppet, letting you pull him around, seemingly indifferent to where he went. This made you, dragging the ragged old man toward the hotel, look suspicious.

So, a uniformed courier and a shabby homeless man were both stopped by the hotel security at the door.

No matter how you explained that you were a guest at the hotel and that you had brought the old man here because you saw he was dying and wanted to change his mood, the hotel security staff wouldn’t let you in.

You, along with the homeless elderly man, stood outside the brightly lit hotel lobby. Spring would have been just one step away, yet you felt only a biting chill.

The room card in your hand, like a last-ditch effort, waved in your hand, but it had no effect.

Several security guards surrounded you like beggars harassing guests. They claimed you were disturbing the other guests’ experience and the hotel’s style and asked you to move to another hotel. They offered you some compensation, hoping only that you would check out.

You endured the pointed comments and curious glances of the guests coming in and out, feeling like you were being tortured by their cold gazes over and over again.

The homeless elderly man, however, seemed to have anticipated this. He showed no sign of humiliation but instead chuckled, looking even more unhinged.

They wouldn’t let you in, and you didn’t want to cause any trouble with an elderly man in your care. In the end, you reluctantly chose their option and were forced to check out.

The head security officer brought two thousand yuan from the front desk and, with a look that sounded like you’d gotten a great deal, shoved it into your pocket, explaining that it was your refunded room fee and compensation for their breach of contract.

You supported the old man, leaning against him as you exited the hotel.

“Think positively. Didn’t you get a few hundred yuan for free?”

As you left the hotel, the old man continued to comfort you.

“In this world, money alone isn’t everything. Even if you win the lottery and have a fortune, people still value your skin. You’ll encounter this kind of thing more often.”

For a moment, you thought you’d misheard.

Once you confirmed that you’d heard the word “lottery,” you shuddered, staring at him in disbelief.

Thinking the old man knew about the bizarre events that had happened to you, your heart pounded like a drum. Your grief and resentment faded. You took the old man’s hand, hailed a taxi, and took him directly to your rented basement. The old man remained submissive throughout the journey, showing no curiosity about you. He remained silent until he sat on your cot.

Until you boiled water and served him a bowl of steaming hot instant noodles.

The braised beef noodles, without chili, were topped with a sausage. When the lid of the braised noodles was opened, the small, cramped room was filled with fragrance.

The most basic of human needs ultimately triumphed over everything. The old man took the noodles, hesitated for a moment, and began to devour them voraciously.

After swallowing the hot bowl, the old man seemed to come alive; even his numb face seemed to have regained its radiance.

“Thank you.”

He was like a machine that had finally been turned on, suddenly finding a new mode.

“It’s me who has caused such a good man like you to suffer with me and to be looked down upon.”

“It’s not your fault. It’s those people who have problems.”

You worried that the old man might become so upset that he would seek his own death, so you quickly tried to comfort him: “It’s okay for me to suffer a little. Who doesn’t suffer in their entire life?”

The old man looked at you, hesitant to speak, and finally sighed.

Seeing the atmosphere was right, you took the opportunity to ask about the lottery. Besides that, you’re still preoccupied with what he said last night while grabbing your hand, but now’s not the right time to ask.

At the word “lottery,” the old man looked you over, noticing your clear, unkind gaze, and suddenly burst into laughter.

“You might not believe it, but I also won the lottery.”

You, like a child ready to listen to a story, promptly handed him a cup of hot water.

Then, holding the warm cup, the old man began to tell his own story.

Many, many years ago, when he was still a young man, he took over his father’s job at a factory, securing a stable job.

But the old man hated mechanical work. From a young age, he loathed monotony. Whether studying or working, he couldn’t stand the repetitive, mechanical grind. At school, he often argued with his teachers over this, and at the factory, he struggled with his superiors and colleagues, enduring constant criticism and sarcasm.

But back then, the world was far less open than it is today. Aside from working in factories and tilling the fields, there were no legitimate livelihoods. Being a “self-employed business owner” was still a label that brought shame upon the entire family, and any business could only be done in the shameful black market.

The old man couldn’t stand the repetitive, robotic factory routine, so he slacked off every day and was eventually fired.

Back then, being fired carried a stigma: no legitimate employer would hire you, and no decent woman would marry you. Half out of necessity and half out of interest, the young man began secretly dabbling in smuggling on the black market. He was eventually caught by the inspection team and imprisoned for many years.

By the time he was released, times had changed, and he had transitioned from youth to middle age. Like most ordinary people lost in the rapid pace of change, he didn’t know what to do and could only muddle through life.

Having been fired, jailed, and broke, a man like him naturally couldn’t attract any women. Even his family disliked him and gradually distanced themselves from him. Only an uncle who had watched him grow up took pity on him and asked him to help out at his workplace. Whenever the company had goods to ship, they would call him over to unload them and earn some money.

Originally, this kind of work, while hard, offered the possibility of being considered by the factory for long-term cooperation. Besides the lack of a formal position, the earnings were similar to those of ordinary workers. However, something happened that made the middle-aged man feel bad for his uncle’s efforts.

Back then, the “national lottery” was very popular. You could scratch a ticket for two or three yuan, and you could win anything from a basin of toothpaste to a washing machine, a window air conditioner, or even a Santana sedan.

Many people, desperate enough to take out their entire savings, clutch boxes of lottery tickets and sit under a stage displaying Santana sedans, scratching off each ticket one by one, only to end up with nothing but a basin of toothpaste and leave cursing.

But the old man was incredibly lucky. He took a gamble with all his savings and unexpectedly won a Santana.

The days after winning the Santana felt like a crazy dream to him.

People who should have looked down on him wouldn’t respect him just because he won a Santana; they would be drawn to him by a group of mean-spirited people with ulterior motives.

The only cousin who treated him well earnestly urged him not to sell the Santana but to get a driver’s license and use it to become a taxi driver or even a driver for wealthy people, learning a trade.

The biggest hurdle for many taxi drivers is a car, but he already had it. With a driver’s license, he would never have to worry about food and clothing. He was even willing to borrow money to get the license.

But he was already so overwhelmed by the good fortune of “winning the jackpot,” and with all the people around him trying to persuade and instigate him, he ultimately sold the car.

Not only did he sell the car, but he also listened to those people’s lies, believing that his cousin didn’t want him to live a good life and wanted him to work for others forever.

In an era when a “ten thousand yuan household” was considered wealthy, a Santana wasn’t something you could buy with just money. Many people would spend hundreds of thousands of yuan on a car. He sold the car at a high price, pocketing a large sum of money, but he had no plan or purpose.

God had blessed him, giving him a chance to change his life, but after receiving the money, he spent his days in debauchery. Given the price level of the time, someone with hundreds of thousands of yuan looked upon everything as cheap. He began to surround himself with a group of drinking buddies, who would sometimes feast and drink, then persuade him to start various businesses, and eventually, they even led him into gambling…

Under these circumstances, his wealth became his own, and he gradually drifted away from his cousin. His cousin, disappointed that he had failed to live up to his expectations, eventually gave him a wide berth and stopped associating with him.

He, with a “huge sum” of hundreds of thousands of yuan in his hand, wanted to buy everything he saw and try everything. In the end, he only got a bunch of junk that might have been valuable at the time but later became worthless.

At the instigation of his cronies, he embarked on various “business ventures,” but he lost everything he did, ultimately losing all his money.

His gambling career evolved from minor to major and then into a rigged scheme. Within two years, he had squandered hundreds of thousands of yuan.

After losing his money, his former friends deserted him, leaving him with no genuine friends. They all viewed him as a scapegoat and a fool.

The people who had looked down on him continued to look down on him after he won the lottery, and their disdain for him grew even stronger as he fell into depravity.

He was already middle-aged, with no achievements to his name. After two years of living a life of extravagance and debauchery, he had tried everything and could no longer bear ordinary life. The psychological gap was too great, and his high expectations and low skills led to mental problems over the years.

He still couldn’t stand the monotony of life and had been relying on odd jobs to make a living. In his youth, he could still work hard, but in his old age, he had no means of livelihood. He would occasionally scavenge for scraps and eat what he could; otherwise, he would starve. His health was deteriorating, and he was plagued by illness.

When you met him today, the bridge he’d been sheltering in was gone. Although you gave him a bag of pancakes that morning, by evening he was so starving he couldn’t even walk, and even suicide was beyond his control.

He thought about how his life had ended up like this, blaming himself for it. He also figured that he would die of illness or starvation sooner or later, so he might as well die sooner rather than later…

So, after falling, he lost the will to live and simply lay there, unable to get up.

You hadn’t expected such a reason for his “fainting” after the fall. You felt very complicated and didn’t know what to think.

The old man’s mental state was indeed not very good. He spoke about the events of the past in a disjointed manner, repeating some of them repeatedly, some of which were either fantasies or dreams. For example, when his cousin urged him to get a driver’s license, he said he agreed, then denied it and continued to mock him. Another time, he said he agreed to learn but then found it boring and went back to selling his car. His inconsistent behavior defied logic and was constantly interspersed with regrets about that day.

If a normal person had heard this, they would have thought the old man was a lunatic, someone who couldn’t distinguish between dreams and reality.

But you are different. You’ve experienced this cycle so many times that you relate to it whenever you hear something similar.

You begin to wonder if the old man had experienced the same thing in his youth but simply couldn’t stand the boredom of driving due to his personality, so he chose to sell his car at the end of the cycle.

This suspicion makes you more cautious about your future choices. If the old man’s “crazy talk” is true, a wrong decision could easily lead to a lifelong nightmare like his.

Half probing, half sincerely seeking advice, you recounted your story to the old man, humbly asking for his advice on what to do.

“Don’t dwell on it. You’re not like me, unable to work. The same thing keeps happening, and I get irritated to death.”

The old man was in a state of frailty, his body even weaker. Once relaxed and full, he leaned against the headboard and fell asleep.

“Once the first day’s deliveries are finished, the day will be over, and then the next day’s deliveries will begin…”

Hearing your insane remarks, he spoke as if he were listening to something completely ordinary, half asleep.

It still sounded like something mad.

You were already delivering packages, and you had already finished your day’s deliveries, and you were still delivering the next day…

Wait?!

You shuddered.

What the old man said was, “Deliver all the packages.”

So the point shouldn’t be your choices but rather the importance of delivering all the packages you have?

You shook the old man, wanting to ask more, but he was already sound asleep, snoring loudly in your bed, and no amount of shouting would rouse him.

With a complicated expression, you helped him onto the bed, covered him with a blanket, and set a bench at the foot of the bed. Thinking about the old man’s answer, you fell asleep in your clothes.

》》》

The next day, you woke up again, and the first thing you did was check the bed.

The homeless man you had helped home last night had vanished without a trace, and you could find no evidence of his existence. It was as if everything you experienced last night was just a dream.

You sat up dazedly, looking at the bench neatly placed far away and the blanket covering you, feeling a sense of uncertainty about the day.

But the next moment, you saw the uniform hanging on the wall, and your eyes grew firmer.

There was no other way, so you might as well give it a try.

Starting today, you must deliver all the packages…

Nothing left behind!

CONTENT END 52

chapters.title: Undeliverable Packages (Part 11)
chapters.content:
This time, you decided not to change anything. Just like your first day on the job, you accepted all the packages assigned to you, neither greedy nor lazy.

You arrived at the company at the same time as your first day. As expected, your driver had already sorted out the packages you were supposed to deliver that morning and piled them under your car on a cart.

You completed all the procedures and took away the packages you were supposed to deliver this morning.

You bought enough food to last the day and went to the street corner where the homeless elderly man was huddled. You gave him the food you had prepared and slipped him two hundred yuan.

After leaving the street corner, you searched online for the phone number of the city’s homeless shelter, told them that the elderly man there was homeless and had suicidal thoughts, and then went to work.

When you passed the intersection again, you saw the staff from the homeless shelter taking the elderly man away.

You’ve seen online that there are counselors, social workers, and volunteers. With their help, perhaps the elderly man’s desire to die after living on the streets could be changed.

In the following days, to allow enough time to find all the difficult packages, you delivered them extremely quickly, running up and down the stairs. When you made a phone call, you didn’t bother to talk too much. You went upstairs when told to and waited when told to.

The only thing you disagree with is asking for a next-day delivery.

For those who aren’t home and want a next-day delivery, you ask for an address where they can sign for it. It could be a friend’s house or a reliable shop downstairs. You don’t mind making an extra trip or going a little further, as long as they have a way to receive it.

It’s a good thing that couriers value their deliveries. Most of them, upon hearing your request, will offer a temporary storage location or someone to sign for it. But some are completely unable to accommodate.

“I just changed jobs and came here. I have no relatives or friends, so I have no place to store it.”

A young man told you on the phone, “Delivering to work won’t work either. I’m at a training institution, and they’re closed today.”

Facing such deliveries, you’re overwhelmed.

“Don’t you have any colleagues you get along with?”

Thinking of your boss, you suggested, “Could you ask a colleague to sign for it? I can deliver it to your colleague’s address.”

“But I’ve only been working here for a short time. Why would I bother someone…”

Most people, upon hearing such a suggestion, would question why it had to be delivered today. But this young man simply hesitated, clearly not someone with a strong personality.

“When it comes to getting along with colleagues, it’s all about you bothering me and me bothering you. It’s so calculating; you’ll never fit in.”

You listened anxiously and began to share your valuable experience in bonding with your comrades in the barracks. “Look, when you first started working, you felt shy about treating people to meals or chatting with them. But when someone collected a package for you, you had something to talk about and formed a bond. You owed them a favor, so you had to repay it. That’s how people become familiar with each other. How can you be afraid of trouble?”

“Don’t you have any colleagues you particularly want to get in touch with? This is a great opportunity!”

The other person, listening to your serious nonsense, was actually fooled. Stunned, he sheepishly uttered a girl’s name.

“Well, then, I’ll call my colleague. Wait a minute, and I’ll call you back when I’m sure.”

Having convinced one person, you breathed a sigh of relief and continued on to the next delivery. You delivered a package to a steamed bun shop, carrying a lollipop, coaxing the overweight kid from the other family, and declining the hostess’s offer of a large bun; you honestly didn’t have time to eat.

You climbed up to the house that had previously given you a bad review, a large plastic bag tucked into your pocket. Without being told, you immediately grabbed the kitchen waste in your own large plastic bag and strode downstairs.

After throwing away the garbage, you discovered that the customer had not only given you a hundred-word positive review, praising your looks and thoughtfulness to the heavens, but had also sent you a five-and-a-half-dollar “soda money” tip.

You smiled, finding this person quite interesting.

Just a few steps outside, the soft-spoken customer called, excitedly telling you that their female colleague was willing to sign for your package and texting you her address and phone number, asking you to deliver it again.

You see, this female colleague lives right on the way to a package you’re supposed to deliver, so you immediately agree. When you’re delivering it to her, she curiously asks if she’s the one who asked you to sign for her.

You honestly tell her it was you who suggested it. The young man is quite shy, and he’s afraid of bothering others.

The girl breathes a sigh of relief and readily signs for the package. She also asks you to deliver a few packages, allowing you to earn some extra cash.

You follow this method, and most of the packages you previously had left uncollected. Although some require a detour or an extra trip, as the number of packages gradually decreases, you feel more and more relieved, as if you can already see yourself breaking free from this cycle that will repeat itself for who knows how many times.

At noon, you get a call from your driver asking you to return, and he happily drives one of your few delivery trucks back to your business location.

Your driver was surprised when he opened your delivery truck, stunned by your sign-off rate. Then, pleased to add a bit more to your delivery, he added a bit more.

“Are you so lucky today? Then do more!”

You: …???

After lunch, you dropped your chopsticks and, feeling overwhelmed, drove your overloaded delivery truck back to work.

You took out the package from Mr. Xiao, which you’d considered “difficult miscellaneous,” set the alarm again, and began your afternoon delivery.

You checked the time. The cat litter girl should still be awake. You delivered her package early and repeatedly reminded her not to open the door to strangers and not to hang underwear out on the balcony. Young women living alone should be careful.

As she looked half-horrified and half-suspicious, you helped her put the package away, petted the cat that was rubbing against your feet, and closed the door for her.

You ran downstairs again, knocked on the door, and asked if the air conditioner needed cleaning. After receiving a positive response, you took out the business card of a reputable appliance repair and cleaning shop you’d found on the way and handed it to the landlord, telling him that many of the “guerrilla” air conditioner and pipe cleaners out there are unreliable these days and that he should consider this reputable appliance repair shop.

Then you left the complex and continued delivering packages to other homes.

Everything seemed to be going smoothly. At this rate, it might not be impossible to deliver all the packages today.

Until your delivery truck arrived at the doorstep of an apartment in an older complex.

You weren’t familiar with these extra packages; your driver had forced them on you at noon, so this was your first time in this complex. Holding the sorted packages, you stood in front of the buildings, bewildered, trying to identify the directions and building numbers.

“Oh my! Whose child is that? Where are the adults?”

You hear someone yelling from home across the street, and you instinctively look up…

You spot a child’s head poking out of a small window in the fourth-floor security grille, climbing down.

Startled by this, you drop the package you’re carrying and run forward, narrowly catching the child who’s just fallen.

The moment you catch the child, your arms feel like they’ve been struck by a sledgehammer, and the pain contorts your features.

Your training instinctively forces you to roll back half a circle, relieving the force while holding the child close to you.

But your arms are so painful you can’t lift them, and your waist seems twisted. After all, this is an emergency, not a routine exercise, so you can’t adjust your posture in time.

The person who was watching from the window earlier thought you’d been killed by the child. Terrified, they shouted to you and quickly called 120 emergency services from the window.

You were sweating profusely from the pain, and the mischievous child in your arms was still struggling. You had no way to stop him and could only watch helplessly as he stepped on your possibly broken arm in an attempt to stand.

In the chaos, the child stepped on you, causing you to scream and finally faint from the pain.

Over an hour later, you woke up in the hospital, next to an elderly man you didn’t recognize and your trainer.

Both were thrilled to see you awake, and told you not to move, as both your arms were broken.

“I still have to deliver packages…”

But the first thing you did after waking up and struggling to get up was deliver packages.

“What deliveries?! The doctor said if you don’t recover well, both arms will be damaged. Get some rest!”

The trainer grabbed your head and pushed you back down.

“Then, what about my packages…”

You were obsessed with the packages you hadn’t delivered, your face flushing with anxiety.

“Is there anyone to deliver it?”

“You’re in trouble, and all you have is your work badge. The hospital and the police have called the company, and everyone’s so worried they can’t even think about your delivery! Your car is even locked downstairs!”

Your driver, seeing you’re so focused on the delivery, completely unconcerned about the potential damage to your arm, scolds you bitterly.

“What’s going on in your head? Do you think you’re Superman? You caught a falling child with your bare hands!”

“How can you talk like that? That young man is a hero! He saved my grandson! That felled a person. How could you not save him?”

The old man next to him paled at the driver’s words.

“If you care about your child, just keep a close eye on him. Leaving him alone to play while you take a nap is not childcare at all. Why are you still opening the windows when you have a child and security bars installed? Are you taking off your pants to fart?”

Your master had been holding back for a long time, and now he finally couldn’t help it. “You only care about the child? You’re the only one with a child? If anything happens to him, how am I going to explain it to his parents?”

The old woman was speechless after being confronted by your master. In front of you, the one who saved her life, she couldn’t argue anymore and could only sulk.

Hearing your master’s words, you finally understood what had happened.

You had never mentioned your family’s situation to your colleagues at the company, so naturally, no one knew that both your parents were dead, leaving you homeless and alone.

But hearing your master’s words in your defense, your heart warmed, and your eyes welled up a little.

“I was just reacting instinctively; I didn’t think too much about it.”

You tried to smooth things over and asked the old lady, “Is the child okay?”

You breathed a sigh of relief when you heard the child was fine.

Yes, he was still jumping around after falling from the building, so he should be fine.

But how brave and energetic must a child be to not cry after falling from the building and to step on others? It’s certainly difficult for such a lively, curious child to be raised by an old lady of his age.

While you breathed a sigh of relief, you also began to regret it. With this incident, you were definitely going to miss your delivery today.

“Oh no, I can’t make the delivery today.”

You lifted your casted arm, feeling the sharp pain, and could only shake your head and sigh.

“Don’t worry, I won’t let them underpay you for your lost wages!”

The master thought you were worried about this and earnestly urged you to focus on recuperating. “You’re still young and don’t know the severity of the aftereffects. You must take good care of yourself!”

“Yes, yes, young man, take good care of yourself. We won’t skimp on your lost wages, medical expenses, or nutrition. You saved a life, so it’s only right that we take good care of you!”

The grandmother quickly agreed.

A while later, the child’s parents arrived. It turned out that both parents worked and couldn’t get home from get off work at noon, and they got off work late at night, so the child was left in the care of his grandparents.

But the child was so naughty; the noise kept the two elderly people awake all day and night. This afternoon, the grandmother couldn’t resist a nap and fell asleep while the grandfather was washing dishes in the kitchen and tidying up, so he didn’t notice the child had climbed up the security grille in front of the table.

It just so happened that they had hung something under the grille to dry that morning and forgot to lock the window, which led to this incident.

The child’s parents thanked you profusely and offered you a red envelope, but you politely declined.

After all, the package couldn’t be delivered today, and you’d have to do it again tomorrow. Even if you took the red envelope, you wouldn’t be able to receive it. But for the child’s parents, they’d already paid it. Why burden them with it?

Your driver poked you in the head again, eager to take the money for you.

The next half day was a chaotic mess. One moment a reporter heard the news and came to interview you, the next a local TV station came to film based on a tip from a resident. You didn’t get any rest at all. By the time everyone had dispersed, before nine o’clock, you’d already fallen asleep.

Before falling asleep, you’re still concerned about whether the delivery truck has been driven back to the company.

》》》

The next morning, as soon as you open your eyes, you immediately feel your arms.

Thankfully, yesterday’s events haven’t left much of a shadow on you, and your arms are still functioning normally.

Still terrified, you get up and, for the first time, pull out a small notebook from your rental apartment and begin meticulously jotting down the things you need to address.

[Homeless Elderly Man]

[Qin Rourou, Air Conditioner Operator]

[The Cheated Flight Attendant]

[Remember to Take Out the Trash]

[A Child Is About to Fall from the Building Around 2 PM]

[Call Mr. Xiao and tell him to keep his phone on, as he has a delivery this afternoon.]

You read through each item, realizing how much can go wrong with just delivering a package. And as the number of repetitions increases, the number of things you have to deal with increases as well. You can’t help but sigh.

Now that things were organized, you felt less anxious. You woke up early and went to Tang Court for breakfast, picking out some of the leftover items you’d been craving.

After breakfast, you packed up the dim sum you’d specially ordered and left untouched, giving it to your chef on the way to work.

The chef was delighted with the breakfast you brought him and became even more welcoming to you.

You told him you wouldn’t eat lunch at the company on your first day delivering packages alone, fearing you wouldn’t be familiar with the area. You’d pick up the afternoon’s deliveries and eat on the way, but in reality, you were planning to treat yourself to a delicious meal.

You weren’t greedy; you just wanted to find a good restaurant for lunch and order one or two dishes each day. This way, you could satisfy your appetite without having to worry about running out of money when the cycle ended the next day.

Even if the cycle didn’t end, you could still order different dishes every day and never get bored.

In fact, you were starting to worry that you’d end up like a homeless old man, trapped in a cycle. You started to find some fun in your routine to avoid going crazy like him.

As you drove your delivery truck out, you called “Xiao Heyun” on the side of the road.

You used to call him every hour, but now you know his phone number by heart.

After hearing your call and hearing that he had a package arriving that afternoon, Mr. Xiao Heyun became extremely alert.

“Why are you calling me now for a package that’s arriving this afternoon? You said it was cash on delivery and asked me to pay in advance and leave it somewhere. How can I be sure it’ll arrive this afternoon? If the item is damaged, how can I prove it and file a claim? Or is it already broken, and you’re trying to evade responsibility?”

You were impressed by Mr. Xiao Heyun’s “logic” and “vigilance.”

It turns out that you, tongue-tied and incapable of lying, couldn’t justify any of his questions.

And right now, the package hasn’t been sorted by the transfer center yet. You can’t be assigned to deliver Xiao Heyun’s package until the transfer center delivers it at noon. And right now, you really can’t get a package to deliver to him.

But thankfully, he confirmed he wouldn’t turn off his phone that afternoon.

“I won’t turn off my phone that afternoon. I’ll be waiting for your call. If there’s a cash-on-delivery package, please send it later. I’m out for something this afternoon and won’t be back until four.”

This was the first glimmer of hope you saw.

You happily checked off the unfinished items on your notepad one by one. At noon, you enjoyed a delicious lunch at a nice, elegant restaurant. Then, you took time out that afternoon to deliver cat litter and knock on the door of the house where the child fell, reminding them to lock the security screen.

After finishing all the important tasks, you set about diligently delivering every package you couldn’t reach, including those whose calls went unanswered and whose addresses no one was home at.

Under your impatience to call people, many package owners opted to have others collect their packages, leaving them with somewhere to go.

For those whose phone numbers you couldn’t reach, you simply skipped the calls and knocked directly on their doors. Some had family members at home, so you delivered to a few more. At this point, you only have six or seven undelivered packages left, and you can’t get through to them by phone. You decide not to leave work until you’ve finished them all.

But after a whole day of tossing and turning, you realize you can’t deliver them all by yourself.

Especially the package from “Xiao Heyun.” He promised you that morning that he’d leave his phone on, but you still can’t get through.

Angry, you take his package away after getting off work, find his house according to the address, and simply sit outside his door waiting.

He can’t stay out all night, right? You decide to wait until he gets home.

You waited in the hallway all night until you couldn’t bear it any longer and fell asleep leaning against the wall. Xiao Heyun still didn’t return.

When you opened your eyes again, you felt extremely depressed.

The frustration of only having one package left and not being able to deliver it gradually wore away your patience.

After all, one person’s abilities and energy are limited. You began to feel that delivering all the packages in a single day was simply impossible.

You feel like you’re not feeling well. You might need to sort yourself out, or you might be experiencing mental problems.

At this point, you have two options:

Talk to the cat litter girl, or ask your master for help.

CONTENT END 53

chapters.title: The Undeliverable Package (Part 12-1)
chapters.content:
Your mind tells you that your master is the expert when it comes to delivering packages, and you should ask him for help.

But your heart simply wants to find someone who can confide in you and share your inner distress.

Since falling into this cycle, you’ve been living each day like an ordinary day, saving this, helping that, yet you seem to be nowhere and see no hope.

Those you meet today will be forgotten tomorrow;

Those you save today will become your everlasting responsibility tomorrow.

You’re not sentimental, and you don’t know where this feeling of exhaustion and loss comes from. But you know that your master, who shares your pragmatic personality, is certainly not sentimental either.

So you decide to pluck up your courage and go talk to the cat litter girl to see if you can develop some new ideas.

You left home early again, delivering breakfast to a homeless elderly man for the nth time. You called the homeless shelter on the corner, then grabbed a quick breakfast and headed to work.

As usual, your driver praised your enthusiasm on your first day on the job and personally loaded your car.

You finished your morning delivery as quickly as possible, staying up until noon when he called and returning to the delivery point to pick up the afternoon’s shipment.

After lunch, it was almost one o’clock. Having called ahead, you carried the cat litter and delivered it to Qin Rourou’s house.

Perhaps because her job didn’t require her to leave the house, she was always in her pajamas, which made you a little uneasy.

This was unlike the previous times, when it was either for her safety or to face suspicion. Every time you met her, it was an emergency situation. It was strange to think you were trying to strike up a conversation with a stranger like this.

It was a bit like a scumbag who would flirt with a girl who looked good in scantily clad clothes.

Considering you’re just a poor courier, not a rich or handsome guy, you might be mistaken for a toad trying to get his hands on a swan…

So you mustered up the courage to speak to her several times, but your eyes faltered every time you caught sight of her rose-red silk pajamas, and you were unable to open your mouth for a long time.

“What’s up?”

Qin Rourou, however, was surprised to see you didn’t leave after delivering the cat litter and asked with a frown.

“Nothing…”

You were speechless and decided to just let it go.

Just as you were about to sign the form and tell her to be careful, her cat darted out from nowhere, threw its front legs onto your calf, and leaped up as if trying to climb a tree, meowing as it did so.

“Oh, sorry, Pipi is usually very timid.”

The young lady hadn’t expected her cat to use the courier as a scratching post. Startled, she quickly reached for it. However, the more she pulled, the tighter the cat gripped, even extending its claws. Even the courier’s uniform, sturdy and durable, couldn’t withstand the cat’s claws. You felt as if your calves were instantly pricked by a spike, and the “spigot” seemed to be dangling from your leg and stabbing upwards. You were immediately stunned.

This cat was obviously a rare breed. You didn’t dare kick it, but if it continued to crawl, it would reach your waistband. That’s a vital part; how could you let it scratch you!

You were furious and anxious, and the young lady was also extremely worried. You didn’t dare move, and the young lady tugged at your leg. Seeing her hand trying to comfort the kitten rising higher and higher, you finally couldn’t help but hold her shoulder.

“I’ll do it myself. I’ll figure it out myself!”

Your face flushed red as you stammered, “Really? The more you scratch it, the crazier it gets!”

When the little sister came to her senses and looked up at you, she immediately noticed the awkwardness of your position and took a few awkward steps back, watching you squat down and soothe the kitten with a particularly gentle and charming voice.

Finally, the kitten, Pipi, lay in your arms like a spoiled little girl, letting you stroke its back and purring comfortably.

You saved your pants and your lower body. Although your thighs and calves stung a little, you breathed a sigh of relief.

“Is your leg okay? Do you want some medicine?”

When you looked up, you saw Qin Rourou blushing too.

Though you didn’t understand why she was blushing, your initial worry dissipated after this. Holding the kitten, you hesitated for a moment before finally asking her.

“Miss Qin, actually…”

—

Half an hour later.

“So, I told you, when you finally can’t stand it anymore, come and talk to me?”

Sitting on the sofa across from you, Qin Rourou, wrapped in a cashmere shawl, listened to your story with a very relaxed attitude, occasionally raising a few questions.

“Yes, I don’t know why you trusted me and told me such a private thing.”

You said puzzledly.

It’s a bit embarrassing to tell a stranger about your childhood crush.

Not to mention that she was supposedly the only one in the world who knew about it.

“You must be a very good person…”

Just from the repetitions of your dry narration, Qin Rourou had pieced together an image of a responsible, motivated, and upright person.

Willing to show kindness to someone she’d only met once, who told such a bizarre story, Qin Rourou was certain that her timeline self must have had a strong impression of you.

Even now, Qin Rourou felt no sense of guardedness. Instead, she found you, a very approachable young man.

Although she didn’t know if these words were just a way to flatter yourself, she chose to trust you once again.

You were still holding the kitten, Pipi, in your arms. No matter how you coaxed it, it refused to leave.

Being so close to the young woman and sharing your own affairs, the tension and anxiety kept your hand on the kitten’s back, stroking it repeatedly.

You were using this method to relieve your excessive nervousness.

Just then, there was a knock on the door.

“Ah, it must be the air conditioner guy.”

You stood up, as if waking from a dream, still holding the cat.

“I’ll go get rid of him.”

Qin Rourou raised an eyebrow and followed you silently.
