The door opened, and as expected, the air conditioner guy stood behind it, armed with tools.

Seeing a young man holding a cat opened the door, the air conditioner worker froze for a moment, instinctively telling you he’d made a mistake. But you were already impatient with his repeated attempts to find an opportunity and angrily shooed him away.

Turning around, you saw Qin Rourou looking at you with a hint of surprise, hugging the cat awkwardly.

“Was I too harsh?”

You worried Qin Rourou might think you were a bad person. “It can’t be helped. He’s got evil intentions. If I don’t act tough and scare him, I’m afraid he’ll come back next time.”

“No, no, I saw how patient you are with cats. I didn’t expect your toughness could be so reassuring.”

Qin Rourou praised you in her soft, sweet voice, as soft and gentle as a cat’s.

You felt your scalp tingle, and your face flushed again.

At this point, Qin Rourou completely believed you. After learning more details, she brought a notebook from the room and began to analyze the situation with you.

“Generally speaking, this kind of loop usually occurs when something unusual happens to you, perhaps something fatal, or something memorable or special…”

Qin Rourou noted the time of your first loop on a piece of paper and looked up to ask, “Are you sure nothing strange happened to you on your first day?”

“No, it was just a normal day. It was my first day on the job, but I’ve actually been running this route with my master for two months, and I’m very familiar with it.”

You’ve also pondered this question: “Until I finished delivering a package and woke up from a nap, I didn’t even realize I was back on track. It was perfectly normal.”

In reality, the homeless elderly man, Qin Rourou, the unfaithful woman, and the child who fell from the building were all unique events you discovered after delivering packages.

But these people actually had nothing to do with you. Even if you didn’t save them, they wouldn’t have caused you any “fatal harm.”

“Isn’t the root of the cycle yours?”

Qin Rourou unconsciously twirled the pen in her hand. “Then what could have been the beginning of this?”

“I met an old man…”

You rattled off the solution the homeless man had given you.

“That might be a step in the right direction, but it’s not easy for you couriers to deliver all the packages, right?”

Qin Rourou asked.

It’s easy to imagine. With hundreds of packages, there will always be some that can’t be delivered due to problems like unreachable addresses or incorrect addresses. Delivering 100% of them must be a daunting task.

“Yes.”

You listed the items that were most troublesome for you, including the expensive cash-on-delivery package from “Xiao Heyun.”

“You said his phone was accessible this morning but not this afternoon? What about now?”

Qin Rourou reminded him, “Why don’t you try calling now?”

In front of Qin Rourou, you dialed Xiao Heyun’s number and put it on speakerphone.

The beeping sound tells you his phone isn’t turned off but simply unreachable.

“Did you receive this package on the first day?”

Qin Rourou suddenly asked.

“Yes, it wasn’t delivered on the first day.”

You wondered why Qin Rourou was so concerned about this package and answered in confusion.

She twirled her pen, pondered for a moment, and muttered to herself:

“When someone buys something, especially something valuable, they’ll always keep track of where their package is and whether it’s damaged. If the courier called you this morning to tell you it would be delivered that afternoon, you definitely wouldn’t turn off your phone to avoid missing it.”

“You said he couldn’t get through to you in the afternoon, and you once waited until midnight only to find he hadn’t returned home that night…”

She couldn’t help but pull her shawl closer around her and shuddered.

“Have you ever considered that perhaps something happened to the owner of this package that afternoon?”

A sudden, eerie silence fell across the room.

In the past, hearing such words wouldn’t have been so shocking, but after so many cycles, you’ve seen so much that you can no longer treat these parcels as ordinary items.

They carry the love and hate of people or reflect a person’s current life situation. Every parcel is delivered with the hopes of its owner.

Among those undeliverable packages are wives who have been betrayed, young women who have been assaulted, and shy white-collar workers who can’t fit in and are afraid of causing trouble for others…

He has directly or indirectly changed their lives and their life trajectories.

If that’s the case, perhaps something unexpected is happening to this person named “Xiao Heyun”?

“So what should I do? Do you mean for me to find a way to solve this ‘Xiao Heyun’ problem?”

After a long pause, your brow furrowed.

“I’m just a courier, not a police officer, not a savior. Where can I find this Xiao Heyun now?”

CONTENT END 54

chapters.title: The Undeliverable Package (Part 12-2)
chapters.content:
You and Qin Rourou searched the internet for information about “Xiao Heyun,” but it was like looking for a needle in a haystack, finding nothing concrete.

Although you used your position to find Mr. Xiao Heyun’s address, phone number, and ID information, it didn’t help you track him down.

Even though you’ve truly saved many lives, you don’t have a sense of being a savior. Otherwise, you wouldn’t be saving homeless elderly people or assaulted women. You’d be focusing on the 2 p.m. bus accident and the numerous natural and man-made disasters across the country…

How insignificant can your power be?

Probably the point where you can’t even hold your head high and walk into a five-star hotel.

“Is that so…”

As an ordinary woman, it was no surprise that Qin Rourou harbored a certain yearning for “heroes.”

After hearing you were completely clueless about how to save someone you didn’t even know, Qin Rourou’s face flickered with bewilderment for the first time.

She began to help her think of a solution.

“If he could still answer his phone in the morning, could you wait for him at his door early in the morning, tie him up and trap him the moment he showed up, then deliver the package to him in the afternoon and force him to sign for it?”

Qin Rourou asked, her imagination running wild.

“What if the cycle breaks? Wouldn’t I be a kidnapper?!”

You shook your head in panic.

“Aren’t you already a prisoner of time?”

Qin Rourou spread her hands.

“I’d rather repeat myself every day than go to jail!”

Unfortunately, such a literary suggestion didn’t resonate with you; you continued shaking your head like a rattle.

She had no choice but to start thinking of a solution again.

“Then could you rush to your courier company’s sorting center early this morning and pick up Xiao Heyun’s package so you can deliver it this morning?”

Qin Rourou asked again.

“No, we can’t. Each department has its own responsibilities. We can’t proactively request any packages until they’ve been assigned to our points by the computer.”

You reluctantly declined the offer.

“How about calling the police and saying he’s in trouble?”

“Then if the police ask me what happened and where it happened, what will I say? I can’t explain how I know. What if something really happened and I’m arrested as an accomplice?!”

“Well, I’ll just accept my fate and let this cycle repeat itself!”

The more you discuss the issue, the more you’re stuck. The young lady’s advice doesn’t offer any insight. You lean back on the sofa in frustration and close your eyes.

“I think you could try my method. If you really can’t hold on any longer, being locked up isn’t necessarily better than going through this cycle all the time.” Qin Rourou took the cat from your arms, lightening the “burden” on you.

You nodded, deciding that if it really came to that, you’d have no choice but to try tying up Xiao Heyun and forcing him to stay home until he received your package this afternoon.

You couldn’t possibly get into trouble while tied up, could you?!

You stayed with the young lady for over an hour, but seeing it was getting late, you quickly excused yourself and continued your delivery.

In any case, having such a serious conversation and having someone offer you serious advice—regardless of whether it worked or not—at least you were no longer alone in this world, and some things were no longer without someone to talk to.

After this interaction, the slight awkwardness you had towards each other had largely dissipated, and strangely, you felt like you’d known each other for a long time, treating each other like friends.

“Let’s have dinner together tonight. I’ll make something.”

As she walked you out, the young lady said, “After dinner, we can go see a movie.”

“I have a lot of movies about your situation. With so many films of this genre, perhaps there are many people in the world who have gone through the same thing.”

The young lady suggested earnestly, “You could watch some of these movies. Maybe they can give you some context for your current situation.”

“Okay, thank you.”

You agreed.

With yesterday’s experience behind you, you diligently delivered most of the packages over the next few days. If it weren’t for the time you wasted with the young lady, you would have been able to deliver them even faster.

But Xiao Heyun’s package still hadn’t been delivered. It was like a thorn in your throat, yet you felt helpless.

Today, you didn’t expect the cycle to end. You pedaled your tricycle back to the delivery point and told your driver that you had a date after getting off work and couldn’t join them for dinner.

Your colleagues at the company started to tease you, asking if you had a girlfriend. You stammered, explaining that it was just a girl you met while delivering packages, not your girlfriend. As a result, you were ridiculed for having the audacity to do something unethical, and everyone came to cheer you up.

No matter how you explained that you were just having a meal, your colleagues would only chuckle. You were so annoyed that you took off your uniform at the office, changed into some ordinary clothes you’d left behind, and blushed as you refused to leave.

“I’m not leaving! I’m staying for dinner!”

“Get out, young man!”

Your master laughed, knocked you on the head, and shoved you out the door.

“You have to be bold and careful when pursuing a girl. Don’t come back halfway!”

Blushing, you went to Miss Cat Litter’s house and knocked on the door.

“You’re here? Just one more dish would be nice. I don’t cook fancy dishes, just simple, home-cooked dishes. Don’t be offended.”

She pointed to a pair of slippers in the entrance hall.

“These are the new shoes I just bought this afternoon. Wear these.”

“Oh, okay.”

You couldn’t quite match her familiarity yet, so you slipped on the blue bear slippers, a bit flattered, and followed her into the house.

It was already getting dark, and the lights in the house glowed with a soft, yellowish light, casting a warm hue on everything, including the people inside.

Qin Rourou was no longer wearing that odd nightgown, slip dress, and cashmere shawl. She looked much younger and cuter in her conservative home clothes, which made you feel less uncomfortable.

She had tied her hair up to cook, and from behind, you could see her slender neck and graceful figure, everything beautiful, like a painting.

You washed your hands and emerged, staring intently at the kitchen, feeling a sense of lost in thought.

You couldn’t remember how long it had been since you’d stood in a brightly lit house like this, watching someone cook for you.

In the army, you eat the big pot meals in the cafeteria. In the company, you eat the boxed meals provided by the company. You live alone, and when you eat occasionally, you only have simple meals or even instant noodles to satisfy yourself.

If you hadn’t experienced this cycle, you might never have set foot in one of those exquisite, high-end restaurants and tried those amazing delicacies.

But even the food in a fine restaurant is different from a meal prepared specifically for you.

Qin Rourou brought out the food and saw you leaning against the doorpost, staring intently at her. She smiled and joked, “What are you looking at? Wash your hands and eat. Afterwards, we’ll watch a movie. I usually practice copying movies, and I’ve saved a bunch of them. I found the right ones for you this afternoon. I guess we’ll be watching all night.”

During her workshops, she’d also stayed up all night watching movies and practicing routines with her colleagues. She was used to staying up late to “do homework.”

But this was her first time watching a movie at home with a man she barely knew.

You woke up as if from a dream, quickly washing your hands and helping to serve the food and carry the plates.

The meal was indeed just homely fare: a dish of tiger-skin green peppers, a dish of scrambled eggs with tomatoes, a dish of braised pork, and a small clay pot of milky white corn and pork rib soup—all delicious and appetizing.

You were already hungry after a busy day, and the food was so delicious that you forgot to even talk and just focused on eating.

This attitude of the diners was a great encouragement to the chef. The young lady happily watched you diligently eat, and, fearing you’d be too polite to eat only the vegetables and not the meat, she occasionally offered you a few bites of food.

You were full from the meal, and after finishing, you instinctively stood up to help the young lady clean up the dishes and kitchen, washing all the pots and bowls, wiping the stove and draining the water, and scrubbing all the rags.

After dinner, you rested for a while before heading to the small living room to watch a movie recommended by the young lady on her phone projector.

There were movies both old and new, horror and suspense, and even a few action films, truly eye-opening for you, a film-loving person.

Seeing the protagonist in the movie, trapped, manage to learn so much during this time, you were particularly amazed by the inspiration.

“Isn’t that a waste of years?”

You stared wide-eyed at the protagonist, who spent the day constantly switching women. “Isn’t this bad? Isn’t this just being a scoundrel?!”

Such progress in just one day—too damn fast!

“If you meet the right person, even if you’ve only known them for a day, it’s not impossible.”

In the pitch-black atmosphere, the flickering light from the large screen made it difficult for either party to see each other’s faces.

“…it all depends on who they are.”

The young woman leaned on the other armrest of the small sofa, using the dim light to discreetly glance at your long legs, which almost took up most of the sofa, and said softly.

“Huh? But this is just a middle-aged, overweight man.”

You shook your head in confusion.

The young woman looked away with a hint of disappointment, returning her attention to the screen.

“If one day, you stopped the cycle and returned to your normal life, would you still come to see me?”

She suddenly asked.

You froze, thinking for a moment.

“… Most likely, right?”

The dim light obscured your expression, and the realization that you wouldn’t remember anything tomorrow made it impossible to lie. You easily spoke your mind.

“I’m just a deliveryman living in a shabby basement. Your house may not be big, but it’s exquisitely appointed. Judging by your conversation and the sheer number of books piled in it, you must be quite educated. And I enlisted in the army after graduating from high school…”

If it weren’t for such a bizarre encounter, you and she would have been just casual acquaintances, one standing outside delivering a package while the other signed for it inside. How could there be any deep friendship?

“We’re from completely different worlds.”

“But as long as the cycle continues, I’ll definitely come to your rescue every day.”

You mistook her melancholy for concern and told her firmly, “We’re friends now. I’ll never let anything happen to you!”

“Then remember to come and rescue me every day.”

The young lady smiled softly, her eyes gleaming brightly.

“Yes, every day.”

You made a promise.

The middle-aged man on the screen finally found true love. On that night, as the two embraced each other, time quietly moved on to the next day.

The movie ended the next morning, as the hero and his beloved woke up in each other’s arms.

Seeing the way the movie ended, you pulled your leg back a little awkwardly.

Your leg had already touched the young lady’s, and the contact was warm and soft. You’d been so engrossed in the movie earlier that you hadn’t noticed, but now that the movie was over, you felt a burning sensation.

Noticing your awkwardness, the young lady turned on the lights, signaling for the two of you to take a break, drink some water, and eat something before watching the next movie.

The sudden brightening of the lights dispelled the slightly ambiguous atmosphere. Relieved, you stood up to drink some water and use the restroom, then returned to the sofa to watch the next movie.

It’s a movie about fulfilling dreams. After a cycle, the protagonist finds his true inner longing, abandons his current, phony life, and begins pursuing his dream anew.

“What about you? What dreams do you have buried deep in your heart that you’ve never fulfilled?”

The young lady chatted with you as if it were just a casual conversation.

“My dream?”

You were stunned.

“Yeah, maybe, like in the movies, when you start fulfilling your dreams, the cycle ends?”

After watching two movies and feeling a little tired, the young lady stretched lazily. “Think about it?”

It’s been years since anyone asked you questions about dreams and the future.

So you thought for a long time before answering uncertainly.

“Yes… go back and continue studying?”

“Huh?”

The young lady paused as she stretched.

“My family wasn’t well-off back then. If I went to college, my mom would have had to work part-time, which was too much work. So I volunteered to join the army. I didn’t know at the time that enlisting after college would preserve my student status, making it easier to stay in the army or apply to officer academy. Even then, when I understood, it was too late…”

You unconsciously rubbed your shoulder. “I’m twenty-two now. I can’t continue serving, but I should still be able to study, right?”

That being said, there were still some concerns about resuming education at such an old age.

Not to mention the time, energy, and money involved. Would the things I learned after work be accepted by society? Would others look at me with strange eyes?

As these concerns grew, he never took the leap.

“You could apply to the police academy, right? Being a police officer should be pretty much the same as being in the military,” the young lady said. “Our provincial police academy recruits high school veterans. You’re not too old, so if you pass the exam and go to the academy, you can still study. Sign up for a tutoring class and ask how to take the entrance exam. With your physique and fitness, you’ll definitely have no problem. And since you’re a veteran, maybe there’ll be extra points.”

“Really?”

You sat up straighter unconsciously, completely oblivious to what was happening in the movie.

“Is that even possible?!”

“You can give it a try!”

The young lady smiled at your excitement and said, “Your time is free anyway, so there’s nothing wrong with asking more questions and trying more. Besides…”

“How do you know what the homeless old man said is right?”

She played with her hair with her fingers, glancing at you casually.

“Huh?”

“Look, every movie has a different way to escape the cycle. Some involve finding true love through romance, while others involve discovering one’s true inner longing. Since you’re stuck on the delivery route, why don’t you try each method?”

The young lady raised an eyebrow at you.

“If nothing works, there’s still time to deliver again. At least you’ve experienced a different life.”

On the TV in the living room, the hero and heroine are in love on a dangerous battlefield;

In reality, you face a new invitation at a loss.

Should you follow the old man’s answer and continue delivering packages until you’ve delivered them all?

Or should you try the young lady’s advice and try each method?

CONTENT END 55

chapters.title: The Undeliverable Package (Part 13)
chapters.content:
After a night of movies, it would be a lie to say you weren’t tempted by this kind of life.

You’re just a young man in your early twenties, not some ascetic. You still have the passion and hope that youth should have. It’s just that the world is too difficult and has been especially harsh on you, putting aside all the arrogance you once displayed in the military.

Now, inspired by the young woman, a surge of heroic spirit welled up in you.

If middle-aged men can find joy in hardship and improve themselves during these difficult times, why wouldn’t a young man like you dare to try?!

But when you thought about the reality, you calmed down.

“I’m broke right now, and I can’t lose my job. No one knows when this cycle will end, so I still have to go to work during the day…”

You looked at the young woman’s disappointed eyes and suddenly smiled. “But after work, I can definitely try a different way of life.”

The young woman was very happy for you and even offered you some advice.

“If you truly believe that looping can offer you many opportunities, you could deliberately not deliver all the packages. That way, the time is essentially free, right? Think about it more positively. If you could have lived to be a hundred, these extra loops mean you’ve actually lived a little longer. Don’t dwell on yourself as if you’re trapped in time.”

On this point, the young woman and the homeless old man share the same sentiment. “Although it’s boring to experience the same thing every day, the world is vast. The world within your established circle is still new, and you can explore its boundaries bit by bit…”

You completely understand the young woman’s current thinking. She probably thought that without her earnest persuasion, you’d simply turn around and go back to delivering packages.

But you’re really not that inflexible.

You chatted until two in the morning. Your long, routine life was wearing on you, and you dozed off frequently. The young woman, however, seemed like a night owl, and she seemed more energetic the longer she stayed up.

Finally, you declined her offer to take a nap on the couch. Considering it inconvenient for a single man and a single woman to share a room, you yawned and decided to return to your own rental. You repeatedly reminded the young lady to keep an eye on the door and remember to lock it. With a movie on repeat crammed into your head, you drowsily prepared to leave.

Before leaving, the young lady suddenly grabbed you.

“Hmm?”

You looked at her hesitant face under the streetlight, thinking she was still worried about your daytime self. You couldn’t help but promise again, “Don’t worry, I’ll definitely come rescue you during the day and won’t let the bad guys succeed.”

“That’s not it…”

She hesitated for a moment, perhaps figuring someone like you wouldn’t understand unless you explained it clearly. Finally, she bit her lower lip and mustered the courage to speak.

“If you want to try the relationship method, you can come see me…”

“Huh?”

Thinking you were half asleep, you shook your head.

Once you’ve spoken, it’s much easier to say it again.

“My requirements aren’t high, and I have a good impression of you. I’m actually quite a homebody. Apart from work, I spend every day at home creating. Sometimes I don’t even leave the house once a week. I rely on my phone for socializing and online shopping. But deep down, I’ve always longed for something wonderful and new to happen to me.”

She bravely confided her true feelings to you.

“If you’re willing, I’m willing to share this with you. I believe I’d do the same in every timeline. If you want someone to walk with you, to experience a different life every day, just knock on my door…”

This was practically a confession or a courtship, leaving you, still emotionally clueless, speechless.

Speaking so bluntly must have stretched the young woman’s limits. Seeing your eyes widen and her face flush, she said nothing more. Instead, she gently closed the door, shutting out her shyness along with it.

You made it all the way downstairs and back to your rental apartment, your mind still a blur.

Did you…get a girlfriend?

But you haven’t even started pursuing her yet?

No, you haven’t even decided whether to pursue her yet?!

With a tangled web of thoughts, you drifted off to sleep.

The next morning, you began writing your plan for the day one by one. When you got to “Save Qin Rourou,” you added a few more items.

[Save Qin Rourou and invite her to dinner after getting off work.]

[Inquire about the police academy entrance exam.]

[Learn a skill.]

You looked at your packed schedule, washed your face with cold water, and began a new day.

To avoid losing your job after the cycle, you continued to diligently perform all your courier duties. But in your spare time, such as while waiting for someone to pick up a package, you would use your phone to research how veterans could apply to the police academy and what materials and documents they needed.

You discovered that Qin Rourou was right. The provincial police academy does accept veterans with a high school diploma or higher and even offers bonus points.

Although your student status was still in your hometown, you enlisted only after receiving your high school diploma and university acceptance letter. You simply didn’t report to university, thus not meeting the provincial recruitment requirements.

You excitedly copied down the entire registration process from the website, feeling as if you had discovered another world.

You meticulously completed the tasks in your plan, including the “try it with her” suggestion the young woman had given you.

Thankfully, over the next several cycles, each “young woman” accepted your invitation, dressing up beautifully for a date after getting off work and learning about your life over dinner.

As the young woman had said, she was curious and receptive. After learning about your life, she enthusiastically discussed every possibility with you, taking you on a quest you would never have attempted on your own.

She dragged you to the city’s famous barbershop, where you tried out all sorts of hairstyles you’d never imagined, but in the end, everyone agreed that your natural buzz cut was the best.

She enthusiastically accompanied you shopping, selecting every outfit for you to wear after getting off work. Although these clothes would disappear the next day, in the process, you truly understood what style suited you and what clothes would make you feel comfortable and presentable.

Even the boring fittings you’d consider were made less tedious by someone offering honest advice and suggestions instead of sales pitches.

Although you always felt like she was treating you like a dress-up doll from your childhood, you were still touched by her care.

Every day, like any other couple, after work, you’d discuss dinner plans, your partner’s taste, and their favorite dishes on WeChat.

You’d search for popular restaurants that had been recommended online, and after trying them, you’d either rave about them or plan to meet up again.

Two single young people, both of whom often ate dinner alone, surprisingly quickly got to know each other this way.

You played video games and went to amusement parks together. You accompanied her to friends’ parties and to the cinema to see a movie she’d always wanted to see. You also tried doing nothing but chatting away the entire evening.

She accompanied you to trial classes at a training center offering courses in baking, English, cooking, accounting, electricianship, childcare, computer design, computer operation, and programming. In the end, you chose computer operation and driving, while she chose baking and flower arranging.

You began to get to know Qin Rourou better and better, and your affection for her gradually deepened. For her, every day she saw you was new, and she always maintained an utmost curiosity and desire to explore you.

With someone you “dated,” every day became different, and the repetitive routine seemed less unbearable.

You began to see that there wasn’t anything wrong with the cycle, and you began to understand why so many people loved the feeling of “being in love.” The feeling of being needed was truly wonderful.

One time, you chatted with her on WeChat at work and almost missed saving the child.

Because of that incident, you were still haunted, and you stopped thinking about romance while working.

Because you never knew if your future would be reborn because of your love, and things that had passed might never come back.

But over the ten days or so you spent “reacquainting” with Qin Rourou, your feelings for her deepened. Although it was only a few days, after opening up to each other, you could no longer treat her as just “friends.”

However, to her, you were just a stranger she had just accepted.

Maybe she will believe you for various reasons, and maybe she will enjoy the excitement like a movie plot. But if this stranger “you” always shows a particularly familiar attitude towards her inexplicably and starts to use some intimate body movements and a familiar tone, her vigilance and rationality will still prevail.

So, where one day you could be so direct and direct with your first name, the next day you’re politely just calling each other “Mr. Song.” One day you could chat about anything, the next day you have to start with “self-introductions” again…

Your life feels like a bugged game, where both parties are trying to win each other’s affection. Your affection level is almost maxed out, but once you restart the game, it’s back to the passing line, while yours continues to rise, never reaching a “mutually in love” ending.

The deepening, unrequited feelings have made you lose your composure. You panic, you start to feel pain, and you no longer want to be in a relationship.

So, on the twentieth day of this cycle, you decide to “break up” this strange relationship, even though the wonderful feeling has become addictive and the other person is unforgettable.

One day, you quietly put cat litter at her doorstep and sent her a text message. Then, you waited at the stairwell, beat up the air conditioner operator as he tried to come up, and angrily chased him out of the complex.

But feelings can’t be suppressed. The more you suppress them, the deeper your longing. Looking at your sister’s apartment building, you struggled mightily. Finally, you gritted your teeth and turned away, never choosing to see her again.

For the next few days, you mechanically repeated your delivery duties like a wandering spirit, using every trick in the book to convince the recipient to come pick it up.

You tried to numb yourself with work, but without the anticipation of after-hours work, you seemed to have lost your former drive.

“Hello…”

You weakly called the courier, glancing at the name on the delivery slip.

“Mr. Xiao Heyun? You have a package. Are you home now…”

You paused mid-sentence, staring at the package in your hands in disbelief.

Xiao Heyun?

It was clearly two o’clock in the afternoon, and this phone call, which had never been answered in the afternoon, was now connected?

Excitement and shock left you speechless. Hanging up the phone and looking at the status of the call, a thought flashed through your mind.

Perhaps this was the opportunity to change!

Perhaps if I could just send the package today, the cycle would end!

“Mr. Xiao, you have a package containing valuables. I’m delivering it. Where should I send it? It’s cash on delivery. Are you home now? Is it convenient for you to pick it up?”

You spoke excitedly, feeling like tears were about to fall.

“Huh? What package? I’m not in the dorm. Just leave it in the security office!”

But the other party seemed busy and didn’t want to answer your call.

You’d tried this before: the security guards in this complex wouldn’t accept cash-on-delivery packages marked as valuables. Even if you offered to pay for the package, they wouldn’t agree to sign for it temporarily, fearing the possibility of liability.

You begin to emphasize to Mr. “Xiao Heyun” that this is a cash on delivery and that it’s best to sign in person or to deliver it to a designated collection point, even if it’s a bit far.

You don’t want to delay even a minute. Who knows if he’ll be able to get through the next minute?

“Then can you deliver it tomorrow?”

He tells you he doesn’t have a friend who can sign for a valuable package, and he’s not home. Furthermore, the package contains a camera he bought on Xianyu, a second-hand online shopping site, and he must inspect it in person before signing for it.

You desperately offer to compensate for any losses, but he doesn’t even give you a chance to plead.

“Courier, I’m really busy. How about you sort out other deliveries first? If that doesn’t work, I’ll contact you later, and you can pick it up at the delivery point yourself, okay?”

Xiao Heyun’s tone is urgent. After saying all this, he hangs up.

You anxiously call back, hoping to discuss other solutions, but he hangs up.

You persevere, ready to blow up his phone if you can’t figure out how to make calls. But after a few tries, you discover he’s blocked your number?!

You’ve been through this cycle so many times, and this time, the experience of getting through is the only one that stands out from the others.

You begin to believe that this package is the most important opportunity to end this cycle.

So you immediately turn around and drive towards the cat litter girl’s house.

You want to tell her the good news and borrow her phone. Using her phone, you call Xiao Heyun and ask him to accept your package, no matter what.

Focused with the hope of ending this tedious cycle and longing for a bright future with the girl, you anxiously speed through the streets.

But in your impatience, you lose your usual caution and carefulness. Just as you’re halfway through the road, you realize you’ve accidentally run a red light.

An SUV, just exiting the intersection, collided with you, sending you and your vehicle careening off. Your head hit the concrete floor hard, and then the falling delivery truck struck you again.

A pounding headache washed over you, accompanied by a blurring of consciousness, and you passed out.

When you opened your eyes again, you were back in the morning in the basement.

Looking at your unscathed head in the mirror, you knew you hadn’t escaped the cycle. And because of your careless accident, you’d wasted a precious day, accomplishing nothing.

You didn’t know if the child had been rescued. Anxiety and regret had you pacing the room like a trapped animal, unable to calm down.

You’d seen hope, only to lose it. You didn’t know if today would bring the light of day…

You had begun to believe that delivering Xiao Heyun’s package was the only way to break free from the cycle. Various internal and external factors compelled you to make a decision.

You decided to keep Xiao Heyun at home today and not let him go out.

CONTENT END 56

chapters.title: The Undeliverable Package (Part 14)
chapters.content:
Young people these days tend to stay up late, especially those living in the apartments along “Programmer Street.” Most of them are programmers from nearby tech companies. Overtime is commonplace, and even if they don’t, they still have to stay up until one or two in the morning.

So you weren’t worried about running into Xiao Heyun early in the morning.

You didn’t wear your uniform but instead changed into casual clothes, which you rolled up and stuffed into your backpack. You looked like an ordinary programmer carrying a laptop bag to work.

You easily made your way into the apartment building, waited for a moment by the entrance, followed the residents who were jogging early in the morning, and took the elevator to the thirteenth floor.

You had spent the previous night squatting outside Xiao Heyun’s house, so you were already familiar with the situation there.

There are two households per elevator on the thirteenth floor, but the one on the right probably hasn’t rented out yet. No one’s been home all night, and the lights haven’t been on. The one on the left is Xiao Heyun’s place. You feel under the doormat and inside the electrical box, but there’s no spare key. This suggests he lives alone and is a cautious, meticulous person who wouldn’t leave any security risks.

But that doesn’t mean you can’t stop him from leaving.

You take out the super glue you’ve prepared and drip it through the narrow opening of the security door, filling it completely around the entire gap. You then drip glue into the keyhole, completely blocking it.

You figure that programmers don’t get up too early, so if they open the door after waking up, it’s already before they leave.

Most people, when they open a door and it won’t open after a push, check to see if the lock is broken or the safety is off. You’ve dripped super glue everywhere you can, sealing the keyhole shut. The door is difficult to open with even a lot of force.

This house is most likely rented. As an ordinary tenant, you’re unlikely to risk a large sum of money by violently destroying the security door. The most likely option is to call the management to repair it.

With all the back-and-forth, plus the need to change the door and locks, it might take several hours. As long as it’s delayed until noon, the package can be sorted, and you can rush over to deliver it immediately.

This is the method you chose. You’ve also considered Qin Rourou’s suggestion of kidnapping someone, but you still have to consider your future. No matter how bizarre your circumstances, Qin Rourou might accept your criminal record, but her family might not. Therefore, you must ensure that you have a clean record to have the confidence to pursue such a good girl.

But you underestimated Xiao Heyun.

After completing this “prank,” you immediately ran back to work. You didn’t want to be late and lose your job, but you also didn’t want to miss Xiao Heyun’s package.

After you finished delivering all the morning’s packages and finally made it to noon, you were rushing to Xiao Heyun’s house with the packages. As you stepped out of the elevator, before you could even make a call, you were tackled by the rushing property management security guard.

It turned out that Xiao Heyun hadn’t called the property management at all. Instead, after noticing super glue had been dripped under the crack in the door, he’d called the fire department to break it down and then called the police.

This apartment building has a property management office. There are no security cameras in the hallway, but there are in the elevator.

The only person on Xiao Heyun’s floor at that time was you, carrying a large bag. Although you had no criminal record and couldn’t be traced, your targeted targeting of Xiao Heyun’s family must have had a purpose. Therefore, the police had the property management office monitor the elevator security cameras, waiting for you to appear so they could immediately apprehend you and wait for the police to arrive.

As for Xiao Heyun, the fire department arrived and simply removed the door frame. Since this was caused by inadequate security, the property management agreed to cover the cost of replacing the door. Xiao Heyun then called the landlord to personally oversee the matter, as it was her house after all.

So, from beginning to end, Xiao Heyun simply lay at home, made a few phone calls, and the matter was resolved.

When it was time to leave, he asked the landlord’s wife to oversee the door replacement, returned to her for the key, and then grabbed his bag and headed out the door, without wasting any time at all.

From beginning to end, you didn’t even see Xiao Heyun.

The police, having received the news, rushed over and took you away.

They suspected you were plotting revenge, and after discovering you had no connection with Xiao Heyun, they repeatedly questioned you about your actions.

You insisted it was just a prank, but your position as a courier is somewhat sensitive. The police were concerned that your intentions might give you the opportunity to commit further crimes in future deliveries. So they called your company and informed your team leader that you might be abusing your position to pull off such a “prank.”

Sitting in the police station, you knew you were definitely out of a job this time, and in a way you least expected.

You simply applied super glue, and there were no other adverse consequences, nor was it a serious offense. Therefore, the police decided to detain you for five days and order you to pay for the security door, a total of 2,000 yuan.

You obediently paid the fine and prepared to wait until tomorrow to try another method. Then, looking up, you noticed it was almost 2 p.m. and suddenly remembered that the cat litter girl hadn’t been rescued yet!

So you quickly requested that the police go to the girl’s complex and protect Qin Rourou, who lived on the fifth floor. You emphasized the air conditioner worker’s background and appearance.

“What? Are you a gang?”

Such detailed information once again raised the police’s suspicions.

“Tell the truth! Were you responsible for breaking the door, and did your accomplices disguise themselves as locksmiths and doormen to commit burglary or robbery? Don’t think you’ll be off the hook just by revealing your accomplices. Confessions are treated leniently, while resistance is punished severely!”

To convince the police to take your case seriously, you gritted your teeth and confessed.

The police immediately dispatched to Qin Rourou’s residential complex. They broke into the building in the nick of time, saving the young woman from near-violation and arresting the air conditioner worker who had illegally invaded the residence.

But when the suspect was apprehended and tried, his confession completely contradicted your previous account.

The suspect denied knowing you and had no knowledge of the “superglue” incident. He simply admitted that he had seen a young woman living alone in the victim’s home and had impulsively committed the crime.

You were repeatedly questioned, yet you offered no plausible explanation. Around 4:00 PM, you then suggested a child would fall from a building in a certain residential complex around 4:30 PM and described the security netting features of that particular home.

According to your lead, the police went to that complex and, as expected, rescued the child. Thanks to their foresight, the child was safe, and no one else suffered an arm injury like you did. Everyone was happy.

Now, the police at the police station looked at you with a bewildered expression.

You knew your actions were highly uncharacteristic, and there was no rational explanation.

If you were more resourceful, you might have been able to come up with something like a “prophecy,” but you’re so tongue-tied that you can’t come up with anything convincing, so you can only remain silent.

All investigations have reached a deadlock. You’re a veteran, always highly motivated in the military, earning the title of model soldier year after year. Since finding self-employment, you haven’t made any mistakes. Aside from that ridiculous act of applying super glue, there’s no motive or purpose for you and your accomplices to commit this crime.

Not to mention that your “clues” did indeed save two families.

“Don’t you have anything else to say?”

The police, likely curious about you, didn’t press you with forceful questioning. Instead, they patiently tried to explain, “How do you know all this?”

The air conditioner operator’s home invasion could be considered an accomplice, but a child’s near-fall while their grandparents were home couldn’t be considered part of a gang plot, could it?

Forget about the possibility of conspiracy. Even if it could be, what good would it do?

You breathed a sigh of relief after learning that everyone you needed to rescue had been rescued. You prepared to passively resist, spending the night in the detention center, waiting for another chance tomorrow.

However, before you could even be locked up, another officer came looking for you.

This officer had a kind face. Without his uniform, you wouldn’t have guessed he was a police officer. He looked like a teacher. Upon seeing you, he smiled and pulled a stool in front of you and sat down.

“My last name is Zhang. You can call me Lao Zhang or Officer Zhang.”

He showed you his ID and pulled out a photo from his phone, motioning for you to look at it.

“Look, do you recognize this man above?”

The man above was a handsome, refined young man wearing half-rimmed glasses. Although it was an ID photo, he still had a hint of a smile on his face, looking like someone who would be very approachable.

Though unsure of what a criminal police officer wanted to see you for, you still looked at him cooperatively for a long moment, then shook your head blankly.

“No, I don’t know him.”

“Think about it,” Lao Zhang gently reminded you, “or maybe you’re more familiar with this name, like…”

He watched your expression intently.

“Xiao Heyun?”

You were startled at the name, your body trembling slightly.

Such a subtle change caught Lao Zhang’s attention, and he immediately narrowed his eyes.

“You know this name? Why? Where have you heard it before?”

Instantly, Lao Zhang’s gentle demeanor suddenly changed, like a sword unsheathed, revealing his true detective nature.

You felt a little uneasy under his gaze and spoke honestly.

“I delivered his package, so I know his name.”

“There’s probably more to it than that, right?”

Old Zhang stroked the photos on his phone. “I’ve heard about what happened to you. It seems like you did something bad, but I think you might know something and want to do something good, right?”

His gaze locked on you, and you nodded involuntarily.

“Then can you tell me why you suddenly went to seal Xiao Heyun’s door so early in the morning?”

With your cooperative attitude, Old Zhang’s attitude softened.

He pulled the stool closer to you, lowered his body, and leaned in close to you.

“Don’t you want him to go out?”

You hesitated, but then, considering you had to repeat the same thing the next day, you weren’t afraid to tell the truth, so you nodded again.

“How did you know he was going to get into trouble? Was it the same as when you warned the police about the air conditioner worker and the child falling from the building?”

Old Zhang seemed even more nervous, even swallowing as he spoke.

Of course it was the same. With so many packages, he was the only one he couldn’t deliver to every day. Something must have happened that afternoon.

You continued to nod.

“He definitely had an accident.”

Old Zhang’s hand trembled as he gripped the phone, his eyes fixed on your expression.

“At 1:45 this afternoon, a passenger discovered a bomb on a bus in this city and reported it to the police. When we arrived at the scene, the bus was trying to force its way onto the more heavily traveled cross-river bridge. To prevent further casualties, my colleagues had to drive their vehicles to force it to stop…”

He closed his eyes.

“My colleagues were affected by the bus explosion and are still in the hospital.”

Even though you’d suspected Xiao Heyun would have accidents every afternoon, you never imagined something like this would happen to him. You were horrified and stared back at him in disbelief.

“This young man named Xiao Heyun was on the bus at the time.”

Old Zhang, seeing your expression, knew you had no idea what was happening to him either. He looked a little lost. “Passing vehicles saw an argument inside the car, and an on-site investigation revealed that Xiao Heyun had collapsed next to the caller. He was either arguing with the caller, or he and the caller were trying to subdue the criminal but failed and tragically died…”

“We investigated Xiao He and found out that you glued the door of Xiao Heyun’s house shut that morning, sealed the keyhole, and then left to go to work…”

He looked at you, who had already lost his mind, and suddenly shouted in your ear.

“Tell me, do you know something?”

CONTENT END 57

chapters.title: The Undelivered Package (Part 15)
chapters.content:
You, poor you, of course, knew nothing.

You’re just an ordinary person trapped on the same day, not a prophet. How could you possibly know what would happen to Xiao Heyun that afternoon?

You just learned from the police officer that the bus he was riding had exploded.

Thinking back to the bus-tank truck collision you witnessed during your first loop, you gasped and suddenly understood why the packages couldn’t be delivered every afternoon.

If Xiao Heyun was on a bus that was bound to crash, how could you deliver a package to a dead person?

Instantly, your heart darkened.

You’re just a veteran, not a special forces soldier. Bomb disposal isn’t within your capabilities, and you have no idea what’s really going on.

If you have to deliver this package to stop the cycle, then there might be no hope of stopping it at all.

Old Zhang certainly doesn’t believe any “prophetic claims,” ​​but he believes your blocking of Xiao Heyun from leaving the house and your sending the police to Qin Rourou’s house to rescue the child are somehow connected. He even questioned the arrested air conditioner worker, trying to find a connection between you.

But no matter how hard Old Zhang tried, he couldn’t find any suspicion or motive for your involvement, let alone any connection.

He questioned you repeatedly for a long time, only to find you knew nothing, and he returned empty-handed. He had the heavy responsibility of investigating the bombing case and couldn’t afford to spend too much time with you. He had to let others continue questioning you while he dealt with the relevant matters.

You broke someone else’s door, and you were already facing a public order. Add to that the Xiao Heyun incident, and you were locked up for a day and a night, spending the most agonizing night of your entire cycle in the police station.

Waking up again, you wiped your face dejectedly and stood in front of the sink mirror, examining yourself carefully.

You have close-cropped hair, thick eyebrows, large eyes, and a square face. Although you’ve been out of active service for a while, your skin still retains the tan you once had in the military. You’re not one of those “fresh meat” types so popular these days, but you look incredibly energetic.

Originally, every morning when you woke up, you would have seen a vibrant face in the mirror.

But now, your eyes were filled with fatigue.

At the beginning of the cycle, you had no expectations and didn’t understand much, so you remained true to your original aspirations, delivering packages day after day, even finding it enjoyable.

Right now, you already have a girl you care about, and your mind is focused on your set goals. There are so many things you want to do with the girl you care about, and all of them require a “tomorrow.”

So you can’t take the risk.

You’ve considered whether calling the police directly could have prevented the bombing, but you’re unsure whether you can gain their trust, or whether you’ll be arrested as an accomplice or a suspect.

You’ve considered boarding the No. 45 bus and trying to stop the bombing. But after a day of detention at the police station, you don’t know who carried the bomb or how many criminals were on the bus, making it impossible to stop it.

Besides, you don’t dare bet that you’ll be “resurrected” the next day. What if you die while trying to stop the bombing? You’re truly dead, with no tomorrow?

You begin to feel anxious and confused, a conflict brewing within you. Your moral compass and your rational mind are tugging at each other. One side tells you to try to rescue the people on the bus; the other tells you to choose a cautious approach. If the package doesn’t make it, at most you’ll be stuck in a cycle, but if you’re on the bus, you’ll most likely die.

Carrying this burden, you’re in a state of despair after leaving the house. While crossing the street to give breakfast to a homeless elderly man, you’re nearly hit by a car.

“Young man, did you sleep well last night?”

The old man, who took the breakfast, looked you over and saw the problem.

“Are you worried?”

You nod with a wry smile.

“It’s great to be young. You have so much to think about. Unlike me, I’m just waiting for the day I die and ascend to heaven to live a good life.”

He sighed as he munched on a pancake.

“There are so many things I should have done when I was young, but now that I’m old, I can only regret them. But what’s the point of regretting? Time is gone; it can never be returned…”

“What if time gone could ever be returned?”

You muttered to yourself.

“God doesn’t give people such good things easily. Otherwise, everyone would have the opportunity to correct their mistakes, and the world would be in chaos.” The old man curled his lips. “For example, if I didn’t work hard back then, I would have lost my job, and a hardworking person would have taken it. If time could go back and I didn’t quit, it would be the turn of that hardworking person to lose his job, and his life might be changed. Don’t you think that makes sense?”

You were stunned, not expecting such words from a down-and-out old man who had been wandering for half his life.

“Who hasn’t wished they could go back to the past? Everyone has. Everyone’s personality determines the path they take. I’m one of those people. Even if I don’t fall into this pit, I’ll fall into the next one. There’s no avoiding it, and turning back time is useless. God has everything planned out. Your path is your own, and the way you live is your own choice. So don’t mess around!”

He spoke, wiping away tears.

You were silent for a moment, unsure how to respond.

“Forget it. My brain isn’t very good, and I’m talking incoherently. Don’t listen to me. It’s all nonsense!” The old man looked up. “Kindhearted people like you must be blessed by God, unlike me.”

You left the old man and, out of sight from the street corner, called the shelter.

On the way to the service point, you kept thinking about what the old man had said, especially his theory that “if everyone could correct their mistakes, the world would be in chaos.”

You didn’t know what would happen to the world if you changed the fate of the old man, Qin Rourou, and the child, but you knew that if you didn’t save them, your conscience would be in turmoil.

You arrived at the service point, took over your assigned work for the day, and then began delivering packages as quickly as possible.

After delivering the morning’s packages, you didn’t choose to go home but instead knocked on Qin Rourou’s door.

“Who is it?”

Having not received a call from the courier beforehand, Qin Rourou was wary of you, a stranger, and asked you through the door what your purpose was.

You felt a pang of pain and suddenly felt that even if you died like this, it wouldn’t be such a bad thing.

The thing you had feared most at the beginning of the cycle had finally happened.

“My name is Song Budao. I’m 23 years old. I joined the army at 18 and have been serving ever since. I just arrived in this city at the beginning of this year and am currently a courier…”

Qin Rourou’s favorability rating has once again reached zero. She knows nothing about you. You lean against the closed doorframe, eyes lowered as you explain your background.

“Your name is Qin Rourou. You’re from S City. You graduated from XX University and are currently a screenwriter. Your biggest hobby is watching movies. You have thousands of movies stored on your computer. Your favorite is “The Shawshank Redemption,” and your favorite director is Christopher Nolan. You have a cat named Pippi at home. It was given to you by a college classmate when they graduated and left the city…”

The door swung open, and that familiar figure appeared before you. She was wrapped in a warm woolen shawl, staring at you with wide eyes.

You leaned against the doorframe and suddenly stood up straight. Seeing fear written across her eyes, you could only manage a gentle smile and softly reassure her:

“Don’t be afraid. I’m not some weird person. You told me all this…”

You sighed.

“But it’s about you in another timeline.”

The girl once again demonstrated her incredible tolerance. Upon hearing such strange words, she neither immediately shut the door and called the police nor cast a wary eye on you, treating you like a lunatic or a stalker.

“What are you talking about? Can you explain it more clearly?”

She pursed her lips, questioning you with a mixture of suspicion and curiosity.

So, standing at her door, you briefly recounted your story, including the little story she’d told you about her secret crush.

You didn’t mention the past between you and her that kept reminiscing.

You didn’t mention how you went from shopping for clothes with me to carrying her bags, nor did you mention the lavish feasts and street vendors, or the moonlit amusement park tonight, or the promising training center in the future.

You suppressed the fluttering flutter in your heart, lowering your head slightly, not wanting her to see more of what was in your eyes.

If you were destined to have no tomorrow, why bother others?

You told her bizarre story like a friend visiting another.

After hearing what you said, she blushed and took a step back.

“Okay, I believe it 80% of the time. Come in and talk first.”

Perhaps finding it strange to stand at the door and listen to a stranger’s story like that, she let you in again.

You worried again about her kindness and warmth.

If you weren’t there in the other timeline, could she have escaped her destined fate?

You thought about it and suddenly felt relieved. If you in other timelines had “disappeared,” the other cat litter delivery drivers wouldn’t have called at that time in the afternoon, much less delivered it to her house. She might have avoided disaster.

After all, she only opened the door so easily because of your promise.

It was all fate.

You closed your eyes and smiled bitterly.

“If what you said is true, then coming to see me today is the same as before?”

Qin Rourou brought a cup of hot milk and handed it to you.

“Do you want me to have dinner with you today or go shopping with you?”

“Neither.”

You took the mug and held it in your hands.

Looking up, you looked her in the eye intently, as if trying to memorize it.

“I came here hoping to get your help.”

“Huh?”

Qin Rourou was a little confused.

“Can you ride an electric scooter? Do you have a driver’s license?”

You suddenly asked.

“Hmm? Yes, yes, I have a driver’s license.”

Qin Rourou was still confused.

“That’s good.”

You breathed a sigh of relief and began to explain.

“Well, I have something very important to do at two o’clock this afternoon, which might delay my delivery. Besides, there’s something else this afternoon that someone needs to stop…”

You told me about the child who fell from the building.

“I’m alone. I can’t be in the east and west at once. It’s a bit embarrassing to say, but…”

You held up your mug and asked shyly, “Could you please deliver a package for me this afternoon and save the child while you’re at it?”

Qin Rourou was stunned by your request.

“Deliver, deliver?”

Qin Rourou scratched her face. “Of course I can, but I’ve never done it before, and I don’t have much experience. I might not do it right, and it might hinder you…”

“It’s okay. Deliver as many as you can. I’ll leave you my ID and work phone. It’s a daily routine anyway. If today’s delivery isn’t good, I’ll do it again tomorrow.”

You looked at her with a particularly sincere expression. “And that child, don’t take it yourself. The first time I did, both my hands were broken. You’re so thin, you might get hurt even more. Just go upstairs and tell your family it’s unsafe for him to play on the windowsill. I’ll tell you the approximate time.”

“Huh? Okay, okay. Then I’ll go change and pick up the package with you.”

She walked into the bedroom, a bewildered look on her face.

You breathed a sigh of relief when she agreed.

As you spent time with her, you discovered she was a very proactive person. Her body often took action before her mind reacted. This was especially evident when she was with you. For example, you might be talking about going to the amusement park, and the next moment she’d already bought the tickets…

So, as long as you told her what you wanted and got her agreement, she would immediately follow suit.

Your goal wasn’t to get her to deliver the package but simply to get her out of the house.

The explosion occurred at 1:45 p.m., just as the air conditioner technician arrived. You’d always promised her you’d come to her rescue, but this time, you were afraid you’d break your promise.

So, you hoped she was somewhere safe at the time, not realizing something like this would happen to you.

You took her downstairs, after she’d changed her clothes, and told her you had a heavy workload and that she was new, so it would be best if she didn’t go home for lunch. You called the driver to tell him you wouldn’t be back for lunch and then took her out for lunch. During the meal, you explained the delivery process.

After receiving the call from the driver, she followed your delivery truck to the office. You asked her to wait at the milk tea shop next to the office while you returned to your business location.

You received the packages sorted that afternoon and drove the truck to the milk tea shop to pick her up.

She was clever and quickly learned how to drive your electric scooter. You entrusted everything to her, telling her to be safe on the road and to drive slowly. Then you took Xiao Heyun’s package from the package.

“If everything goes well, I’ll meet you at this milk tea shop at 5:00 p.m.”

Holding the package, you said to the girl who had made your heart flutter, “If things don’t go well and I can’t make it back, just drive the scooter to my delivery point and hand it over to my driver; his last name is Ding.”

“What… are you going to do?”

Qin Rourou felt a surge of unease and suddenly grabbed your arm.

“Why can’t you come back?”

“It’s nothing serious. I’m delivering packages, just a long way away.”

You shook the package box in your hand.

“Didn’t I assume that I have to deliver all the packages to complete the cycle? This one is the most troublesome, and I always fail to deliver it, so I made a special trip this time.”

Qin Rourou frowned, doubtfully letting go of your hand.

After all, no matter how bizarre the situation, you’re still just a stranger to her. After you explained it this way, she wouldn’t ask any more questions out of concern for an acquaintance or friend.

“Goodbye.”

Watching her hand loosen, a wave of sadness suddenly welled up in your heart, but you took a step forward and gently hugged her.

“I hope you’re happy.”

Be happy every day.

She struggled uncomfortably for a moment, but you immediately let her go and turned away.

You had already said goodbye to her properly.

After parting with Qin Rourou, you took off your uniform, bought a mask, and then found a newsstand you knew, paid your phone bill, and called the police from a pay phone.

You had stumbled upon this newsstand a while ago. The owner was an elderly man who not only sold newspapers and books but also kept landlines, a gradually obsolete device, and provided convenient services like public phones and electric scooter charging.

You reported the bombing at 1:45. The police, upon learning of your information, took it very seriously and repeatedly inquired about the details. However, you knew little about bombings and couldn’t articulate a single explanation, so you hurriedly hung up the phone.

The elderly man at the newsstand looked at you in panic. You dropped a coin and hurried away.

After crossing the intersection, you hailed a taxi and headed straight for the last bus stop on the 45 bus before the bridge.

Due to the unique nature of the bombing, neither the police nor the media disclosed much information. You hadn’t paid much attention to the news in each of your previous iterations, so you didn’t know the specific license plate number of the vehicle involved in the accident.

But you knew the time of the accident.

The 1:45 explosion occurred in the center of the bridge, and the two stops on either side took about 25 minutes. Including the time it took to get to the approach bridge, you used your phone’s map to calculate that the bus from the last stop to the center of the bridge would take about 15-18 minutes. If you just squatted there, the No. 45 bus that arrived at this stop around 1:25 would most likely be the one involved in the accident. The No. 45 bus runs about every fifteen minutes. You squat on the platform, anxiously watching each bus approaching from Yanjiang Road.

You have two plans.

The first is to board the bus as quickly as possible upon arrival and drag Xiao Heyun off. If he refuses, use force to get him off.

Officer Zhang has shown you a photo of Xiao Heyun, and his features are so distinct that you’ll definitely recognize him.

Once he’s off the bus, you’ll have him sign for the package. At most, you’ll get scolded or even beaten up to vent your anger.

If time runs out, you’ll prepare to implement plan two: stay on the bus and help.

From Officer Zhang, you learned that Xiao Heyun had previously negotiated with the criminals and tried to prevent the bombing but was outnumbered and tragically sacrificed. You think, after all, you’re a veteran, and if he has you on the bus as a helper, perhaps you could be of some use.

Of course, he had to sign for the package first.

You waited nervously for the bus to arrive, your arms folded in your anxiety.

Around 1:20, a bus that met the criteria pulled in your direction. You checked the time, figuring it was unlikely there would be another Bus 45 around that time, so you scurried a few steps toward the bus stop, the package in hand.

You planned to run as soon as the bus doors opened.

However, the bus was moving incredibly fast, not even stopping at the stop, simply passing you by, never mind opening its doors.

Instinctively, you chased after it, running after it.

You vaguely spotted two people standing by the rear window. One man was holding something, his arm around a woman’s neck, a pose reminiscent of those movie hostage-taking scenes.

Could that be the criminal?

The bus sped up, reaching the approach bridge and heading straight for the main bridge. You, chasing after it, gradually lost your strength, breathing in exhaust fumes but failing to catch up. You collapsed beside the bridge pier, exhausted.

You watched the bus drive away, bewildered.

CONTENT END 58

chapters.title: The Undelivered Package (Part 16)
chapters.content:
You sat on the ground, a single thought in your mind.

Why didn’t that bus stop? ]

Before, you were unfamiliar with this incident, so you didn’t understand whether the bus had never stopped at a station or if something else had happened.

However, before you could react, the bus on the bridge exploded.

Boom!

The earth-shaking explosion startled you so much that you dropped the package in your hands, sending it careening off.

The bridge was crumbling.

Flames pierced the sky.

But you weren’t the most out-of-control person.

Cars about to enter the bridge slammed on the brakes after the loud bang. There were constant rear-end collisions and collisions. Others, attempting to make a U-turn, were stuck in the traffic, unable to move forward or backward.

More and more drivers opened their car doors, got out, and peered toward the bridge, trying to understand what was happening.

From the bridge, blood-stained people could be seen running frantically toward the other side, their heads covered. In the background, thick smoke billowed over the bridge like a dust storm.

Many kind drivers and passersby stepped forward, helping those fleeing and curiously asking what was happening up ahead.

“A bus exploded!”

A middle-aged man, his face covered in glass, screamed. “It’s horrible! All the glass in my car shattered, piercing my face! I was so scared of more explosions behind me that I abandoned my car and ran!”

“Yes, a bus suddenly stopped mid-drive, blocking the road. I saw people getting off to check. Just as they reached the door, it exploded, sending blasts sky-high. It was horrific!”

Another young man was shaking like a sieve, probably frightened by the shattered scene. “My car was stuck inside. I was so scared, I abandoned it and ran.”

An accident of this magnitude on the bridge would only make traffic even more chaotic than at the bridgehead. Besides, no one knew if there would be just one explosion. In the panic, it’s natural to abandon your car and run.

Gradually, more and more people ran down from the cross-river bridge. Most were uninjured. After all, those who managed to escape first were already stuck behind.

But those who were helped or carried out later were mostly in horrific shape.

At this moment, your mind was completely blank.

The roar of the explosion still rang in your ears, accompanied by the shrill cries and agonized wails of the crowd. The lofty ambitions of those who had tried to help before boarding the bus were all shattered by the horrific flames and thick smoke.

You had already mentally anticipated that if you failed to intervene, you would suffer the same fate, but even so, the bloody scene before you still shook you to your core.

Never before had you realized so clearly the true meaning of this explosion, which seemed to you like an “everyday” event.

If you had just boarded the bus, perhaps one of those shattered limbs would have been part of you.

“Help! This person has been pierced by the explosives!”

A tall young man was pacing the bridgehead, his shirt sleeves rolled up to his elbows, checking on the injuries of those being carried out, like a doctor. His eyes swept over the idlers standing at the bridgehead, and he spotted you sitting by the pier. He pointed.

“Big guy over there, come and help! This person needs to be moved out immediately. It’s so congested here, the ambulance won’t be able to get through!”

You were half-conscious, distracted, until someone tapped you on the shoulder.

You looked up and saw a woman with long, flowing hair.

“That person is calling you.”

She gestured to look the other way.

“Please help too!”

Hearing the person’s shout, you awoke as if from a dream and rushed over to help.

The bus explosion paralyzed traffic in the entire bridge area. Ambulances, fire trucks, and police cars were dispatched quickly, but the traffic was so bad that most vehicles were stuck outside, unable to enter to assist.

At that moment, under the leadership of that tall young man, the drivers and passersby at the bridgehead formed a makeshift rescue team. Working alongside the medical staff, they carried or even shouldered the most seriously injured, evacuating them from the traffic jam.

You were a member of this “makeshift rescue team.”

You were young, strong, diligent, and attentive. You had participated in numerous rescue operations with the military and were experienced in evacuating casualties.

Most importantly, you were neither afraid of the devastation at the explosion site nor did you disdain the blood-soaked victims. Your composure infected the others present, and under your influence, those helping you became increasingly skilled.

It soon became apparent that among all the helpers, you were the most hardworking and useful. So, both the tall young man and the subsequent medical responders were constantly “ordering” you around.

But you had no complaints, simply wanting to help save as many lives as possible.

The hectic and frantic rescue efforts at the scene dispelled your fear and anxiety about the explosion. Your attention gradually shifted from “Xiao Heyun” and

“delivering packages,” and you devoted yourself wholeheartedly to saving lives.

Soon, the traffic police took over the area and evacuated traffic. The ambulance and fire trucks successfully made their way to the bridgehead. The role played by your “makeshift rescue team” was gradually replaced by the “regular forces,” and you could finally take a break.

After loading the last burn victim into the ambulance, the tall young man patted your shoulder, reminding you not to carry any more, and handed you a bottle of mineral water.

You wiped the sweat from your forehead and followed him to a slightly cleaner spot to sit down. Only then did you realize your back and waist ached, and your legs, straining from exertion, were trembling slightly.

The young man wasn’t much better off, covered in blood.

You both ignored the dirt, were exhausted, and only wanted to rest.

“Such a major accident, I wonder how many casualties it caused.”

The young man, with a sparse face, leaned against the wall, frowning as he greeted you. “I heard someone planted a bomb on a bus. Apparently, the passengers discovered it, but they didn’t have time to get it out…”

“There were too many people and cars on the bridge,” he sighed.

You said nothing, just sipped your water.

You couldn’t tell him that you’d managed to call the police before coming here.

But whether it was due to lack of time or the vague information you provided, the situation had reached a point of no return.

And you, in fact, just wanted to deliver a package.

Speaking of deliveries, you belatedly realized that the package you were supposed to deliver was missing.

When the explosion suddenly occurred, you were startled by the loud noise, and the package slipped out of your hands. Then, in the chaos, you were so focused on saving people that you never even remembered to retrieve it.

But who cares about deliveries these days?

You wiped your face and smiled wryly.

“I see you’re carrying the stretcher very professionally. Did you work in a hospital before?”

Perhaps sensing the solemn atmosphere, the young man changed the subject.

“No. But I was a soldier before, and I participated in earthquake rescue efforts in XX City and the evacuation of injured personnel following the flash flood in XX City.”

You said modestly, “I wouldn’t call myself a professional; after all, I’ve done similar things before.”

“So you’re a courier now? That’s a waste, isn’t it?”

The other person asked curiously.

“As long as I can support myself, there’s nothing to waste.”

You knew the other person had recognized your courier uniform and shook his head in self-mockery.

“Are you interested in working at the Municipal Medical Emergency Center? While our work is busy, the pay is good, and we need people like you. The center is currently recruiting logistics and medical support staff for the social emergency department. No experience is a problem; we have specialized training.”

The young man sized up your muscular figure and suddenly started poaching.

“Huh?”

You were stunned.

“Oh, I forgot to introduce myself. I’m the ambulance driver at the Medical Emergency Center. My name is Feng Rui.”

Feng Rui slapped his forehead and said to you.

“You’re a driver? I thought you were a doctor!”

Your eyes widened in surprise.

The young man’s method of assessing the severity of the injury and providing emergency treatment was so professional that you had assumed he was a doctor on vacation.

“I used to be a doctor, but due to some things…”

He paused for a moment, then quickly regained his composure. “You might consider the job I’m talking about. I think you have the potential and the ability to do it well.”

You chatted for a while, realizing your personalities were perfectly compatible. The ambulance driver, Feng Rui, was cheerful and humorous. Now, once out of the tense atmosphere, he frequently spouted off amusing remarks, making you laugh several times.

“Oh, I finally got a day off, and it’s even more tiring than working.”

As he spoke, he seemed to notice something and suddenly stood up.

“I’ll call you later. I saw someone I know. I’ll excuse myself for now.”

You watched him leave and noticed he was walking towards a female traffic police officer, who was tapping her arm with exhaustion.

You and he had been chatting so well that he’d insisted on exchanging WeChat and phone numbers with you and even sent you a bunch of job postings at emergency centers.

You couldn’t resist the offer, so you cheerfully added the friend and accepted the job recommendation. But deep down, you knew that no matter how much you struck up with him today, once that day was over, even if you ran into this new friend on the street, you’d be nothing more than strangers brushing past each other.

Unless you chose to work at the emergency center just to make this friend…

Shaking your head, you recalled the police academy Qin Rourou had accompanied you to learn about and suppressed the thought.

You stood up melancholy, realizing it was getting dark. Pulling out your personal phone, you saw it was already past six.

You and Qin Rourou had agreed to meet at the milk tea shop at 5:30 if everything went well, and you would take the delivery truck and package back.

If things didn’t go well, she would wait until six, and if he didn’t return, she would drive the truck back to the delivery point.

Your phone was littered with missed calls, both from Qin Rourou and your master.

When rescuing people, the situation is chaotic and noisy, and there are many injured people. Your cell phone keeps vibrating in your pocket, interfering with your rescue efforts, so you switch the phone to silent mode.

Now that you have some free time, you finally have a chance to call back.

You dialed Qin Rourou’s number, and the phone only rang twice before being picked up.

“Thank God, you finally answered!”

Qin Rourou’s tone was tinged with complaint. “I followed your instructions and drove to the delivery station. The driver you mentioned detained me and insisted on finding you before releasing me. When will you come to rescue me?”

“I’m so sorry, so sorry!”

You knew that doing this would likely result in losing your job in this timeline, but to protect Qin Rourou’s safety and minimize the company’s losses, you had no choice but to do it.

“Don’t talk so much. Come back soon! I was so worried when you didn’t come back. I was so worried, afraid something might happen to you!”

Qin Rourou urged from the other end of the line.

“I did everything you told me to do. I even went to the neighborhood. The child is fine.”

“You little brat, hurry back! You’re breaking the rules and regulations, even running around with a package labeled “valuable items.” The team leader was about to call the police, but I called the police. If you don’t give us a good reason, expect bad luck!”

The master, having snatched the phone, yelled at you from the other end.

You promised to come back immediately and hung up.

It was impossible to get a taxi in this situation. Fortunately, a kind man carrying the stretcher with you just drove by. Knowing you were going back to the company, he enthusiastically let you in and took you home.

When you arrived at the delivery point, the atmosphere was terrible.
