Qin Rourou sat on a small round stool, her hands folded on her knees, nervously glancing at the door. Seeing you finally return, a smile lit up her face.

Your colleagues, who were eating, glanced up at you when you came in. Instead of inviting you to join them, they lowered their heads to devour their food.

The stern-faced team leader had been glaring at you since you entered, as if you were a “fugitive” with bad behavior. Your master, standing in the corner, was smoking a cigarette. Seeing you return, he tossed his cigarette to the ground and stomped on it.

“You still remember to come back?”

He stomped out his cigarette, his expression as if he wanted to rush over and beat you up.

“You’re incredible! On your first day at work, you went out on your own and left a package for someone else to deliver? What if it gets lost? What if something happens along the way?”

You accepted the scolding sincerely and expressed your willingness to bear all consequences, even if it meant getting fired.

However, your attitude infuriated your master.

“Is this a question of whether or not to take responsibility? You just say you don’t want to do it, so what? Who are you threatening? I’ve worked so hard to train you for two months, I’ve taken such good care of you, and you’re slapping me in the face. Don’t you know that?”

Your master was furious, glaring at you.

“And what about that package? Where did it go?!”

“Lost.”

You lowered your head and muttered.

It was indeed lost, and we don’t even know where it went.

“Either you compensate the customer for all their losses, or we’ll call the police.”

The cold-faced team leader had already checked the contents of the package and had no more leniency for you.

“We’ve contacted the customer who sent the package. The package contained a 90% new SLR lens, valued at 12,000 yuan. They can provide relevant receipts as proof. The customer chose insurance, so you must compensate them in full.”

Your face paled.

Twelve thousand yuan, even if you put all your money together, wouldn’t be enough.

“Also, you were absent from work for half a day today and delegated the work to someone outside the company. This is a serious violation, and we can’t keep you here any longer.”

The cold-faced team leader said, “After compensating the client for their losses, resign. If you’re fired, your reputation and your file will be in jeopardy.”

“What were you doing this afternoon? Your girlfriend won’t say a word when I ask her. We don’t know when you left or what you were doing, and we can’t keep you in custody! If it wasn’t just your package that was lost, she’d be implicated too!”

Your master was exhausted, as if he’d encountered a pair of thieves.

“I’m not his girlfriend.”

“She’s not my girlfriend.”

“You and Qin Rourou,” they said in unison.

“Is that the point?”

Your master glared at you, annoyed. “What’s wrong with you?”

Qin Rourou glanced at you worriedly, and you, coincidentally, glanced over, worried about implicating her. Your gazes met, then averted, both of you looking awkwardly at each other.

“Damn! What’s that affectionate stare you’re giving each other now?”

The master went berserk.

“Hey, look! Is that Song Budao?!”

A colleague, who was eating, asked the person next to him, holding up his phone.

“What’s that? Why was he over there at the bridge this afternoon?!”

Seeing everyone else looking over, the colleague who had been playing with his phone during lunch turned up the volume on his video.

It turned out that when you and Feng Rui were rescuing the injured that afternoon, a member of the media present had recorded the scene. Coupled with the fact that many bystanders and those involved also took photos, your group of rescuers quickly became a trending topic, capitalizing on the buzz surrounding the explosion.

Among them, you, the courier, stood out particularly because you were wearing your company uniform.

Seeing you in the video, sweating profusely as you carried the stretcher back and forth, your arms and legs trembling with exhaustion, yet you gritted your teeth and persevered, everyone fell silent.

CONTENT END 59

chapters.title: The Undeliverable Package (Part 17)
chapters.content:
Today’s explosion had already become the hottest news online. You hadn’t paid much attention to it before because you were so busy delivering packages that you had no time to stop and check your phone.

This explosion caused numerous casualties, but it also highlighted many fearless heroes, such as the ambulance driver Feng Rui, who calmly directed the evacuation of the injured at the scene.

The leading organizers are certainly admirable, but those like you who bravely stayed at the scene, watching over and saving lives, despite the danger, should never be taken for granted. After all, no one knows if the explosion will only happen once, and those who bravely stayed at the scene are heroes.

“Since you were doing a good deed, why didn’t you say so just now?”

After watching the video, the cold-faced team leader felt a little uncomfortable and said with a hint of complaint, “And even if you were going to save people, you shouldn’t have handed the delivery truck over to someone else.”

Now, the team leader didn’t say anything about taking the package away without permission being considered theft.

You knew the team leader and the others had misunderstood, and you wanted to explain that you hadn’t entrusted the delivery truck to Qin Rourou to save people. However, before you could open your mouth, Qin Rourou winked at you frantically, and this distraction prevented you from explaining.

It was your master who noticed something was amiss.

“Your delivery area isn’t over there by the bridge. How did you get there this afternoon?”

Your master was terrified. “Running around like that! What if it explodes and you get hit?”

At this moment, your master’s primary concern was your safety, which made you feel a surge of warmth.

“He said he had a particularly troublesome package, and the delivery person was waiting for him at the bridge. He couldn’t sign for it, and if he didn’t deliver it, he wouldn’t accept it, so he went over there!”

Qin Rourou thought of your explanation today and, fearing you wouldn’t be able to articulate it, quickly explained for you. “He was worried that delivering that package would delay the other deliveries, so he asked me to watch the delivery truck while he went over there with the packages!”

You didn’t expect Qin Rourou to speak up for you, and you looked over gratefully.

“When faced with such unreasonable customers, there’s no need to give in to them. Besides, the package is insured for a large sum. Who knows if they’re trying to extort the insurance?”

Your master frowned and instructed you.

“There are so many scammers these days. Some people ship a broken, valuable item and insure it for a high price, only to claim it was damaged during delivery after unpacking it, hoping to defraud you of the quoted price. We’ve been in this business for a long time and have seen it all. We know you have good intentions, but we can’t be completely unprepared!”

You can’t say you weren’t scammed, and that “Mr. Xiao” didn’t deliberately force you to deliver the item across the bridge.

At this moment, Mr. Xiao in this timeline should have met with disaster once again.

“Next time you encounter a difficult customer like this, don’t deliver to them. If the recipient refuses to sign for the package or is unable to sign, if there’s a disagreement during communication, or if the recipient’s package repeatedly goes undelivered, the package can be returned to the sender. The company has relevant regulations.”

The cold-faced team leader also followed suit: “This is how the company protects itself and its employees. Although we’re in the service industry, we don’t have to unconditionally comply with customer demands. Was the package you lost the one destined for the bridge?”

“Yes, Mr. Xiao Heyun, the one I was delivering to, was on the bus that exploded. I was planning to deliver it to him at the stop closest to the bridge…”

Your mood darkened at the mention of Mr. Xiao.

“In the end, I didn’t catch up with the bus, and it exploded. Then, there was chaos on the bridge, and the package was lost.”

Upon hearing that the recipient of the package was on the bus, everyone at the delivery point fell silent again.

Everyone knew it was impossible for anyone in the car to survive an explosion of that magnitude. This package was destined to be undelivered.

“Hey, I’ll contact the sender and explain the situation. I hope they’ll understand and reduce the compensation.”

The cold-faced team leader, despite his cold exterior, was kindhearted. He finally relented and offered to help you find a solution.

“But if they can’t understand, you’ll have to pay over 10,000 yuan. If you don’t have the money, you can pay it back in installments.”

“I understand. Thank you, team leader.”

You knew the cycle was likely to repeat itself, and the debt of over 10,000 yuan wasn’t enough to crush you immediately, so your emotions didn’t change much.

But now you knew the package contained a camera worth tens of thousands of yuan. You couldn’t leave it lying around. You have to be extra careful next time.

Don’t let the cycle stop and ruin yourself over a package.

The cold-faced team leader called the sender’s number right in front of you, but no one answered. After several calls, a woman’s voice came through the speakerphone. “Hello, are you Mr. Jiang’s family member?”

The cold-faced team leader asked curiously, perhaps not expecting a woman to answer the phone.

“Doctor Jiang has something going on and can’t answer the phone right now. If you need anything, could you please call back in a few days?”

The woman said, her voice choking with sobs, “I’m his colleague.”

Since she had said that, the cold-faced team leader couldn’t ask any further questions and could only hang up.

“Something’s wrong? What could it be?”

Your master curiously leaned over to check the address displayed on the computer.

“Orthopedics Department, First People’s Hospital of XX City? Is this a doctor sending this?”

“Probably.”

The cold-faced team leader glanced at you.

“You’re lucky! The other party was busy and couldn’t immediately pursue your claims for the damages. This gives you a few more days to resolve this matter. But don’t get carried away. Next time you encounter this kind of situation, contact the sender as soon as possible to see if you can return the package to avoid further losses for you and the company.”

“I understand…”

You replied with a wry smile, unable to say you didn’t have “a few days” nor did you need “a few days” to resolve the situation.

Wait—!

At that moment, a thought flashed through your mind.

What if, for example, if the recipient is unable to sign for or refuses to sign for a package, or if it’s repeatedly undeliverable, it can be returned to the sender…

Then if you can’t deliver a valuable item during the day, could you take advantage of the sender’s cherishment of the item and request a return to the shipping address?

At most, you’d have to cover the return fee!

If that were possible, then you wouldn’t be unable to deliver all your packages!

This hypothetical possibility instantly excited you, and your mind was filled with plans for how to deliver every package tomorrow. Excited, you didn’t want to waste any more time; you just wanted to get some sleep and rush off to deliver the next day.

Unfortunately, things in this world don’t always go as planned.

Just as you were about to confess to the cold-faced team leader that you were “willing to take full responsibility” and take Qin Rourou away, he suddenly received a phone call.

“Hello? Uh-huh. This is the Marriott Express location. Off-duty? We’re all still here. Yes, everyone’s here. No one’s taking a day off today. You’re asking about Xiao Song? Xiao Song’s here too.”

The cold-faced team leader finished the call with a series of hums and ahs. When he looked up, he gave you a strange look.

“The provincial TV station wants to interview you. The higher-ups said this is a great opportunity to showcase the positive social energy of our employees. We hope you’ll cooperate with the interview and not leave for now. The company said you performed very well this time and will award you a bonus from the employee incentive fund. We hope you’ll focus on the company’s long-standing commitment to social responsibility in the interview.”

He seemed to agree that you’d had a very “full” day and couldn’t help but sigh.

“Your luck has turned.”

“So, do I have to quit?”

You hadn’t yet grasped the meaning of the cold-faced team leader’s long string of words, but you did understand the mentions of “you performed well” and “giving you a bonus.” It couldn’t be a bad thing after all.

“Resign?! ​​This is a blessing in disguise! You’re going to be famous!”

“Your master,” he said angrily.

“You might even have to pay for the camera!”

“Alright, stop gossiping! The TV station people are on their way. Let’s clean up the delivery point quickly. We don’t want them to come over and film our messy workplace.”

The cold-faced team leader didn’t have time for any more pleasantries. He urged everyone in the office to get moving.

Seeing Qin Rourou still sitting against the wall with curious eyes, he quickly gave you a chuckle.

“Someone’s coming to interview you later. Your girlfriend wouldn’t be right here. Tell her to go back or wait in the back.”

“She’s not me…”

You watched the cold-faced team leader walk away, and you blushed as you apologized to Qin Rourou, “I’m sorry, they misunderstood.”

“It’s okay, it’s okay.”

The young woman in this timeline wasn’t angry. She smiled and shook her head, then leaned in to whisper, “You said you were going to do something important this afternoon. Are you going to stop that bombing?”

Her eyes sparkled with a hint of admiration. You knew she was deliberately misunderstanding you because of this series of coincidences, so you quickly waved her off.

“No, no, I really was delivering a package, but it just didn’t make it to the truck!”

“I know it’s hard for you to explain, so I won’t ask any more questions.”

Qin Rourou smiled, giving you an “I understand” expression and winking. “If you need my help tomorrow during your cycle, just come and see me. I delivered the package for you today, and I didn’t think it was too difficult. I should be able to handle it tomorrow, too.”

You knew she wouldn’t believe it was just a coincidence, so you sighed and tried to send her out.

“No need to send me off. I haven’t even met anyone to interview yet, so this counts as interviewing. I’ll just pretend to be your company employee and wait in the back workshop.”

Qin Rourou smiled, said hello to your master, and went back into the workshop.

“You still say she’s not your girlfriend, talking and laughing, and you just got so close!”

Your master, carrying boxes, passed by you. Seeing you staring blankly at Qin Rourou’s back, he couldn’t help but elbow you hard. “What are you looking at, little brat? Come over and help!”

“Huh? Oh, sure!”

You woke up as if from a dream and quickly rolled up your sleeves to help.

As he got closer, your master noticed brown stains on your black company uniform. They were obviously blood stains from that afternoon, but the dark color of the uniform made them hard to see.

Thinking of what you’d been busy with all afternoon, your master’s heart grew stronger, and his attitude towards you became even more amiable.

But for you, what happened next was even more tiring than the whole afternoon of moving the injured.

You’d never been interviewed before, and you didn’t know how to convey your company’s “positive social responsibility.” And you were incredibly clumsy with your words, unable to deliver a smooth and articulate message.

It’s already after getting off work, and the publicity department of your courier company has urgently sent you a potentially useful interview script. But before you’ve even finished reading it, reporters and photographers have already swarmed the delivery point.

Faced with question after question from the reporters, you constantly stumble, your clumsiness so embarrassing that your master and the cold-faced team leader are embarrassed. Even the reporters think this is going to turn into an “interview disaster.”

When the reporter asks, “Why are you there?” the cold-faced team leader and your master look at you nervously, worried you’ll reveal your afternoon dereliction of duty.

“I have a very important package to deliver. It says, ‘This person is a pillar of the nation; please give him priority delivery.'”

As soon as you opened your mouth, several TV crews burst into laughter.

This tactic is often seen on express packages. Sometimes it’s written “Pillar of the Nation,” sometimes “Future Star.” It’s simply a way to attract the courier’s attention, something meant to make both the recipient and the courier happy, but no one would take it seriously.

Only you know what a remarkable person Mr. Xiao Heyun is.

Officer Zhang said that Xiao Heyun discovered a bomb in the car, called the police, and negotiated with the attackers. Although he failed to subdue the attackers and ultimately died, he lived up to the title of “Pillar of the Nation.”

On the other hand, he, despite being a veteran, simply didn’t have the courage to give up his life and face the explosion head-on.

“That was a precious package, carrying so much.”

It carried the sender’s hopes, the recipient’s expectations, and even more, his vision of escaping his shackles.

“I wanted to deliver the package quickly. I knew the courier’s owner was on the No. 45 bus, so I went to the nearest bus stop to get him there. Who knew his car would explode…”

At this point, the smiles on the interviewers’ faces slowly faded.

No one could have imagined that your reason for going to the scene would be so tragic.

》》》

After the TV interview, the cold-faced team leader sent the TV crew away, and you personally walked Qin Rourou home after the interview.

You didn’t have any transportation to take her home, but fortunately, the delivery point wasn’t far from Qin Rourou’s home, only a twenty-minute walk. So, Qin Rourou declined your offer of a taxi and decided to walk back with you.

On the way back, she asked about the details of your past interactions with her from other timelines.

A cool night breeze caressed the quiet path, and a gentle girl stood by the dimly lit roadside, walking side by side with you. These scenes blended together, seeming to be filled with a kind of magic, soothing your tired and anxious heart from the day.

You enjoyed the quiet atmosphere, slowly slowing your pace.

You walked Qin Rourou all the way home, watching her go inside.

She stood at the doorway, telling you it was getting late and that you could rest at her house, but you declined.

“Remember to come see me tomorrow.”

As you left, she smiled and said, “Although I’m not a hero, I’m happy to help heroes.”

You thanked her and promised to come see her.

From your answer, she knew you would definitely deliver the package tomorrow. A look of admiration crossed her face, and she suddenly stood on tiptoe and kissed you.

You were stunned, covering your face in idiotic fashion.

“If you’re done tomorrow night, we can go on a date.”

She looked at your dazed expression, smiled, and said this.

Then she shyly closed the door.

You returned to your rental apartment with a silly smile.

You haven’t washed your face today. As you lay in bed, the intense anticipation rising in your chest made it impossible for you to fall asleep as you wished. You tossed and turned, unable to fall asleep.

You simply sat up and searched online for details about the explosion that had happened today.

After a long time of tossing and turning, your head began to feel dizzy again, but the flash of inspiration you had at the delivery point did not disappear.

“Tomorrow, tomorrow I must deliver all the packages!”

You closed your eyes and said to yourself.

“I want to end this…”

Then go on a date!

CONTENT END 60

chapters.title: The Undeliverable Package (Part 18)
chapters.content:
As soon as you opened your eyes, you immediately got out of bed without any delay.

After brushing your teeth and washing your face, you dressed in plain clothes, stuffed your company uniform into a large bag, pocketed all your cash, and headed out the door.

Yesterday, because you lost your package, the company wanted you to compensate them. So, the cold-faced team leader pulled up the shipping information and insurance amount for you to see, fearing you might think the company was blackmailing you.

From yesterday’s shipping information, you learned that this package had been sent the previous evening from a county-level city in this city, just over two hours’ drive away—not too far. However, because the package wasn’t picked up until 7 p.m. the previous evening, it wasn’t sorted and delivered until noon the next day.

You can’t intercept it en route, but you can find a way to have it returned before delivery.

One option is to return the package after receiving it, claiming it can’t be delivered. However, if you realize it can’t be delivered after just one day, not only will the sender be upset, but your supervisor and the cold-faced team leader will definitely make you carry the package with you for a few days.

The second option is to ask the sender to cancel the shipment and try again next time.

Sometimes, packages get mixed up or sent to the wrong address, and the sender will try to retrieve them. If the package hasn’t been delivered by then, you can request a return by contacting the courier. Of course, the shipping fee will not be refunded.

You’re targeting the second option.

After all, this package contains a camera worth 12,000 yuan. If you hear something’s not right with the package and the courier offers to return it for inspection, most people will agree. After all, a dispute involving over 10,000 yuan is a huge investment, and no one wants to have to deal with such a situation later.

Before that, you need to deliver all your morning packages. After receiving a package at noon, contact the sender as quickly as possible. Then, take a bus to the county-level city under your jurisdiction and personally deliver the package to the addressee for inspection.

At this point, you can use the excuse of non-delivery as an excuse to request that the package be withdrawn without any issues and have them discuss it with the recipient before re-delivering it to avoid further delays.

Most things are difficult to communicate over the phone, but face-to-face communication can be more sympathetic. It’s normal for a lowly courier like you, with a meager salary, to worry about a “valuable package” not being delivered or encountering problems along the way.

If all else fails, you’ll have to beg them to return the package.

Determined, you leave early, buy the homeless old man breakfast, and force-feed him 500 yuan to stop worrying.

Turn the corner, call the shelter, and immediately head to Mr. Xiao Heyun’s apartment complex.

Before leaving, you find a flyer in your rental apartment and write a letter on the back, detailing the explosion on the Bus 45 at 1:45 p.m.

Yesterday, when you gave your interview late, rumors, both true and false, were already circulating online, and the news media had also learned some details from various sources. You learned from them that the explosive was definitely a pressure cooker. Based on the repeated occurrences of explosions at 1:45 p.m., you infer that the explosive in the pressure cooker might have a timer. In other words, if the danger had been eliminated before that time, there was a high probability that the explosion would have occurred.

You’re an orphan, alone. Upon learning of this, you should have risked your life to try to stop the explosion. But before your mother died, you swore to her that no matter what difficulties you faced, you would live well and not give up easily.

Furthermore, you now have a girl you care about, and you want to try to rekindle your family. You can’t risk your life.

You tried calling the police, but it was too late.

By midnight, you couldn’t find any detailed information about the explosion online. You didn’t know the perpetrators or the exact location of the explosives in the car. You couldn’t think of any other way to prevent such a bombing, and you could only hope to minimize casualties.

The fact that Xiao Heyun was able to find the explosives in the car and then mediate with the perpetrators after calling the police shows that he’s brave and careful, and he trusts the police. Placing your hopes on him might be better than putting your own hopes on him.

You wrapped yourself up tightly and climbed up the stairs through the unmonitored fire escape. After stealthily appearing at Xiao Heyun’s door, you forced a flyer with the words “Death Prophecy” through the crack in the lower door.

After confirming that the flyer was mostly inserted, you left the complex with a sense of relief.

In the following days, you quickly delivered all the morning’s deliveries, leaving only a few scheduled for the afternoon, which wasn’t a big deal.

Then you went to a barber shop and had the barber give you a buzz cut.

This was the hairstyle you and Qin Rourou had tried out several times before deciding it was the best for you. She loved it the most and had praised your hair shape for it, saying it made you look energetic and gave people a sense of security.

After all this, you knocked on Qin Rourou’s door with a nervous heart.

Perhaps because of your new hairstyle, you weren’t subjected to the same constant interrogation through the door as last time. After learning you had something to discuss with her, she hesitated for a moment before opening the door.

You showed her your ID and work permit, reintroduced yourself, and recounted your story.

As always, Qin Rourou readily accepted your story, but in this timeline, she didn’t believe delivering all the packages was the solution to ending the cycle.

But she figured, since the cycle repeats every day, it might be worth a try.

So you chatted with her for a while, bringing up the bombing that always happens at 1:45 p.m., the air conditioner technician who’d arrive that afternoon, the flight attendant whose husband had cheated on her, and the child who might fall through the security grille.

Qin Rourou meticulously wrote everything down on paper, promising you that she’d remember it, that she wouldn’t stay home that afternoon, and that she’d go save the child.

You thought about your “evening date,” hesitated for a moment, and ultimately didn’t speak. If time keeps repeating, even if you go on a date with her tonight, even if you confirm your relationship tonight, what good is that?

The next day, you still have to bring your ID and work permit to “introduce yourself.”

After discussing the whole story with Qin Rourou, you discuss how to successfully deliver Xiao Heyun’s package back.

You’re not very articulate, and some things are difficult to say, but Qin Rourou isn’t. She helps you come up with many ideas and provides you with many insights, which puts you at ease.

When you get a call from your driver asking you to go back and load the goods, you exchange phone numbers with her, say goodbye hastily, and rush to the company’s delivery point as fast as you can.

Seeing how clean your car is, your driver is delighted and, as before, excitedly tries to load more, but you, startled, stop him.

Seeing that the number of deliveries for the afternoon doesn’t exceed your assigned delivery area, you breathe a sigh of relief and quickly ride your delivery truck to the city’s high-speed railway station. At this moment, your phone popped up with your ticket purchase information. Qin Rourou, notifying you of Xiao Heyun’s package, had already bought you a train ticket to the county-level city and arranged a pickup.

You rode your delivery bike to the underground parking lot, parked and locked it somewhere, then grabbed your ticket, carried the package destined for Xiao Heyun, and boarded the train bound for the sender’s city.

It was a weekday, so the train wasn’t crowded. You took your seat, carefully cradling the package in your arms, and pulled out your phone to call the sender, “Doctor Jiang.”

“Hello? Huh? Is there a problem with my package?”

Dr. Jiang, upon hearing you say there was a problem with his package, immediately became alarmed. “Could it have gotten damaged along the way? There’s a camera inside!”

“I saw it said valuables, and the camera is insured, but the package is so light. I was worried something might have happened, so I called to let you know.”

You gave the excuse you and Qin Rourou had agreed on.

“Extremely light? Could it have been swapped?”

Dr. Jiang’s thoughts shifted. “It was an expensive lens when I sent it, and you took photos of it. If it’s become something else, it must be your fault!”

“Yes, but I’m just a courier. If there’s a problem during transportation, it would be unfair for me to bear the responsibility. And now the recipient can’t be contacted, so I can’t deliver it. Look, there’s something so expensive inside. Can I send it back to you so you can inspect it in person?”

You’re worried he won’t… He was willing to accept it, having already considered all his worries. “The package is still intact. If you open it and everything is fine, then we’re all happy. I’ll pay for the courier fee if you send it again. If it’s moved, it must have been a problem during transportation. I’ll provide you with proof, and you’ll provide me with proof, and you can file a claim with the company.”

“What’s this about delivery or not? You’ve got me confused!”

It should be lunchtime, but Dr. Jiang still seems very busy. This is evident in the constant interruptions he receives from the other end of the line as soon as he answers the phone.

You faintly hear a patient complaining about the doctor taking personal calls during consultation time, wasting their time, or something.

“What do you mean by consultation time? I’ve already finished seeing all the specialists this morning. I’m sympathetic to you all for coming all this way and waiting in line for so long, so I’m giving you an extra appointment! The morning appointments were already over, and I should have been off duty at noon. I’ve been seeing you all this time, and I’m using my personal time to see you. What’s wrong with me taking a personal call on my personal time?”

Dr. Jiang, perhaps because he hadn’t eaten or drunk anything all afternoon and had been working so intensely for so long, had a bit of a short temper and was quite rude on the other end of the line.

“If you don’t want to see me, just book another specialist this afternoon. I can go grab a bite!”

Listening to Dr. Jiang’s complaints, you couldn’t help but sigh at the hardships of every profession.

Even a humble courier like you can fill your lunch even when you’re busy. Who would have thought such a respected doctor would even go hungry?

From his tone, it sounded as if voluntarily working overtime to see patients beyond their scheduled appointments was commonplace.

The patient on the other end fell silent, seemingly acquiescing to Dr. Jiang’s “personal call.”

“If you want it delivered, just deliver it. I’m in Clinic 3 of the Orthopedics Outpatient Department at the First People’s Hospital. If you can’t find me up front, come find me in the inpatient department in the back.”

But after all that arguing, Dr. Jiang didn’t want to hear any more of your explanation and just wanted to hang up.

“I hope there’s nothing wrong with the delivery. If it’s been swapped or misplaced, I’ll hold you accountable!”

You finally got his promise, overjoyed. Without even worrying about the threats, you promised to deliver it as soon as possible.

After you hung up, the woman next to you looked at you sympathetically.

“Young man, the delivery was wrong, and you still have to go to City K to deliver it to the sender?”

“Yes.”

You couldn’t explain, so you smiled helplessly.

“You just started working, right? Only when you’re new would you be so serious about something like this, even going so far as to go down there and get tangled up in the grassroots.”

Locals refer to prefecture-level cities under their jurisdiction as “xiaxia.”

“Yeah, that’s right.”

“Hey, work’s tough these days. Don’t worry too much, young man. Talk to the other person politely, don’t get into arguments, or you’ll end up being unreasonable.”

The woman sitting next to you was also alone. Perhaps worried you’d be frustrated by this, she started to soothe you with examples of her own mistakes from her early days, rambling on and on.

You were grateful for her kindness, but your thoughts had already drifted to the People’s Hospital, further away. You were considering how to convince Dr. Jiang to withdraw the package and resend it and how to get back before dark to deliver the remaining packages.

You spent the entire journey feeling both grateful and anxious. Almost as soon as the bus arrived at the station, you eagerly disembarked, your package in hand.

The driver Qin Rourou had arranged for you was already waiting at the door. You climbed in, gave the address of “First People’s Hospital,” and breathed a sigh of relief, leaning back in the back seat to rest.

The prefecture-level city wasn’t large, so it didn’t take long for them to get you to the hospital. You disembarked, asked the hospital guide on the first floor about the orthopedics department, and immediately rushed up the stairs.

Upon reaching the orthopedics department, you greeted the nurse at the door, explaining that you had an appointment with Dr. Jiang to deliver a package. The nurse then led you into the orthopedics clinic.

The clinic was already empty. A doctor in his forties was carefully examining an X-ray. Perhaps his eyes were uncomfortable with the constant exposure to light; he took off his glasses, rubbed his eyelids, and put them back on, his face etched with fatigue.

“This leg needs surgery…”

He pointed to a crack and said, “This isn’t an ordinary bone fracture…”

You waited quietly outside the now-empty clinic door, waiting for Dr. Jiang to finish seeing the last few patients and discuss the package with you. Just then, you felt someone forcefully push you away.

You steadied yourself and noticed a burly middle-aged man had forced his way through the doorway. He charged straight at Dr. Jiang, who was looking at an X-ray on a lightbox.

You vaguely noticed something long-handled hanging from the middle-aged man’s waist.

Years of military training had given you a glimpse of something amiss. Seeing the man walking forward with his head lowered and his hand on his waist, alarm bells went off.

“Be careful—!”

Instantly, you didn’t care about whether it was a delivery or not. You shoved the package into the nurse’s hands and rushed over.

At the same time, the man pulled out something from his waist. It was a meat-cutting knife?!

“Jiang, you cut off my son’s leg, and today I want yours too!”

Everyone was stunned by this sudden turn of events.

You used all your strength to knock down the burly, middle-aged man. However, he remained remarkably calm. Even as he fell, he still raised his hand, attempting to cut Dr. Jiang’s ankle with his knife.

“What are you standing there for? Run!”

The situation was urgent, and you didn’t have time to think. You held down the man’s left arm with one hand and used your other to grab the knife.

“Call security for help!”

Dr. Jiang finally woke up and ran away. Seeing Dr. Jiang flee, the man, enraged, engaged you with his knife.

Although you had received professional combat training, the man was incredibly strong and armed, putting you at a disadvantage in a bare-handed confrontation. In the chaos, you sustained several scratches on your arm and a gash on your face.

Fearing he might chase you and injure someone, you gritted your teeth and held the armed man tightly inside the clinic.

“He’s got a knife! Don’t come in until security arrives!”

Thinking you could get through it tomorrow even if you got hurt, you simply kept shouting at the door and fought him alone.

The screams from the ward and the hallway were incessant. With injuries imminent, your nerves were already high, and distracted by the screams, you took several more stabs.

Luckily, the man had no strategy, just wielding the knife recklessly. It wasn’t long before the security arrived, armed with a riot fork, and subdued him.

After the man was subdued and tied up and taken away by the security, Dr. Jiang, trembling with fear, entered the clinic and hurriedly called for help in examining your injuries.

“First, calm down…”

You sat breathlessly on a stool, your face and body covered in blood, clutching Dr. Jiang’s arm.

“Please take the package back!”

The author has something to say:

Before leaving, you found an advertising leaflet in your rental apartment. You wrote a letter on the back, detailing the explosion on the Bus 45 at 1:45 p.m. You then slipped it under Xiao Heyun’s door.

Xiao Heyun, waking up early this morning without his glasses, thought, “There seems to be a piece of waste paper on the floor? Did I not clean it up yesterday, or was it a flyer stuck somewhere?”

Muttering about complaining to the management about letting in the flyer, he crumpled up the flyer without even looking at it and threw it into the wastebasket.

chapters.title: The Delivered Express
chapters.content:
Your company’s jackets and uniforms are very sturdy. That knife is for cutting, not stabbing, so the wounds aren’t actually deep. You know your wounds are only flesh wounds, so you’re more concerned about whether the package can be delivered.

But to others, your “bloodied” appearance is terrifying.

“Why bother with the package now? You saved my life. I won’t even care if the camera is lost!”

Dr. Jiang felt a wave of dread as he thought of the knife-wielding man just now.

He had eaten at 8 a.m. and hadn’t eaten or drunk anything yet. When that man drew his knife, his legs were truly weak, and he hadn’t had the energy to fight him. He was about to die, but this delivery guy saved him.

In a sense, you saved him, and he’s naturally grateful.

But you insisted on taking care of work first.

Seeing your insistence, Dr. Jiang had no choice but to open his package in front of you. He was relieved to find that the camera he had sent was perfectly packaged, with no issues at all.

“Now we’re all relieved. Look, it’s intact!”

Dr. Jiang carefully placed the lens back into its box and said, “Your wound needs attention. Take off your clothes and let me see if it needs stitches. Also, the knife might not be clean. You’d better get a tetanus shot…”

“I’m glad the package is fine. Please send it again.”

You pulled the pre-prepared delivery slip from your pocket. “Dr. Jiang, please call customer service and tell them to ask for the package to be returned. I’ll have the company remove it from your shipping information.”

“What’s wrong with you? You’re still bleeding. It’s infected and inflamed. It’s a serious condition!”

Dr. Jiang, because of his occupational illness, insisted on treating your wound first.

The two stubborn people clashed, but the nurse standing nearby smoothed things over. She tended to your wound while Dr. Jiang focused on returning the package.

You stripped naked and sat in the orthopedic clinic, where the doctor and nurse examined and tended to your wound. At this moment, the corridor was crowded and noisy. Many people in the hospital had heard that someone had been attacked and had flocked over to watch the incident. However, fearing they might be attacked themselves, they had watched from a distance, some filming and some taking photos.

After the attacker had been abducted by the hospital security, they finally dared to gather around, craning their heads in front of the orthopedic clinic to stare at you and Dr. Jiang, pointing and making comments.

“Did you see that doctor? I heard he ruined someone’s leg and got hacked!”

“That delivery guy was so unlucky, getting stabbed for no reason!”

“Being a doctor is so dangerous these days; he even got hacked.”

“You’re wrong. Why didn’t other doctors get hacked, but he did? There must be something morally wrong with him!”

“Why did the leg get hacked? Didn’t he give him a bribe?”

“Who would dare choose him for treatment after this? He ruined a perfectly good leg…”

It was hard for you to sit there and listen to everyone gossiping, let alone Dr. Jiang.

His hand holding the tweezers paused, his eyes suddenly reddened, and he lowered his head in embarrassment.

“Doctor, don’t be sad. They’re all talking nonsense.”

You don’t know what Dr. Jiang is like, but you don’t think someone who skips lunch to give you an extra appointment can be a bad person. “They’re just good at talking, but when things get tough, they’re too quiet to say a word. Why bother with them?”

“Oh, I regret studying medicine.”

Dr. Jiang shook his head. “I have parents and children to support, and I’m away all day. I can’t take care of my family, and now I’m risking my life at work…”

You feel bad, but you don’t know how to comfort him.

Soon, the police arrive to take your statements and learn about the case.

It turns out that a few months ago, the hospital brought in a child who had been in a car accident while jaywalking. His right leg and hand were heavily injured, and he was in shock and in a coma.

With such serious injuries, he should have been transferred to a hospital in the provincial capital for treatment, but by then, the child had already suffered major blood vessel damage, and his muscles and bones had been unable to reconnect. Without treatment, his life would have been in danger on the way to the hospital. To save his life, Dr. Jiang opted to amputate his leg.

The child’s amputation at such a young age was certainly difficult for his family to accept, especially his father, a chef.

Later, he heard somewhere that a leg with such an injury could have been saved if sent to a major hospital, but his son’s leg had been delayed. Furious, he sued the hospital.

Later, based on the diagnosis and pathology report, the reviewing department ruled that Dr. Jiang’s choice was correct. The patient’s family lost the case, and it was later dropped.

No one could have imagined that months later, the child’s father would actually harm someone.

At noon, Dr. Jiang’s appointment was a late one. The clinic was already sparsely populated, with the security guards and other doctors and nurses mostly off for lunch or naps. If you hadn’t happened to be there, Dr. Jiang would have certainly died.

After taking the statement, your wound was treated, and you received a tetanus shot at the hospital. You were anxious to get back to deliver the package.

Dr. Jiang had originally wanted to treat you to a meal, but upon learning that you were a courier from City W and had come by train specifically to check on his package, he was immediately impressed. He no longer tried to persuade you to stay but simply added your WeChat and phone number, repeatedly reminding you to take good care of your wounds.

With your face bruised and bandaged, you boarded the train back home, bracing everyone’s surprised gazes.

The successful withdrawal of Xiao Heyun’s package was a huge encouragement to you.

After a flurry of activity, it was already four in the afternoon. Suddenly, you remembered the bus bombing that had occurred that afternoon. After a moment’s hesitation, you pulled out your phone and prepared to search for it.

You had been deliberately avoiding the bus bombing, fearing bad news.

However, before you could even open a search engine, Qin Rourou called.

“Song Budao, your advance warning worked!”

Qin Rourou’s voice on the other end of the line was cheerful and excited. “That Bus 45 didn’t explode. Someone on board called the police and successfully subdued the bomb-carrying attacker. Together with the other passengers, they took the bomb away! The police then blocked the bridge, took over, and successfully defused the bomb. I think it might be Xiao Heyun. The online reports also mentioned a man named Xiao and his friend, a woman named Li.”

You were startled, then overwhelmed with ecstasy.

“He’s so strong!”

You were filled with sincere admiration. “That man named Xiao Heyun is so much braver and more capable than me!”

To have the guts to continue riding that Bus 45 after receiving your advance warning and to subdue the attacker and assist the police in defusing the bomb—this is something no ordinary person could do.

Ask yourself: if you had received such a warning, even if you didn’t believe it, you would never ride a bus again.

“What are you talking about? Even after such a situation, you still persist in doing good deeds every day. That’s quite impressive!”

Qin Rourou’s heart sank when she heard that a bombing was about to occur in the city that morning. By noon, she was even more worried. She simply went to wait on a high building with a view of the bridge.

When the police blocked the bridge, she knew someone must have called the police. She didn’t know if it was Song Budao or Xiao Heyun, but regardless of who it was, she was genuinely happy that the matter had been resolved successfully without causing further casualties.

You, too, were overjoyed to hear that the police had blocked the bridge first, preventing further casualties, after experiencing the tragic scene last time.

“I’ve already rescued the child. How’s everything going on over there?”

Qin Rourou asked curiously.

“It went smoothly. Doctor Jiang agreed to return the package. He said he’d explain it to Xiao Heyun and send it out again tomorrow.”

You beamed at the mention of this. “I happened to see someone trying to attack Doctor Jiang when I arrived, and I just happened to save him. If I’d been later, the package wouldn’t have been delivered!”

“What happened? Why is there another attack?”

You quickly told Qin Rourou what had just happened.

“Oh my god.”

Hearing that the man had drawn a knife, she exclaimed.

“That’s too dangerous.”

Qin Rourou worried for you. “If you’re still in the cycle tomorrow, don’t go to rescue someone unarmed. At least bring someone with you to help.”

“I have a feeling I won’t be in the cycle again.”

For some reason, you felt incredibly relieved and elated. Although your body was covered in minor wounds, you didn’t feel any pain at all.

“This package could have been considered a death package. Both the sender and the recipient were in danger, but now, both are alive and well. Perhaps my cycle is for this, to save them.”

You previously only knew that Xiao Heyun died in the car during the explosion, but you didn’t know that at the same time, the sender of the package, Dr. Jiang, also suffered a similarly vicious attack.

Judging by the chef’s utterly ruthless act of seeking out a boning knife, Dr. Jiang in the other loops must be in much worse shape.

If it weren’t for the bus bombing, such a vicious incident might have quickly gained traction and made the news. However, the bus bombing generated such a strong buzz that the internet was flooded with news about it. The attack on the doctor in City K, like so many other news stories deliberately ignored during this period, will likely fade into obscurity.

“That must be it.”

You spoke with growing excitement.

“I’m just a courier. I ensure the safe delivery of packages and the safety and happiness of both the recipient and the delivery person. Perhaps I’ve fulfilled the mission entrusted to me by Heaven.”

“I hope so. I wish your dreams come true.”

Qin Rourou smiled. “If the loop stopped tomorrow, you could do whatever you want.”

“Yes.”

You said with a pointed smile.

“I have a lot of things I’m getting ready to do…”

After hanging up the phone, you stared out the window. Though covered in wounds, you felt an indescribable sense of satisfaction.

Everyone’s safe; that’s truly wonderful.

After getting off the train, you grabbed your delivery truck and, not wanting to waste a moment, continued your delivery.

Luckily, you’ve delivered these packages many times before, so you’re familiar with them. Although it’s almost dark, you’re still confident you can finish them all before the end of your shift.

On your way to the delivery, you passed a street vendor you’d bought lottery tickets from before. For some reason, you pulled over and bought a lottery ticket.

You’d memorized the winning numbers by heart.

The big screen in the square played news about a bus bombing that was successfully prevented by passengers. The passengers, though still terrified, excitedly boasted about their heroic actions.

“As soon as the young man yelled, I knew I couldn’t run away, so I just went up and joined them in pinning down the man!”

“I knew the driver wasn’t a good person the moment I got on the bus. He didn’t say a word the whole time!”

“The young man and woman meant well, but they were young, inexperienced, and weak. How could they have prevented the bombing without our help?”

The passengers on the news chattered endlessly, but there was no mention of the interviews with Xiao Heyun and the woman surnamed Li, the biggest heroes.

You parked your car beneath the big screen and quietly watched the news.

After confirming that it was indeed Xiao Heyun who had prevented the bombing, you smiled with relief and rode away like a hidden knight, “dumbfounded and departing.”

Because you returned so late, you didn’t finish your work for the day until around seven or eight o’clock. As expected, you were scolded when you returned to the company’s business location.

However, upon seeing the bandages and facial injuries and hearing that you’d stopped a gangster while delivering a package to the doctor at the hospital, the stern-faced team leader kindly gave you the day off tomorrow, bringing you good news.

Today had been a busy and exciting day, leaving you exhausted both physically and mentally. Add to that the fact that two tragic events had been successfully averted, and you were filled with excitement and a lingering sense of anticipation. So, as soon as you got off work, you returned to your rental apartment, set your alarm for 9 a.m., and fell asleep.

The next morning, you were awakened by the blaring alarm.

Having accidentally pressed on the wound on your face while sleeping, you woke up with a burning pain. But the next moment, you understood what the pain was and sat up with a jerk.

You pulled out your phone, looked at the date and time displayed, and couldn’t contain your emotions, tears streaming down your face.

You’ve been trapped in a time loop for over twenty days. Though you comfort yourself daily by treating this time as a gift, the anxiety you feel is impossible to dispel. With each cycle, the responsibilities you shoulder grow, and the mental pressure intensifies. You can’t tell when you’ll finally give up.

With each cycle, you dare not act recklessly or indulge yourself. You live cautiously in “today” while daring not to truly hope for a “future.”

But today, your cycle finally stops!

After a good cry, you wash your face, take out the anti-inflammatory medication Dr. Jiang gave you, and go to the community clinic to get a replacement.

Then you head straight to the department store where you bought clothes and buy the new outfit you’d loved.

Looking at your fresh, clean self in the mirror, you grin with satisfaction, but that smile quickly gravitates to the wound on your face, and your grin turns into a snarl.

After leaving the mall, you returned home with your old clothes and went to a flower shop near your home. You bought eleven pink roses, holding them shyly in your arms, and called Qin Rourou.

After learning she was home, you hugged the roses, hiding your face behind the bouquet, and walked rather sheepishly toward her house.

Just then, you passed by the lottery station you’d passed last night and saw the poster on the doorway that read, “Yesterday, xxxx surprisingly won a 500 million jackpot!” You couldn’t help but take a few more glances.

These few glances caused your eyes to suddenly widen.

Of course, you weren’t the one who won first prize; otherwise, the poster on the doorway would have read, “Yesterday, this lottery station surprisingly won a 500 million jackpot!”

But yesterday’s winning numbers were only slightly different from the ones you bought!

You rushed into the lottery station excitedly, but the owner, upon seeing you, grabbed your arm with even greater excitement than you.

“Hey young man, did you know you won second prize? You’re so lucky!”

The boss was impressed. “You were so close! You were so close to winning first prize. That’s 500 million!”

When the people at the lottery station heard you’d won second prize, they all gathered around.

“How much is the second prize?”

“First prize is five million, so second prize should be at least a few hundred thousand, right?”

“There are more second prizes this round, so each ticket only gets 12,000 yuan,” the boss said.

“Tsk, only 12,000 yuan?”

“What? That’s not much.”

The lottery players who had arrived after hearing the news dispersed.

“But you won a hundred prizes, didn’t you?”

After the crowd dispersed, the boss winked at you.

“Hahaha, you’re right!”

You finally broke down and burst into laughter.

Although you only won second prize, you bought a lot!

12,000 yuan and 100 winning tickets is still 1.2 million yuan!

The kind boss taught you how to claim your prize at the provincial lottery station, told you how much you’d earn after tax, and asked if you could hang a sign outside the door advertising your winnings.

You happily agreed, thanked the boss, and walked out of the lottery station with a swagger.

Right now, that lottery ticket is sitting in your wallet. It’s a 500 million jackpot, and no one would care about you, the second-place winner.

Although you’re not very good at socializing, you can ask Qin Rourou to accompany you to collect the prize this afternoon.

You happily headed straight for the flower shop you’d just been to. As soon as you entered, you called out to the owner:

“Boss, take these flowers apart and give me eighty-eight more!”

Then the owner was happy too.

You clutched ninety-nine roses, carrying them like cat litter, and scurried up to the fifth floor of Qin Rourou’s house.

When she heard your footsteps, Qin Rourou opened the door, her eyes instantly filled with an overwhelming sea of ​​pink roses.

“What are you doing…”

Qin Rourou blushed.

“I, I’m on vacation today.”

The first time you confessed your feelings to someone, you stumbled and threw roses in their face.

“Can I, can I…”

“Can you please go on a date with me!”

You mustered up your courage, summoning the energy you’d used to in training, and shouted it out in one breath.

The sound echoed through the hallway, startling the old man next door. He opened the door to see what was going on, and when he saw what was happening, he couldn’t help but smile through his narrowed eyes.

Your face flushed like a monkey’s butt.

Qin Rourou was stunned for a moment, then reached out to take the pink rose you offered her with a sweet smile.

“Sure.”

(Delivered package, end.)

The author has something to say: This concludes the main story. Both of these brothers have experienced their springtime in life, a blessing in disguise. Tomorrow there will be three or four short side stories, covering the aftermath of Li Shiqing and Xiao Heyun; the aftermath of the young man and Qin Rourou; and the aftermath of the incident with the driver’s daughter. Thank you all for your continued support!

CONTENT END 62

chapters.title: Extra: You and Your Future
chapters.content:
You successfully escaped the loop.

Until the final moment, when the wheel of time began to turn again, you couldn’t comprehend why you had entered the loop or why it had ended. Ultimately, you could only attribute it to that package you had finally handled.

Think carefully; Dr. Jiang was a good doctor who treated and saved lives. If he hadn’t been in trouble, he would have saved countless lives in his lifetime. By saving Dr. Jiang, you indirectly saved countless lives. From this perspective, perhaps Heaven’s delay in time meant you hadn’t been meaningless in trying again and again.

The same goes for Xiao Heyun. Because he survived, so did so many other passengers on the bus, as well as those who should have been affected by the explosion…

The thought that Xiao Heyun had avoided a life-or-death disaster thanks to your early warning filled you with joy.

Perhaps it was the pleasure of “doing good deeds anonymously.”

Unfortunately, the heavens weren’t willing to fulfill your wish of “doing good deeds anonymously.” Because of the bus bombing, Dr. Jiang’s attack by the patient’s family didn’t become a major issue. However, Dr. Jiang didn’t let this cause him to neglect the courier’s life-saving act. The next day, he sent a banner to the delivery company that read “Bold and Brave” and called your company to express his gratitude.

Your company already has a reward system for good deeds that “promote positive social energy.” As soon as Dr. Jiang’s banner arrived, everyone at your delivery company was commended by the organization, and the incident even appeared in the company’s internal newspaper.

You had just confirmed your relationship with Qin Rourou, a beautiful, gentle woman with a pleasant voice. You were already feeling very proud, and then the next day, the banner arrived, and the company even had the head of the entire region call you to encourage you and express their support for you as a potential cadre. You truly achieved success in both love and career.

Dr. Jiang’s case later had a sequel. Because the child’s father was the family’s breadwinner, and the child was young and disabled, Dr. Jiang ultimately chose not to sue the assailant after mediation. However, the losses incurred still had to be remedied. The assailant compensated Song Budao for medical expenses, and the hospital also awarded him a bonus for your bravery. Together, the two sums amounted to around 50,000 to 60,000 yuan.

This makes you even more impressed by the difficulties doctors face. The other party had clearly attacked with a knife, but under pressure from public opinion and reality, they ultimately had to sympathize with the vulnerable. After all, the hospital also had to maintain its reputation, and a fuss would be detrimental to both parties.

Everyone thought the child’s father had extenuating circumstances, but who could have imagined that Dr. Jiang had elderly parents and young children to support?

I heard that as soon as the incident was over, Dr. Jiang enrolled in a Sanda class and stopped actively adding extra appointments. He would go to the class after work for a while and even get up for a run in the morning, fearing that he would run into this situation again if he ran out of energy. After all, not everyone would always come to his aid.

You won one hundred second prizes, and after tax deduction, you received a little over one million in prize money.

While the million-yuan bonus wasn’t enough to buy you a house in this city, it was enough to allow you to pursue your passions without worries.

After receiving the money, your first action was to give up your basement apartment and rent a one-bedroom apartment next to the cram school. While it wasn’t large, it was conveniently located near the business center. Most importantly, you were tired of living in basements, and this one was so bright it made you squint. The landlord even gave you a balcony plant.

Although the floor was high, as a courier, climbing stairs was the last thing you feared.

With a decent place to live, you wouldn’t feel so cramped when your girlfriend occasionally visited.

After settling into a stable home and job, you delivered packages during the day and attended cram school at night. Six months later, you took the exam for the local Police Academy and were successfully admitted as a police officer, achieving a perfect score on the physical fitness test.

Your father was a fallen police officer, and you yourself are a police officer, with numerous experiences of bravery. Naturally, you had no problem passing the political review.

On the day you were admitted to the academy, you officially resigned from the delivery company and, along with your girlfriend, Qin Rourou, treated all the colleagues who had taken care of you to a farewell dinner.

That night, everyone was drunk. Your master burst into tears, clutching your hand and wailing:

“I really like you, young man! You’re diligent and measured, hardworking, and not only are you willing to endure hardships, but you’re also not stingy, and you’re so ambitious! If I had a son like you, I’d die without regrets!”

He sobbed, “I knew you’d be able to study, but I didn’t expect it to be so soon!”

For the past six months, you haven’t been shy about attending evening classes. You’ve always been an open and honest person. Months ago, you mentioned that you were cramming for high school courses and that you wanted to become a police officer, fulfilling your military dream.

Now that your dream has come true, everyone is happy for you, but they’re also reluctant to let you go.

Seeing Master crying so hard, Qin Rourou thought for a moment and whispered something in your ear.

“Master, if you don’t mind me, I’ll be your son!”

For the past six months, Master has been taking care of you, teaching you step-by-step at work and caring about your daily life.

He helped you move, and he even put the pots and pans in the kitchen in order and delivered them to you.

“My biological father died young, leaving me an orphan. I’ll take you in as my Heavenfather. I’ll be filial to you and take care of you when you’re sick and in pain!”

You whispered in Master’s ear.

Everyone was stunned by these words.

Master wasn’t a capable man; otherwise, his wife wouldn’t have run away. He was a truly kind and loyal person, but in an era when even the most vulnerable struggled, this became a flaw, leaving him unable to protect his own family.

Later, times improved, and job opportunities abounded. He worked diligently for the industry’s most prestigious courier company for nearly ten years. Although he didn’t become a team leader, his income was comparable to theirs. Ultimately, he was just a courier.

But you were willing to accept him as your Heavenfather. Those whose families were unhappy understood each other’s longings best.

Instantly, the master burst into tears, tearfully accepting you as his “godson.”

With everyone witnessing, you, as was custom back home, knelt down, offered the master a glass of wine, and called him “Dad.” This effectively acknowledged your identities.

Watching you like this, your colleagues were delighted. They drank bottle after bottle, and finally, everyone stumbled home.

Qin Rourou walked you back to your bachelor pad. Before leaving, you clutched her hand tightly.

“Rou Rou, I have a dad!”

You whimpered.

“Hmm.”

Qin Rourou wiped your face.

“I have a girlfriend too!”

“Okay!”

Qin Rourou rolled her eyes.

“Rourou, I’ll treat you well from now on, forever!”

Your voice was incredibly gentle.

“I know; I believe it.”

Qin Rourou sighed and wiped your face.

“You have to wait for me. Once I’m a police officer, I’ll have the confidence to marry you. Otherwise, how will your family agree? Once I marry you, I’ll have a family again.”

You kept mumbling, “That’s great! I have a family again, almost. My mom will be so happy…”

Qin Rourou’s nose felt sore, and she finally couldn’t hold back her tears.

“It will happen.”

She lay on your chest, her arm around your neck, and said, “A person as good as you will have everything.”

》》》》

A few years later, you graduated from the Criminal Investigation Department. Immediately, you took the public security recruitment exam in October of that year, fearing you’d exceed the age limit if you delayed any longer.

Because you had excellent grades in school, excellent physical fitness, and a strong physique, you aced the written, interview, and physical tests throughout the exam process. You were successfully accepted into the Municipal Criminal Police Brigade and became a glorious police officer.

On the day you reported, Qin Rourou, now a renowned screenwriter, drove you there.

Two years earlier, Qin Rourou’s script, “Endless Cycle,” was made into a film. It became an instant hit, becoming a dark horse in the film and television industry that year. She subsequently produced several imaginative and innovative TV series, focusing on the social and livelihood issues of ordinary people, and gradually gained a reputation in the industry.

She’s now both wealthy and famous, but her homebody nature and her devotion to her boyfriend remain unchanged.

To make it easier for you to meet her, she bought a studio apartment near the Police Academy where you worked once she had enough money. Later, when you were accepted into the Criminal Investigation Team, she planned to buy another apartment near the team. Everyone joked with you that she was determined to become a “cop’s wife.”

You didn’t have any narrow-minded prejudices about “living off as a gigolo” or “being kept by a woman.” When you heard your girlfriend was buying a house near the city bureau, you gave her all your savings of over a million yuan and told her to go ahead and buy it, without asking about the property rights.

On the way to report, Qin Rourou pulled the property deed from the glove compartment and handed it to you.

“The deed has been issued. The down payment is 2.2 million yuan, so we’ll split it in half.”

She said with a smile.

“What do you mean, half and half?”

Thinking it was just another 30-40 square meter studio apartment like before, you flipped through the deed in confusion, only to see it listed as a 120-square meter, three-bedroom apartment, owned by two people. You looked up at her again.

“Why such a large house?”

“I need to raise a child, and I need a study, so it needs to be bigger,” Qin Rourou said calmly.

You understood her meaning, your eyes lit up, and you were speechless with excitement.

“Look, this is our house, and there’s a lot of mortgage debt. We’ll have to pay it all together every month. So, what do you think we should use as a couple?”

Qin Rourou winked at her boyfriend.

“Husband and wife! We absolutely have to use our husband and wife names!”

You weren’t stupid at this point, and you quickly made the decision.

“I’ll ask for leave, have a witness, and get the marriage certificate!”

For the past few years, you’ve spent Chinese New Year in Qin Rourou’s hometown. Her family is very pleased with you. If you weren’t still studying, they would have urged you to get married long ago.

Considering your own job wasn’t stable yet, you didn’t want your girlfriend to be laughed at back home, so you insisted on getting a job before getting married. Otherwise, you’d be leaving her family feeling embarrassed.

Now, you’re a civil servant, a glorious police officer. While you’re not exactly rich, you believe you can bring her honor, security, and happiness.

“It’s only your first day on the job. Isn’t that a bit bad?”

Qin Rourou, surprised by your quick action, was also stunned.

“I think they’ll understand!”

You said with a smile, “Having my work anniversary and my wedding anniversary together—how meaningful!”

You were escorted to the entrance of the Criminal Police Brigade, where someone was already waiting.

“You’re the new guy, Xiao Song, right? I’m the colleague who’s helping you get acquainted with the situation, and I’ll be your mentor from now on. My last name is Zhang.”

A familiar face appeared before you.

You were stunned.

“What? Do I look scary?”

Old Zhang, seeing you staring at him, touched his face in confusion.

“No. You just look a lot like someone I know.”

You remembered Old Zhang’s red eyes from that replay, and you felt more confident and excited about your future relationships.

He’s a good cop.

“Okay, I’ll get you acquainted first…”

“Report!”

You suddenly saluted.

“Huh?”

Old Zhang was stunned.

“Please ask your supervisor for an hour’s leave. I need to get my marriage certificate!”

Old Zhang, a trustworthy police officer, not only granted your leave after learning the whole story but also took you to get your police number, uniform, and formal attire in advance so you could wear your handsome uniform for your wedding photos.

In the Civil Affairs Bureau’s wedding hall, you, in your police uniform, with your beautiful girlfriend nestled beside you, became a sight to behold.

“Come on, bride and groom, look here! It’s time for the photo. One, two, three…”

The new and old officers stood by, smiling as they witnessed the happiest moment of your life.

“Congratulations on your wedding!”

End
